summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, spread over three disk sides, that won the C64 demo compo at X 2008 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2008.
why: Sceners praise its polish, the flow between parts, the vector work and Dane's soundtrack. Several describe it as a demo that keeps growing on you with repeat viewings.

quote.text: Now, after having watched it countless times, I can safely say that I am blown away.

summary: Batman Group's Amstrad CPC demo, which won the CPC demo compo at Forever 2011 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2011.
why: It also took Best Technical Achievement and Public Choice at those awards, and was nominated for Best Graphics and Breakthrough Performance. Tagged as using the Batman theme.

summary: Oxyron's two-disk-side C64 demo, the thirteenth Coma Light, which won the demo compo at X 2012. Code is by Axis, Peiselulli and Bitbreaker, music by Fanta.
why: Sceners single out Fanta's soundtrack and samples, the parallax part, the vectors with balls and the perspective scroller, and many rank it among the best C64 demos.

quote.text: I love everything about this demo, but one thing really stands out for me - the sound, music and samples.

summary: Resource and Chorus's three-disk-side C64 demake of the Amiga demo Desert Dream, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: Sceners admire how close the effects get to the Amiga original, with Fanta's soundtrack fitted to three SID voices. Opinion on remakes was split, but the effort behind it was widely praised.
highlights: Amiga tunes on three SID voices

quote.text: Amazing that a large number of the effects actually look VERY close to the original, guess it shows the power of the C64 in the hands of the right coders!

summary: Logon System's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2017. Code and graphics are by Overflow, music by Tom&Jerry.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2018. The source is available for anyone who wants to see how it was done.

summary: lft's 256-byte C64 intro with music, which won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2017. lft did both the code and the music.
why: Sceners are amazed at fitting a tune and a glitchy visual show into 256 bytes. lft's detailed writeup on his website is praised too, and it was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2018.

quote.text: This is the way to steal a show -- do something nobody has seen in as few bytes as possible.

summary: Glance's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2010.
why: Sceners praise the smooth vectors and the variety of effects, and one calls it a technical milestone. A themed design and an extensive note file on the disk also get mentioned.

quote.text: A thoroughly enjoyable demo with non stop action and varied effects.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2003. Viznut did the code, graphics and music, with graphics from ccr.
why: Tagged as using speech synthesis, and Viznut handled the code, graphics and music himself.

summary: Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights' demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4, which won the Alternative Platforms Demo compo at Evoke 2014.
why: A win on a less common platform. It features the picture Meanmachine by Nero and uses Krill's loader, and the tags say it runs in an endless loop.

summary: Condense's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. NoRecess did the code, CeD the graphics and Aki the music.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2019. The source and a writeup are both available.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at X 2010. It is dedicated to the memory of Jerry/Triad and Sammi Hoyt Barakat.
why: Sceners single out the scrolling panda picture, the parallax landscape and the soundtrack, with tunes by Danko, Abaddon and Magnar. It was also nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

quote.text: I love the humongous scrolling pictures (panda, endpart).

summary: Instinct and Booze Design's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2009 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009.
why: Sceners single out the long 3D section, the recursive zoomer, Archmage's graphics and Dane's minimalistic soundtrack, which was kept lean to leave rastertime for the effects.

quote.text: State of the art, innovative demo effects here.

summary: Aeon is a ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, which won the Combined Low-End compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2008.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2008. Graphics are by pROF, with animation by G.D. and music by Key-Jee.

summary: Booze Design's two-disk-side C64 demo, entered at X 2014 as The Booze Demo, where it came second. It carries a political message and uses X-FLI.
why: Sceners single out the rotating raster bars, with some calling it the best C64 effect so far. The fractal zoomer, palette rotators and the demo's message are also mentioned.

quote.text: the rotating rasters was the best effect!

summary: Censor Design and Oxyron's four-disk-side C64 collaboration, the party version of which won the demo compo at X 2014. The name fuses Oxyron's Coma Light and Censor's Wonderland series.
why: Sceners single out the textured cube, the scrolling intro picture, the graphics and logos, and the massive credits part. The mix of styles from so many contributors sparked a long debate about coherence.

quote.text: The demo features some of the nicest demo gfx and logos ever made and some really solid code.

summary: lft's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2016. He did the code, graphics and music himself.
why: Sceners praise how the rain-soaked story, the minimalistic art and the music hold together, and that it is all the work of one person. It earned four Meteoriks 2017 nominations, including Best Storytelling.

quote.text: I love how the parts are connected by the story and how well the music bridges the parts and holds them together (the rain scenes are crazy good).

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC 4K intro, which won the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2018. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Tom&Jerry the music.
why: A compo win in the 4K class on the CPC. The tags mark it as isometric and set to loop endlessly.

summary: Chiphead is an Atari VCS 2600 demo by KK of Altair, which won the Atari VCS 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. KK did all the code.
why: Nominated for the That's Not Possible On This Platform award at The Meteoriks 2017. Tagged as a demake with dance animations and a rave theme.

summary: Smash Designs and The Obsessed Maniacs' two-disk-side C64 remake of the PC demo Second Reality, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1997.
why: Sceners rate kb's SID soundtrack highly, and one thinks it beats the original's music. Views on the conversion's execution are mixed, but it remains a favourite for people who know the original.

quote.text: The music in this remake is incredible, particularly part 4.

summary: Reflex's two-disk-side C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1995. PVCF did the music, with code by Guru, kb and Quiss.
why: Sceners remember it as the demo that showed PC-style effects such as rotating tunnels running on a C64, and for PVCF's techno-influenced tunes. It was voted third best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: I was absolutely blown away with the PC style effects, it was just a total revelation to see that rotating tunnels etc. could be done on the C64.

summary: Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights' demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4, which won the Commodore 8bit Demo compo at Revision 2011.
why: Mad did the code, Degauss the code and music, Nero the 2D graphics and Decca the fonts. It uses Krill's loader.

summary: Numen is an Atari 8-bit demo by Taquart, which won the demo compo at Lato Ludzików 2002. Fox and Eru did the code, Dracon the graphics and X-Ray the music.
why: The tags list bump mapping, Phong shading, a cube, a torus, a Rubik's cube, a dancer and Einstein, so it is packed with 3D and shading work for an 8-bit machine.

summary: Bold is an MSX demo by Dvik and Joyrex, which won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2009. Moran composed the music.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. The video title also bills it as the winner of that party.

summary: SHizZLE is a demo by Team Pokeme for the Pokemon Mini, which won the wild demo compo at Breakpoint 2005.
why: The video title says it runs on real Pokemon Mini hardware. The fact sheet has no credits or tags beyond that, so this is a short entry.

summary: Oxyron's C64 sequel to Natural Wonders, which came second in the C64 demo compo at X 2008. Axis wrote the code, with music by Fanta and Kasmo and graphics by Oys and Yazoo.
why: Sceners single out how the music is synced to the parts, including filters that dim as black shapes cover the pictures. The vector effects, transparent balls and the greetings end part also get praise.

quote.text: I like the way how Fanta's audio track has been fitted to the parts. Definately the best synchronising to date!

summary: Oxyron and Crest's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. It has a hidden part and a notefile with exact credits for each part.
why: Sceners praise its design, polished presentation and music, and many call it the demo to show people new to the C64. It features pictures by Cyclone and DeeKay that placed in the party's graphics compo.

quote.text: Still one of the best demos, and one of the best demo soundtracks ever, if not THE best.

summary: A three-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Pal did the graphics, with music by several composers including Scarzix and Wiklund.
why: Sceners single out the hires graphics used throughout, the long scrollers and the soundtrack. It was made as a tribute to the people who organise Datastorm.

quote.text: Such a beautiful demo full of outstanding graphics, music and code.

summary: Phantasy's Game Boy demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Dalton did the code, Exocet the graphics and zabutom the music.
why: A podium finish on the Game Boy, with music played by a Carillon player according to the tags.

summary: Weed is a ZX Spectrum demo by Triebkraft, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CAFe 2003.
why: The fact sheet gives no credits or tags, so the compo win is all there is to say.

summary: Mona is a 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit, who did all the code. The video title gives its size as 250 bytes.
why: Its Demozoo note points to a code golf thread titled Let's draw Mona Lisa, where it has been ported to many different programming languages.

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2012. Groepaz and Peacemaker did the code, with music by Dane and graphics by Pal, Nerdine and Peacemaker.
why: Sceners value its mood and art over raw tech, and Dane's somber soundtrack. The credits tree, the fire routine and the mix of hires and multicolour are often mentioned. It marked a Hitmen comeback.

quote.text: To me, it's already a classic, seems to get better and better the more often I watch - and listen to!

summary: Fairlight and Instinct's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Backslash 2007 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007.
why: Sceners single out the growing-branches opening, the pipe effect and the clean, hires, full frame rate effects. Goto80's experimental soundtrack divided opinion.

quote.text: the growing branches and the triangle head over blue and purple backdrop, has to be the most original demo part i have seen in ages.

summary: CyberPunk is an Atari 8-bit demo by Lamers, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Ajcek and Szeryf did the code, with music by Wieczor.
why: The tags mark it as a cyberpunk-themed demo using speech synthesis and 256k.

summary: Gejmbåj is a Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with code and graphics by Snorpung and music by Nordloef. The video was captured on a real Game Boy Pocket.
why: Nominated for Breakthrough Performance and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2010. Tagged as 2mbit and set to loop endlessly.

summary: From Scratch is an Amstrad CPC demo by Vanity, with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and music by Tom&Jerry. The video title describes it as 50Hz and 4k.
why: Nominated for Public Choice at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as a plasma demo.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Floppy 2004. It loops endlessly and has three alternative soundtracks, and the tags call it scene poetry.
why: Sceners praise its stylish design, the flow of fades between parts and Dane's music, which one comment says plays at four times speed. Several name it as their favourite Booze demo.

quote.text: The transitions are not too short or too long, the pace is perfect.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC demo, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Ultrasyd the music.
why: The tags list a kaleidoscope, plasma zoom, rotozoomer, twister and zoom scroller. It also includes a Pulpo Corrosivo cracktro coded by Toms.

summary: In The Future is a ZX Spectrum demo by Hooy-Program, which came second in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2016. Gasman did the code, graphics, music and lyrics.
why: Tagged as karaoke, with the lyrics written by Gasman himself. It was nominated for Best Storytelling at The Meteoriks 2017.
highlights: Written, drawn and scored by Gasman

summary: High Hopes is a NES demo by Aspekt, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007. Ruuvari did the code, graphics and music, with code and design from thefox.
why: A compo win on the NES, made by just two people according to the credits.

summary: KPACKU Deluxe is a ZX Spectrum demo by Kpacku, which won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015. Trefi did the code and prof4d and Tutty the graphics.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2016. Tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode and 128K.

summary: Mescaline Synesthesia is a ZX Spectrum demo by deMarche, which won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2009.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as using multicolour mode and 128K.

summary: UnMEC is an Atari 8-bit demo by Agenda, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. xeen, Pr0be, Koala and Svoy share the code.
why: It won Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2017. Music is by stRing and Caruso, graphics by Piesiu, Ooz and Ripek.

summary: Syntax Infinity is an MSX demo by Tulou and Traktor, which placed fifth in Console/Real Wild at Breakpoint 2009. Esau did code, graphics and music.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2009. Tagged as MSX2.

summary: Plush's C64 4K intro, which won the 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2006. Krill wrote the code and Fanta the music, and the source is available.
why: Sceners single out the voxel landscape and the rotating planet, and many call it one of the best 4Ks. Krill released the source and tools so others could reuse the ideas.

quote.text: it has impressive, although PCish effects (nicest voxel landscape I've seen on c64 at least).

summary: Break Space is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2016. The credits list a dozen contributors across code, graphics and music.
why: The credits name a dedicated 3D engine by X-Trade, plus 3D modelling and 2D animation, which suggests a 3D-heavy production.

summary: Byterapers' C64 demo, the third Follow The Sign, which won the C64 demo compo at Assembly 1996. Mr. Sex did the code and AMJ the music. The party version is known as the 75% version.
why: Sceners praise AMJ's fast-paced soundtrack, the voxelspace routine and the blocky effects, and note how smoothly the parts flow. It was voted 17th best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: This is one of the best blocky-effects demos out there. Never boring and great music.

summary: Error 23 is a C64 demo by The Dreams and Resource, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2006 and won Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2006.
why: Sceners single out the bump mapper, the rubber vector over Leon's picture and the horizontal twister. The party version was unfinished, which several commenters regret.

quote.text: i didnot think i would be impressed by a bump mapper again, but this one was extremely good looking.

summary: Egypt, 2600 BC is an Atari VCS demo by Genesis Project, which won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17. Shadow did the code, Mermaid the music and graphics.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018.

summary: Triad's two-disk-side C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017. Flex was a guest musician, and the code is shared between five coders.
why: Sceners love its 1980s neon look, with a grid, sports cars and venetian blind fades, plus the glowing raster bars and Flex's soundtrack. It was nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018.

quote.text: This is the demo that got me fully hooked on C64 demos - tons of style, so much feeling, and a Flex soundtrack to die for.

summary: I am the seed is a ZX Spectrum demo by Inward and Cyberpunks Unity, which came second in the 8 Bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2005. Elfh did the code and text.
why: Nominated for Best Effects and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2005. Moran did graphics, and Miguel did graphics and music.

summary: A two-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Noice and Offence, which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Winks did the music and Pal the graphics.
why: Sceners single out the cover of an Amiga Enigma tune, the tribute to the Ocean loader music and the colour cycling. The three-line scroller also gets mentioned, though some find there are too many scrollers.

quote.text: it's the Enigma tune that draws me back to this time and again.

summary: 64ever's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at X 2001. The released version, 1.1, only reached the public in November 2002, and a mini-diskmag notefile comes with it.
why: Sceners praise its story, graphics, music and consistent mood, and several say it deserves a higher place in the CSDb charts than it has.

quote.text: great graphics, great music and great everything but above all it tells a story, that's the coolest thing!

summary: Recycler is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper, which won the ZX Spectrum 640k Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2012.
why: A win in the 640k Spectrum class at Chaos Constructions 2012.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo with a tape-loading title, which won the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009. evilpaul did the code and graphics, 4mat the music.
why: A compo winner made by two people according to the credits. It is also listed as a pack.

summary: Your Song Is Quiet (Part 2) is a ZX Spectrum demo from The Planet of Leather Moomins, Inward and Cyberpunks Unity, which won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2007.
why: Elph handled code, music and direction, ps did the graphics and direction, and Delilah added more graphics.

summary: Cauldron is a C64 demo from The Dreams, Exceed and Resource, which won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2008. Linus did the music, AmN and Leon the graphics. A bugfixed 101% version followed in 2014.
why: Sceners praise the witch graphics, the 4x4 plasma and light-flare effects and Linus's tune. A few commenters point out that much of the artwork comes from the game Cauldron.

quote.text: It is a nicely designed demo with well done effects, graphics and music.

summary: IO is an MSX demo by Logon System, which won the Other 8-bit Demo compo at Forever 2015. Overflow did the code, CeD the graphics and Aki the music.
why: Nominated for the That's not Possible on this Platform award at The Meteoriks 2016.

summary: (core) is an Atari VCS 4K intro by wAMMA and Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, which placed fifth in Console/Real Wild at Breakpoint 2007. Ilmarque did most of the work, with Viznut's speech synth and scroller code.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007. Tagged as using speech synthesis.

summary: Fairlight's sci-fi C64 demo, which came second in the demo compo at Floppy 2005. Hollowman did code and graphics, with music by Jeff and Maktone.
why: Sceners praise its space atmosphere, coherent design and Jeff's soundtrack. The eclipse effect, vector astronaut and robot-head society are often mentioned.

quote.text: Absolutely amazing atmosphere this demo manages to create. Brilliant screenplay, very coherent both graphically and soundwise.

summary: Ghost NOP is an Amstrad CPC demo from Pulpo Corrosivo and Futurs', which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2024. Toms wrote the main code, rexbeng did the graphics and Zik the music.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. The credits include a 3D sprite, coded by OffseT with graphics by Hwikaa.

summary: Wonderball (aka Happy Birthday Diver) is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by introspec and Triebkraft, made as a birthday present. introspec did the code and design, Key-Jee the music.
why: Tagged as a birthday present with randomized visuals, and it needs a Spectrum 128K.

summary: SHAPE's C64 demo, which came fourth in the demo compo at X 2014. GRG did the code and music, Archmage the graphics. The final version adds directory art, a note file and a second disk side of music.
why: Sceners praise the soundtrack, the comic-like graphics and how well sound and visuals fit together. The disco plotter and the 3D VU meter bars are often mentioned.

quote.text: There is just a magic in how Shape combine sound and visuals.

summary: Censor Design's twelfth Wonderland, a C64 demo on an Alice in Wonderland theme that won the C64 demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Magnar did the music.
why: Sceners single out the colour-cycling effects, the chaos zoomer and the flip scroller, and many rate Magnar's soundtrack highly. Some thought the pacing and the sampled sound effects were hit and miss.

quote.text: part after part with amazing effects that most of the time fools you into thinking you're actually watching a really, really good AMIGA demo.

summary: Drunk Chessboard is an Atari 8-bit intro by Infinity, which won the Intro compo at QuaST 1996. The video title calls it a 16k intro. Fox did the code, Qba the graphics and X-Ray the music.
why: A compo winner from the mid-1990s Atari scene, made by a three-person team according to the credits.

summary: XAYAX's Atari VCS demo, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. SvOlli did the code and graphics, Skyrunner the music, with more graphics from Titus, Deft and Veto.
why: Tagged as 32k and as featuring the Amiga ball, the checkered bouncing ball from the Amiga's own 1984 demo, here running on the 2600.

summary: Metamerism is a demo for the Commodore C16/Plus 4 by Bauknecht and The Electronic Knights, which won the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012.
why: Mad did the code, Degauss the music and code, and Nero the 2D graphics and colours. It uses Krill's loader.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s third Misery, a demo for the C64 DTV that won the Wild compo at Main 2009. Jammer did the music, with code from Benson, Peiselulli and Streettuff.
why: Sceners call it the most polished DTV demo so far, singling out the fast raycaster with its hidden part, the rotozoomer and the 1280-colour picture. The source was released afterwards.

quote.text: I have no idea how they can get the rotozoomer and wolf3d engine running so fast.

summary: Onescreen Colonies #1 is an Amstrad CPC demo by Vanity, which came fourth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics, with music by Tom&Jerry and Shaft.
why: The music is split between Tom&Jerry and Shaft.

summary: Baltak Rampage is an MSX2 demo by Traktor, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Esau did code, graphics and music, with Bore on code.
why: Five artists share the graphics, and the credits include ASCII graphics by Pumbaa.

summary: A C64 collaboration between Horizon, Instinct, Triad and Focus, which won the demo compo at X 2006 and was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform. Jackasser and Pernod coded it, Linus did the music.
why: Sceners praise its clean design and sense of motion, the giant twister and double zoomscroll, and Linus's tunes. A few find it short or light on effects.

quote.text: A great demo with great sense of motion and great clean design!

summary: Pure is an Atari 8-bit demo by LaResistance, which won the Demo compo at Glucholazy 2008. Pr0be did the code, Born the music and Powrooz the graphics.
why: A compo winner made by a team of three according to the credits.

summary: CRTC³ is an Amstrad CPC demo from Flower Corp., Futurs' and X-Men, which won the Combined Demo compo at Alchimie 2017. The video title calls it a 6128+ cartridge demo.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2018. Roudoudou did the code, Hwikaa the graphics and Zik the music and music player.

summary: Tailwind is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gemba Boys, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2016. Aki did the music and some of the graphics, and the tags mark it as AY music.
why: Noby, mborik and Busy share the code, with graphics from mborik, Lamer Pinky and Aki.

summary: Ascend is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Mafia and Cluster, which won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Kylearan did the code and design, KK the music.
why: Tagged as 32k.

summary: SHAPE's full-disk-side C64 demo, the 100% version that completes their Artillery 85% from Little Computer People 2009. GT did the music, Archmage the graphics and 6R6 the main code.
why: Sceners rate GT's tune as one of the best SID soundtracks and admire Archmage's multicolour pictures. Some point out that the pictures had appeared in earlier releases.

quote.text: Great tune Geir, it keeps evolving all the way through and never gets dull.

summary: Ganzfeld is a ZX Spectrum demo by Baze, which came third in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist. The fact sheet has no credits.

summary: Focus's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Big Floppy People 2006. Its design is built around words, with code by Mirage, The Dark Judge and WVL, graphics by Sander and music by Hein.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2006. Sceners praise the minimalistic design, the choreography and Hein's funky tune.

quote.text: A demo that uses minimalistic gfx in a stylish and coherent way.

summary: Reditus is an Atari 8-bit demo by Zelax, which won the Demo compo at QuaST 2004. Święty did the code, Pink the music, with graphics by Dracon and Pazur.
why: A compo winner on the Atari 8-bit, with a four-person credit list.

summary: Eerie Forest is a one-screen intro for the Amstrad Plus/GX4000 by Logon System, based on Shadow of the Beast. It came second in the Combined Demo compo at Alchimie 2017.
why: Overflow did the code and the graphics and music conversions, with extra design and animation by TotO.

summary: SHAPE's two-disk-side C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017. Archmage and Carrion did the graphics, with music by Linus and Kristian Røstøen.
why: Sceners single out Archmage's graphics, the stencil effects and the smooth transitions, and several say it should have won. One calls it a prod that blurs the line between demo, slideshow and art.

quote.text: It's one of those prods that erases the lines between demo, slideshow and art.

summary: A two-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Noice and Offence, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Pal did the graphics, and nine coders share the code.
why: Sceners praise the slick transitions, the snake plasma and Pal's graphics. A few feel it leans on scrollers and lacks a bit of heavyweight code.

quote.text: this is pure and unadulterated transition heaven.

summary: Triad's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Dane did the music, and the demo loops endlessly.
why: Sceners single out the fisheye terrain view, the greetings upscroller and the dancing martial artist at the end, set to Dane's music. The usual complaint is that it is short.

quote.text: I love the narrativity and the flow. Great effects and overall feeling.

summary: C-Drug is an Atari 8-bit demo from Agenda, Mad Team and LaResistance, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11. The video title calls it an Atari 130XE demo.
why: Probe and Tebe share the code, stRing did the music, and Ooz and Ripek the graphics.

summary: Plush's C64 demo, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. Krill wrote the code, Fanta, Gangstar and Dgazz did the music. It is tagged as German-language and humorous.
why: Sceners praise how well the parts are linked and its distinctive style, and several name it their favourite C64 demo. Many are surprised it dates from 2000.

quote.text: each time i dig it out of my diskbox i think of the transitions between parts in this demo.

summary: Black Mail's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at the Silicon Limited Winter Party 1991. Hein did the graphics, Jeroen Tel and Reyn Ouwehand the music.
why: Sceners credit it with a turning point in C64 demo design, and praise the pixel art, the soundtrack and the flow. Its joyport interaction and Mix-e-load loader are often recalled. Voted joint 18th best in Design #1.

quote.text: it created a turning point in design and style in the world of C64 demos.

summary: Breaking Baud is an Amstrad CPC demo by CRTC, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Doz and MaV did the code and McKlain the music.
why: Graphics are by Jeni, rexbeng and Tunk (font), and the source is available.

summary: A Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with code and graphics by Snorpung and music by Nordloef. The video was captured on a real Game Boy Color.
why: Tagged as 1mbit and set to loop endlessly.

summary: OMD - Orb MegaDemo is a VIC-20 demo by Orb, which came second in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. Ultra and 4-Mat did the code, with 4-Mat on music.
why: Keops made the loading screen. A podium finish on the VIC-20.

summary: Censor Design's three-disk-side C64 demo, the thirteenth Wonderland, which came third in the demo compo at X 2016. It carries an Alice in Wonderland theme and dance animations.
why: It won That's Not Possible On This Platform at The Meteoriks 2017. Sceners single out the sampled Prodigy finale, the bob snakes and Joe's pixel art; some find the design less finished than usual for Censor.

quote.text: Rock solid demo, with a good pace, cleverly built layered routines, and an ace digi that has some of the cleanest bass drums I have ever heard on a C64.

summary: New View 48K is a ZX Spectrum demo by Conscience, which came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2015. Alone Coder led the code, with music by nq.
why: Nominated for the That's not Possible on this Platform award at The Meteoriks 2016. Tagged as a sprites record and as using multicolour mode on a 48K Spectrum with AY sound.

summary: Fairlight's 1970s disco-themed C64 demo, the 75% party version, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2005 and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2005.
why: Sceners praise the design, the colour use and Reed's disco soundtrack, though some argue it does not feel much like the 1970s. Abaddon points to the improved version 1.1 as the one to watch.

quote.text: The programming is cool, but the design is the thing that stands out.

summary: Phortem is an Amstrad CPC demo by Condense, listed for both the CPC and the Amstrad Plus. The video shows the Amstrad Plus version.
why: No Recess did the code, CeD the graphics, Dma-Sc the music and Arnoldemu the disc loader.

summary: Notizen aus der Provinz is a C16/Plus 4 demo by The Electronic Knights, which won the Combined 8bit Demo/Intro compo at SceneCon 2007. Degauss did the code, graphics and music, with graphics from Luca.
why: A win in a combined 8-bit demo and intro compo.

summary: DTC is an Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders and Arkos. Ramlaid did the code, Beb the graphics and design, and Jedi the music.
why: The end part uses music by David Whittaker.

summary: Goa is a ZX Spectrum 128K 4K intro by Extreme Entertainment, which won the 4K Intro compo at Funtop 1998. Exploder did the code.
why: The source is available, and it was ported to the ZX Next in 2026.

summary: Where Have All The Pixels Gone? is a Vectrex demo by the Carnegie Mellon University Computer Club, which won the Combined Demo compo at Pixel Jam 2012. It is also listed as an invitation.
why: Tagged as featuring Nyan Cat. Eight people share the code, graphics and music credits.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, which won the demo compo at X 2024 and Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2025. Trident wrote the code, The Sarge and Soya did the graphics, Fegolhuzz and Danko the music.
why: Sceners praise the story and direction, the pace and the new effects such as the zooming bobs and FLESCOS. Many say it makes a strong case for concept demos on the C64.

quote.text: A supremely entertaining demo with a breathless, exhilarating pace.

summary: Triad's C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013. Dane did the music and Twoflower the graphics, including the fullscreen picture St. Joaquin.
why: Sceners praise the smooth transitions between the work of many coders, the design and the soundtrack. Some feel the killer effects are missing, and a few note echoes of Edge of Disgrace.

quote.text: Twoflower's graphics are wonderful, Danes music fits perfectly and the code masters do a brilliant job to create a coherent, flowing, smooth as silk prod.

summary: Add Mortem is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Arise and Joker, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at speccy.pl party 2025. Jammer did the music, with code from Luke, Wacek and Dalthon.
why: It won Best Demo at the GOTY ZX Spectrum Awards 2025 and Best Soundtrack at The Meteoriks 2026, where it was also nominated for Best Oldschool Production.

summary: Prosonix and Offence's comeback C64 demo, a press-space megademo that won the C64 demo compo at X 2010. It is dedicated to the memory of Unitrax and uses Iron Maiden and joker themes.
why: Sceners praise its spirit, graphics and music, and the interweaving scrollers and isometric DYCP. Some find it uneven or dislike the press-space format. It was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

quote.text: this one oozes the right spirit and creativity I like.

summary: Consciousness's ZX Spectrum Enhanced demo, which won the Enhanced 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2015. Code is by VBI and Rob F., with music by nq and graphics by Nodeus, Mellona and Brightentayle.
why: A compo winner on the enhanced Spectrum, tagged ts-conf, with a three-person graphics team and NQ/Skrju appearing as a guest artist.

summary: Metalvotze's demo for the Vectrex, which won the Alternative Demo/Intro compo at Buenzli 2008.
why: A compo winner for the Vectrex. It's tagged nsfw, so mind where you watch it. The source was once available, but the links were down as of 2021.

summary: Fairlight's story-driven C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2005. Hollowman did the code, graphics and concept, with music by Goto80. Nominated for two Scene.org Awards in 2005.
why: Sceners call it eerie, nauseating and coherent, and it grows on people over repeat viewings. One calls it the best story-based demo on the C64.

quote.text: This is the best story based demo on the C64. I always liked both themed and story based demos and wished there were more of them.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC from Logon System, with code by Overflow and music by McKlain.
why: A small, size-limited CPC production. The fact sheet has little else to go on, so the video will tell you more than we can.

summary: New Generation, Zelax and Radiance's Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Demo compo at Lost Party 2024. The video here is captured on real hardware.
why: A compo winner with a cyberpunk, Blade Runner-themed look and a synthwave soundtrack, tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. It needs 1 MB of memory.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo, first in the Wild compo at Gubbdata 2021. Quiss did the code, with music by kb and PVCF and graphics by Felidae. Commenters describe the 1541 disk drive producing the video signal.
why: Won Outstanding Concept and Outstanding Technical Achievement at the Meteoriks 2022. Sceners keep coming back to the sheer cleverness of using the drive itself, music included.

quote.text: this is what the scene is about for me, doing something 'impossible'.

summary: Booze Design and Instinct's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at X 2010 and nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the 2010 Scene.org Awards. Code by HCL, JackAsser and Dane, graphics by Archmage.
why: Sceners single out the isometric voxel routine, the huge rotozoomer that reaches into the borders, and the smooth transitions. Some thought it deserved to win the compo.

quote.text: Excellent in every aspect, fantastic code, supersmooth design and transitions and beautiful graphics etc.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. Code by Ajcek, Alias and Szeryf, with graphics by At0m and Gepard and music by Wieczór.
why: A compo winner, with a three-person code team. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum by SerzhSoft and Gasman, first in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2019. SerzhSoft did code and graphics, Gasman the music. This is the party version.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement and Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2020. A full intro, music included, in 4096 bytes on a Spectrum.

summary: LaResistance's Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2007. Pr0be did the code, Powrooz the graphics, and Born the music and the 3D objects.
why: A compo winner. Born's credit includes 3D objects, which is the thing to look for here.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Moonshine Dragons 2022. It uses the Sparkle loader. Code by Luke and Wacek, with music by Jammer and Rodney and graphics by Rodney, Wacek, Biter and Bimber.
why: Won Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2023. Commenters praise the design and surprises, and argue over how much is precalculated animation and how much is real-time code.

quote.text: Wacek and the Arise team never disappoints. The amount of determination, talent and work that went into this demo is paramount.

summary: Bonzai's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at X 2016. It spans two disk sides, with code by Trap, Walt and Ricky and music by DRAX, Laxity, Metal and Scortia.
why: It opened the compo and went down very well with the crowd, and sceners welcomed it as a comeback. They single out the sinewave zoom scroller, the Star Wars-style upscroll and the transitions.

quote.text: I love the way how this combines oldschool vibes with perfect sync and transitions.

summary: Inward and Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2007. This is the first part of a two-part title.
why: A podium finish in a Breakpoint wild compo. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best way in.

summary: The Next Level is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2008. Viznut did the code, graphics and music.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the 2008 Scene.org Awards. It's tagged for speech synthesis, which is the thing to listen for.

summary: Ate Bit's demo for the ZX Spectrum 128, first in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. evilpaul did the code and graphics, with music by 4mat.
why: A compo winner for the 128K Spectrum, made by a two-person team.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, first in the C64 Demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001. HCL did the code and graphics, with three more graphics artists and seven musicians credited. This entry is tagged as the party version.
why: It wasn't released at the party because of bugs; a final version followed in November at X2001. Commenters point people to that bug-fixed release.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. Code by Ajcek and Szeryf, graphics by Gepard, Johny, Odyn1ec and At0m, music by XTD. The video is the party version at 1080p50.
why: A runner-up from the same team that won the XL/XE compo at Silly Venture 2k12 with Boogie Nights.

summary: Byterapers' C64 demo, second in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2009. Suckho did the code and graphics, with music by GRG. It's tagged as an endless loop.
why: Commenters like the soundtrack and the smooth twisters, and were surprised by how good the 8x8 plasma looks. One notes it as Suckho's first C64 release.

quote.text: The rest of the demo was great, twisters looked so smooth and who knew 8x8 plasma could look so good.

summary: A co-op between Censor Design and Oxyron: a two-sided C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2015. It uses the Bitbreaker loader and has a large team of coders, artists and musicians.
why: Nominated for three Meteoriks in 2016. Sceners praise the bitmap stretchers added to the effects, Joe's graphics and the music, and describe side 2 as a music-driven piece.

quote.text: Really powerful demo with great coding, gfx and music.

summary: Agenda's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Probe did the code, with graphics by Ooz, Piesiu and Ripek and music by stRing. It's tagged 128k.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Battro is a 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Batman Group, with code by Rhino, music by McKlain and graphics by Mac.
why: A compact CPC production in the 16K size class. The fact sheet has no placings or comments, so there is not much more to add.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Breakpoint 2007. Graham and Axis did the code, Yazoo the graphics and Fanta the music, with Koala pictures by Oyise at the end.
why: Sceners welcomed it as Oxyron's return, and several named it their favourite of the Breakpoint compo. They single out the design, the graphics, the vectors and the music.

quote.text: Smooth routines and especially the music had some suprising elements.

summary: Noice's demo for the ZX Spectrum 128, second in the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012. Shadow did the code, Frost the graphics and Yerzmyey the music.
why: A runner-up at Sundown with a music credit for Yerzmyey. Little else is on record.

summary: Lepsi and Miracles' C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Silesia 5 in 2011, nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. It uses the Krill loader and features Joodas's fullscreen picture Sprocket.
why: Commenters call it original and well made, with high-quality graphics that fit the effects, and some count it among the best demos they've seen. They single out the x-rotators and the soundtrack.

quote.text: Excellent gfx and code, great soundtrack (especially Apparatus.sid!).

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo, first in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2016. TmK did the code, Rainman and bfox the graphics, Nik-O the music and Zeebr the direction. The source is available.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at the Meteoriks 2017. The video is a full-resolution, no-flicker 50Hz capture, and the demo carries a graffiti tag.

summary: Logicoma's 4K intro for the C64, second in the Combined Intro compo at Solskogen 2017. Ferris did the code and graphics, H0ffman the music, 4mat the sound driver and Wobble more graphics. The source is public.
why: Sceners were pleased to see Logicoma on the C64 and noted it as Ferris's first C64 prod. One hears EDM vibes in the bass notes and arpeggios of the tune.

quote.text: super nice 4k intro, and especially since it's your first one!!!

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo, fourth in the C64 Demo compo at X 2010 and nominated for Best Technical Achievement at the 2010 Scene.org Awards. It processes audio in real time, and a white paper explains how.
why: Sceners were stunned that a 1MHz machine can time-stretch sound live, and some call it the best work on the C64 so far. Several also single out the accompanying white paper.

quote.text: Real time timestretching on a 1mhz machine? You gotta be kidding.

summary: Darklite and Offence's ZX Spectrum 128 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2023. Neon did the code, Pal the graphics and Response the music. It uses the ZX multicolour mode.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2024, so worth a look for what the multicolour mode makes possible on the Spectrum.

summary: A monochrome Atari 8-bit demo by Masters of Electric City and Checkpoint, third in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. bob_er did the code, mOdmate the graphics and Dhor the music.
why: A podium finish that sticks to a single-colour look. The video is a 720p, 50fps capture.

summary: Phantasy's Game Boy demo, fifth in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2005. Dalton and Lai wrote the code, Exocet did the graphics, and Goto80 and Mr. Death made the music.
why: A Game Boy demo with a chess part and a plasma part. Several parts rely on interlacing, so screenshots don't show them as they look in motion.

summary: Techno Lab's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the 8bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2018. Kowalski did the code and Nik-O the music, with tools and support from wbcbz7.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, first in the ZX Spectrum 640k Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2011. It uses the ZX multicolour mode.
why: A compo winner from the group that later won the same compo again with Across The Edge in 2016.

summary: Be No Sqr is a Sega Master System demo by Psidum, Sim and Slimeball, second in the Coding compo at the SMS Power Anniversary Coding Compo 2016. Psidum did the code, Sim the graphics and Slimeball the music.
why: Nominated in the That's Not Possible On This Platform category at the Meteoriks 2017.

summary: Speccy.pl's demo for the SAM Coupé, first in the 8Bit Demo compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2015. Sir David did the code, Cat-Man the graphics and Ziutek the music, with design support from Tygrys. The video is the big-screen party showing.
why: A compo winner on the SAM Coupé.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2012. Krusty and Eliot did the code, with graphics from Exin, CeD, Supersly and Voxfreax and music by McKlain and Dma-Sc.
why: A podium finish at Revision for the CPC, with a sizeable credit list for graphics and music.

summary: Extreme Entertainment's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Demo compo at Funtop 1998. TeeRay did the main graphics and 3D scenes, Exploder the code, rendering and camera work, and Visual the music. It features TeeRay's pictures Starin' At The Sun and Mark Anthony.
why: A compo winner whose credits list 3D scenes, rendering and camera work.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari 8-bit Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10. The code is credited to JAC, Ooz the graphics and 505 the music.
why: A compo winner. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Samar Productions' two-disk-side C64 demo that won the 8 Bit Demo compo at Intel Outside 1998.
why: One commenter calls it one of the most underrated C64 demos, and others cite the soundtrack, the pictures and the effects. A commenter notes the tunnel-vector part uses the disk drive for calculating.

quote.text: Outstanding soundtrack, some amazing pictures and crazy effects like the filled tv cube, tunnel, dot sphere, 4x4 effect zoomer etc.

summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS (2600) demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007. visy did the code and design; Ilmarque did code, graphics and music.
why: A podium finish for a two-person team on the Atari VCS. There are no comments on the sheet, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Floppy 2005 and was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. Iopop did the code, Twoflower the graphics and Dalezy the music.
why: Dalezy of Creators appears as a guest musician. It was reviewed in Nordic Scene Review 1 in April 2005.

summary: aTaRSi is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Sounds System, Crest and Tristar and Red Sector Inc., first in the Realtime Demo (Oldschool) compo at Nordlicht 2013. Peiselulli did the code, DeeKay the graphics and Tjoppen the music.
why: A compo winner and a three-group collaboration on the VCS. Enthusi wrote the scrolltext code.

summary: Horizon and Instinct's C64 demo, fourth in the C64 Demo compo at X 2008. JackAsser and Pernod did the code, Archmage the graphics and RaveGuru the music.
why: Sceners praise the twisters, RaveGuru's soundtrack and Archmage's pictures. The common complaint is that it's too short, and one asks what it is about.

quote.text: Very slick and enjoyable demo. Love the music and the nice gfx from Archmage.

summary: Deary is a 32K intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, third in the Realtime Demo Size-Limited compo at Demodays 2012. Hopper did the code and 505 the music.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited compo from a two-person team.

summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2008. Ilmarque did code, graphics and music; visy the engine code and design; Viznut the 3D cube part. The video calls it an 8K demo.
why: A compo winner. The 3D cube part by Viznut is the credit to watch for.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. It's tagged 128k and hires. bob_er did code and graphics, Dhor graphics and music.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture 2k12, the same party where Lamers' Boogie Nights took first place.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, first in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CAFe 2019. TmK did the code, bfox the graphics, nq the music and Zeebr the direction. It uses the ZX multicolour mode, and the source is available.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2020. The video is the final version, v2, with no flicker.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Multimatograf 2024. Diver and G.D. did the graphics, sq and Kowalski the code and nq the music. The video is the final version.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. G.D. is credited with 3D graphics.

summary: No Pets Allowed is an Orb demo for the Commodore PET, tagged for the CBM 4032. Ultra did the code, Ilkke, Leon and Mirage the graphics, and 4mat the music and some code.
why: The video shows both the speaker and SID versions, so you can hear how the music changes between them.

summary: Oxyron's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2013. Graham did the code, Yazoo the graphics and Booker the music, with a charset by Amarok.
why: A compo winner. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: The final version of Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo Prozac Dream, shown in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17 with no placing recorded.
why: The earlier party version took second place a year before at Silly Venture 2k16. Gepard, Odyn1ec, At0m and Johny are credited with graphics, Alias, Ajcek and Szeryf with code, and XTD with the music.

summary: Melange is a ZX Spectrum invitation production by Light Future and 4th Dimension, first in the Invitation compo at Chaos Constructions 2000. CyberJack did the code, Diver the graphics and MmcM the music.
why: An invitation that won its compo. Key-Jee is credited with fixing some of the music patterns.

summary: A Commodore PET demo by Shiru, first in the LowEnd Demo (Combined) compo at CAFe 2022.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2023.

summary: Noice's Atari VCS (2600) demo, first in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. Shadow did the code and Ilmarque the music.
why: A compo winner with a two-person credit list.

summary: Onslaught's C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Flashback 2014. Algorithm and Conjuror did the code, SoNiC and Algorithm the music, and the credits list five graphics artists.
why: Sceners single out the line shadow circle, the tile twister and the streamed music at the end. Full credits and a description of each part are in the note program on side 1.

quote.text: Enjoyed the show, particularly the shadow circle and end part.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2017. Gasman is credited with code, music, graphics and text. It uses the ZX multicolour mode and has a Berlin tag.
why: A compo winner made by one person. The multicolour mode is the thing to watch for.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's VIC-20 demo, first in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2003. Viznut did the code, graphics and music. It's tagged for speech synthesis.
why: Nominated for Best 4k Intro at the 2003 Scene.org Awards. Listen for the speech synthesis.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's C64 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2012. Viznut did the code, text and graphics, with more graphics by ccr and Parkitus and music by Ilmarque. It's tagged politics and anticapitalism.
why: Commenters call it unstable, violent and glitchy, and mean it as praise. Some enjoy the intentionally broken parts and the interference part, and one calls it an interesting concept.

quote.text: Unstable, violent & glitchy. A successful experiment!!

summary: Kiss Kill is a ZX Spectrum demo by Candy Says and Gasman that won the Wild compo at DiHalt 2013.
why: A wild compo winner. There are no credits or comments on the sheet, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Genesis Project's demo for the Enterprise 128, first in the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2016. Shadow did the code, Illmidus the graphics and Jason C. Brooke the music.
why: A compo winner for the Enterprise 128.

summary: A NES/Famicom 64K intro by Excess Team, deMarche and Mega Cat, made as an invitation to CAFe 2019. Third in Wild at TokyoDemoFest 2018 and second in the CAFePARTY 2019 Invitations at CAFe 2019.
why: It placed in two compos. Adam Bazaroff did the graphics, Nik-O the music, and mr287cc and TmK the code. The source is available.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. It's tagged 256k. Ajcek and Szeryf did the code, At0m, Gepard and Odyn1ec the graphics and Wieczor the music.
why: A compo winner and the group's second Silly Venture win in a row after Boogie Nights in 2012.

summary: Bitshifters' demo for the BBC Micro, tagged for the BBC Master, that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2018. KieranHJ did the code and effects, Henley the music code and Atari ST YM port, and Mad Max the music. The source is available.
why: A compo winner, with the music coming over from the Atari ST's YM sound chip.

summary: ISO is an Atari VCS (2600) demo by JAC, first in the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11. JAC did the code and graphics and Jakub Husak the music. The source is available.
why: A compo winner. JAC also won the Atari 8-bit compo at Silly Venture 2k10 with Silly Things.

summary: Origo Dreamline's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at the Light and Phenomena Easter Party 1992. Mixer and CLF did the code, with music by Zardax and Mixer and graphics from BX, Fox, Gordon and Crony.
why: Commenters call it the first real trackmo on the C64 and say it was far ahead of its time in 1992. They single out the filled vectors, the real-time Mandelbrot fractals and Zardax's tunes.

quote.text: It was a real jaw dropper when it was released.

summary: Machined is a ZX Spectrum 128 demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, third in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. The video is the final version.
why: A podium finish at Sundown. The fact sheet has no credits, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Xenon's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at X 2008. WVL and Megabrain did the code, A-Man and Arne the music, and Electric, Oxbow, Sander and Valsary the graphics.
why: Sceners single out the animated pig part, the 3D scroller and how closely the effects follow the music. One says it has the best soundtrack of the X 2008 demo entries.

quote.text: great partydemo! i especially dig the (outstanding) music sync with the visual effects, which can be found everywhere throughout the demo.

summary: Triple Threat is an Atari 8-bit demo by Mystic Bytes, Noice and Agenda, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. Shadow did the code, Ripek the graphics and BeWu the music.
why: A three-group collaboration that finished one place behind Lamers' Gene.

summary: Resource's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at X 2001. Oswald did the code, with graphics by AmN and Sander and music by Dane, GRG and Mitch. It uses the Krill loader.
why: Resource's own notes say the house came down at X 2001. Commenters call it a milestone, with an epic soundtrack, Amiga-style effects, and bump mapping and a light mask that stand out.

quote.text: This really is one of the highlights of c64 demos ever. It has power, it has show, it has everything.

summary: SHAPE's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2014. GRG did code and music, Knut code, Archmage the graphics and Kristian music. Tagged for plasma, a tunnel, sine dots and bobs.
why: Sceners praise it as a demo with a message, with Archmage's disturbing artwork and a haunting soundtrack. It manages all this on a single disk side.

quote.text: The effects and soundtrack go hand in hand with the awesome graphics.

summary: The final 100% version of Booze Design's Royal Arte for the C64. HCL did the code and graphics, with more graphics by DeeKay, Forbidden Cult and Valsary and music from six musicians.
why: Commenters single out the sprite FPP effect, the smooth DYPP screen, and the border scrollers. It's a demo people say they keep going back to.

quote.text: this is such a great demo! i keep on watching it, equally amazed every time.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at The Party 1995. It is a single file of about 35 KB containing three hidden parts. Graham did the code, Biz Kid and Sire the graphics and Jeff the music.
why: Ranked 15th best demo in Design #1 in 1997. Commenters praise the music, the bitmapped vector rotator and the fast horizontal scaling, and one remembers seeing it live as a turning point.

quote.text: This demo made a huge impression on me. Still looks and sounds amazing

summary: Arise and Joker's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at the speccy.pl party 2023.1. Wacek and Luke did the code, Bimber and Wacek the graphics, and Pator and MCH the music.
why: Nominated for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023 and tagged for the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy invitation to Alternative Party 2009, which won the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2009. Äkknäkk did the graphics and Maitotuote the code. The video is live footage from the compo.
why: A compo winner on the Game Boy, tagged as using the Carillon player.

summary: A multi-group Amstrad CPC megademo by Futurs', GPA, Pulpo Corrosivo, Vanity, Benediction, Dirty Minds and Shinra, titled for 30 years of the Amstrad. It's tagged as a sprites record.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at the Meteoriks 2017. The credits list eight coders, plus a large team of artists and musicians.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2013. drwho and Lovebeam did the code, and Sweetbutt the graphics and music.
why: A compo winner made by a team of three.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo, second in the Demo compo at X 2004. Clarence did the code, Leon the graphics and DRAX and Fanta the music. This is a hardware capture.
why: Commenters like the old-school code, the rasterbars and the elephant picture, though some feel parts run long.

quote.text: Excellent demo. Nice music, graphics and code. And the elephant picture is sublime.

summary: Crescent's 256-byte intro for the C64: an interactive raycaster, written by Wisdom. The source is available.
why: It made the Slashdot front page in 2013, and commenters were amazed to see a raycaster fit in so little.

quote.text: I've been impressed by some 1k js effects recently and was thinking, no way could the c64 do the same, but here I am proven wrong

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo, sixth in the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2011 and nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. Pantaloon, Hollowman, Abaddon and Alfatech did the code and Louie the graphics.
why: Sceners enjoy its humour, especially the extra-large Mario part and the graffiti train. One was surprised it placed so low.

quote.text: Hilarious extra-large Mario part and nice idea about the street art going on the trains.

summary: Bandwagon's MSX demo that won the Demo compo at Plutonium 2000. nf did the code, Mermaid and Scythe the graphics and Gspot the music.
why: A compo winner on the MSX. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Bonzai's three-disk-side C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at X 2018 and nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2019. It has a hidden part and a humorous streak.
why: One scener's favourite of the whole compo; others praise its design, transitions and soundtrack. Burglar picks out the shade scroller, the diagonal charset scroller and the huge parallax logo.

quote.text: Design, transitions, editing and soundtrack just ooze of impossible awesomeness!

summary: Camelot's Tower Power for the C64, here in its 100% version. Slammer did the code, Jeff the music and music player, and four artists did the graphics. A note is on disk 1.
why: Commenters call it the trackmo of its era and praise the vectors, the vector fly-ins and the colour snakes in the round vector part. It placed joint sixth in a 1997 Design ranking of best demos.
highlights: colour snakes in round vector part

quote.text: This was THE Trackmo for a long time. In line with demos from Black Mail, Brutal, Crest and other groups, this was probably the demo that helped shape the 1990s.

summary: Large Unified Theory is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, first in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2010. Viznut is credited with the code.
why: A compo winner on the VIC-20 with a single credit, for Viznut's code.

summary: A three-disk-side C64 demo by Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, third in the Demo compo at X 2014. Pantaloon, Perplex, Puterman, Stein, Bjørn, Che and Zaphod share the code, with graphics by Pal and music by OMP.
why: Sceners praise the consistent theme, the transitions and the zoom boxes between parts, and Prosonix's big soundtrack. One felt the music and visuals didn't sync up.

quote.text: The consistent theme and nice transitions ties the effects together beautifully.

summary: Taboo's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Visual Party 4.0 in 1994. This is the 50% version.
why: Ranked 11th best demo in Design #1 in February 1997.

summary: Singular Crew's C64 demo that won the Wild Demo / Animation compo at Function 2017. It needs four C64s running in sync. Scorpy and Soci did the code, Poison and Leon the graphics and Vincenzo the music.
why: Sceners like the idea and how well it is executed, and are impressed that four machines stay in sync.

quote.text: Splendid idea, well executed.

summary: Life On Mars's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2014. introspec did the design and code, Diver the graphics and Fatal Snipe the music. This is the party version.
why: A compo winner that was designed and coded by one person.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Vanity, first in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2020. Hicks did the code, Beb the graphics and Tom&Jerry the music.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2021: a full intro with music in 4096 bytes.

summary: Dirty Minds' Amstrad CPC demo that won the Wild Demo compo at Forever 2012. Optimus did the code, Voxfreax the graphics and Sice the music.
why: A wild compo winner on the CPC. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Genesis Project's Sega Master System demo, seventh in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Shadow did the code, Illmidus the graphics and NightBeat the music.
why: Little else is on record. The same group also made the Enterprise demo First Contact.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s demo for the C64 DTV, which won the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Streetuff did code, graphics and text, with more code from Benson and Peiselulli, graphics by Spotter and music by Linus.
why: Commenters note TRSI keeping the DTV moving with a major demo, and single out the hires graphics, the vectors, the tunnel and the MOD player. One would have liked more dynamic part linking.

quote.text: MOD-player was cool, aswell as the highres vectors and tunnel and etc. etc :)

summary: Ate Bit's invitation to Sundown 2006 for the ZX Spectrum. evilpaul did the code and graphics, with music by Matt Furniss.
why: It won Most Original Concept at the 2006 Scene.org Awards and was also nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform.

summary: Overlanders' Amstrad CPC demo, whose video title mentions 50Hz and 4k. Madram did the code, Beb the graphics and Shap the music.
why: The music credits also list Ben Daglish, Rob Hubbard, David Whittaker, Geoff Follin, Tim Follin and Wally Beben, a long list of composers for a single CPC demo.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at X 1995. Quiss did the code and PVCF the music.
why: Ranked first best demo in Design #1 in February 1997. Commenters call it a trendsetting trackmo with loud, energetic music and a parallax chess zoomer.

quote.text: one of my favourite demos ever. watching it now, it still gives me that same energy kick as it did the first time i saw it, almost 30 years ago!

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII story demo for the C64, third in the C64 Demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Goto80 did the music, Mathman the code and acidT*rroreast the graphics and story.
why: Commenters like the live-drawn PETSCII art, which stays in time with the music. A couple say it changed their view of PETSCII. It was reviewed in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: My favourite from the competition. So simple and so much style.

summary: Otomata Labs' Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2026. It's tagged 32k. Natt did code, graphics and music, with more code from AArt1256 and artёmka.
why: A compo winner with a six-person credit list, including graphics by Grongy and music by Enfys and nIkO.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. HCL did code and graphics, Jackasser code, Archmage, Jailbird and Dane graphics, and Dane and RaveGuru the music.
why: Axis calls it the deserved winner. Others enjoy the oldskool style with scrollers everywhere, plus the DYPP scroller, transparent rasterbars, a dot ball and a morphing line vector.

quote.text: I have to say this is the deserved winner. There is so much cool stuff in this.

summary: Bauknecht's demo for the C16/Plus 4, third in the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Mad did the code, Sire the music and graphics and Decca more graphics.
why: A podium finish on the C16/Plus 4 at the Oxyron Party.

summary: Derivative 2600 is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Mafia and Cluster, second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2015. Kylearan did the code and design and KK the music. It's tagged 32k.
why: Nominated in the That's not Possible on this Platform category at the Meteoriks 2016.

summary: Digital Mafia's Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Atari 2600 Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13. KK is credited with code, music and the idea.
why: A compo winner made by one person.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Xenium 2024 and nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2025. It uses the Sparkle loader. Luke and Wacek did the code, Biter and Bimber the graphics and Jammer the music.
why: Commenters see it as a worthy sequel to E2IRA and praise Jammer's soundtrack and the design. They single out the dithered landscape with motion blur and the shadow-casting rubber cube.

quote.text: Not a single second wasted here, pure killer parts from top to bottom.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994. A rave-flavoured sample demo that opens with an old-school digi intro before moving into design-led parts.
why: Sceners call it a groundbreaking style change and a milestone in C64 demo design. Demozoo notes it as the 4th best demo in Design #1 (February 1997).

quote.text: Tons of exciting effects. This one really entertained me. Cool techno tunes as well. I particularly like the balls on grid and the pinball physics.

summary: Punkfloyd's realtime demo for the NEC PC Engine SuperGrafx, which took second place in the Realtime Demo compo at Demodays 2012. Code and music are by nop, graphics by LaTortue.
why: A compo podium finish for a SuperGrafx demo. The source code is available if you want to see how it was done.

summary: Impossiblator 3 is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, with code, graphics and music all by Viznut. It came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards 2007, with one person behind every part of it.

summary: HEOHdemo is Shiru's NES demo, which won the Console Demo/Intro compo at CAFe 2019. It carries an epilepsy warning.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2020. Both the source and a writeup are available, so it's a good one to watch and then read up on.

summary: Jitter is a demo for the Atari Lynx by Desire, which won the Atari Lynx Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. Heaven and Axis wrote the code, with a team of graphics artists and music by Nainain and Jakub Husak.
why: A compo winner on the Atari Lynx, with a large team of graphics artists and two musicians behind it.

summary: Detroyt is a ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft that won the Demo compo at ASCii 2003. Code is by psndcj, music by Key-Jee, and graphics by Diver, prof4d and G.D.
why: A compo winner with a clear split between code, music and a three-strong graphics team.

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo with a pirate theme, which came 5th in the Demo compo at X 2016. Nominated in the That's Not Possible On This Platform category at The Meteoriks 2017.
why: Many commenters call it their favourite from X 2016 and think it deserved to place higher. They single out the code, the soundtrack and the run of parts, from Donkey Kong rasters to the endless bobs.

quote.text: Killer music and very fast flow, tons of cool parts.

summary: Backtro is an Amstrad CPC demo from Logon System, released in 2001, with code credited to Overflow.
why: A short factual card is all the fact sheet supports: a single-coder CPC demo from the early 2000s.

summary: Phosphorizer is a 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Loonies and Logicoma. It won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A compo-winning 4K for the Plus/4. Blueberry coded it, H0ffman made the music and Ferris wrote the cruncher.

summary: Dizzzruptor is a multi-part ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Hooy-Program that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2012. Yerzmyey's AY music runs through every part.
why: Six parts from a crew of coders, with guests including Mat, Tygrys and Alone Coder. It won its compo.

summary: Extend's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Zoo 1998. Barfly and Tape coded it, TBB wrote the music and Electric drew the graphics, including interlaced fullscreen pictures.
why: Commenters single out the interlaced graphics, the trancey TBB tune and the sharp, clean-cut way the screens follow one another. One of Electric's pictures is his Zoo 97 graphics compo winner, My Trans.

quote.text: No fuzz about fades and transitions, just sharp cutting. And of course not to forget some of the finest interlace graphics.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s Ghost In The Machine is a demo for the Commodore 64 DTV. It won the Combined Demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2007.
why: Commenters treat it as a proper multipart demo for the DTV and a sign the platform can carry one, picking out the fast shadebobs, the multicolour plasma and Linus's music.

quote.text: Finally a decent multipart demo on the DTV. Great work guys!

summary: Invasion Of The Big Pixels is an MSX demo by Noice, with code by Shadow, music and graphics by Ham and further graphics by ptoing. It took second place in the Combined Demo compo at Grep White 2008.
why: A podium finish for a small MSX team in a combined compo.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Compusphere 2015. Shadow coded it, Redcrab drew the graphics and Stinsen made the music.
why: Commenters like its bug theme, the cute sprites and above all the dot twister plotter, and keep saying they wish it ran longer.

quote.text: Never seen a twister plotter before. Looks great. The SID tune rocks as well with this.

summary: The Asskicker is an Atari 8-bit demo by Shadows that won the Demo compo at QuaST 1996. Konop coded it, Cedyń did the music and Titus the graphics, with a hidden part by Bewesoft.
why: A 128K compo winner whose tags list Gouraud shading, plasma, a zoomer and a Wolfenstein effect. The video is titled AssKicker on steroids, from the Silly Venture 2017 wild compo.

summary: Bonzai's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Gubbdata 2021. It was named Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022.
why: Commenters praise its style, the transitions locked to the soundtrack, and the humour, including the team avatar scroller and a double DYPP. Several say it sets a new bar for C64 demos.

quote.text: Beautiful artwork, music, flow, impressive effects and the Bonzai humour... this one has it all!

summary: Genesis Project's three-disk-side C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2020. Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement and Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2021; source is available.
why: Commenters describe an art-driven demo with a coherent theme, a rich soundtrack and some serious code behind it, notably a full-width bitmap upscroller that streams from disk.

quote.text: It's clearly a labor of love with much attention to detail.

summary: RGBA is a 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, with music by 505 and a font by Ooz. It won the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A compo-winning 16K intro, with a video title that spells the name out as Rasters Girls Beer Atari.

summary: Somewhat Less Limited Capabilities is a ZX81 demo by Noice, which came 6th in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.
why: A ZX81 demo that made the top six in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.

summary: Bauknecht's C64 demo, coded by Mad with music by Mad and Sire and graphics by Sire. It came second in the Wild / Alternative Platform compo at Evoke 2007 and was nominated for a Scene.org Award.
why: Commenters call it fresh and un-C64-like, and rave about its scrollers. Parts are advanced with the space bar rather than running as a trackmo.

quote.text: The rotating scroller is the best oldschool effect I've seen in a long time.

summary: Byterapers Inc.'s C64 demo that won the C64 Demo compo at Assembly 1995. Mr. Sex coded it, Zardax made the music and Mike drew the graphics.
why: Commenters call it a newschool classic and single out Mike's logos and the way the music fits the effects. Demozoo lists it as the joint 6th best demo in Design #1 (February 1997).

quote.text: very nice 4x4 routines, the gouraud at the end is lowreso but fast on the other hand, overall a very well done newschool classic.

summary: The Best Intro Ever is a 4K intro for the C64 by Razor 1911, which won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2016. rez did the code and graphics, with music and the player by 4mat.
why: Commenters single out 4mat's tune, a full soundtrack squeezed into a 4K, and the smooth expanding circles and dots.

quote.text: The tune is awesome, having a full featured soundtrack of this quality in 4K intro is rare.

summary: Timmy is a ZX Spectrum demo by Speccy.pl made for the Timex Computer 2048 and 2068. It won the Demo compo at Riverwash 2014.
why: A compo winner aimed at the Timex Computer 2048 and 2068. Tygrys wrote the code, Ziutek the music, and Piesiu and At0m the graphics.

summary: Reliable Fraud is a ZX Spectrum 48K demo with AY music, made by Zoo. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2011.
why: A compo winner on the plain 48K Spectrum with an AY soundtrack by V0yager. Tygrys coded it and Slayer did the graphics.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 tribute to Star Wars, which won the C64 Demo compo at X 2018. Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2019.
why: Commenters rate the SID arrangements of the film's music above all, along with the humour, the colour-cycling parts and the full-screen pixel art. Some tire of the theme but admit the effort.

quote.text: At first I thought that the Star Wars theme might have worn off a bit recently, but there's so much freshness in this prod it amazes me. The music remixes alone are out of this world.

summary: Scrollwars is a three-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, placing second in the C64 Demo compo at Baroque Floppy People 2013. Pål Syversen drew the graphics.
why: Sceners praise the design, the music and Pål Syversen's graphics, plus effects such as the circular twister and twisting torus. Demozoo notes a review in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: Fantastic graphics, Pål you just outdid yourself - it's massive! Code is very fresh, music superb.

summary: 20 Y is a Game Boy demo by Snorpung, with music by Nordloef. The video title dates it 1989 to 2009, and it is tagged as an anniversary demo that loops endlessly.
why: A one-coder Game Boy demo marking an anniversary. It is tagged NSFW, so watch with that in mind.

summary: Shade is a Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Wilds that won the Demo compo at Árok 2007. Larry coded it, Randy made the music and Chronos drew the graphics.
