why: A compo winner on the C16/Plus 4.

summary: A joint C64 demo from Fairlight, Censor and Offence that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. Pantaloon and Bob lead the code, with LMan's tune in the end part.
why: Commenters like the pacing and momentum, the colour-cycling spheres and Bob's ball effects, and keep asking how it was done.

quote.text: it has all been put together with so much talent and dedication, and with amazing pacing and forward momentum.

summary: Gnork is a VIC-20 demo by Desire that took third place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018. It needs the 16K RAM expansion.
why: A podium finish for a VIC-20 demo at a major party. Heaven wrote the code, BokanoiD drew the graphics and Triace composed the music.

summary: Manifesto is a ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2014. drwho and Lovebeam share the code and Nick Roll made the music.
why: A compo win in a combined 8-bit field, beating demos from other machines.

summary: Fossil's two-disk-side C64 concept demo that came 5th in the C64 Demo compo at X 2018. Bjørn Røstøen and Knut M. Clausen share the code, Archmage did the graphics and Linus the music.
why: Commenters rate its transitions, sync and soundtrack very highly, and several think it deserved to place above fifth. They also single out Archmage's graphics and the sense of storytelling.

quote.text: I love the music in this one and the whole thing is so smooth.

summary: Irreality 1k is a ZX Spectrum 1K intro by SerzhSoft that won the ZX Spectrum 1k Intro compo at Forever 2014.
why: A compo-winning intro that fits into 1K on the Spectrum.

summary: Quantum Disco Brothers is a 64K intro for the NES by wAMMA. It came second in the Demo compo at Stream 2006.
why: A podium finish for an NES production, built by a team of two coders, an Ilmarque soundtrack and five graphics artists.

summary: The Revision 2012 Invitation is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo from Hooy-Program and Royal Belgian Beer Squadron. Gasman wrote the code and music and FRaNKy the text. It won the Other Platform Demo compo at Datastorm 2012.
why: A party invitation that won a compo in its own right.

summary: BB is a 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K with AY by introspec. It won the 8 Bit 256b intro compo at Multimatograf 2014 and is tagged politics and Russia theme.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte class, tagged with a political theme.

summary: Rain is a ZX Spectrum demo by Life On Mars that took second place in the 8Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2016. It runs on the 48K and 128K models.
why: introspec did the code, graphics and text, working with Diver on design and graphics, and Mister Beep wrote the music.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo that came second in the C64 Demo compo at The Party 1997. Graham coded it, DeeKay drew the graphics and Fanta wrote the music. It is interactive, with controllable effects.
why: Commenters are amazed at how much fits in about 50 KB, from controllable Gouraud shading and 3D dots to a playable engine in the final part, and rate Fanta's tune among the best.

quote.text: I still can't believe how all these effects can fit into 50 KB! ABSOLUTELY AMAZING, especially the playable DOOM clone at the end of the demo.

summary: Over Relaxed is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by sibCrew that won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2017. It is tagged as using ZX multicolour mode.
why: A compo winner with a team of two coders, two musicians and a graphics artist: rook, wbcbz7, Robat, Quiet and Nik-O.

summary: Bonzai and Pretzel Logic's four-disk-side C64 demo that came second in the Demo compo at X 2023. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2024 and for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023.
why: Commenters rate it as a new benchmark for storytelling on the C64, with a mood that shifts from 80s nostalgia to the present, and many call it their favourite of the compo.

quote.text: It is the most rewatchable demo I know, like a favorite movie that you can watch over and over again.

summary: Datafresh is a C64 4K intro by Loonies and Darklite that won the C64 4k intro compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer. Blueberry wrote the code and Response the music.
why: Commenters call it one of the best 4Ks and say it beat bigger demos at the party. They single out the zooming plasma and fast ECM shaders.

quote.text: the code is very very clever here, one of the best 4ks I guess

summary: Some Nasty Effects is a BBC Micro demo by CRTC (shown on a BBC Master) that won the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2015. Puppeh and Joey wrote the code, GreaseMonkey the music and Tunk the teletext final screen.
why: A compo win for a BBC Micro demo, ending on a teletext final screen.

summary: Imation is a TI-8x (Z80) calculator demo by Deus Ex Machina, listed as a 64k, that won the oldskool demo compo at Dreamhack 2000.
why: A compo winner on a TI-8x calculator.

summary: Riyadh is an MSX demo by Bandwagon that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001. nf coded it, Gspot made the music and Scythe and Nitro made the 3D graphics.
why: An Assembly compo winner on MSX, with a credits list that gives 3D its own line.

summary: Hardcore Petting is a silent Commodore PET demo made in PETSCII, coded by Shadow. It took third place in the Oldschool Demo compo at @Party 2010.
why: A podium finish for a demo with no sound at all, built from the PET's character set.

summary: Elements is an Atari Lynx demo by Desire that came 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2017. Heaven coded it, Triace composed the music and Premium and BokanoiD did the graphics.
why: A Lynx demo that made the top five at a major party.

summary: Raiding Party is a Vectrex demo by Rift that took second place in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2017. Fell coded it and Bex made the music.
why: A podium finish for a Vectrex production.

summary: Oric Tech is an Oric demo by Defence Force that took second place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2015. Dbug did the code and graphics.
why: A podium finish for an Oric demo, with an intro tune by Jochen Hippel and sample loops from Kraftwerk's Musique Non Stop.

summary: Evil Influences is a BBC Master demo by Bitshifters and Desire that won the Old School Demo compo at Nova Online 2020. VectorEyes and Henley coded it, Dya made the music and Visionvortex and Luther the graphics.
why: A compo winner and a joint effort between two groups on the BBC Master.

summary: Twistex is a 256-byte intro for the Vectrex by Orb, coded by Ultra.
why: A 256-byte production on the Vectrex.

summary: See Sharp is a Sharp MZ-700 demo by Fit that took third place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2011. Marq coded it and Yzi made the music and a couple of the effects.
why: A podium finish at Assembly 2011 for a Sharp MZ-700 production.

summary: Buggy Boy is an Oric demo by Defence Force that won the Other Demo compo at Little Computer People 2004. It is a single-file demo, and the source is available.
why: A compo winner with music by Dma-Sc and Twilighte, graphics by Dbug and Mermaid, and code by Dbug.

summary: Oric Giga Demo is an Oric demo by Defence Force that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2001.
why: A compo winner built by a team of four coders: Dbug, Jede, Twilighte and kouiskas, with graphics by Exocet and a picture conversion by Twilighte.

summary: Kojiki is a NES demo by wAMMA, made as the Alt.Party 2007 invitation. It won the Demo compo at Boozembly 2007.
why: An invitation demo that won a compo. visy and pahamoka coded it, and Ilmarque made both the graphics and the music.

summary: Teletextr is a BBC Micro demo by Bitshifters that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2017. It is built around teletext, with the source available.
why: A compo winner that works within the BBC Micro's teletext display, with graphics by Horsenburger, code by KieranHJ and music by Jrlepage, Svetlana and AbbeAbyss.

summary: Apple Vision is an Apple II demo by Bob Bishop, dated 1 April 1978 in the database. The video comes from Steven Weyhrich's a2history channel.
why: A very early Apple II demo from the 1970s, worth seeing as a piece of history. The fact sheet gives no placing or credits beyond Bob Bishop.

summary: Electric Force is a 256-byte intro for the Vectrex by Frog, who coded it. It took second place in the Tiny Intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: Nominated for Tiny Intro at The Meteoriks 2016. The source is available if you want to see how 256 bytes are used on the Vectrex.

summary: Tendonin is a Game Boy demo by Rebels that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2022. Skarab coded it, Critikill did the graphics and AceMan the music.
why: A win at one of the biggest parties for a Game Boy production.

summary: Zenith Of Puberty is a Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by The Electronic Knights that won the Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2007. Degauss made all of it: code, graphics and music.
why: A one-person effort tagged as using interlaced blending. Demozoo notes it doesn't run in VICE, so use YAPE.

summary: Abre Los Ojos is a Commodore PET demo by oobc that won the Wild compo at Zoo 2015. The video title says it ran on a CBM 8032. Bass Cadet and oo shared the code and graphics, with music by Bass Cadet.
why: A wild-compo win for a PET demo built by two people.

summary: Space: 1999 - The Trailer is an Oric demo by Defence Force that took second place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2010. Dbug coded it, Twilighte wrote the music and Chema drew the graphics.
why: A podium finish for an Oric production built as a trailer, according to its video title.

summary: Unknown Worlds is an Atari Lynx demo by New Generation that won the Atari Lynx Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k23 WE. It was on the Meteoriks watchlist for 2024.
why: The credits give 3D its own line, shared by Solo and kris3d, with code by Solo and Laoo and a multi-composer soundtrack.

summary: Barbitoric is an Oric demo by Condense and Defence Force. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at State of the Art 2002 and came second in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2003.
why: Two compo podiums, a large team of coders and graphics artists, and music by Twilighte.

summary: Severely Limited Capabilities is a 512-byte intro for the unexpanded ZX81 by Noice, coded by Shadow.
why: A 512-byte production on the unexpanded ZX81.

summary: Lynxed is an Atari Lynx demo by Desire that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2016. Heaven coded it, Triace made the music and BokanoiD, Alien and Ozan drew the graphics.
why: A compo win for an Atari Lynx demo.

summary: There Are No Limits is a ZX81 demo by Noice, released in 2009.
why: A follow-up of sorts to Noice's other ZX81 productions only by platform. The fact sheet has no placing, credits or tags.

summary: Kings of Skweeeden is a Sharp MZ-700 demo by Flush and Up Rough that won the True Wild Demo compo at Datastorm 2018. MooZ coded it and made the graphics, and Glafouk did the music.
why: A wild-compo win for a Sharp MZ-700 production, with the source available.

summary: Knark is a Game Boy Color demo by Phantasy that won the Other Platforms Demo compo at Little Computer People 2003. Lai coded it, Goto80 made the music and Jailbird drew the graphics.
why: A compo win on the Game Boy Color, with Jailbird of Booze Design as a guest artist.

summary: XV is an MSX2 demo by Hedelmae that took third place in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2017. fragment coded it, Leaphion made the music and Plokk did the graphics.
why: A podium finish at Assembly for an MSX2 demo.

summary: Chunky Disaster is a Sega Master System demo by Darklite and Offence that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Black Valley 2024. Neon coded it, Pal drew the graphics and Response wrote the music.
why: A recent compo winner on the Master System, and on the Meteoriks watchlist for 2025.

summary: Neotokyo is a Sharp MZ-700 demo by Ivory Labs, Quadtrip and Fit that came second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Simulaatio 2018. It is tagged as an Akira franchise tribute.
why: A joint production by three groups, with code by branch and visy, music by Yzi and a team of graphics artists.

summary: High Color is a SAM Coupé demo by Speccy.pl that won the Wild compo at speccy.pl party 2018.1. Sir David coded it and drew graphics with Cat-Man, and Pyramex was a guest musician.
why: A wild-compo win for a SAM Coupé production.

summary: Two By Two is a TI-8x (Z80) calculator demo by Noice that came 8th in the wild demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: A calculator demo from Noice that made the top eight at Breakpoint.

summary: Apple II Cycle-Counting Megademo is an Apple II demo by VMW Software Production that won the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2018. Deater coded it and drew the graphics, and Dascon made the music.
why: A compo winner whose video title says it is a 64k megademo. The source is available.

summary: Oh is a demo for the Spectravideo SVI-328 by Five Finger Punch that took second place in the combined demo compo at Gerp 2016.
why: A podium finish for a Spectravideo demo in a combined-platform compo.

summary: Silly Venture 2k14 Invitro is an Atari Lynx invitation to the Silly Venture 2k14 party, made by Sage, Inter, Resistance and Lamers. Sage and Sachy coded it, Samurai drew the graphics and Nainain wrote the music.
why: A party invitation on a handheld, with an ASCII graphics credit for ne7 and text by Grey.

summary: SILLYNX is an Atari Lynx demo by Dekadence that won the Atari Lynx Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17. BriteLite coded it, Bracket did the graphics and Ricky Martin made the music.
why: A compo winner whose music is a cover of Cccan't You See by Vicious Pink, according to Demozoo.

summary: News is a PC Engine demo by Up Rough that took second place in the True Wild Demo compo at Datastorm 2017. MooZ coded it and Octapus made the music. The source is available.
why: A podium finish for a PC Engine production built by a two-person team.

summary: Auto Portrait is a Thomson demo by The Undead Sceners that took second place in the Old School Demo compo at Very Important Party 2014. Gilles coded it, and a team of artists drew the graphics.
why: A graphics-led Thomson demo with credited pieces including Planet Thomson, Druid and a drive belt autopsy.

summary: Defender Of The 8-Bits is a SAM Coupé demo by D.T.A. Software Studio that won the Other 8-bit Demo compo at Forever 2016. Antony coded it and DJM made the music.
why: A compo winner on the SAM Coupé, built by a two-person team.

summary: Waterline is a ColecoVision demo by Krüe that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Blockparty 2010. It is tagged as a concept demo.
why: A compo winner on the ColecoVision, tagged as a concept demo.

summary: Nyan Cat TO8 & MO6 is a Thomson tribute to Nyan Cat by OlivierP, dated 2011. The source is available.
why: A Nyan Cat port for the Thomson, shown on a TO8 in the video.

summary: Survival is a 128-byte intro for the ZX81 by frag. The source is available.
why: A 128-byte production on the ZX81, one of the smallest size classes there is.

summary: Oh La Belle Bleue is a 32K intro for the Thomson by Puls, released in 2011.
why: A small Thomson production. The fact sheet has no placing or credits.

summary: Untum is an intro for the Atari 7800 by Desire that took third place in the Combined Oldskool compo at Under Construction 2018. Heaven coded it, Triace wrote the music and Alien drew the graphics.
why: A podium finish for a demo on the 7800, with a video recorded on a PAL console.

summary: The Datastorm 2017 Invitation is a PC Engine invitation from Up Rough that won the Animation & Wild compo at Edison 2016. MooZ coded it and Octapus made the music. The source is available.
why: A party invitation that won a compo in its own right.

summary: 1E78 is an Atari 7800 demo by Desire that came 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019. Heaven and Probe coded it, Triace composed the music and BokanoiD and Alien drew the graphics.
why: A top-five finish at Revision for a demo on the 7800.

summary: Pre-Release is a Spectravideo demo by Five Finger Punch that won the oldskool demo compo at Edison 2015.
why: A compo winner on the Spectravideo 3x8. The fact sheet gives no credits.

summary: Here Be Dragons is a demo by Slipstream that took second place in the oldskool demo compo at NOVA 2022. The video title says it runs on the Dragon 32.
why: A podium finish for a Dragon 32 demo.

summary: Applesoft Basic Bot is an 8K intro for the Apple II by Desire that won the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2020. Deater coded it and mAZE made the music.
why: A compo win for a small Apple II production.

summary: Mode 7 Demo is an Apple II demo by Deater. The video title describes it as an 8k lores Mode7 demo.
why: A short Apple II piece. The fact sheet gives no placing or credits.

summary: Nyan7800 is an Atari 7800 take on Nyan Cat, coded by Moerder, with music players by Tjoppen and Paul Slocum. It took second place in the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2011.
why: A podium finish for a 7800 Nyan Cat tribute.

summary: SkyNet is a trackmo for the Vector-06C by Kirov Coders Group that won the Demo compo at DemosFan 1998. Sunami did the code and music.
why: A compo winner for the Vector-06C. Fan Soft converted the graphics and Kan Soft made the graphics tool.

summary: This SAM Coupé demo is by Sir David, who coded it and drew the graphics with Ziutek, with music by Yerzmyey. It was released in 2014.
why: A SAM Coupé showpiece with a Yerzmyey soundtrack. The fact sheet gives no placing.

summary: Dragon Pepper is a demo by Genesis Project that took third place in the oldskool demo compo at Gerp 2020. The video title says it runs on the Dragon 32.
why: A podium finish for a Dragon 32 demo.

summary: Slow Motion is a SAM Coupé demo by D.T.A. Software Studio, with code by Antony and music by DJM. It was released in 2014.
why: A SAM Coupé demo from the same pair behind Defender Of The 8-Bits. The fact sheet gives no placing.

summary: Lowtech is an Apple II demo by Imphobia, coded by Wiz, which came 13th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2021. The source is available.
why: An Apple II entry at Revision Online 2021 with its source available.

summary: Space Project is a Thomson demo by Puls, released in 2007.
why: A Thomson demo. The fact sheet has no placing or credits.

summary: Tandy Assembly is a demo for the Tandy Color Computer 2 by The Invisible Man and Utz. The Invisible Man did the code and graphics and Utz the music.
why: A Color Computer 2 demo, titled a first release in its video.

summary: Waypoint X is a demo for the KC 85 / Robotron KC 87 by Moods Plateau, which came 10th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2009. dOc.K made the code, graphics and music.
why: A single-person demo for the KC 85 / KC 87 that finished in the top ten of its compo.

summary: Noice's comeback C64 demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by Archmage and music by Dane, which placed third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2008.
why: Several sceners thought it should have won. They single out Archmage's consistent graphics, the tunnel and vectors, and the smooth overall design and flow, even if the effects themselves aren't new for the C64.

quote.text: The effects aren't new for the C64 but the overall design, flow and smoothness give me that feel-good feeling.

summary: Focus's monochrome concept demo for the C64, placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2001: a black-and-white room with a sofa, captioned with everyday ways of wasting time, set to Mindflow's ambient music.
why: Sceners single out the minimal black-and-white design and Mindflow's music, and hold it up as proof that a demo can work without heavy effects. It was later remade for the ZX Spectrum and released as PC and Mac screensavers.

quote.text: More proof that you don't need raster-killing effects and ugly routines to make an excellent demo.

summary: Camelot's C64 demo, placed third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. Code by Cruzer, graphics by BizKid and Cruzer, music by Jeff with guest tunes from DRAX and 4-Mat.
why: Sceners single out the effects: an unlimited-bobs routine with unusually many frames, colourful Kefrens bars, a zoomer behind a sprite stencil, and a 1536-dot part. Several said it looked like an Amiga demo. Some found the graphics and linking weaker, and it's short.

quote.text: I realize that perhaps some of these effects are not totally impossible to do, but you have managed to make them alot more beautiful than anyone else before.

summary: Alone Coder's ZX Spectrum 48K demo with AY music, which came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2013.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2013 that sticks to the stock 48K Spectrum. The video credits it to Alone Coder and friends.
highlights: graveyard picture with a glowing orb

summary: Mad Team's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari demo compo at Forever 2009, with code by Tebe, graphics by Ooz and music by stRing.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2009. The stills show large hand-drawn pictures by Ooz built around a stage magician, carrying the prod visually.

summary: Focus's C64 demo by Ben (code) and Hein (music and graphics) that won the demo compo at X 2004: abstract, minimal design built from impossible isometric shapes, circles and squares.
why: Sceners single out Hein's GoatTracker soundtrack and the fresh, different design, with the isometric impossible shapes and the Tetris part drawing particular praise.

quote.text: WHAT A DESIGN! It's always good to see something totally different. Love it!

summary: Crest's Commodore 64 demo that needs a 16MB REU, streaming full-colour NUFLI animations from the expansion memory. It won the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2010.
why: Sceners praised the technical side and the colourful animated screens, including a seamlessly looped underwater animation. A Rick Astley rickroll gave it what one commenter called a very high crowdpleaser factor.

quote.text: Obviously a lot of work went into this, and it was a joy being rickrolled after for a second actually believing this finally was "Meet Crest". :-)

summary: Performers' four-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at X 2023, with a large crew of coders and guest artists, music from dEViLOCk, Jammer, Linus and LMan, and a part replaying 100 classic games.
why: Winner of what sceners call perhaps the strongest C64 demo compo ever, and of Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2024. Comments single out the 100-games part, Bitbreaker's vector scenes, the music and the humour.

quote.text: The 100games-part stood out. This is not only a demo-part, this is digital art taken to some uber-next level.

summary: Bay 6's ZX Spectrum demo written in BASIC, which won the ZX-Basic compo at Base-X 2015. Code and graphics by Diver, AY music by Nik-O. The video is the party version.
why: A compo-winning demo for the Spectrum's built-in BASIC, inspired by Haujobb's You Should. Worth watching to see what Diver got out of a language not known for speed.

summary: Entire's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2013, with code and music by Rob F. and graphics by Mellona and NINBER.
why: A compo winner that makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode, according to its tags, and it was made with the Pentagon clone in mind.
highlights: music by Rob F. and Fine Soft.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2012, mixing comic-style story screens with isometric graphics and particle effects.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2012 from a large Thesuper crew, with code by drwho and Lovebeam, graphics by Sweetbutt and music by Nick Roll.

summary: Pex Mahoney Tufvesson's C64 demo, made with Uwe 'THCM' Anfang on SID research, placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. It pairs long, clean sample playback with glitchy character-mode visuals, an a cappella quartet part and a scroller.
why: Sceners single out the sample quality, calling it the cleanest they had heard on the SID, along with the a cappella part and the scrolltext. The crowd at the party reportedly went wild for it.

quote.text: Incredible sound quality. I'm looking forward to finding out how this works. Also: best scrolltext ever.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 4K intro by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, music by Response and graphics by Pal. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A 4K intro that placed second at Revision and was nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Hooy-Program and Agenda, with code by Alone Coder, Hellboj and Szuwarek, music by Yerzmyey and graphics by Piesiu and Aki. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2011.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2011 and a cross-group collaboration. It is worth a look for its chunky, colourful attribute-style effects on a stock 48K-class machine with AY music.

summary: Fairlight's C64 art demo by Hollowman (code and graphics) with music from guest Goto80, winner of the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2016. Poetic text screens alternate with dithered bitmaps and animated effects.
why: Sceners welcomed it as Hollowman's long-awaited return, praising the mood and how well Goto80's soundtrack fits the visuals. One commenter notes it is in memory of text-adventure author Paul Panks. Some found the text parts slow.

quote.text:
Excellent in all possible ways. Narrative and emotional expressions, 
accompanied with beautiful music.

summary: Resurrection's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Lak with graphics by Powrooz and music by PG, which came second in the Atari demo compo at Forever 2008.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2008. It opens on a detailed hand-drawn title picture of a woman and a yellow taxi against a city skyline.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Fourth Dimension and Triebkraft that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at DiHalt 2007, built around a cartoon kid and a star.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2007. The stills show hand-drawn monochrome cartoon scenes mixed with wireframe vector shapes.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2012, with vector parts, a zoomer, a plasma-style interference effect and a "turn disk" picture of a punk girl.
why: Sceners single out the 16-colour plasma/interference effect, the transitions and the music, with Wiklund's second tune drawing particular praise, along with graphics by Louie and Prowler.

quote.text: A lot of great effects, tied together by fitting transitions and great music.

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo, coded and designed by Groepaz with music by Moog and Xiny6581 and graphics by Cupid and Death, which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: Sceners single out the physics parts, with falling blocks and fluid effects, and a marching squares part at the end. Several call it a coder's demo that brings effects to the C64 which hadn't been done before.

quote.text: i LOVED the physics part. It is just wonderful. I could have watched that way longer.

summary: Slight's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari 8bit demo compo at QuaST 1995, with code by Seban, Soused Teat, Rzóg and The Last Byte, and graphics by PW and Dracon.
why: A compo winner from the mid-90s Polish Atari scene. Its tags point to a dancer, morphing, a zoomer and a scroller, and it is noted for the 'stickman's world' theme.

summary: Triebkraft and 4th Dimension's ZX Spectrum demo, which won the 8 bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2004.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, and a joint production between two groups.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Schafft and Hedj that placed third in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: It was nominated for Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2016, a sign of standing well beyond its compo placing.

summary: Offence and Prosonix's four-disk-side C64 demo, placed fourth in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. It runs as a string of press-space parts, opening with a 2001: A Space Odyssey style intro featuring a talking HAL eye.
why: A Scene.org Awards nominee that sceners call a huge, graphics-heavy throwback to the late-80s megademo. They single out the film-like 2001 intro, the Tron part, the scene heroes part and the large vertical twister.

quote.text: I didn't think I'd ever be impressed by a demo again like I was in 1988-90. But I was wrong. This is outstanding.

summary: Resource and Coma's two-disk-side C64 trackmo, third in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1997, with code by Edhellon and Oswald, graphics by Tyrant and Splash, and music from Da Blondie plus guests Eclipse and Taki.
why: Sceners call it an overlooked favourite: fast-paced, colourful effects, strong graphics and fonts, and nice transitions that still look modern. Even the compo winner's member admits Void deserved the win.

quote.text: Great music, beautiful and colourful effects and graphics, many fresh new ideas with nice transitions. And quite long.

summary: Extend's C64 demo from X 2016, coded by Barfly and Mankeli with graphics by Duce and Electric and a Barracuda soundtrack. It placed 18th in the demo compo after being shown last, following a break.
why: Sceners widely call it underrated for its placing, praising the fresh hires pixel work, the psychedelic atmosphere and Barracuda's techno SID tune. Several rank it among the best at X 2016.

quote.text: The music and visuals create an atmosphere like nothing else in the competition.  Excellent pixels, fantastic looking effects and great music!

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that placed 2nd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2019: ABBA-style silhouettes and dance animations cut tightly to a gabber soundtrack by Nik-O.
why: Tagged for extreme sync between music and visuals, it pairs ABBA imagery with gabber. A writeup on how it was made is available in Russian.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Benediction and Arkos that came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2021, with code by Krusty and Eliot, music by Targhan and graphics by Voxy and Tom et Jerry.
why: A podium finish at Revision's oldskool compo and a nomination for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022 put it among the year's stand-out 8-bit demos.

summary: Scoopex's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2019, with code by Mr. Spiv and lordcoxis, music by LaesQ and graphics by Pheel, Xile and K-0s.
why: A Forever compo winner that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to get more colour onto the screen than the stock attribute grid usually allows.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by g0blinish that won the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2014, framed as a television set with a screen showing changing pictures and effects.
why: It took first place in the Retro Demo competition at Demosplash 2014, beating entries from other retro platforms.

summary: Booze Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a Western theme, winner of the demo compo at Fjälldata 2025. Effects-heavy parts by a large coding team, set among colourful hand-drawn pictures by Mirage, Archmage and Dane.
why: Won Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2026. Sceners single out the VIC trickery and the way the code serves the graphics; coders admit to watching it in a debugger to work out how it's done.

quote.text: even better: the code seems to 100% serve the beauty. to me this is the most important achievement

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo by HCL and Dane that won the C64 demo compo at Deadline 2005: a slow, design-led run of Japanese-themed parts, layered shapes and big pictures in XFLI and IFLI.
why: Sceners single out its calm pacing, Dane's music and graphics that some call among the best on the C64, with clever layer techniques hidden under the design. Many keep coming back to it years later.

quote.text: it is a true peace of art.. it is so peaceful, so relaxing, serene..

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo from X 2016, where it placed 7th: a long run of effects parts with graphics by Carrion, Se7en, Peacemaker and Cupid, code by Groepaz, HCL and Peacemaker, and music by Linus.
why: Sceners praise its polish, flow and graphics throughout, and the soundtrack gets repeated praise. Several feel it deserved a far higher compo placing. Commenters single out the ice effect in the intro and ending, and the shadow-casting routine.
highlights: ice effect in intro and ending

quote.text: it's seriously polished from back to front and it never gets boring because of it. not to mention the proper flow, superb gfx throughout and brilliant soundtrack.

summary: A four-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence that came third in the demo compo at X 2012, opening with a Star Wars-themed section and moving through scrollers, a huge picture upscroller and a credits part.
why: Sceners single out the sheer amount of pixel art from Pal, the smooth Star Wars scroller and the atmospheric end credits. Some found it too long, but its scope is the point.

quote.text: Pal, you are a pixel animal. Bringing us this unfuckingbelievable amount of finest pixel art in just one demo.

summary: Samar's C64 demo, the 100% final version of I Love The Cube, coded by Mr Wegi with music by Conrad and graphics by Isildur and Conrad. Cube-themed vector parts over hi-res pictures such as the lollipop girl.
why: Sceners praise the big vectors, the dot-plotter scrollers and Conrad's music, and many felt this final version was a clear step up from the party release. Its sense of humour gets a mention too.

quote.text: Amazingly smooth and stylish demo, respect to the Samar guys!

summary: Kkolor is a ZX Spectrum demo by Triebkraft and 4th Dimension. It won the 8 Bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2005, with code by psndcj, graphics by pROF, Diver and G.D., and music by C-jeff, Fatal Snipe and Key-Jee.
why: A first-place winner at Chaos Constructions 2005, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties. Two well-known Spectrum groups made it together, and it fills the screen with bold blocks of colour.

summary: The final version of Censor Design and Oxyron's big multi-disk C64 demo, with fixes over the 2014 release and a large team of coders, graphicians and musicians.
why: Sceners single out the music, especially the main tune on disk 1, the smooth effects and Mirage's big scrolling owl logo. Several call it one of the best C64 demos they've seen.
highlights: flying bee parts with zooming gfx

quote.text: The music in this one is superb, main tune on disk 1 may be one of the best demo-tunes ever made (imo).

summary: A 1K intro for the Commodore 64 by 4mat, released at Forever 2006, where it won the Commodore 1K Intro competition. Symmetrical, colourful chunky patterns grow and shift to a beat.
why: Sceners praise its fluid visuals and stomping beat squeezed into 1K, with one noting a Psychedelia influence. 4mat later released the source in DASM format.

quote.text: Love the Psychedelia influence.  Very fluid visuals and a stomping beat - all in 1k.

summary: Viznut's C64 4K intro for Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, winner of the C64 4K intro compo at Breakpoint 2010: a wordless story told with only three big pixels moving in sync with the music.
why: Sceners single out how much storytelling it gets out of almost nothing and how tightly the pixels' movements are synced to Viznut's music. Many read it as a boy-meets-girl relationship with no happy ending.

quote.text: Incredible what little requires for storytelling.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, released at Chaos Constructions 2006, where it placed third in the 8-bit 640k demo compo.
why: A podium finish at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties from a collaboration between two groups. The video shows a dithered portrait set beside colourful animated effects.

summary: Resource and The Dreams' C64 demo that came third in the demo compo at X 2004, with code by Bubis, Ninja and Oswald, graphics by AmN, Leon and Sander, and music by GRG.
why: Sceners single out the fast bitmap and maths effects, especially a smooth-running Julia fractal and huge vectors bigger than the screen, along with GRG's energetic soundtrack. Some felt it looked unfinished, but most enjoyed it.

quote.text: My favorites are the vectors inside vectors and that Juhlia, wow! (Not many times I had seen a decent running Juhlia in any 8bit machine. Perhaps 1 or 2 times only).

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo, coded, drawn and scored by Gasman, which took second place in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: A one-person production that placed second at Forever and made the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist.

summary: Fairlight and Genesis Project's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2026: a conjuring-trick themed show built around Redcrab's animated PETSCII, border sprite effects and a nod to LFT's demo 9.
why: Sceners single out Redcrab's PETSCII animation as some of the best ever made on the C64, alongside border tricks and an all-border upscroller at the end that even other coders found hard to explain.

quote.text: it's the animation that stands out most - because I don't think this quality of animation has been done on C64 before

summary: UKScene Allstars' ZX Spectrum demo, coded and scored by Gasman with graphics by Equinox, that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006. It opens on a mock platform-game title screen.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2006 against oldskool entries from other machines, and a showcase for Equinox's colourful Spectrum graphics alongside Gasman's code and music.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Hooy-Program and Benediction, with code by Krusty, graphics by Voxy and music by Aki. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2012.
why: A podium finish at Revision in the oldskool 4K category, and the source is available for anyone curious how it fits in the size limit.

summary: Dirty Minds' 1K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Optimus, which won the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2014. It renders a voxel landscape in dithered blocks inside a small window.
why: A voxel landscape squeezed into 1K on a stock CPC, and it took first place at ReSeT 2014. The source is available for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Dirty Minds' 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Optimus with music by Aki. It placed second in the Demo compo at ReSeT (.fr) 2012.
why: A size-limited CPC intro that held its own against full demos, taking second place in the Demo competition at ReSeT 2012.

summary: Offence's C64 demo, coded, drawn and scored by Kristian Myklebust with a bob part by Geir Ytterdahl, placed 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013. Flat-colour silhouettes and landscapes move to a minimalist tune.
why: Sceners praise its catchy demo flow, the minimalist jew's harp music synced to the action, the airplane scene and the fact that it loops endlessly. It went down well at the party itself.

quote.text: It has a really nice and catchy demo flow. The Music is also extremely nice and special. It works very well with the action on-screen, and the synchronizations with the airplane etc - really great.

summary: Horizon's C64 demo, the last one from the group, which won the C64 demo compo at Hurricane and Brutal Summer Party 1992. It mixes filled and morphing vectors, a raytraced part and atmospheric graphics, with music by Boogaloo and Bappalander.
why: Sceners single out the smooth filled and glenz vectors, the morphing hidden-line objects and the raytracer, all remarkable for 1992. Some credit it with introducing the techniques later used for filled vectors on the C64.

quote.text: Must have seen the vector part a hundred times. It was the first filled vectors I ever saw on a C64. Morphing! Glenz! Come on! And smooth as well.

summary: Progress's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, winner of the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997, with code and graphics shared across Fux, Mic, Rom, Kolver and KSA.
why: It won its compo at Enlight 1997, and it is tagged for the Spectrum's multicolour mode. The stills show large, grotesque hand-drawn pictures such as a screaming face with a gun to its head and a bloodshot eyeball.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer, with code by moh, Hollowman and Pantaloon and music by Wiklund. A quick-paced run of full-screen effects ending in an endless loop.
why: Sceners single out Wiklund's soundtrack, the pacing and transitions so smooth you forget they are transitions. The fractal zoom and the tunnel also get repeated mentions.

quote.text: Really nice and smooth demo, with very nice transitions, so seamless that you forget it actually is a transition.

summary: Extend's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2015, a homage to the Aerial Core BBS of 1991–92. Code by Mankeli, music by Barracuda, graphics by Electric.
why: Sceners call it fresh and free of the usual mannerisms, embracing the machine with PETSCII and glitches rather than hiding it. Comments single out the transitions, the plasma and the final effect.

quote.text: A totally fresh approach and style, free from the usual mannerisms (sorry :-) Embracing the machine instead of trying to hide it, if you know what I mean.

summary: Illusion is a ZX Spectrum demo by X-Trade, with code by Dark and LD, graphics by Dark and Dangerous, and music by Deni. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1996.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Enlight 1996, so it's a good look at what a winning Spectrum demo from the mid-1990s offered.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 16K demo with code, music and graphics by Gasman, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sunrise 2011. Effects play in a framed window beside the Justin Beeper logo while a scroller runs below.
why: A compo winner at Sunrise 2011 that fits in a 16K Spectrum and plays its soundtrack on the beeper, with one person, Gasman, behind all of it.

summary: A 16K Amstrad CPC intro by d0z with music by Mr. Lou, which won the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2012, beating other old-school entries with a 16K CPC intro, and its source code has been released.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation intro for the Retrokomp / Load Error 2015 party, made by Wanted Team and Lamers with code by Szeryf, music by mCCnEx and graphics by At0m.
why: It won the Oldschool Intro compo at Riverwash 2015.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum 640k demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2013. Gasman handled code, graphics and music, with a font by Equinox.
why: It won its compo at Chaos Constructions 2013, and almost all of it is one person's work. It uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to get far more colour on screen than the machine normally allows.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Skrju and Triebkraft, placed 4th in the 256b intro compo at Raww.orgy 2010.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept at the Scene.org Awards 2010, a rare honour for something only 256 bytes long.

summary: Genesis Project's tiki-themed one-file C64 demo, winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Edison 2013, with code and graphics by Mermaid, extra graphics by hedning and music by Stinsen. It plays as an endless loop.
why: Sceners single out Mermaid's hires graphics and animation, Stinsen's drum-heavy tune and how much is packed into a single file. Several also praise the final picture before the loop and the directory art.

quote.text: This is a perfect marriage of music, art and light-heartedness.

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Code by Heaven, music by BeWu and Triace, and graphics from six artists including Alien, JAC! and Premium.
why: A full Atari 8-bit demo from a group better known on other machines, shown in a strong Revision oldskool compo and well received on Pouet.

summary: Censor Design's four-disk-side C64 demo, the fourteenth in their Wonderland series, placed 3rd in the demo compo at X 2023. It runs from a fractal intro through a KISS concert part to a sampled rap finale.
why: It won the 8-bit demo award at Siggraph Asia 2023 and was a Meteoriks nominee. Sceners praise the story tying the parts together, Talent's graphics, the smooth music design and above all the digitised rap end part.

quote.text: Pushing the edge with a rap part with so much visuals and the longest singing vocals I ever heard on the C64.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2022, with code by Kowalski, psndcj and sq, graphics by Diver, 3D and animation by Rollerbob and music by Nik-O.
why: A first-place compo winner from a well-staffed Spectrum team, with dedicated credits for 3D and animation work alongside the pixel art and soundtrack.

summary: Eye-Q Team's ZX Spectrum demo, winner of the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2022, built around graphics by Grongy with music by Fatal Snipe and code by Z and Organism.
why: It took first place in the Retro Demo competition at Demosplash 2022, and its title puts graphician Grongy's artwork at the centre.

summary: Gemba Boys' underwater-themed ZX Spectrum 128K demo, which placed second in the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2014. Code by Busy, Noby, Mike and mborik, graphics by mborik and Ellvis, music by Aki.
why: A runner-up at DiHalt 2014 from a large Slovak crew, built around a single aquatic theme from start to finish.

summary: Performers' two-disk-side C64 demo, a tribute release that took 3rd in the C64 demo compo at X 2018, with code, graphics and music from a large cast including Bitbreaker, Mahoney, DeeKay, Jammer and LMan.
why: Sceners single out the music and its use of samples, and above all the greetings scroller part, which several call their favourite of the compo. Fast shaded vectors and a 50fps fullscreen cube also get praise.

quote.text: Right balance between fine design, hard effects and good flow. The final mod music screen is pretty awesome too.

summary: Crest's 1992 Commodore 64 demo, released at Christmas, with code by Crossbow and Vision and music from Deek, DRAX, JCH, MSK and Xayne. Expect border and sideborder scrollers, DYPP scrollers and a varying set of parts.
why: Sceners rate it for its VIC-II trickery and its soundtrack. They single out the multicolour brick wall in the borders with balls running through it, the DYPP part, and the way parts and the directory change between runs.

quote.text: I never saw a demo with more apparently impossible-to-do VIC-tricks.

summary: Skrju's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2017. Flat-coloured shapes turn over a grey screen beneath bold, cheeky text captions.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions, one of the main parties for Spectrum demos. It comes from Skrju, a well-known Spectrum group.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s VIC-20 demo for a machine with a 16K RAM expansion, placed 6th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2010. Code and graphics by Streettuff, extra graphics by Veto, music by Linus.
why: A rare VIC-20 entry at Breakpoint from a long-running group, showing what the chunky low-resolution machine can do once it has extra memory.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC intro from 2006, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by Tom&Jerry: a long snake of shaded balls weaves over a purple patterned backdrop while a scroller runs beneath.
why: Tagged as a sprites record, it pushes the number of moving balls the CPC can handle on screen. It's well liked on Pouët, with almost no dissent.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC demo, the fourth in the Onescreen Colonies series, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by Zik, Tom et Jerry and e-dredon. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #5 in 2025.
why: A compo winner that its own end screen bills as the close of the series, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.
highlights: credits from Hicks, Beb and three musicians

summary: Noice's first ZX Spectrum demo, a 48K production coded by Shadow with music by Yerzmyey, a logo by Piesiu and a font by Sy-Klone. It placed 3rd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2012.
why: A podium finish at Forever on the group's first outing on the Spectrum, with guest contributions from Piesiu of Agenda^Mystic Bytes and Yerzmyey of Hooy-Program.
highlights: character-block patterns in a framed window

summary: An Atari 2600 demo by Noice, coded by Shadow with music by Ilmarque, which placed second in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11.
why: A second place in a dedicated VCS demo compo at Silly Venture, and a rare chance to see what a small team can draw out of the Atari 2600.

summary: Desire's Atari 800 XL/XE demo for 64K machines, fourth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Parts include voxel landscapes, a voxel sphere, a Wolfenstein-style part, a tilt/rotator and a Rescue on Fractalus-style mountain.
why: A packed showcase of 3D techniques on stock Atari 8-bit hardware, built by a large crew of coders and artists. An IRQ loader keeps music and effects running while the next part loads.

summary: Noice's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, with code by Shadow, graphics by Rayden and music by 6R6. It won the Other Demo compo at Big Floppy People 2007.
why: An early multipart showcase for the DTV hardware. Sceners praised its filled vector in chunky mode, shadebobs and interference effects, and several said it felt like a mix of C64 and Amiga style.

quote.text: Feels like a mix between C64 and Amiga. Nice stuff. :-)

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Ilmenit that won the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2022: a monochrome forest of grey tree trunks shown in two side-by-side panels, with sound.
why: It won Lovebyte's oldschool 256-byte compo and then Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2023, which puts it among the most recognised tiny intros on the Atari.

summary: A 32-byte Commodore 64 intro by Ate Bit, coded by 4mat: a glitch piece that churns colour blocks and character-set garbage across the screen while generating its own sound.
why: Sceners point out how much it gets from so little: by their count it fits into about 20 bytes, with what one calls "procedural" music and digi sound through $D418.

quote.text: impressive, 20 bytes with "procedural" music (so to say) :D

summary: Mahoney's C64 concept demo, placed 6th in the Demo compo at X 2014. Code and music by Mahoney, with graphics from Prowler, Redcrab and Mahoney, built around a sung song with a message.
why: Sceners single out the sampled vocals and the message, and note that the song is Mahoney's own rather than a cover. Several called it their favourite of the compo and a distinctly Mahoney style of demo.

quote.text: I hope Mahoney never stops, really original stuff, extra cool that it's not a cover either. And a message too ;)

summary: Oxyron's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, winner of the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2017. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by dEViLOCk and No-XS, graphics by Yazoo.
why: Sceners called it the best DTV demo so far. They single out the motion-blurred rotozoomer, the vector tunnel flights, the Gouraud-shaded vectors, the opening Oxyron logo and the music.

quote.text: The tunnels are exquisite and the first Oxyron logo (intro) is unbeatable! The music is also very nice!

summary: A 23-byte audio-visual intro for the Commodore 64 by 4mat of Ate Bit, released in a 32-byte intro category in 2011. It churns the screen into glitchy character garbage and colour blocks while playing a beat.
why: Sceners were struck that synced sound and visuals fit in 23 bytes, with praise for its clever use of kernal data in zero page and for how it improves the longer it runs. Its glitch aesthetic split opinion.

quote.text: Love it! It just gets better the longer you keep it running. Really clever stuff.

summary: Booze Design's Commodore 64 demo, released as a party version at Floppy 2005, where it took third place in the demo compo.
why: An unfinished party version of a Booze Design demo, as the "73%" in its title and the party-version tag suggest, placed third at Floppy 2005.

summary: A four-disk-side Christmas megademo for the C64, made jointly by Offence, Atlantis, Genesis Project, Lethargy and Bonzai under the name The Santas. It won the C64 demo compo at Forndata X-Mas 2020.
why: Sceners praise the festive mood, the graphics and above all the soundtrack of carefully made cover tunes. Commenters also note that dozens of contributors from several groups put it together in nine weeks.

quote.text: This certainly has a collection of beautiful graphics and solid effects, but for me the absolute highlight is the soundtrack. Each cover is extremely tasteful and lovingly crafted.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2018, coded by Houbba, Icon, Iopop and Powerslave with music by Dalezy and graphics by Twoflower.
why: Sceners praise how sleek and fluid it is, singling out the diagonal sideborder hires scroller, the transparency part and the hires starfield behind the final greetings. Several also call it a fine tribute.

quote.text:
totally did it for me again. really sleek and fluid!

and that starfield is about the greatest i know.

summary: HARD Software's Atari 8-bit demo, coded, drawn and scored by Téli Sándor alone, which won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: A one-man production that took first place in the Atari XL/XE demo competition at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Dirty Minds, coded by Optimus and Antitec with graphics by Optimus, Rex and Sice and music by Sice. It placed second in the Wild Demo competition at React 2003.
why: A second place in the React 2003 Wild Demo compo. This video shows the colour version, uploaded by the coder Optimus himself.

summary: Samar Productions' C64 demo, the finished 100% version of Dream Travel, marking 18 years of the group, with code by Hermit, doZe, Mr Wegi and Skull, graphics by Isildur and Skull, and music by Jammer and Randall.
why: Sceners saw it as a leap in design and coherence for Samar, praising its colourful, carefully animated parts, pixel-perfect graphics, smooth transitions and detail. Many single out the bitmaps and the isometric coffee mug.

quote.text: Everything on this demo looks awesome and is so well animated and pixel perfect. If only more demos were made with this kind of love and such attention to animation, transition and detail.

summary: Dentifrice's Atari 2600 demo, third in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18, with code by Kezax, music by Glafouk and graphics from Exocet, Easy, Remdy and Logan Walters.
why: A podium finish in a dedicated VCS demo compo, and a sizeable graphics team for a machine this limited. It's tagged with a Space Invaders reference.

summary: Genesis Project's all-PETSCII C64 demo, with graphics and idea by Redcrab, music by Stinsen and code by Norrland. It won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2016.
why: Sceners single out the detail Redcrab gets from the plain character set, the flow and storyline, Stinsen's soundtrack and the dancing alien. Several admit it changed their minds about PETSCII.

quote.text: These gfx have so much versatility and detail that I can't believe my eyes it's done with PETSCII!

summary: lft's solo C64 demo, with code, graphics and music all his own, which came second in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2025: a magician figure conjures nine coloured digit sprites that circle him and end up side by side, even in the upper border.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at the Meteoriks. Sceners praise how it builds up the trick step by step, seemingly beating the eight-sprites-per-line limit, and admit they still can't work out how it's done.
highlights: digits moving into the upper border

quote.text: Great trick, that isn't immediately obvious, which is quite a feat on a platform where so many tricks have been done.

summary: Resource, Chorus and Singular's single-file C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2012, with graffiti-style titles, a floor mapper and vector fonts. This is the 100% final version from November 2012.
why: Sceners single out how much it packs into one file, from the blocky sideborder plasma and wobbly kefrens to Soci's animated vector fonts.

quote.text: Great show for a one-filer. I especially liked the wobbly kefrens and the font.

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2013, a group effort with code and graphics from a long list of contributors and music by Aki.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Forever 2013 and brings together a large Slovak and Czech crew, including Noby, mborik, z00m, Busy and UB880D, in one production.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo that won the 8 Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2017, with code and graphics by TmK, extra graphics by KloyanA and music by Nik-O.
why: A compo winner at Multimatograf 2017 from deMarche. The video is the group's own no-flicker capture.
highlights: dithered portrait of a crowned face

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Cyberpunks Unity and Inward, coded by Elfh with music by Moran. It came third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2004.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2004, one of the main Spectrum parties of its day, from a collaboration between two groups. Elfh wrote both the code and the text.

summary: Darklite and Offence's 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum, with code by Neon, graphics by Pal and music by Response. It won the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2026.
why: A first place at Revision in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo, beating the other size-limited entries across platforms.

summary: Micro is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gemba Boys, coded by Noby, Busy, mborik and Mike with graphics by Ellvis and Aki and music by Aki. It came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2014.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2014 from a large Slovak crew pooling several coders. It's a solid example of the 128K Spectrum demo style of its time.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Flashback 2012: an animated pirate story with code, graphics and text by Mermaid and music by Mr. Death.
why: Sceners single out Mermaid's hand-drawn pixels and animation, the storytelling and the family-friendly charm, along with the cover of the pirate tune from Pippi in the South Seas.

quote.text: One can tell it's a labour of love. Instantly recognisable pixel goodness, and everything fits so well together. Makes it all look easy

summary: Fairlight's story-driven C64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2006. Blocky robot characters act out a melancholic tale in stark black-and-white hires, set to Smalltown Boy's SID.
why: Sceners praise it as poetry rather than record-breaking: clean, artistic design, good flow and a melancholic story whose lyrics come from Dire Straits' Romeo and Juliet. Several felt it deserved better than 4th.

quote.text: Very artistic and clean. Good flow, accompanied by a great soundtrack. This proves that a demo is not all about breaking the most records.

summary: Ilmenit and Piesiu's 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro that won the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021: a little steam train crossing a desert under a streaked blue sky.
why: Won Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022, and fits a whole scene plus sound into 256 bytes.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at DiHalt 2011.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2011, and well received on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, a silent wireframe cube turning over shifting background colours. It placed 6th in the Atari ST/800XL Demo/Bootsector compo at Outline 2011.
why: A tidy example of how much a 256-byte Atari intro can fit, and the source code is available for anyone curious about how it's done.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's VIC-20 demo, coded, drawn and scored by Viznut, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A compo winner at Assembly on one of the least-used 8-bit machines, made entirely by one person, Viznut, who handled code, graphics and music alike.

summary: Cluster's Atari VCS demo, released at Revision 2014, where it placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo. Code and design by Kylearan, music and player by KK, in a 32K cartridge.
why: A well-received Atari 2600 demo placing in Revision's oldskool compo, which shows how much a 2014 VCS production could still pull out of the console. Its stills show it doesn't take itself too seriously.

summary: Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence's C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013: a western-themed intro, physics-driven ball parts, sphere scrollers and a talking greetings head.
why: Sceners single out the physics parts (the pendulum, the bouncing balls inside a sphere), the Censor-style scrollers, the spoken greetings with a deforming mouth and the humour, with several calling it the strongest demo of the compo.

quote.text: This is the best demo from the compo in many ways, full of wonderful parts and innovative effects.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum demo, which came second in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2011, built around chunky full-screen colour effects and scrolling text.
why: A podium finish at Alternative Party 2011 for a Spectrum demo with a firm communist theme in its greetings and graphics.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2015, coded by Clarence with graphics by Leon and music by guest DRAX of Maniacs Of Noise, Camelot and Crest.
why: Sceners single out Clarence's code: very smooth movement, a fullscreen AGSP part, extended FLD, sprites in the upper border and a puzzling 4-char-wide sprite trick. Several call it a benchmark tech demo despite its short length.

quote.text: Holy f**k! The most fascinating routines I've seen for ages! Guess I'll have to watch this again and again to figure out how it's done.

summary: A two-disk-side C64 co-op demo by Bonzai, Fairlight, Genesis Project, Censor Design and Offence that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019. Its theme is the groups poking fun at each other's trademark parts.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at The Meteoriks 2020. Sceners single out the humour, the friendly 'coopetition' between five groups, the lush graphics and the all-border DYPP scroller.
highlights: music by Laxity, LMan, Magnar, Stinsen

quote.text: Neat effects, lush pixels, groovy tunes, a little bit of fight, and a lot of love for the greatest machine ever to exist.

summary: Trilobit's Atari 2600 demo, coded, drawn and scored by Ilmarque with a story by visy. It came 3rd in the Atari 8-bit demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10.
why: A VCS demo that placed against Atari 8-bit computer entries at Silly Venture, and one of the few on the 2600 to credit a story.

summary: Vanity's 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC, placed 4th in the 4K intro compo at Main 2010. Code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and music by Tom&Jerry.
why: A raycasting engine squeezed into 4K on the CPC, packed with exomizer, from a well-known CPC group.

summary: Razor 1911's C64 4K intro, coded by rez with graphics by Sector 9 and music by Ziphoid, placed third in the Oldskool 4k compo at Revision 2014. A framed pattern effect runs under a Razor logo while a scroller loops.
why: Sceners welcomed Razor 1911 back on the C64 and praised its design, transitions and music for a one-file 4K. Its author has said it was his first release.

quote.text: This is really nice and more so that its only 4k.  The patterns in the middle are really effective.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo from 1991 by Logon System, coded by Overflow with graphics by Ze Big Boss and music by Jonathan Dunn taken from the game Renegade III.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it's a well-liked early Logon System production from the group's coder Overflow, made outside any compo.

summary: A 32-byte intro for the Atari VCS by SvOlli, with Imp credited for hardware design and soldering. It won the Wild compo at Deadline 2018.
why: A compo winner squeezed into just 32 bytes on one of the most constrained machines around, and the hardware credit suggests the entry went beyond a plain cartridge.
highlights: hardware design and soldering by Imp

summary: Fairlight's war-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Big Floppy People 2006, with code, graphics and concept by Hollowman, extra graphics by Jackasser and music by zabutom.
why: Sceners praised how its theme holds from start to finish and how smoothly story and effects flow together, singling out the physics animations, the parallax aeroplanes and zabutom's tune, plus a hidden 'Boten Anna' cover.

quote.text: A demo with a theme that works the whole way from the beginning to the end,  now that is something you don't see every day! Very nice use and selection of effects.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by bob_er with music by Dhor, which won the Atari 8bit demo compo at Glucholazy 2007. It works in text mode throughout.
why: A compo winner built around text-mode graphics, tagged as such, making it a good pick for anyone interested in what character-based visuals can do on the Atari.

summary: Fairlight and Instinct's C64 demo from Black Birdie 2005, a tribute to the LCP party built around digitised scener portraits, a kaleidoscope-filled vector, raycaster maze, tunnel, twister, chesswaver and an end upscroller.
why: Sceners like its mix of serious code and an unserious, sarcastic attitude, singling out the kaleidoscope, the fast raycaster with Maktone's face jumping out of the maze, and the high-quality end upscroller.

quote.text: This is how a fast production should always be: Good music, nice graphics, sweet sarcasm, serious code and unserious attitude.

summary: Elysium's three-disk-side C64 demo built around a science-lab theme, winner of the demo compo at X 2026. Music by Shogoon, with code from Digger, Brush, MMS, YTM and others, plus a hidden part.
why: Sceners praise its full-border vector work, the haunting big-eye animation, the CRT text effects and Shogoon's soundtrack, and welcome Elysium's return with a demo whose concept runs through every part.

quote.text: the flow, soundtrack, storyline, code, gfx, art direction, polishing, literally everything was 11/10 :)

summary: Agenda's Atari XL/XE demo that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code from five coders, graphics by Ooz, Piesiu, Raphis and Ripek, and music by AceMan, Caruso and stRing.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture 2019 that went on to the Meteoriks 2020 watchlist, made by a large team of Atari 8-bit regulars.

summary: An 8K intro for the ZX Spectrum by T$ Ripoff Institute, with code, music and graphics all by Gasman. Made as a birthday present, it placed third in the combined intro competition at Nordlicht 2014.
why: A one-person 8K production that placed at Nordlicht 2014. It was made as a birthday present, and its tags tie it to Raving Tomatoes.

summary: Panoramic Designs' C64 demo from 1992, shared =7th in the C64 demo compo at Hurricane and Brutal Summer Party. Music comes from several hands, including Ben Daglish, Olav Mørkrid and GT.
why: A long-standing CSDb favourite. Sceners single out the layered parallax, sprites caught between foreground and background effects, the ghost-byte "i" drawn with $d016 alone, the "Blue" and "Home" parts and the speed-changing end scroller.

quote.text: Very thematic, strongly designed, deep and dark and brooding and beautiful...

summary: New Generation's two-disk-side Atari 8-bit demo that came second in the demo compo at QuaST 2004, with code by Solo and Laoo, graphics by Tiger and music by Miker, X-Ray and Solo.
why: A podium finish at QuaST 2004 from a full New Generation line-up, and it is well regarded on Pouët with no thumbs down.

summary: Digital Reality's ZX Spectrum demo from 1996, which placed fourth in the ZX Spectrum demo competition at Enlight 1996.
why: A mid-nineties Spectrum party demo from Digital Reality that held its own at Enlight 1996, finishing fourth in the Spectrum demo compo.

summary: Arise's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Silesia 8 in 2017, with code by Luke, Mojzesh, Wacek and Rodney and music by Jammer. Parts include textured faces, split vectors, glenz marching cubes and an all-border chessboard.
why: Sceners single out its design, syncing and transitions, calling it fresh and stylish. Bitbreaker held it up as proof that good transitions beat storytelling-heavy design, though some found the texture rotator runs long.

quote.text: A good proof that cool transitions work way better than lots of artsy fartsy design that focusses on storytelling only. You hit the sweet spot with this.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 48K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2014, with parts coded by Gasman, Lvd, TK90X Fan, Ralf, Hellboj and Alone Coder.
why: A first place at Forever 2014, and a collaborative piece pooling six coders and four graphicians, with music by Yerzmyey and Mister Beep across AY and beeper.

summary: Singular Crew's Commodore 64 demo, placed 5th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2008.
why: A Breakpoint 2008 wild-compo entry from Singular Crew, well received on Pouët. The fact sheet is thin, so it's one to judge for yourself.

summary: A one-file C64 demo by Plush, Instinct and Oxyron, coded by Krill, Jackasser and Graham with music by Fanta. It placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2004 and has hidden parts and an interactive mode.
why: Sceners praise the smooth, polished effects with an oldschool touch, Fanta's atmospheric soundtrack and the transitions. Several also single out JackAsser's debut as a coder.

quote.text: a really nice demo doing a great job combining really smooth effects with an oldschool touch.

summary: Agenda's Atari 8-bit demo from Silly Venture 2k13, where it placed third in the Atari XL/XE demo compo. Code by Probe, music by stRing, graphics by Ooz, Ripek and Piesiu.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, with three graphicians credited. That points to a demo built around its artwork.

summary: A C64 demo by Extend and Genesis Project, coded by Elder0010 with graphics by Sulevi and music by psych, that won the demo compo at Transmission64 2025. Its abstract narrative carries an AI-critical message.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2026. Sceners praise the coherent design from a three-person team, Sulevi's pixel work, psych's soundtrack and the way the parts flow together.

quote.text: There is a mesmerizing flow to the demo, both due to the rhythmic beat of the music, the somewhat abstract narrative that still gets a message through, the unusual color choices, and the awesome effects.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2018, with music by Ole Marius Pettersen and graphics by Pal.
why: Sceners single out the intricate animations, the helix scroller, Pal's design and OMP's soundtrack, which one commenter called probably his favourite tune from all the Datastorm compos.

quote.text: Beautiful design! Mesmerizing anims and classic soundtrack from Prosonix. The tube scroller looks awesome!

summary: Onslaught's C64 demo marking the group's 20th anniversary, coded by Conjuror and Algorithm with guest artists Yazoo, bizk and ptoing. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Under Construction 2015.
why: Sceners praise its polish, transitions and soundtrack by Adam and Psycho8580, and single out the rotating pyramid, the twister parts and the circular scroller over the opening fullscreen picture.

quote.text: Highlights for me were the rotating pyramid and the circular "scroller". A splendid soundtrack and gorgeous graphics also helps make this a remarkable release.

summary: A short C64 demo from Oxyron, coded by Axis and Graham with graphics by Yazoo and Oys, that came third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2009.
why: Sceners single out the fullscreen glenz vector, the mirrored vector and Oys' fullscreen graphics, along with Fanta's Rob Hubbard-style Light Force tune and Kasmo's end music. It is a compact production with a good flow.

quote.text: Wow, I really enjoyed this small piece, nice flow and great tune.

summary: Spirius is a ZX Spectrum demo by mayHem, released at Enlight 1997 where it was entered in the ZX Spectrum demo competition. Code is by Fyrex and Mouze, graphics by Amok and music by Demon.
why: A late-1990s Spectrum demo from the Enlight 1997 compo with a named crew covering code, graphics and music. It's worth a look for the Spectrum demo work of that period.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by mr.plop, dr.kvetch and sugar ass m.d., which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at DiHalt 2010.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at DiHalt 2010 and is well liked on Pouët.
highlights: digitised faces beside a big green logo
toilet picture with "I will wait for you at the end"

summary: Agenda's Atari XL/XE demo, which won the demo compo at Lost Party 2026. A large team effort with code by six coders including Ilmenit and xeen, graphics by four artists and music from AceMan, Caruso and stRing.
why: It took first place in the demo competition at Lost Party 2026, and it is a big production for the platform that needs a 320K machine.

summary: A 1987 Commodore 64 cracktro by Eagle Soft Incorporated for their release of Mini Putt, showing the group's eagle logo picture above a scrolling message.
why: A straightforward example of late-1980s C64 cracking-group intros, with a large hand-drawn eagle as the centrepiece.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by PG and MaPa, placed second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2010.
why: A second place in a 1K compo at Forever 2010, packing a scroller-themed show into a kilobyte on the Atari 8-bit.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Mortel and Arkos from 2005, with code, graphics and music by Targhan, Rainbird, Ramlaid and Grim, plus graphics from Beb and Supersly.
why: A joint effort from two CPC groups with a long list of graphics contributors, so the artwork is a large part of the draw. No compo placing is recorded.

summary: Hoaxers' C64 demo for a 512K REU, winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2015, built around large artwork by Joe and others, with a hires rotator, bitmap movers and scrollers.
why: Sceners single out Joe's huge, detailed graphics and a soundtrack that doesn't sound like typical SID fare. Even those wary of REU demos called it the best of its kind so far, with the hires rotator drawing particular praise.

quote.text: Hires rotator made my jaw stretch way too much

summary: A joint Commodore 64 demo by Atlantis and Padua that won the C64 demo compo at Transmission64 2021. Eight coders and several artists contributed to a run of effect and graphics parts themed around the Unity logo.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022. Sceners single out the smooth transitions and flow, the "Japanese sun" hi-res part, the fist part, and the music by Toggle and Mibri.

quote.text: High-spirited and well designed.. great flow and gfx.  Music could not be more suitable.

summary: SHAPE's C64 demo, the party version shown at Little Computer People 2009 where it placed 4th in the C64 demo compo. Code by 6R6, graphics by Archmage, music by GT. The finished Artillery 100% followed in 2010.
why: Sceners single out GT's soundtrack above all, along with the graphics, a Tetris-style screen wipe and a twister with fresh moves. Some noted the reused graphics but still rated it highly.

quote.text: Great graphics, great design and coding execution and a very awesome sound track!

summary: Mahoney's 4K intro for the C64, winner of the C64 4K Intro compo at Datastorm 2017. It runs in an endless loop and carries the message "I belong with those who don't belong".
why: Sceners were surprised by how much fits in 4K, including samples, a sprite mixer effect and glitchy, organic-looking visuals. They also called it original and emotional.

quote.text: One of the highlights from the entire compo. Very original and emotional, crammed down in just 4k.

summary: Tjoppen's 4K intro for the Atari 2600 VCS, which won the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2012.
why: A compo winner at Revision on one of the most constrained machines around, coded single-handedly by Tjoppen in 4K.

summary: Ikon Visual's comeback C64 demo, coded and drawn by Munkey with music by Olsen, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Syntax 2010 with filled 3D vector tunnels and shapes.
why: Sceners welcomed it as the return of Ikon Visual and a rare non-European release, singling out the speed of the effects, the music sync and the octagonal tunnel.

quote.text: Very fun and fast...the octagonal tunnel was a fun ride.

summary: Digital Reality's ZX Spectrum demo from 1997, which placed second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997. Code by Flying, Orion and Sauron, graphics by Radio Alex, Terror, Oz and Arty, music by Bloody Joseff.
why: A runner-up at Enlight 1997 from a large Digital Reality team, with credits that include 3D and video graphics by Oz alongside design by Arty.

summary: Oxyron and Crest's Commodore 128 demo, second in the Wild compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001. It comes in two halves, one on the C128's VDC chip and one on the VIC. This video shows the VIC part.
why: It is one of the very few real C128 demos. Sceners single out how colourful it is: Crossbow coaxed new colours out of the VIC with the C128's $d030 bit, and Graham's VDC work is called a milestone.

quote.text: Both VDC and VIC parts are very colourful and great to watch.

summary: Carillon's VIC-20 demo, coded and drawn by Heatbeat with music from Reed, Dizzy and Major Tom, which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2004.
why: A placing at Assembly's oldskool compo against bigger machines is a fair showing for an unexpanded VIC-20. Worth a look for anyone curious what the smallest Commodore could do in 2004.

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum 128K by Darklite and Offence, coded by Neon with graphics by Pal and music by Response. It placed third in the Oldskool Intro compo at Revision 2022.
why: A Revision podium finish in a mixed oldskool intro compo, squeezing a multicolour-mode show into 4K with Shrinkler compression.

summary: LaResistance's 64K intro for the Atari 8-bit, tagged as a remake of an Oxygene production. It came 2nd in the Atari 8-bit Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, with code by Pr0be and Fox, graphics by Ooz and music by Miker.

summary: wAMMA's 4K intro for the Atari VCS, released at Icons 2007 where it placed second in the demo competition. Credits are shown in vertical text between banded colour bars.
why: A second place in the Icons 2007 demo compo, and a 4K production on the Atari 2600 from a team of five, with code by visy, Ilmarque and tatu.

summary: A Commodore PET 8296 demo by Rabenauge, Plush and Crest, with code by Bodo, Krill and Insane. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2025.
why: Besides its Deadline win, it was nominated at The Meteoriks 2026 for both Best Oldschool Production and Outstanding Technical Achievement, which is rare recognition for a PET production.
