summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 64 DTV by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Benson and Peiselulli with music by Jeff, marking 25 years of Krawall. It came 3rd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2015.
why: One of the few releases for the C64 DTV joystick-computer, squeezed into 4096 bytes. Sceners praise its fast change of effects and call it worth adding to the flash memory.

quote.text: Great demo for DTV! Fast change of effects.

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo from Stream 2005, where it took second place in the demo compo. Code by BriteLite, music by Intensity.
why: Sceners single out the effects and Intensity's trance soundtrack. They also praise BriteLite's code, from the dithered flexible bar to a clever trick of fitting eight 2x2 pixels into a character.

quote.text: A great soundtrack, exactly my kind of thing. The demo is very good aswell, that dithered flexible bar is my favourite effect

summary: A C64 demo by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Street Tuff to a tune by Intensity. It placed third in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2011, up against PC and WebGL entries.
why: Made as a tribute to the late musician Arman (Intensity). Sceners praise the smooth precalculated animations packed into a one-filer, the transitions and the tight sync to the music.

quote.text: Amazingly smooth effects, and all this precalculated animation in a one-filer! I'm impressed. Good sync, too.

summary: New Generation and Zelax's joint Atari 8-bit demo that won the demo compo at Lost Party 2022, with code from five coders, graphics by Tiger and Blasph and music by Tatqoo, Miker and LiSU.
why: First place in the Lost Party 2022 demo competition, and a large collaboration between two groups pooling a big crew of coders, artists and musicians.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource and Logicoma, coded by Edhellon with music by H0ffman and Ferris's packer. It came second in the Oldskool Intro compo at Revision 2022.
why: A runner-up in a strong Revision oldskool intro compo, squeezing a run of colourful effects and a soundtrack into 4K on the often overlooked TED machine.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a 1930s gangster theme, winner of the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2025. Graphics by Talent, DeeKay and others, music by LMan, Psycho8580 and Magnar.
why: Sceners call it one of Censor's freshest and most stylish demos, singling out Talent's dithered graphics, the projector-noise film styling, new spins on Kefrens bars and Magnar's end tune. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2026.

quote.text: Everything in this demo is so damn slick, smooth, quick, flowy.  Looks effortless, even if I know there's shitloads of work behind it.

summary: Mahoney's demo for the Vectrex, the vector-display console, which won the demo compo at Isterparty 2014.
why: A compo winner on an unusual platform: the Vectrex draws everything as glowing vector lines rather than pixels, so it's a rare chance to see demo effects on a vector screen.

summary: Traction and Brainstorm's C64 one-file demo, coded by Preacher with graphics by Phase1 and music by Buzzer, placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Mostly black-and-white screens of text and images, opening with a Marshall McLuhan quote.
why: A first C64 demo from newcomers that sceners welcomed warmly, praising its atmosphere, Buzzer's tune and how fresh it looks despite a very limited colour palette. The source is available.
highlights: text hidden in ones and zeroes

quote.text: Also extremely cool how you stick to such a limited colour palette and still make all screens look fresh and appealing.

summary: Baze's 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro competition at Forever 2017.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2017, squeezing its full-screen visuals into just 1K of code.

summary: Co-Operation's demo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4, which won the demo competition at Árok 2006.
why: A compo winner on the Plus 4, a machine with a small but dedicated demo scene. It took first place in the Árok 2006 demo competition.

summary: Trilobit's Atari 2600 invitation intro for Outline 2009, coded with graphics and music by Ilmarque and text by visy. It won the Oldskool Intro compo at Numerica 2009.
why: A compo winner on one of the most restrictive platforms around, and an invitation from the VCS scene for the Outline party.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Speccy.pl and Lamers, tagged as a parody, that won the Combined Demo compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2013. Code by Tygrys, music by Ziutek on the AY, graphics by At0m.
why: It took first place in the combined demo competition at RetroKomp / Load Error 2013, and its parody tag points to a tongue-in-cheek take on the demo form.

summary: deMarche's demo for the ZX Sprinter, an enhanced Spectrum-compatible machine, which won the Combined Demo compo at Multimatograf 2025. Directed by Zeebr, with code by TmK, music by Nik-O and graphics by TmK, Rainman and Nodeus.
why: A first-place compo winner at Multimatograf 2025 and on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist, showing what the Sprinter hardware can do in a modern demo.

summary: Razor 1911's single-file C64 demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2015. Code and design by rez, graphics by Kenët and Made, music by Ziphoid. The title is 1911 written in hex.
why: Sceners call it stylish and colourful, and nearly all of them single out Ziphoid's tune. Kenët and Made drew all the graphics specifically for this demo.

quote.text: Stylish and colorful demo. Awesome music by Ziphoid <3

summary: M&M's Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at S:T Lars Meeting 2007, built around a missing-person story, with code by MagerValp and music by zabutom.
why: Sceners remember it for its dark, creepy mood and its tie to a real missing-person case, and many single out zabutom's Boards of Canada cover, "Turquoise Hexagon Sun".

quote.text: Got reminded of this one today. Had to comment again. This demo stays in your mind. So moody.

summary: Genesis Project's Atari VCS demo, coded by Shadow with graphics and music by Mermaid, placed third in the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A compo-placing demo on the Atari 2600, a machine with very little to work with, from a group better known on other platforms.

summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by Trefi with music by nq, which placed second in the 8-bit demo compo at Multimatograf 2015.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, with the whole visual side down to a single person, Trefi.

summary: Performers' three-disk-side C64 music demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2016. It runs as a themed show built around a concert, with music from LMan, Linus, Mixer and others, and graphics by DeeKay, Bitbreaker, Redcrab and Veto.
why: Sceners single out the greetings part, which several call their favourite demo part ever, along with the cute kid-voice credits and LMan's Thrust remix. Many treat it as a music demo to replay for nostalgia.

quote.text: It feels like the C64 all-stars with all those familiar C64 game icons in one place.

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo that streams full-motion video with sound from a DivIDE interface. It won the Realtime Wild Demo compo at Outline 2010, and this recording is live footage from the party screen.
why: A compo winner that shows the Spectrum playing streamed video from a DivIDE, something the stock machine was never built for. The subtitles promise full details, including the player code and converter utility.

summary: Elysium's folk-themed C64 demo, made for the folk theme at Xenium 2024 and winner of the C64 demo compo there, with graphics by Joe, Mikael, Jetboy and Valsary and music by Shogoon and Randall.
why: Sceners single out the soundtrack, especially Shogoon's leads that sound improvised on a real instrument, along with the graphics and its cheerful countryside mood. Nominated for Best Oldschool Production and Best Soundtrack at The Meteoriks 2025.

quote.text: Huge breeze of fresh vibes with one of the most gorgeous soundtracks I've ever heard <3

summary: Fairlight and Offence's C64 demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014, with code by Pantaloon, music by Danko and graphics by Pal and Louie64.
why: Sceners single out the smooth organic tunnel, the Mr Fisk sprite and the vertical scroller, and several compare its attribute scrollers and Danko's music to a Censor Design demo.

quote.text: Great release, love the credits and the organic moving tunnel stuff.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, coded by Tygrys with graphics from Darklight, CatMan, Slayer and At0m. It took second place in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2017.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2017 with a large graphics team behind it, and a good look at what Polish Spectrum sceners were doing in 2017. CatMan provides the music as well as graphics.

summary: Extend and Dekadence's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2009, built around a run of twister variants with graphics by Duce and fragment and music by Barracuda.
why: Sceners single out the twisters, especially a grey-shaded one whose lighting looks almost photorealistic, and Duce's design. The IDM-leaning soundtrack divided opinion, but some found it kept getting better on rewatching.

quote.text: I find myself watching this again six months later, surely the mark of a great demo.

summary: Dekadence's C64 4K intro, coded by BriteLite and SounDemoN with music by SounDemoN, which won the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2005.
why: A Breakpoint compo winner, reviewed in Nordic Scene Review 1. The one CSDb comment singles out the strange sounds SounDemoN gets out of the music.

quote.text: A demon of sound truly he is. Something seriously strange about the sounds in the music there is.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014, with code by Bob, Lavazza and CRT, graphics from a large team including Leon, and music by Magnar.
why: Sceners rate it well above its 5th place, singling out the serpent ribbon part, Magnar's soundtrack, Leon's hires art and heavy VSP trickery made for the original breadbox C64.

quote.text: The serpent ribbons are really cool, and so are many of the other parts.

summary: Radiant's one-file C64 demo, placed 4th in the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2026: a song about Pouet's forum drama, with the lyrics typed out over a cartoon pig on a field of trumpets.
why: Sceners love it as a song with lyrics, a joke about Pouet threads set to a SID tune and presented as a small demo. Jammer also pointed out a clever use of colours to mask sprites.

quote.text: What a lovely way to present a message, or tune for that matter! The world needs more sid's with lyrics!

summary: SerzhSoft's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum Tiny Intro (256b) compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions in the 256-byte category, one of the tightest size limits on the Spectrum.

summary: NOOP's first C64 demo, a humorous 'pimp my bento' story that won the Real Wild compo at Assembly 2015. A lunchbox gets assembled ingredient by ingredient, ending with portraits of the crew.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a fresh, funny debut, praising its cartoonish graphics, fun texts and the unexpected tentacle. It was nominated for New Talent at The Meteoriks 2016.

quote.text: A good mixture of 1985 graphics, a weird but fresh and very enjoyable story, some nice effects and some nice humor.

summary: Atari 2600 demo by Digital Sounds System, coded by Tjoppen with music by Knoeki, which came 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2012.
why: A sample-playback showcase on the VCS: the on-screen text claims 1 min 10 sec of 5-bit PCM at 3 kHz squeezed into 32 KiB, with a podium place at Stream 2012.

summary: Insane is a 1997 ZX Spectrum 48K demo by 3SC, with code by Baze and Astex and graphics and music by Baze, using AY sound. It's tagged as running on the TK90X, the Brazilian Spectrum clone.
why: An early demo from 3SC, with Baze handling code, graphics and music himself. It's well liked on Pouët, with no thumbs down.

summary: Skrju's monochrome ZX Spectrum demo, winner of the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2007, with graphics by tanya_2308, music by nq and code by sq.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2007, and it's a good example of a demo built on a mood and a strict monochrome look rather than on effects.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that came second in the demo compo at Floppy 2003, with code by Hollowman, graphics by Hollowman and Tempest, and music by Goto80.
why: Sceners call it stylish and modern, single out Goto80's music and its neat screens, and JackAsser credits it with drawing him into C64 coding.

quote.text: I just love this demo. :) It sucked me in to C64 coding.

summary: Nuance's Vectrex demo, coded by Nitro, which won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012. Wireframe vector graphics glow on the console's built-in vector screen.
why: A compo winner on a rarely used platform, and a chance to see demo effects drawn on the Vectrex's vector display instead of a raster screen.

summary: Dual Crew's C64 demo on a white background, coded by Zaz with music by Jan Harries, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners single out the colour-filled hires vectors, including an Elite Thargoid and a final object in six colours with black outlines, along with the clean design and Jan Harries' tune.

quote.text: These color-filled hires vectors are visually the tastiest I've ever seen. I love the font animation too.

summary: An invitation demo for the NOVA online party by Bitshifters and Torment for the BBC Master, which placed second in the Demo compo at Outline Online 2020.
why: A runner-up in the Outline Online 2020 demo compo, coded by Henley and Kieran with music by Rhino. It carries an epilepsy warning, so expect flashing visuals.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation demo by Lamers for Silly Venture 2018, with code by MKM and Szeryf, music by XTD and graphics by Moonwalker. It placed 8th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018.
why: A party invitation that went on to compete at Revision, made by a team of Polish Atari regulars. Worth a look for how it promotes the Silly Venture party through big chunky text and animation.

summary: Gods of the Universe's two-disk-side demo for the Commodore Plus/4, which won the demo compo at Árok 2018. Code by Lavina and Ati, graphics by Harry, Shadow and DLST, music by Celticdesign.
why: A first-place demo from Árok, the Hungarian party, and a substantial two-disk-side production for the Plus/4, with three graphicians credited.
highlights: waving logo over a dotted backdrop

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2019, opening with Dane's huge multiscreen ring picture before a run of scrollers, zoomers and an Amiga-ball vector.
why: Sceners single out Dane's spiralling intro picture, the rotating scroller and the colourful zoom scroller, calling it a worthy winner packed with top-notch routines, even if some found it short.

quote.text: The intro is awe-inspiring, setting the stage for an onslaught of awesome complicated routines.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper, that came third in the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012.
why: A podium finish in a mixed low-end compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2012, where it was placed against prods from other 8-bit machines.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010, with graphics by Louie64, code by Abaddon and Pantaloon, and a zabutom remix of a Dubmood tune.
why: Sceners praise Louie64's graphics, especially the suited skeleton man, along with the stylish design, the music and the isometric rising and falling pillars. Several welcomed it as a strong debut from Fairlight's PC demo section.

quote.text: the pace and the sync to the music is great, not to speak of that skeleton. Also love the overall design! outstanding demo!!

summary: A joint Atari XL/XE demo by New Generation and Zelax that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 WE. It needs 1MB of RAM and features shaded 3D objects.
why: It was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, which the Demozoo notes call a world first for an Atari 8-bit production.

summary: Extend's two-disk-side C64 demo, crashed on the compo machine at Zoo 2024 and then released in final form at Transmission64 2024, where it won the demo compo. It is built around an animation player with heavy VHS-style video distortion and all-border pictures.
why: Nominated for Best Visuals at The Meteoriks 2025. Sceners call it video art rather than a conventional demo and praise how the visuals react to the sound, though some find it repetitive over its length.

quote.text: This is just stunning both visually and aurally (and how the visuals react to sound). Beyond C64 limits. My favourite C64 demo by far from this day on.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, released at Assembly 2014 where it placed third in the Real Wild Demo competition.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's Real Wild compo for the unexpanded-looking VIC-20 is a fair recommendation on its own. The fact sheet holds little more, so expect a short, curious watch.

summary: Five Finger Punch's Atari VCS demo, which won the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2023, with code by Vilcans, Morbid and Imodium, graphics by Corel and music by Triace.
why: A compo winner at Gerp 2023 that was put on the Meteoriks watchlist for 2024, which makes it one of the year's notable releases on the Atari 2600.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Satori, with code and music by Zden and graphics by BexBorder. It placed second in the Oldschool Intro compo at Riverwash 2018.
why: A compo-placed 4K intro on the Atari 2600, with its soundtrack made in TIA Tracker, the VCS's own music tool.

summary: Oof Heads' Atari 8-bit demo for the 130XE, coded by MKM with graphics by Odyniec1 and music by 505. It came second in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k25 WE.
why: A runner-up at the main Atari 8-bit party of 2025, and it was put on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.

summary: Oxyron's one-file C64 demo marking the group's twentieth anniversary, placed 2nd in the demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2011: a big Yazoo logo over a zooming scroller carrying greetings texts from the members.
why: Sceners praise Axis's zoom scroller, which casts a shadow, something one commenter couldn't recall seeing before, along with Fanta's Stevie Wonder cover and Yazoo's logo.

quote.text: Also very nice version of the ZoomScroller in here. You know how to do it!

summary: A 1K musicdisk for the Commodore 64 by Orb, coded and scored by 4mat: four tunes packed into a kilobyte, cycled with the space bar, with a minimal display of coloured bars and a scrolling label.
why: Sceners were struck by how listenable and well composed four tunes could be in 944 bytes, and several singled out the second tune. It's a good example of 4mat's size-limited music work.

quote.text: 4 tunes, 944 bytes? amazingly good quality of sound and composition.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Kitten Rescuers, SinDiKat and Invaders that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023, with code from Baze, Busy, mborik, Mike, Omega and Ped and music by Aki.
why: A first place at Forever 2023 from a large Slovak team effort, and its source has been made available.

summary: Arkos's two-disk-side Amstrad CPC demo from 2004, coded by Targhan (who also did the music and 3D graphics) with 2D graphics by Grim. It includes a pre-rendered 3D movie played back in blocky low-resolution colour.
why: A sizeable CPC production spread over two disk sides, mostly the work of one person. The on-screen text explains how the 2,400-frame movie was modelled on PC and squeezed in with a home-made delta RLE scheme.

summary: Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo that won the demo compo at ASCii 2004, with code and concept by Alff and music by Miguel.
why: A compo winner at ASCii 2004, and a demo built around a message rather than a showcase of routines, as its title and credited concept suggest.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo credited to Peppa Pig, with graphics by DMan, music by Nik-O and code and text by Kowalski. It won the 8Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2016 and stars the cartoon pig herself.
why: It took first place in the 8-bit demo competition at Multimatograf 2016. It's also a Spectrum demo built around multicolour mode, which gives finer colour detail than the stock attribute grid allows.
highlights: "i will break all that you can enhance"

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2015, with code from Noby, mborik, Busy, Mike and Omega and music by Aki.
why: A first place at Forever 2015 from a large Slovak-Czech team pooling several well-known Spectrum coders.

summary: Krap Gang's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2010, coded by Omega and Poke with graphics by Omega and z00m.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2010 that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode, with an Atari ST tune by Big Alec converted by Oedipus.

summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS demo, coded by visy and Ilmarque with graphics and music by Ilmarque, which came second in the demo compo at Stream 2007.
why: A second place at Stream 2007 for a demo on the Atari 2600, one of the most restrictive machines in the scene, with design and direction by visy.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Hacker VBI (code) and Nik-O (music), placed 4th in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2014. It is a political piece built around the Ukrainian flag and the EU circle of stars.
why: A small, openly political prod from 2014, tagged with a Ukraine theme, that took fourth place in Sundown's old school demo compo.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation to Isterparty 2011, with code, graphics and music by Mermaid and extra art by hedning and Uka: a series of hires pictures and animations, including an Easter bunny and a portrait of an old hedning.
why: Sceners praise the hires graphics and animations, singling out the picture of the old man, and note how much effort went into an invite for such a small party. Later credited as the spark for what became Gubbdata.

quote.text:
Lovely production, such an effort for such a little party :)

I like the rounded edges and supreme hires usage.

summary: Agenda's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Code by xeen, graphics by Ooz and Piesiu, music by stRing.
why: It took first place in its category at Silly Venture 2k14, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: wAMMA's 4K intro for the Atari VCS, coded by visy and Ilmarque, which placed 5th in the Allround Real Time compo at Outline 2007.
why: A rare 4K demoscene prod on the Atari 2600, with code, graphics and music by Ilmarque on top of visy's engine.

summary: Glance's C64 demo, the finished 100% version of Protogeo released on the last day of 2020, nearly a decade after the 80% version shown at X. It fits on one disk side and ends on a filled vector cube.
why: Sceners single out the closing cube, a 50fps filled vector with fully realtime rotation, long thought out of reach on the C64, along with the chunky effects, cubist artwork and a melancholic soundtrack that holds the whole demo together.

quote.text: Love that real time cube, and all those any pixel any colour parts.  Excellent soundtrack and cubist artwork, too.

summary: Section 31's three-disk-side trackmo for the Commodore Plus/4, which won the demo compo at Árok 2026. Code by Lavina, BSZ, Larry, Mad, Bubis and Murphy, graphics by DLST, Jeva, Harry and Lavina, music by Celticdesign.
why: A first-place compo winner and a large team effort spread over three disk sides. It shows how far the Plus/4 scene pushes the machine, with SID-cart music alongside the TED.

summary: Xenon's C64 demo that won the demo compo at X 2000, with code by WVL and Megabrain, graphics by Oxbow and Spectator, a guest picture by Genius and music by Arman.
why: Sceners praise its flow: seamless, break-less changes between parts and effects synchronised with the music. The scramble upscroller and the moonlit logo reflection get singled out.

quote.text: the upscrambler is one of the most brilliant ideas for a scroller since the DYCP. kudos.

summary: Amstrad CPC demo by Impact, Praline and GPA that won the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2018. Code by AST, graphics by Barjack and music by Tom&Jerry.
why: A first-place winner at ReSeT 2018, with Barjack's detailed pixel art providing the setting for the demo's scrollers.

summary: Desire's 128K Atari XL/XE demo, the second Arsantica, shown at Silly Venture 2k14: a run of effects parts between large hand-drawn pictures, with code by Heaven, Popmilo and Oswald and music by Triace.
why: The coder's notes list a dense set of effects on a stock 130XE: a fractal flight with Koronis Rift-style depth shading, a shaded texture-mapped planet, a 16-shade rotozoomer and realtime radial blur, most aimed at 50 fps.

summary: Camelot's 256-byte Commodore 64 intro, released on Christmas Eve 2013, which won the Mixed category at the Christmas Fun Competition 2013.
why: A compo winner squeezed into 256 bytes, and a seasonal one at that, from a long-running C64 group.

summary: A 16K intro for the ZX Spectrum 128 by Joker, coded and drawn by Dalthon with music by Pator and Zlew. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Xenium 2021.
why: It took first place in Xenium 2021's Oldschool Demo compo, competing as a 16K intro packed with Shrinkler against full-size entries.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2005, with code and graphics by HCL, more graphics by Jailbird and music by Dane.
why: A lighter-hearted Booze release that sceners rate for its hard-coded parts, Jailbird's pictures and Dane's music. One commenter lists a sprite zoomer over a bitmap among its world-firsts.

quote.text: Hard coded parts with delightful music and gfx.

summary: Offence's 4K intro for the Commodore 64, with code, graphics and music all by Kribust: chunky blocky patterns, scrolling binary digits and a wobbling bar, driven by a hard electronic soundtrack.
why: Sceners call it raw and addictive, praising the banging soundtrack, synced graphics and how long it keeps going without looping. Several admit they left it running for half an hour.

quote.text: This feels like a hammer to the head, but in the most refreshing way possible.

summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2014.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2014, and tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode for finer colour detail than the stock attribute grid allows.

summary: A short Booze Design demo for the C64, put together largely at Árok 2007 by HCL, with music by Dane and Mitch. It took second place in the demo compo there.
why: Sceners single out the opening double stretcher (a two-layer FPD), which many found beautiful, plus the rotating pig. The common complaint is that it's over too quickly.

quote.text: the double fpd looks so beautiful to me I almost cried :) typical awesomeness from HCL.

summary: Invaders' ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by Omega with music by Lamer Pinky, that won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2021. It tells a story set in space.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2021 and a story-led Spectrum demo, with Omega credited for the story as well as code and graphics.

summary: Genesis Project's pirate-themed C64 demo on three disk sides, placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at X 2018. Graphics by Facet, Razorback, Raistlin, hedning and others, with music by Stinsen, Steel and MCH.
why: Sceners single out the sheer amount of pixel work and the coherent pirate theme and flow, and many felt it would have won at most other parties against a less fierce field.
highlights: circle scroller on the light picture

quote.text: Absolutely love this. More than anything is the coherent design / theme and flow. Very well organised and orchestrated <3

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and scored by Gasman, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019. Tagged as karaoke, with on-screen lyrics and messages such as greetings from the UK scene.
why: A runner-up at Revision's Oldskool Demo compo, and a rare Spectrum karaoke demo, with Gasman handling both code and music.

summary: An early Atari 8-bit demo from 1984 by Home Entertainment Centre, credited as a VLM demo. It opens with a text screen announcing that it is being run live, then moves on to coloured symmetrical patterns.
why: A very early piece of Atari 8-bit demo history from 1984. It is worth a look as a record of how computer demonstrations looked before the demoscene's conventions had settled.

summary: Youth Uprising's Game Boy demo, coded and scored by Ferris with graphics by Blake Ridgewell. It placed 2nd in the Combined Demo compo at Pixel Jam 2012.
why: A second place at Pixel Jam 2012 with a strong graphics credit behind it. It's a 4-megabit cartridge production that runs in an endless loop.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by LaResistance, coded by Probe with music by Born, which placed second in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, that packs its show into a small size limit. The video title gives it as 12K.

summary: A multi-platform Wild compo entry by Moonbase Allstars, running across C64, Linux, MS-DOS and a stack of Nintendo machines from GBC to GameCube, edited together as a video. It placed 3rd in Wild at Revision 2024.
why: Won Outstanding Concept at The Meteoriks 2025, recognised for its idea of turning the old platform wars into a single piece spread over many machines. The source is available.

summary: Agenda's Atari 8-bit demo that came second in the demo compo at Lost Party 2022, with code by tr1x, Koala and xeen, graphics by Piesiu, Ripek and Raphis, and music by Caruso and stRing.
why: A runner-up at Lost Party 2022 from a large Agenda team, with three graphicians credited, so the pictures carry much of the show.
highlights: rainy alley scene with a dog

summary: Lamers' Atari XL/XE demo, second in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code by MKM, Ajcek and Szeryf, graphics by Odyn1ec, Blasph and At0m, and music by VLX.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main party for Atari 8-bit demos, from a large team of coders and graphicians.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Computer Crossroads 1993, with code by Bob, Staiger and Guran, graphics by Dragon and music by Swallow and Danko.
why: Sceners recall it blowing the TCC'93 crowd away and call it the peak of Censor Design's career, their first big compo win after many second and third places. Comments single out its music and effects.

quote.text: This demo blew us all away at the TCC'93 party in Gothenburg.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by g0blinish, with music by Fatal Snipe, that came second in the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2017.
why: A podium finish at Demosplash 2017 for a one-coder Spectrum production. It's tagged as a sequel, so it continues an earlier g0blinish release.
highlights: triangle-tiled shapes in cyan, magenta, yellow

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2006, shown here running on a real Game Boy Color. Code by Maitotuote, graphics by Äkknäkk and Lesboduo.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's oldskool compo for a handheld demo, with two graphicians credited and a 1 Mbit cartridge to fill.
highlights: filmed on real Game Boy Color

summary: Debris is a 40k intro for the Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo, released in August 2022, with code by Toms, music by Tom et Jerry and graphics by Toxic.
why: A recent CPC intro from a small team. There are no compo results or comments to go on, but it drew a warm reception on Pouët.

summary: Nuance's first C64 demo, a one-file dentro that won the Combined Low-End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2011. Code by Bitbreaker, music by Intensity, with realtime hires filled vectors, a twister, a spinning globe and packed animations.
why: Sceners single out how much content is squeezed into a single file, the realtime hires vector routine and the twister. Several also note its cheeky juggling animation, hence the nsfw tag.

quote.text: I would go far to say that it is probably the best one filer I have seen with so much content.

summary: A C64 demo by Horizon, Instinct and Triad that won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2005, with code by Iopop, Jackasser and Pernod, music by Dalezy and ne7, and graphics by Twoflower.
why: Sceners praise its clean, minimal, coder-led style: the Kefrens-style ice canyon, the line-crunched colour-cycling circles, a moving censor effect and streamed vector animations. Several single out the closing 'The End' part.

quote.text: the kefrens-style canyon is amazing! and the linecrunched color cycle circles are crazy, you get a really weird feeling watching them.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo, coded by sq, Kowalski and psndcj with music by Nik-O and graphics by Diver. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2025.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2025 that went on to be nominated for Best Demo in the GOTY ZX Spectrum Awards 2025, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by Tygrys with graphics by Slayer and CatMan and music by Ziutek. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: A Polish group's entry that held its own in Revision's Oldskool Demo compo and later turned up again at Decrunch 2015, placing 4th in the Twoje Stare Demo compo.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by sibKrew, coded by rook and wbcbz7 with graphics by Robat and music by Nik-O. It placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A podium finish at CAFe 2019 for a demo built on the Spectrum's multicolour mode, with a cast of cartoon characters asking whether the scene can be saved.

summary: A 4K intro for the C64 by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Peiselulli, Spider Jerusalem and Street Tuff, with music by Street Tuff. It won the Oldskool intro compo at Revision 2013.
why: Sceners can't believe how much fits into 4K: a smooth plasma, sprite stretchers, effects running into the borders and a soundtrack they rate highly. Several say it looks like a whole demo.

quote.text: I still can't believe that all this fits into 4k. I love the supersmooth plasma, the programmed sound and these all border effects.

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2004, with code and graphics by BriteLite, 2D and 3D graphics by fragment, music by Agemixer and a loader by SounDemoN.
why: Sceners praised its polish, Agemixer's soundtrack and its timing and flow. Some called it Dekadence's most enjoyable demo so far, though a few found the animations too precalculated.

quote.text: Dekadence's most enjoyable demo (so far) I think. Good stuff.

summary: PRECALCULATED is a ZX Spectrum demo by Skrju that came second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Russian-speaking parties for Spectrum work, puts it among the stronger Spectrum demos of 2015.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo that came second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011: a sung Swedish cover tune with the lyrics drawn on screen in big decaying letters, ending with a rotating Android logo.
why: Sceners single out the technical feat of fitting minutes of real-time vocoded vocals into the C64 alongside a soundtrack, plus the 1984 theme. Some found it lo-fi, but many call it one of Mahoney's most inspiring experiments.

quote.text: After this was shown at the party i actually felt no need to watch any of the other contributions.

summary: Benediction's 64K intro for the Amstrad Plus, coded by Eliot with graphics by Pandafox and music by Brink. It placed 8th in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2016.
why: A Plus-only production from an established CPC group, with a dedicated pixel artist and composer on board. No comments yet, so the compo entry and credits are what there is to go on.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that won the Low End 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2017 Lite: a Christmas tree drawn from coloured dots.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017 Lite, showing how much seasonal charm fits into 256 bytes on the Spectrum.

summary: lft's solo C64 demo, with code, graphics and music all by lft, placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013. It runs on lft's own disk loader.
why: Sceners praise its flow and soundtrack, and coders were struck by its loader: Krill called fully decoding a GCR disk block on the fly one of the holy grails of C64 coding, achieved here.

quote.text: I love the this demo , flows very well , good design and great effects , this is why demos are so cool.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 demo, a tribute to Last Ninja 3 and a farewell to the Truckstop party venue, which won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2019. Music by Fegolhuzz and Wiklund, graphics by The Sarge.
why: Sceners single out The Sarge's graphics and natural-looking animation, the long credits intro with its lightning effect, and the twister scroller near the end. Even people who usually dislike animation-based demos praise it.

quote.text: I usually don't like animation-based demos, but this one is just so beautiful! Love it!

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2017.
why: A compo winner in one of the scene's tightest size limits, taking first place in DiHalt 2017's low-end 256-byte category.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo that won the 8bit Demo compo at Motorola Inside 2006, filmed here running on an original DMG-001 handheld.
why: A compo winner on the original Game Boy, and a Jumalauta production with a Finnish group's offbeat credits list. Seeing it captured on real hardware shows what the stock screen actually looks like.

summary: Logon System's 1995 Amstrad CPC intro previewing a Shadow Of The Beast conversion: a multi-layered scrolling landscape of clouds, snowy peaks, grass and a stone wall behind a "press fire to play" prompt.
why: Its video is titled as a showcase of parallax scrolling on the CPC, the effect the Amiga original was known for, attempted here on 8-bit hardware.

summary: Fairlight's C64 concept demo by Hollowman, with music by Goto80, that won the demo compo at Floppy 2002: a story told through close-up digitised-style portraits and lines of text.
why: Sceners call it a rare true concept demo, valued for its atmosphere, flow and message rather than effects, and for Goto80's unusual soundtrack that steps away from traditional SID music.

quote.text: Too few people on the scene knows how to do concept demos. True art among tech demos...

summary: Mills' Game Boy Color demo from 2018, with colourful hand-drawn pictures including Homer Simpson eating a doughnut, a smiling Game Boy and a pink "Cute Demo" title screen.
why: A cheerful Game Boy Color demo whose source code is available, with a Simpsons theme running through it.

summary: Megacode's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997, with code and rendered textures by Exploder and music by Visual.
why: A podium finish at Enlight 1997, one of the big Russian Spectrum parties, and it makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: Rabenauge and Plush's Commodore PET demo, shown on a CBM 8296 in the video, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2022. Code by Bodo, Krill, Utz and Zed Yago, graphics by Titus, music by Utz.
why: It won its compo at Deadline 2022 and was nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, a rare honour for a PET production.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo that plays an entire compressed vocal sample (Suzanne Vega's "Tom's Diner") through the SID, with on-screen lyrics and a list of the techniques used. Placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners were amazed that a two-minute song could be crammed into a C64 and played back, praising the PC-side encoding and how all three SID voices help rebuild the sample. Krill said it "really used all the tricks in the book".

quote.text: What?! An entire 2-minute song sampled and crammed into this demo?! This is just... awesome!

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Ate Arse, with code and graphics by Icabod and evilpaul and music by Gasman. It came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006.
why: A placing at Sundown 2006 from a small crew that includes Gasman on music, which makes it a reasonable pick for anyone exploring mid-2000s Spectrum demos.

summary: Overlanders' 2002 Amstrad CPC demo, with code by Madram and Shap, graphics by Beb and music by Shap.
why: A well-liked Overlanders release from the CPC scene of the early 2000s, made by a small team who split the code, graphics and music between them.

summary: A 16K Atari 8-bit intro by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper with music by 505, a font by Ooz and text by Bugger. It placed 5th in the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A compact Silly Venture 2012 compo entry from a small crew that is well liked on Pouët, with credits from several known Atari names.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Baze that won the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2023.
why: Besides its Lovebyte win, it took the Oldschool category at The Nano Awards 2024, a sign of how highly it is rated among size-coded prods.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo that won the demo compo at ReSeT (.fr) 2011, with code by Krusty, graphics by Beb and Barjack, and music by McKlain, Tao and Count Zero.
why: It took first place in the demo competition at ReSeT 2011, and its source code has been made available.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2020: moody winter and nature scenes in multicolour char mode and bitmap, with layered scrollers, snow and northern lights, and music by Dane.
why: Sceners single out the layered scrollers, the aurora effect and the char-mode pictures, and praise how code, graphics and music blend into one atmosphere. Several call it among the most beautiful or touching C64 demos.

quote.text: Thank you guys for this piece of art where everything blends perfectly – code, design, music.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by JTZ (code and graphics) with music by Skyrunner, placed 2nd in the Oldskool 4k compo at Revision 2015.
why: A runner-up at Revision's Oldskool 4k compo, squeezed into the 2600's tiny memory. It's worth a look to see what fits in 4K on one of the most limited machines around.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Rush and Dream Makers Software that placed second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Enlight 1996, with code from Baca, Elf, M. Coder, Evolver and Imp.
why: A runner-up at Enlight 1996, it is a mid-90s Spectrum group production. Evolver and Imp shared the music as well as the code.

summary: Rabenauge's 512-byte Vectrex intro, coded by Bodo with music by Okeanos, which won the 512B intro compo at Nordlicht 2019. It's an invitation to the Deadline 2019 party in Berlin.
why: A compo-winning sizecoded intro on the Vectrex's vector display, a rare platform for party invitations, squeezing music and visuals into 512 bytes.

summary: Altair's Atari 2600 demo that won the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code and graphics by mgo, KK and Traq and music by KK based on an original tune by Malfunction.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture, one of the main Atari parties, and tagged for its dance animations, a lot to get out of the VCS's tiny hardware.

summary: Fossil's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2019, with code by Knut, music by Linus and graphics by Archmage, ending in a large diagonal multicolour scroller.
why: Sceners single out the tight sync between the opening and Linus's funky, filter-heavy tune, and above all the wobbly tilted end scroller, which several call a fresh idea that shows how far a new twist can go.

quote.text: This is exactly how to do a demo! Beautiful, impressive and with tight sync to a hell of a tune.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2003, with code and graphics by AEG and music by SoNiC.
why: Welcomed as AEG's return. Sceners single out the moving tunnel, the polar plasma behind a bitmap and the big morphing vectors, though some found much of it familiar AEG territory.

quote.text: Many nice effects here, some are upgrades of old ones, like the moving tunnel (haven't seen that before), polar plasma behind bitmap (my favorite!), nice and big morphing vectors, textured floors

summary: Bandwagon's MSX demo, coded by Neckfreak with music by Gspot and Neckfreak and graphics by Mermaid. It placed 11th in the Wild Demo compo at Assembly 2000.
why: A rare MSX entry at one of the biggest PC-dominated parties, worth a look for Mermaid's graphics and as a sample of turn-of-the-millennium MSX demo work.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Floppy 2003, coded by HCL with music by GRG. It has a deliberately glitchy, trashy look and ends in an endless loop.
why: Sceners call it one of the best C64 demos of the 2000s and an early post-modern turn for the scene, praising how GRG's music and the experimental visuals work together.

quote.text: The combination of audio/visual work really makes this into something extraordinary.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by PG (graphics and music) and MaPa (idea and code), which came second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2009.
why: A second place at Forever in the 1K category, with music squeezed into the same kilobyte as the visuals.

summary: Extend's C64 demo from Zoo 2022, where it placed 4th in the demo compo: glitchy PETSCII animation set to a soundtrack by Goto80 and Van Damme.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2023. Sceners single out the glitch aesthetic, the pace and the way music and visuals meld, with several who dislike PETSCII calling it their compo favourite.

quote.text: Is it possible for a demo to be fresh and dirty at the same time? Yes it is.

summary: Dekadence's VIC-20 demo from 2003, coded by BriteLite and SounDemoN with music by SounDemoN and graphics by Phase1. It placed second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2003.
why: A second place against other oldskool machines at Assembly is a strong showing for the modest VIC-20, and it's a good example of what Dekadence got out of the machine.

summary: 3SC's ZX Spectrum demo with AY music, released in August 1998 and winner of the demo competition at Doxycon 1998.
why: It took first place in the demo compo at Doxycon 1998, and it is tagged as running on a stock 48K Spectrum as well as the TK90X clone.

summary: Reflex's two-disk-side C64 demo, shown here as the 66% party version that came 4th in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1997. The finished Breitbandkatze 100% followed in January 1998.
why: A placing at The Party 1997 with a large crew of coders and graphicians behind it. Demozoo notes this unfinished version crashes after its "message to AEG" 3D wireframe part, so the video is the easy way to see it.

summary: Aspekt's Commodore 64 demo, coded and scored by Ruuvari, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2005.
why: A runner-up at Assembly 2005's oldskool compo and a one-person production, with Ruuvari credited for both code and music.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by g0blinish, with music by stRing, that placed second in the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k14.
why: A runner-up in its Silly Venture compo, and its source code has been released, so it's a useful one for anyone wanting to see how a small Atari intro is put together.

summary: Slight's 1994 Atari 8-bit demo, placed third in the demo compo at Shadows Copy Party 1994, with code by Rzóg, Soused Teat and Seban and music from four contributors.
why: A placing early-nineties Atari 8-bit group demo with a large crew, and the video is a 50Hz capture from real hardware uploaded by Seban himself.

summary: Togyaf's ZX Spectrum demo for DiHalt 2012, where it came second in the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo. Graphics and concept are by Sand and Robat, with music from guest artist nq of Skrju.
why: A second place in a combined 8-bit compo at DiHalt, made with a guest soundtrack from nq. It is a good pick if you like hand-drawn Spectrum pictures.

summary: Amstrad CPC demo by Benediction and Brainstorm, with code by Krusty, music by Ultrasyd and graphics by Voxfreax. It placed 9th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2011.
why: A real-machine capture of a CPC demo shown at Evoke 2011, from a small three-person team. Its source code has been made available.

summary: Hollowman's C64 demo for Fairlight, with music by Goto80 and a charset by Wiggen, that placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at X 2008: a slow, odd piece of scene poetry built around a crying baby.
why: Sceners single it out as personal, narrative-driven work that stands apart from the effect-heavy entries it competed against, praising the visuals, the storytelling and Goto80's fitting soundtrack.

quote.text: I really adore the narrative, the visuals and the music.

summary: Quiss's C64 4K intro, released by Reflex, that won the 4K intro compo at X 2024. It has code and music by Quiss, graphics by Seytan and directory art by Felidae.
why: Sceners call it the code highlight of X 2024 and can't work out how it fits in 4K. They single out the smooth 3D object and a fast, glitch-free colourful distorter, or 'colorcycler'.

quote.text: the 3d stuff is extremely smooth and the movements get extra interesting because of how the lines twist and turn as the object rotate, combined with the resizing of the corner spheres.

summary: A big collaborative Commodore Plus/4 demo from eleven groups, including Gods of the Universe, Exceed, Synergy and Absence, released at Árok 2024, where it won the demo compo.
why: An Árok 2024 demo compo winner that brought together a long list of Plus/4 coders, artists and musicians, and it made the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist.

summary: Chronic's single-screen C64 demo from January 2007, aimed at Timbaland: a picture of him holding a C64 over rasterbars, with a scroller running along the bottom.
why: A scene response to Timbaland's use of a C64 tune without credit. Sceners praised the music and its message, and DeeKay noted the story had reached MTV news.

quote.text: Thumbs up for this little Demo, been waiting for sth like this!

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro with sound by bfox that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2021.
why: A compo winner that was also nominated for Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022, packing visuals and sound into 256 bytes.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro with sound by superogue of Marquee Design, winner of the 256b retro/alternative intro compo at Flashparty 2020.
why: Took first place at Flashparty 2020 and was nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021. A making-of write-up is available on the Marquee Design site.

summary: Taquart's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Jaskier with music by Greg and graphics by BeWu. It placed 4th in the demo compo at QuaST 2004.
why: A mid-2000s Atari 8-bit demo from Taquart that held its own in the QuaST 2004 demo competition, with a credited three-person team covering code, music and graphics.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo and invitation that came second in the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2016, with code by HCL, Jackasser and Ruk, graphics by Dane and Valsary, and music by RaveGuru.
why: Sceners singled out the particle effects, shadebobs, fast plotting and 3D parts, with several saying it felt like an early-90s PC demo. RaveGuru's music and Dane's hand-repixelled portraits of old men also drew praise.
highlights: waving sprite font in the border

quote.text: Felt like I was watching an PC-Dos demo from 1992. Good work! Really like the particle-thingy and also doing the waving font-sprites in the border are nice.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Music2Eye and Praline, released in September 2018, with code, music and concept by Steph and colours by Barjack.
why: A size-limited CPC production from 2018 that packs its own code and soundtrack into 4KB. No compo placing is recorded, so it stands on its own merits.

summary: Traktor's MSX demo from Breakpoint 2007, where it placed 11th in the Console/Real Wild compo. Code by Esau and Bore, with Esau also doing the graphics and music.
why: A rare MSX entry at Breakpoint from the Swedish group Traktor, with one member handling code, graphics and music.

summary: A C64 demo by Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence made from parts left out of their Datastorm 2017 demo, released outside any compo with music by Stein Pedersen and Scarzix.
why: Sceners were surprised that leftovers could be this strong, singling out the music, especially the cute end tune and its Flåklypa Grand Prix ending, plus the colour cycling and the counting-sheep part.

quote.text: oh my fucking god. this is Leftovers? seriously???!  what incredible creation! the end music is just above perfection.

summary: Arsenic's horror-themed C64 demo, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at X 2010, with code by Axis and Mactron, graphics by Yazoo, Sphinx and others, and music by Fanta.
why: Sceners praise its coherent design and the way its movie-style sequencing follows Fanta's tune, with standout 3D routines and Yazoo's graphics. Several felt it deserved a top-three spot.

quote.text: I especially like the movie-style sequencing in synch with the music and all the nifty 3D parts.

summary: Noice's VIC-20 demo for a machine with a 16K RAM expansion, winner of the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2008. Code by Shadow with help from Marko Mäkelä, Pasi Ojala and Magnus Lind, graphics by Shadow and Flood, and music by 4-Mat.
why: It beat the other entries in Sundown 2008's open oldschool demo compo, a rare VIC-20 win against other platforms. The credits bring together several well-known VIC-20 coders.
highlights: spinning white shapes between colour bars

summary: Blast!'s Sega Master System demo, coded with music by GliGli and graphics by Ced2911, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2017.
why: A compo winner on a platform that rarely gets demos, taking first place in the oldschool competition at VIP 2017.

summary: Digital Reality's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that came 2nd in the demo compo at Funtop 1998. This video, titled as a 2020 edition, sets the party and final versions side by side.
why: A podium finish at Funtop 1998, and a chance to compare how the demo changed between the party release and the final version.
highlights: dithered picture of child and sun
party and final versions side by side

summary: Fairlight's zombie-themed C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Floppy 2004, with code by Hollowman and Puterman and music from Jeff, Maktone and Dane.
why: Sceners praise its consistent horror atmosphere and spooky music, the twisters over rasters, and a closing filled-vector part with an unusual number of objects and camera work.

quote.text: Those rasters with twisters are something really special; awesome stuff. That last vector part is great.

summary: Overlanders' Amstrad CPC demo from 2015, with code by Candy and Camillo, graphics by Beb, and music from Shap, Targhan and Tom&Jerry across its pre-intro, intro and main parts.
why: A multi-part demo from a long-running CPC group, with three musicians each scoring a different section and Madram supplying the music player.

summary: Shiru's New Year intro for the NES, winner of the New Year's Intro compo at DiHalt 2020 Lite. It moves through seasonal scenes and ends on a big "2020" greeting.
why: It took first place in its compo at DiHalt 2020 Lite, and the source is available for anyone curious how it was put together on the NES.

summary: Bitshifters' BBC Micro take on the ST-NICCC polygon challenge, with code by KieranHJ and music by Rhino. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: A compo winner at Revision that plays back the filled-polygon animation from Oxygene's Atari ST demo ST-NICCC 2000 on a 2MHz 6502. The source is available.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo, the eleventh in the Delirious series, coded by Raistlin with music by MCH. It came second in the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2018.
why: Greeted as Raistlin's comeback after a long absence. Sceners single out the circle scroller, the big logos, MCH's soundtrack and the skull picture at the end, and several called it their moral compo winner.

quote.text: Great circular Wheel scroller with priorities and I love the stars in the background of the greeting part.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Kpacku, released in 2014: a birthday gift for nq, with greeting text scrolling beside a glitchy logo before a 'Happy Birthday' picture.
why: A personal gift prod rather than a compo entry. The video title marks it as one of a series of gifts for nq, and it's a good example of the Spectrum scene's habit of making demos for friends.

summary: KivideMaa is a ZX Spectrum demo by Vassa and moroz1999, released in July 2012. It placed third in the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2012.
why: A podium finish at DiHalt 2012, in a compo open to all 8-bit machines, is the main mark of its standing.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by JAC!, released in 2010. A wireframe outline sits over full-screen bands of colour rasters, later joined by scrolling chevron shapes.
why: A small example of how much colour a 128-byte Atari intro can put on screen. It has no compo placing or comments to go on, so it's simply a short, tidy sizecoding piece.

summary: Crest's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at X 1996, with code and graphics by Crossbow, extra graphics by DeeKay and music from Dane, Deek, DRAX, Mitch, MSK and Xayne.
why: Sceners praise its graphics, technical depth and soundtrack, and credit it with introducing new graphics modes such as SHF, SHIF and UFLI. Some find the pace slow, but it is often named among the top C64 demos.
highlights: new graphics modes SHF, SHIF, UFLI

quote.text: Simply one of the best demos for the C64 with tons of eye candy, technical brilliance and excellent SID music.

summary: An NES demo by The Art Of Never Getting Anything Done that won the Beginners Demo compo at Alternative Party 2011, opening on a Soviet-themed take on the Super Mario Bros. title screen.
why: A winning first effort in its compo, with code by Burre, graphics by OrreBorre and Velinje, and music by OrreBorre. The communist parody makes it a light-hearted watch.
highlights: Super Mario Bros. title screen parody

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC 4K intro with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and music by Targhan. It placed third in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2019.
why: Tagged as a concept piece with no effects, it relies on drawn scenes rather than routines, and it made the Meteoriks 2020 watchlist.

summary: Genesis Project's one-screen C64 demo, third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2012: a cluttered beach scene by Redcrab where a man plays a heap of instruments, with dogs and gadgets bopping along to the tune.
why: Sceners call it a charming, funny feel-good demo with something always happening on screen. They single out the detail in Redcrab's graphics and his funky tune, with animations triggered by the SID data.

quote.text: I love how the trumped oscillates with the vibrato, it's little details like that that made this demo so cool.

summary: Samar's C64 tribute demo to group founder Mariusz (Ramos), placed 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2015, built around a huge scrolling painted image with background pictures.
why: Sceners call it a moving, honest tribute, singling out Isildur's artwork, the scrolling tile and background images, and the emotional soundtrack by Jammer and Pece.

quote.text: Very neat tribute demo. Full of sadness. Everything fits together.

summary: A short C64 intro by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., placed 2nd in the Oldschool Realtime Demo compo at Nordlicht 2013: an animated four-colour forest logo by CONS over a big text font, with code and charset by Streettuff and music by Linus.
why: Sceners single out the cute animated graphics, especially the Commodore balloon and the rabbit, along with the charset, the dramatic opening and Linus's experimental tune. Short, but conceptually entertaining.

quote.text: Nice, I really dig the dramaturgic opening, animation, charset, and the balloon of course. ;)

summary: Target Team's ZX Spectrum invitation for the Hackers Top 2010 Spring Edition party, with code by Restorer, graphics by Breeze and music by MmcM.
why: A party invitation from the Spectrum scene, made by a three-person crew and well received on Pouët.
highlights: dithered twister beside a scrolling text bar

summary: Radiance's Atari 8-bit demo for a 1MB-expanded machine, which won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k24 WE. Code by Dante, music by Jammer, graphics by Blasph and Biter.
why: A first place at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, and it made the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist.

summary: A BBC Micro demo by CRTC, coded by Puppeh and Joey with music by Insectecutor, that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2010.
why: It took first place in the Oldschool Demo competition at Sundown 2010, a win for the BBC Micro against other old machines.

summary: Arise's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at North Party 2006, coded by Fenek with graphics by Bimber and music from Jammer, Randall and Rodney, done almost entirely in colourful hires.
why: Sceners praised its fresh hires style, fast realtime vectors and morphs, and a sync with the music that holds it together. Later viewers called it years ahead of the hires revival demos that followed.

quote.text: The amout of real realtime coding without any precalc or animation trickery in this one is breathtaking.

summary: Hooy-Program's 2011 ZX Spectrum intro starring Nyan Cat, with code and music by Gasman and text and font by Aki.
why: A Spectrum take on the 2011 Nyan Cat meme, made the same year the meme took off. It's a light, cheerful piece from Hooy-Program with a scrolling message and a soundtrack by Gasman.

summary: Metalvotze's Vectrex demo, coded by Nitro, which won both the Alternative Demo/Intro compo and the Jury prize at Buenzli 2005.
why: A rare demo for the vector-display Vectrex that took two first places at Buenzli 2005, winning its compo and the jury's vote.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, with code, graphics and music by Viznut and fullscreen pictures by ccr. It placed 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001.
why: A rare VIC-20 entry that held its own against other old machines in a major party's oldskool compo, taking second place at Assembly 2001.

summary: Quadtrip's C64 demo that came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2017, built around a glitch and noise theme, with code by visy and graphics by visy, Isildur and ZanaGB.
why: Sceners single it out as a model of how to use glitch aesthetics in a demo, praising the odd, twisted vibe and the unusual soundtrack by Jammer and Psycho8580.

quote.text: imho, this is the proper way to use glitch/noise theme in a demo. i enjoyed from beginning to end.

summary: An Atari VCS invitation for the SillyVenture 2012 party, released under Mystic Bytes with code by Tjoppen and music by Jakub Husak.
why: A rare demo-style invitation for the Atari 2600, made to announce the December 2012 SillyVenture party.

summary: Booze Design's single-file C64 demo, third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2018: a Jailbird logo screen with vector shapes passing through an animated ring, plus a scroller.
why: Sceners call it a polished, stylish one-screener, praising Jailbird's graphics, the fade-in, the vectors and the helix, and the detail of animating the ring.

quote.text: Love this! Really nice work. Lovely fade in, awesome vectors - and the helix.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, the third in their Biba series, placed 8th in the demo compo at X 2012. It mixes hi-res graphics, vector parts and bobs with a soundtrack by Randall, Rodney and Wacek.
why: Many sceners felt it was underrated at X 2012. They praise its coherent, original style, its hi-res graphics and its soundtrack, and some say they return to it regularly.

quote.text: I see myself boot this one up quite regularly, really really like it a lot and it doesnt grow old. coherent design, superb soundtrack, excellent code, originality, flow, its got it all.

summary: Tochi is a 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Busy and Noro, with Busy credited for graphics and Noro for music. It came second in the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Forever 2017.
why: A second place in a dedicated 1K compo at Forever, from two long-standing Spectrum sceners, packing visuals and music into a kilobyte.

summary: A Sharp MZ-700 demo by Flush and Up Rough, with code and graphics by MooZ and p0ke, extra graphics by AdorU and music by Glafouk. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at Cookie 2017.
why: A compo-winning demo for a rarely seen machine, the Sharp MZ-700. It comes from a joint effort by two groups.

summary: Noice's C64 comeback demo, placed 6th in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Goat-themed parts with raytraced goats, a mirrored techtech and a multicolour end-scroller over a bitmap animation, with music by Dane.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a cheerful return for Noice, singling out the raytraced and rotating goats, the mirrored techtech, Dane's tune "Dear Brandon" and the progress bar, along with the name.

quote.text: Nice little demo, the mirrored techtech is my fave effect! The multicolored end-scroller with bitmap anim is also really nice..

summary: A 32K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo, with code by Toms, graphics by Beb and music by e-dredon. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 in 2024.
why: It took first place in its compo at Benediction Coding Party #4. The video is labelled as showing the "wrong CRTC part", so this recording shows the intro on a particular CRTC variant.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo written in BASIC by Nodeus, who did code and graphics, with AY music by Moran. It came 2nd in the ZX-Basic compo at Base-X 2015.
why: Worth a look as a BASIC-only Spectrum demo that placed in a dedicated BASIC compo, showing what can be done without machine code on a 48K machine with AY sound.

summary: SquoQuo's Atari 8-bit invitation to Revision, released at Datastorm 2013 where it placed 2nd in the Other Platform Demo compo. Code by Hopper, graphics by Hopper, Raven and Farfar, music by 505.
why: An Atari 8-bit invite for one of the big demoparties, good enough to take second place against other platforms at Datastorm 2013.

summary: Bitshifters' BBC Micro demo that plays the Bad Apple video in teletext graphics, with intro artwork by Horsenburger and music by Inverse Phase.
why: A teletext take on the Bad Apple video. The silhouette animation is drawn in chunky Mode 7 block graphics, and the source is available.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo for Kindergarden's 20th birthday, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Kindergarden 2014. Code by Dbug, graphics by Fra and Dbug, music by Count Zero.
why: A compo winner that takes its cue from Amiga cracktros, done on the Oric. Its video title calls it an "amiga cracktro" inspired intro made to mark the party's 20th birthday.

summary: Fatzone's C64 demo that won the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2022, with code by Malmix and Pezac, graphics by Malmix and music by mAZE and Klegg.
why: Sceners praise its flow, smooth transitions and fresh twists on familiar effects. They single out the selfie squasher, a guitar-shredding animation and the colourful detail throughout.

quote.text: An entertaining feel-good code pr0n demo with very clever ideas, and in your own style.

summary: Samar Productions' C64 demo, released as an 80% party version, that won the C64 demo compo at Moonshine Dragons 2022. Code by Golara, Mojzesh and Slajerek, graphics by Isildur and Jetan, music by MCH, Conrad and Jammer.
why: Sceners praise its pace and flow, its 90s-style maths effects and the pixel work by Jetan and Isildur. The dotted mushroom intro and the Flip It part come up again and again.

quote.text: Ultra-stylish, precisely what I want from a Samar production. The flow of the parts is breathless; I can't see how anyone could get bored watching it.

summary: A 16K Atari 8-bit intro by g0blinish, with music by Dhor, that won the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: It took first place in its compo at Silly Venture 2k17, a solid showing for a one-coder 16K production on the Atari XL/XE.

summary: Light's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1991, with code by Flamingo, Waco, Rash and Yabba, graphics by Goblin and Scooby, and music from Bappalander, Bluez, Page and guest Danko.
why: Sceners who were at The Party 1991 remember it shaking the compo, and HCL calls it probably the best Light demo. Comments single out the vectors, a raytracer for its era and Bappalander's tunes.

quote.text: Man, this demo really shook the compo. Even the amigapeople were dropping jaws in awe

summary: A 128-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Gasman of Hooy-Program that won the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2018: a distorted blue and magenta chessboard pattern.
why: A compo winner at Outline 2018, and a 128-byte intro that fits sound in alongside its visuals.

summary: Taquart's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Eru and Fox, which won the Atari 8bit Demo compo at Intel Outside 1997.
why: A compo winner from the late-1990s Polish Atari scene, and one of the better-regarded Atari 8-bit demos of its year.

summary: Chorus's one-file C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2008, with code by Clarence, music by DRAX and Fanta, and graphics by Leon.
why: A coder's demo that sceners single out for its full-screen ECI tech-tech running at 50 fps, the diagonal Kefrens bars and the oldskool DYSP and FPD finale, plus Drax's music.

quote.text: ECI techtech looks quite impressive, I mean it is a colorful effect that covers almost entire C64 screen and runs 50 fps.

summary: Csabo's Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo that won the Pimp My Part compo at Busodore 2011, a contest where sceners rework a given part.
why: It took first place in its compo, and the source is available for anyone curious about how it was done on the Plus 4.

summary: Hoaxers and Wrath Designs' underwater-themed C64 demo, winner of the demo compo at Transmission64 2021 Fall Edition, with code by Firehawk, graphics by Joe and music by Møllpauk.
why: Sceners praise Joe's graphics, the moody soundtrack and Firehawk's code, singling out the merging-outline scroller, side-border image movers and a coral scroller some had never seen before, all on a stock machine.

quote.text: Great graphics and moody soundtrack for submersive atmosphere, with outstanding coding that warrants a peek or two in the memory monitor.

summary: The Obsessed Maniacs' parody C64 demo, coded and scored by kb with a logo by Half-Elf, which placed 6th in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994. It's a fake demo that sends up demo conventions.
why: Sceners call it the best fake demo on the C64 because it's well made rather than a lazy BASIC joke. They single out the dramatic music timed to the gags and the world's smallest scroller.

quote.text: People were suprised at every new effect, and laughed kind a' all the time.

summary: Offence's Space Invaders tribute for the C64, made entirely by Kristian Myklebust and winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Kindergarden 2013. Invaders are rebuilt from isometric cubes, alongside a convincing recreation of the arcade screen.
why: Sceners praise its timing and design, its minimal music synced to the action, and the way the font is reworked to look like the original arcade machine. A one-man effort covering code, graphics and music.

quote.text: I love the concept, I love the execution, as usual your sense of timing, design and a strange ability to make minimalistic music sound super cool is present.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 2600 VCS by Tjoppen, which placed second in the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2012.
why: A 128-byte VCS intro that includes sound and took second place at Outline 2012. The source code is available for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Ilmenit's 256-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE, placed second in the Oldschool Intro 256b compo at Demodulation 2020: a snowy night road running towards a striped rising moon.
why: It won Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, so it is one of the most recognised 256-byte Atari productions of its year.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation to Datastorm 2014, coded and drawn by Mermaid with music by Stinsen: a cartoon car drives along beneath a big Datastorm logo while coloured bubbles drift and the party details scroll past.
why: Sceners call it cosy and singled out Stinsen's tune, the smooth animation of the car and the custom Frankfurter-style charset Mermaid drew for it.

quote.text: Really good idea and perfect animation of the sweet car and the colors flying around!

summary: Atari Inc.'s 1980 in-store demonstration program for the Atari 8-bit computers, coded by Mike Albaugh: a sales loop of captioned screens pitching the machine for home entertainment and family education.
why: A commercial demo from the very start of the Atari 8-bit line, made to sell the machine in shops. It's an early piece of the platform's history rather than a scene production.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by evilpaul with music by Gasman, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006.
why: A podium finish at Sundown 2006 for a small two-person Spectrum team, with evilpaul handling both code and graphics.

summary: Ate Bit's 1K invitation intro for Sundown 2007 on the ZX Spectrum, released at Breakpoint 2007, where it placed 7th in the Console/Real Wild compo.
why: A party invitation squeezed into one kilobyte on the Spectrum, with a solid reception on Pouët.

summary: Game Boy demo by Matt Current, with code and graphics by Janne and music by Sauli, shared 5th in the demo compo at Stream 2006. The video shows it running on a real DMG-001.
why: A placing at Stream 2006 and a solid reception on Pouët make it a good look at what the original Game Boy could do in 2006. It uses the Carillon player for its music and runs as an endless loop.

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo from Little Computer People 2011, where it placed 5th in the C64 demo compo. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by Fanta, graphics from Celtic, Sphinx, Veto and Yazoo.
why: Sceners single out the chainsaw-wielding ninja carving the logo into rock, the colourful vertical bending bars, the Mandelbrot part and Fanta's soundtrack. Several called it their favourite of the party despite its placing.

quote.text: It has the right mixture between creative ideas, technical brilliance and beauty. I also love the transitions.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gasman, who did the code, music, graphics and text himself. It placed 7th in the Wild demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A one-person piece of scene poetry that tells its story through on-screen text. It also uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode, beating the machine's usual colour limits.

summary: Blowjobb's monochrome Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Śmigło with graphics by dely and music by Miker. It placed third in the demo compo at Glucholazy 2008.
why: A third place at Glucholazy 2008, and a tidy example of an Atari demo working entirely in monochrome.

summary: Cluster's 4K intro for the Atari 2600, coded and directed by Kylearan with music by Glafouk. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2017.
why: A podium finish at Revision for a 4K intro on one of the most constrained machines around, from a group that works on the VCS.

summary: Speccy.pl's ZX Spectrum 128K slideshow demo, with graphics by Piesiu, music by CatMan and code by Tygrys. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl party 2022.1.
why: A compo winner built around Piesiu's artwork. The video title calls it a slide show, so the pictures are the main draw, with CatMan's music behind them.
highlights: bearded man with headphones and pipe

summary: Flush's Atari 2600 demo M, coded by flewww with graphics and music by Glafouk, placed 2nd in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A second place in the dedicated VCS demo compo at Silly Venture 2018, from a small team getting big chunky graphics out of the 2600.

summary: A single-part Commodore 64 demo by kompositkrut: a SID cover of the Amazing Horse tune played over a scrolling parallax landscape with a sprite rider on a horse and a colour-cycling logo.
why: Sceners mostly praise the catchy SID cover, with the cheerful presentation of sprites, parallax scenery and fades as a fun extra. Originally released as a music piece and later listed as a one-file demo.

quote.text: Sounds awesome in SID. Very catchy, it keeps spinning round in my head.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE by Marquee Design, coded by superogue, that won the Oldschool 128 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2022.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2022 in the 128-byte class, and a "making of" writeup is available on the Marquee Design site for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Dentifrice's Atari VCS demo themed around Bomberman, which won the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k25 WE. Code by Kezax, music by Glafouk, graphics by Exocet.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture on the 2600, and its source is available for anyone curious how it was done on such limited hardware.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by CNCD that placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's oldskool compo, which makes it a rare chance to see the unexpanded-or-not little VIC-20 taking on bigger machines at a major party.

summary: Pure-Byte's 1987 Commodore 64 demo, coded by Yip with graphics by Conan: a drawn scroll-reading machine with track and scroll counters, selectable texts such as story, scores and greets, and several tunes to switch between.
why: An early C64 music-and-scroller demo built around an interactive control panel. The one CSDb comment remembers loving it as a kid and singles out the tune "5th Dream About Happiness".

quote.text: Did love this demo as kid and the tune "5th Dream About Happiness" is so fucking brilliant

summary: A 1997 ZX Spectrum 128K demo by E-Mage, built from crude hand-drawn pictures and flagged NSFW in its video title. It uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode.
why: A cheeky late-90s Spectrum oddity that Pouët voters rate well, and an example of a 128K demo using multicolour graphics.

summary: Viznut's one-man C64 demo for Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2006: a political piece with blocky abstract visuals, text slogans and a sung speech-synth soundtrack.
