why: Sceners single out the singing speech synthesis, with one predicting it would start a trend in voice-synth C64 tunes. Its rough, deliberately messy look and sound divided opinion, but some call it a demo for refined taste.

quote.text: I think the voice synth tune will start a new trend in c64 tunes - gimme more voice synth!

summary: Still Rising is a two-disk-side C64 demo by Artline, Bloodsuckers, Extend and Orange, coded by Kakka, XMunkki and Space Man with graphics by LeroyB and music by Zardax. It came 2nd in the demo compo at Zoo 2022.
why: Sceners single out the light-sourced veiled statue, which changes viewpoint and zoom, along with Zardax's soundtrack and its nods to the golden years. Several thought it had real flow, and some preferred it to the winner.

quote.text: That light sourced veiled statue effect is incredible. The way it changes viewpoint and zoom makes it work extremely well.

summary: Iris's Oric demo, coded and drawn by Xeron with music by H0ffman, which came second in the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2024.
why: A recent Oric demo that placed second at Nova 2024. Its title plays on the His Master's Voice logo, which it redraws with raster colour running through it.
highlights: His Master's Voice dog and gramophone

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo Shareware, coded by BriteLite with graphics by H7 and music by Player One, placed third in the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2015.
why: A podium finish at Zoo 2015, and a chance to see H7's chunky, character-style graphics carry a whole Dekadence production.
highlights: radial tunnel in a framed window

summary: Inversion's debut C64 demo, coded by Blackis and zoi with graphics by Havocplague and music by Castor, which placed third in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010. It includes the fullscreen picture Heidi.
why: Sceners were surprised it was a first demo, and several said its look and Castor's score felt closer to Atari or Spectrum demos than typical C64 fare. They also praised how well the music fits the effects.

quote.text: I like the way music is attuned with demo effects.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2010: oneframe fullscreen chunky effects in a gigascreen palette, with AY music and Covox digital drums.
why: A deliberate rip-and-convert entry for a compo that welcomed ripped code and graphics. It reworks the effect idea from the Amstrad CPC demo "DTC" and 505's music from the Atari STE demo "More or Less Zero". Source is available.

summary: Hoaxers and Wrath Designs' C64 demo that needs a 512K REU, winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013. Code by Firehawk, graphics by Joe and Grasstust, music by Response.
why: Sceners argued over the REU requirement, but even the doubters praised the visuals and flow. Joe's artwork, the swirling 'floffy' scroller, Response's Star Trek: Voyager tune and the closing globe screen are what people single out.
highlights: end screen with globe in hand

quote.text: Beautiful and unique demo. The graphics are epic! The Voyager theme is cool to listen to along with the complete soundtrack.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, which placed 5th in the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2012.
why: A chance to see how much a 128-byte Atari intro can put on screen: a fifth-place entry from Outline's 128-byte compo.

summary: Fossil's C64 demo for X 2016, coded by Knut M. Clausen with design and music by Jammer, which placed 6th in the demo compo.
why: Sceners praise its fast pace and lack of filler, with smooth vectors, a face twister and Jammer's soundtrack singled out. Several rated it among their favourites of the compo despite the placing.

quote.text: I really love this one. Very polished, not a boring second. No fat on this one whatsoever.

summary: A megademo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Assassins, released in November 2006, with code by Skoro and graphics from Harry, Luca, RRR and Kichy.
why: A multi-part Plus/4 megademo, uploaded by its coder. It was released outside any compo and is well liked on Pouët, with no down votes.

summary: Resource and FIRE's first Plus/4 production under the Resource label, coded by Bubis with a soundtrack by Luca. It won the Wild compo at Forever 2003 and needs a SID card.
why: A Wild compo winner at Forever 2003 and Resource's debut on the Plus/4, a machine many of the group originally came from. Luca's soundtrack was composed exclusively for it.

summary: Taquart's 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit, coded by Eru with music by X-Ray, which won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2008.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2008 that fits code and music into 1K.
highlights: twisting shapes over a character grid

summary: Genesis Project's two-disk-side C64 demo, coded by Raistlin, Elder0010 and Sparta, which placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2023. It is a trackmo packed with graphics, raster and sideborder effects, dedicated to Shadow.
why: Sceners praise its polish, smooth transitions and old-school code tricks: sideborder Kefrens bars with 206 bars, a perspective chessboard, a spiral scroller and a smooth double scroller. It was nominated at Siggraph Asia 2023 and the Meteoriks 2024.

quote.text: a cool modern style with smooth transitiosn with really good effects and new records to raise the bar

summary: Brainwave's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, which came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2000.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions 2000, and tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which squeezes more colours into each character cell than the stock attribute grid allows.

summary: Desire's VBXE-enhanced Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Heaven with graphics by Ozan and SimOne and music by Triace and Vedder. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2017.
why: A podium finish at Nordlicht 2017 and a showcase for the VBXE video upgrade, which gives the Atari 800 a far richer palette than the stock machine.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the demo competition at Gubbdata 2013, with code from a team including Magnar, Bob, CRT and Mirage, graphics by Yazoo and Magnar, and Krill's loader.
why: Sceners single out the smooth square plasma, the swirl and double scrollers, the fade effects in the intro and Magnar's catchy soundtrack, along with graphics that no longer look like conversions.

quote.text: The square plasma thingy rocks! Very smooth and fresh.

summary: Artline Designs' Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2024: a story-driven run of hires scenes following a boy through the night, with music by Flex and Mutetus.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2025. Sceners single out the atmosphere, the soundtrack, the hires graphics and the boy running through the rasters, along with the zoom scroller at the end and the side-border tricks.

quote.text: Graphics, story and the soundtrack go wonderfully hand in hand.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 demo by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, music by Response and graphics by Pal. It came second in the Combined Demo compo at Black Valley 2022.
why: It placed second in a combined-platform demo compo at Black Valley 2022, and its tag marks it as a demo built around cubes.

summary: An 8K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Osmium Path, with code by Optimus and graphics and music by Ham. It came second in the intro competition at Decrunch 2022.
why: A runner-up at Decrunch 2022 that packs code, graphics and music into 8K. It's a compact example of current CPC size-limited work from Osmium Path.

summary: Resistance's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, made with RK/LE Team, which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl party 2018.1. Code by Sachy, music by Dya, graphics by Fra, Slayer and At0m.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl 2018.1, and three graphicians share the credits, so the hand-drawn screens carry much of the show.

summary: Life On Mars' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015, with code and design by introspec and music by nq.
why: A compo winner at 3BM OpenAir 2015, and the video is the final version captured at 50Hz by introspec himself.
highlights: chunky typography with long drop shadows

summary: Crest's third Krestage demo for the Commodore 64, released in 2007, with code and graphics by Crossbow and music by Jeff. It is a single-screen trick demo that pairs moving FLI pictures with VIC-chip effects in the borders.
why: Sceners were stunned by Crossbow's VIC trickery: nine sprites shown in a row, an FLI picture mover and a puzzling upper-border effect, which set off long threads working out how it was done. The bass-heavy tune gets praise too.

quote.text: Crossbow does what he does best, invent new weird things. My deepest respect!!

summary: Atlantis's C64 demo for BCC Party 2018, where it placed 4th in the demo compo. Code by Dr. Science, Merlin, q0w and Tsurugi, music by Rock and Snabel, graphics by Merlin, q0w and FatFrost.
why: Many sceners rated it above its compo placing. They single out the tunnel part, the soundtrack, the fresh credits screen, the bees linking the parts and how well it uses the party motto and Berlin.

quote.text: Lots of detail, love and creativity in here!

summary: A C64 demo by Warriors of the Wasteland, with code and music by A Life in Hell, that placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Syntax 2008. Expect interlaced chunky modes, plasmas, 3D dots and photo-like pictures.
why: Rough and unpolished by its makers' own admission, but sceners praise its innovative code. They single out the near-photorealistic girl in the flip-disk picture and the double-colour plasma at the end.

quote.text: The girl on the flip disk part is the closest to photorealism i've ever seen on a c64.

summary: Dekadence's VIC-20 demo, coded by BriteLite with music by Roz, which placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007.
why: A VIC-20 demo that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Assembly, a rare outing for the machine at a big party.

summary: Genesis Project cracktro for the C64 by Mermaid, who did code, graphics and music, and winner of the Intro Creation Competition 2016. A green wireframe GP logo hangs above a scrolling vector grid while a scroller runs across the middle.
why: Sceners praise its fresh, un-C64-ish Vectrex and Battle Zone style, the design of the logo and the atmospheric music. Several call it one of the best C64 intros they have seen.

quote.text: Wow! So stylish and arcade retro but still feels so fresh :) Excellent intro.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo that placed 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2009: a sequence of big slogan screens such as "Opinions lead to conflict" and "We crack your mind".
why: A concept piece with a political edge, tagged for glitch and noise aesthetics, and a podium finish at Stream 2009.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by bob_er with music by Dhor, which came second in the demo compo at Glucholazy 2008.
why: A podium finish at Glucholazy 2008, and tagged as a text-mode production, so worth a look for what the Atari's character modes can be pushed to do.

summary: Serato's 256-byte Commodore 64 intro, a raycast grayscale city flight that won the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2025.
why: Sceners call it an impressive port for fitting into a single block. Once its precalculation finishes, it runs as fast as the screenshot suggests, and some already treat it as the new visual reference for 256 bytes.

quote.text: This might just be the new reference for 256b (for visuals, LFT still rules what comes to aural pleasure).

summary: Black Sun's finished C64 demo, a bug-fixed 100% version of their earlier party release with additions and a note. Code by Nitro, Snerg and Ninja, music by Jammer. It placed 5th in Twoje Stare Demo at Decrunch 2015.
why: Sceners single out the shaded, moving-light animation on the android's face, the plot effects and vectors, and Jammer's otherworldly soundtrack. Several call it fresh and well coded for only the group's second demo.

quote.text: I love that mask with the moving light source. And the soundtrack is plain and simply insane!

summary: Dual Crew Shining's Game Boy Color demo, placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2012. Code by Dox and Peitchi, graphics by Vodka and thUg, music by Wiklund.
why: A Game Boy Color entry that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Revision, and it runs as an endless loop once the parts are done.

summary: Impact's Amstrad CPC demo from 2021, with code by Demoniak, graphics by Kris, design by CMP and music by Mast. It is built around filled 3D objects.
why: A recent CPC 3D showcase from Impact with no compo entry on record. It was well received on Pouët.

summary: A short C64 one-file demo by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded with music by Virgill and graphics by CONS, that placed third in the oldschool realtime demo compo at Nordlicht 2013.
why: Sceners call it stylish and well made, picking out the floating cubes, the treated face picture and Virgill's music. The usual complaint is that it ends too soon.
highlights: CONS face picture with reddish blur

quote.text: Stylish - the logo infade - the cubes with one side red/blue and the CONS pic with the reddish blur - the noise at the end... really really well made!

summary: A C64 promo for Generation 64, a Swedish book about the Commodore 64 scene, with code by Shadow, graphics by Mermaid, music by Danko and text by Spelpappan. It won the Other Demo compo at Gerp 2014.
why: Sceners liked it as a neat presentation, singling out the portrait of author Spelpappan. Mermaid points out that it only looks PETSCII-like and isn't built from PETSCII characters.

quote.text: this is a nice presentation anyway.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Kael and Fyrex of Mayhem, which won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2018.
why: It took first place in the LowEnd 256-byte intro competition at DiHalt 2018, so it's a good example of how much fits into a tiny Spectrum program.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a Las Vegas theme, winner of the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2026. A big crew of coders, musicians and graphicians deliver a fast run of effect and picture screens.
why: Sceners single out the second disk side's effects, Talent's unusual pixel technique and screens that move and rotate freely, ignoring the 8x8 grid and colour limits. Several call the music superb.

quote.text: The 8x8 grid simply does not exist for you - the whole screen is a free canvas where things can move and rotate freely  with no colour limitations.

summary: A Halloween-themed four-disk-side Commodore 64 co-op demo by Pretzel Logic, Offence, Bonzai, Atlantis, Genesis Project, Wrath Designs and Lethargy, released as The Pumpkins. It won the demo compo at Zoo 2022.
why: Sceners praise its consistent spooky theme, polished presentation and a soundtrack by many composers that still hangs together. They single out the VHS rewind and old-movie effects, the turn-disk parts and the little intermissions.

quote.text: so many themes by so many composers and it feels like one piece, never insistent, always engaging.

summary: Placebo's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2001, with code and music by Sairoos, graphics by Paracels and objects by D-Man.
why: It took second place in the Spectrum demo competition at Chaos Constructions 2001 and is well regarded on Pouët.

summary: Onslaught's C64 demo that placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010: Zak McKracken's bedroom from the classic adventure, redrawn with richer graphics, with Zak walking around and talking. Code by Enthusi, graphics by Veto, music by ReD.
why: Sceners praised it as a cool, original idea with a style unlike the usual demo, and singled out the upgraded graphics of a much-loved game. Several hoped it was a preview of a full remake.

quote.text: This is a totally cool and original demo. The style is drastically different from the norm.

summary: lft's C64 demo from Datastorm 2013, where it placed 7th in the C64 demo compo: a VSP-scrolled logo with a long scroller explaining the cause of the infamous VSP crash and how to avoid it in code.
why: A technical article in demo form. Sceners credit it with finally explaining the VSP crash as a DRAM metastability problem and showing crash-free VSP scrolling that works on crash-prone machines.
highlights: code, graphics and music by lft

quote.text: This is so damm cool, you solved a c64 mystery.. a straight 10 from me... congratulations!!

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Arkos and Benediction, with code by Krusty, graphics by Voxfreax and music by Targhan. It placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2017.
why: A size-limited CPC intro that held its own in a competitive oldskool compo at Revision, and its source is available for anyone curious how it fits in 4K.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 story demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2025, following three characters on a road trip, with code by Trident, graphics by Soya and music by Fegolhuzz.
why: Sceners praise how it weaves a funny, heartfelt story together with C64 effects in a coherent flow. Many say it made them laugh out loud, and they single out the parallax greetings, bobs and sideborder tricks.

quote.text: You (again!) managed to weave together a captivating story and C64 demo effects into a coherent flow. Wonderful work.

summary: Ultimate Megademo is a 1992 Amstrad CPC megademo by Face Hugger, who handled the code, graphics and music on his own.
why: A one-person megademo from the early CPC scene, with every part coded, drawn and scored by Face Hugger. It's well liked on Pouët.
highlights: shaded ball objects over a reflective floor

summary: A 32-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC! that fills the screen with simulated TV noise. The video title presents it as a collection of noise routines in 32 and 16 bytes.
why: A small study in how much static a few bytes of code can throw up on an Atari, with blue, patterned and grey noise variations. It runs without sound.

summary: Genesis Project's Commodore PET demo, coded by Elder0010 with graphics by Elder0010 and LRNZ, placing third in the Wild compo at Gubbdata 2022.
why: A recent demo for the PET, a machine with only a character display to work with, and it placed in the Wild competition at Gubbdata 2022.

summary: Black Sun's C64 demo, released as a 90% version, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010. Code by Nitro, Snerg and Ninja, with graphics and music by Jammer plus guest artists.
why: Sceners single out the light-shaded face, the vector parts built from bobs and multiplexed sprites, and Jammer's soundtrack, which many rank among his best. It was seen as a big step forward for the group.

quote.text: Some really nice effects (face, multiplexed 3D sprites), an excellent soundtrack and a visual style that just speaks to my cyberpunk heart.

summary: Nuance's Vectrex demo, placed 2nd in the Low End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2013. Code by Nitro, graphics by Bitbreaker and Widdy, music by FieserWolf.
why: A rare demo for the Vectrex's vector display from a team better known on the C64, and a runner-up at The Ultimate Meeting 2013.

summary: The Noisy Bunch's C64 demo, placed 7th in the demo compo at X 2012: a SID-focused follow-up to Vicious Sid with a long list of coders, musicians and artists including Jeroen Tel, 4-Mat and Mahoney.
why: Sceners treat it as a showcase of new SID techniques, singling out polyphonic chords on a single SID channel, a 15 kHz sample part, a reverb part and Protracker modules played on the C64.

quote.text: Polyphonic chords on a single Sid channel?? That alone is worth a perfect ten. And The 15KHz sample part... I stared at it for a good few minutes.

summary: AAA Band's ZX Spectrum megademo, shown here in its party version, which came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at DiHalt 2014 Lite. It was made by a large crew of coders, artists and musicians.
why: A runner-up at DiHalt 2014 Lite that pulls together work from around a dozen Spectrum sceners, including code from Rob F, g0blinish, Trefi and SerzhSoft and music by Rob F, Splinter and nq.
highlights: graphics by Mellone, Lee and AAA

summary: A Commodore 64 intro by Digital Sounds System, with code by Street Tuff and graphics by Knoeki, that came 7th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012. The video is live footage from the party hall.
why: A small, informal party release that shows up at a big PC-oriented party's alternative platforms compo. Worth a look for the C64 side of Evoke 2012.

summary: Genesis Project's 2014 C64 demo presenting a new Rob Hubbard tune, "New Frontier", produced as a SID with Max Hall for the film From Bedrooms to Billions, with Redcrab's caricature of Hubbard at the piano.
why: Rob Hubbard's first new C64 music in decades. Sceners single out the full-length tune's Hubbard-style bassline and lead slides, and even those cooler on the music praise Redcrab's graphics.

quote.text: such an excellent tune, building and building towards multiple climaxes. super it's not just a short ditty, but a truly full length composition.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo coded by Acid Maker and Scorpio with music by Jakub Husak, which won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Silly Venture 2k21 WE, one of the main parties for 8-bit platforms.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2020, built around a single idea: everything on screen runs on the diagonal. Code by Shadow, graphics by Facet, music by Stinsen.
why: Sceners praise how consistently the diagonal theme is carried through, along with Facet's pictures and Stinsen's soundtrack, which several single out as the highlight.

quote.text: Love the idea of this demo. Everything is diagonal. Excellent pictures. I can listen to the music the whole day, and I probably will.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Szeryf, which won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k23 WE. Filmed on real hardware.
why: It took first place in its size category at Silly Venture, one of the main Atari 8-bit parties.
highlights: car driving past a dotted skyline

summary: A 254-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, who handled both code and music. It placed 4th in the Atari ST/800XL Demo/Bootsector compo at Outline 2011.
why: A small-size production that fits code and music into 254 bytes, with its source released. It's worth a look for what a single coder squeezed into so few bytes.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Ancients Pledge, with music by NecroPolo, that won the 8-bit demo compo at Euskal 2010. Wireframe objects spin in a grey panel, framed by coloured boxes that echo the lines.
why: A 4K intro that beat full-size entries in the 8-bit demo compo at Euskal 2010. Sceners singled out its screen design and the maze effect.

quote.text: I liked the screen design and maze effect

summary: Taboo's C64 demo from the end of 1992, which won the C64 demo compo at Skylight Party. Code by K.M. and MMS, graphics by Shaman and Wayne, running to roughly half an hour of parts.
why: Sceners single out the plot scroller, with Shadow calling it probably the best on the C64, along with the morphing vectors, raytraced ball and music selection. Some find it slow. It was voted 12th best demo in Design #1 in 1997.

quote.text: But the plot-scroller, wow, probably the best I have seen on the C64, and in the border even for that extra little spice.

summary: A preview of Trilobit's Atari 2600 demo Triptych, coded by visy and Ilmarque, with music and graphics by Ilmarque. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2009.
why: A third place at Stream 2009 for a VCS demo, made by a two-person team where Ilmarque handled code, music and graphics.

summary: Dekadence's beer-themed C64 demo, placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2001. Code, graphics and music by BriteLite, with graphics from Spiikki and music from SounDemoN.
why: Sceners single out its unusual look and atmosphere, the colour choices and the wild, fast music. A review on c64.sk called it plasma-like effects with decent black and white graphics on top, timed to the music.

quote.text: it's totally out there, great theme and colour choice, wild music, very unique demo. has an awesome look to it.

summary: Party Bit 25% is a Commodore 64 demo by Ate Bit (the video also credits Hack'n'Trade). It came 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2013.
why: It is a rare C64 demo written for three SID chips, and it placed in the Sundown 2013 oldskool demo compo.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2005, shown there as a preview and released once finished: an old-school run of parts with code by Clarence, graphics by Leon and music by DRAX, plus a note file.
why: Sceners liked its old-school feel and subtle but effective effects, singling out the 10-sprites-per-line tricks in the lower border and note file, the soundtrack and the simple final part.

quote.text: I really enjoyed this demo and the final part was actually my favourite. So simple but effective. Just beautiful! Lovely tunes as well!

summary: Arise's C64 demo, a sequel, that won the demo competition at North Party 2002. It includes Katon's fullscreen picture Final Fight, which won the graphics compo at the same party.
why: Sceners praise its inventive effects and the care taken over design and transitions. Several call it one of the best C64 demos of its decade, and it is still on many favourite lists.

quote.text: One of the most creative, best designed and most impressively coded demos ever made. Pointy hat off.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Praline, Pulpo Corrosivo and Arkos, coded by Toms with graphics by Barjack and music by Targhan. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: A podium finish in a competitive oldskool 4K compo at Revision, packing hand-drawn character sprites and a tracked tune into four kilobytes, compressed with Shrinkler.

summary: sibCrew's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, coded by wbcbz7 and Denis Grachev with music by Nik-O, which won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2017.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017, beating the rest of the LowEnd demo field on home ground for Spectrum sceners.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Cyberpunks Unity that won the 8-bit 640k demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2006, with code by Alff and Elfh and music by Simon.
why: It took first place in its compo at Chaos Constructions 2006, one of the main Russian scene parties for Spectrum work.
highlights: colourful full-screen effect under the logo

summary: A 1K intro by Alone Coder for an enhanced ZX Spectrum, which won the Combined 8-Bit 1024b Intro compo at DiHalt 2013.
why: It took first place in a combined 8-bit 1K compo at DiHalt 2013, beating entries from other 8-bit platforms within a 1024-byte limit.

summary: Nah-Kolor's four-disk-side C64 demo, made with a large cast of guest coders, graphicians and musicians, that placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2023. This is the party version; Multiverse 100% followed at X 2024.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2024. Sceners single out the 'comafight' fighting sequence, the fake ending with more demo after it, the plasma zoomers and the homages to Censor, Booze and Fossil.
highlights: fake end and hidden extra demo

quote.text: What a behemoth! Lovely and well-crafted by a super-talented team. I really liked the fighting sequence, super well done.

summary: Black Box's Game Boy Color demo, placed 4th in the Console/Handheld compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2004, with code by Credo and Merlin, music by Fusion and full-screen artwork from guest artists.
why: A Game Boy Color demo that brought in guest artists Enok/Exceed, Poison/Singular Crew and Angelday for its full-screen pictures and logos.

summary: A C64 demo by Prosonix and Offence with an alien theme, placed 8th in the demo compo at X 2016. Pal's pictures include a Trump portrait and an alien band playing beside a crashed saucer.
why: Sceners single out Pal's pixel art and the music, and note how much content was built in about five weeks, much of it coded at the party. Effects built from letters and words also get mentions.

quote.text: The alien concert suddenly materializing near the wrecked soucer was the coolest surprise I've seen in a long time. Such great pixel art too.

summary: A C64 4K intro by 4mat and Street Tuff, released in June 2010 during the World Cup: a silhouetted vuvuzela player against the South African flag, with SID sound imitating the horn's drone.
why: A topical joke that landed well. Sceners laughed at how convincingly the SID recreates the vuvuzela, and one likened it to something the 1986 scene would have made.

quote.text: Extremely authentic--it feels like exactly the sort of thing the scene circa 1986 could and would have done.

summary: Joker's 8K ZX Spectrum intro, coded by Dalthon with music by MCH and Pator, which won the ZX Spectrum Intro compo at Xenium 2022. Its original idea is credited to Luke and Wacek.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum intro compo at Xenium 2022. The video is a live recording from the party hall.

summary: Synergy 2 is an Amstrad CPC demo by Impact from 2008, with code by CMP, graphics by BDC Iron and music by Tom&Jerry. Grim linked it and built a cheat part with Supersly and PulkoMandy.
why: A CPC group production with a hidden cheat part that has its own 32K picture and a PulkoMandy cover of a Jonathan Dunn tune.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Resource, coded by Bubis and Edhellon with music by guest artist Jeff, that came second in the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2010.
why: Sceners praise its single effect for its real sense of depth, and say Jeff's tune suits it well. Fitting it into 4K drew credit too.

quote.text: Nice effect, a real sense of depth and the tune suits it well.

summary: Bandwagon's MSX demo from 1998, which won the wild compo at Zoo 1998.
why: A compo winner at Zoo 1998 and well regarded on Pouët, it's a good example of what the MSX scene was doing in the late 1990s.

summary: Triad's minimal, concept-driven C64 demo that came second in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2004: slow, text-free abstract visuals set to ambient music.
why: Sceners praise its calm tempo and restrained design, several saying it should have won the compo. Some found the parts overlong, but many describe it as something to drift away to.

quote.text: I love the calm tempo, it takes a lot of your attention. Its just like listening to the rain or experience a sunset over an open sea.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Tjoppen, who also wrote the code. It placed 9th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2012.
why: A one-person 4K production on the Atari 2600, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, shown at a major German party's alternative-platforms competition.

summary: A small Atari 2600 demo by Noice, coded by Shadow with music by Jakub Husak. It came 6th in the Atari 8-bit Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10.
why: A rare VCS entry in an Atari 8-bit demo compo, worth a look for what Shadow squeezed out of the 2600 at Silly Venture 2010.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo, placed third in the Wild compo at Revision 2025. You plug the audio and video cables in the wrong way round, so the SID makes the picture and the video chip makes the sound.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Concept at The Meteoriks 2026. Sceners praise it as a simple idea with a lot of complexity underneath, and single out the smooth greyscales, the raster effects and the sample at the end.

quote.text: Still the exact same hardware, but a completely new result that feels alien, maybe from near a black hole where the laws of physics don't apply.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo, also known as the VIP4 demo, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2002. A group effort with code by Jede, Twilighte and Dbug and graphics from several artists.
why: It took first place in the Oldschool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2002, and it brings together a large part of the Oric scene's coders and artists in one production.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Dirty Minds, coded by Optimus with music by Aki, that won the CPC Demo compo at Forever 2006.
why: It took first place in the CPC demo competition at Forever 2006, a good example of mid-2000s CPC coding from Optimus.

summary: A Commodore 64 1K intro by 4mat, released under the Ate Bit name, that won the Commodore 1K Intro compo at Forever 2007 (Forever 8).
why: Sceners were struck by how much fits in 1K, singling out the music and its use of samples. One later viewer still wondered how it could even have digis at that size.

quote.text: How the heck is this 1k? Awesome! It even has digis!

summary: Lethargy's two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo, released for the group's anniversary, which won the demo compo at Árok 2021. Code by Visage, Ego, Strepto and others, graphics by Grass, Poison and Leon, music by Vincenzo.
why: Sceners single out Vincenzo's soundtrack, the graphics in the vertical megascroller, the tunnel and a funny end part, along with the bitmap scroller of famous scene names and logos at the start.

quote.text: the gfx in the vertical megascroller rule and the tunnel is awesome. endpart is funny for sure.

summary: Cycleburner's C64 4K intro, second in the 4K Intro compo at X 2023: a minimalist show built around numbers counting through screen memory locations, with a cursor block wandering the screen and out into the border.
why: Sceners single out the original concept and its humour, a clever idea carried through with lots of small details in a very sparse presentation. Many named it a favourite of the party.

quote.text: There's so many clever details with such a minimalistic presentation. It all comes together as very entertaining show, I love it!

summary: Padua's single-file C64 demo, coded by LHS with music by PCH and Sad, which won the Commodore Demo compo at Forever 2008.
why: Sceners note how much is crammed into one file, and single out the 512-dot rotating teapot, the filled vector show and PCH's tune in the second half. Some found the frame rate slow.

quote.text: Really entertaining, and neat design too. I like it a lot.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that placed 2nd in the 8 Bit Intro 256b compo at Multimatograf 2017.
why: A second place at Multimatograf for an intro that fits sound as well as visuals into 256 bytes.
highlights: pulsing bars like a level meter

summary: Atari 2600 demo by Onslaught and Disaster Area, with code by Krion, graphics by Almighty God and music by cTrix. It won the oldschool demo compo at Flashback 2019.
why: A compo winner at Flashback 2019 on one of the most restrictive machines a demo can target. The video is a real-hardware PAL capture.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, made entirely by Gasman (code, graphics and AY music), which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2006.
why: A first place at Forever 2006 from a one-person effort, with Gasman handling every part of the production himself. It runs on a stock 48K machine.

summary: sibCrew's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the 8 Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2017, with code by Denchik, graphics by rook and music by Olezhik.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf 2017 from the Siberian group, with a large team credited for code, graphics, ASCII art and music.
highlights: "To LDIR or not to LDIR" screen

summary: Silicon Limited's C64 demo, coded and scored by Scout with graphics by Tim, which came second in the demo compo at Primary Star 2005.
why: A comeback release, reportedly made in three weeks after years of silence. Sceners single out its style, smooth transitions, funky graphics and Scout's tune.

quote.text: Slick. It's got style, it's got great transitions. Made me happy.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, a picture shown in a new 1280-colour interlaced graphics mode with a scroller over it. It came second in the combined demo/intro compo at Nordlicht 2012.
why: Sceners who saw it on real hardware were struck by how the new mode removes almost all the flicker of standard interlace, and by the transparent scroller.

quote.text: i saw the standard interlace version which flickered pretty good and this new mode which manages to remove the flickering almost completely.

summary: Fatzone's Commodore 64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2011.
why: Sceners called it one of the pleasant surprises of the compo and a clear step up from Fatzone's earlier work. The waves, twister and diagonal bars get singled out.

quote.text: a nice surprise during the compo, neat stuff. enjoyed it.

summary: Kowalski's 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro with sound, which won the 8 Bit Intro 256b compo at Multimatograf 2017.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte category at Multimatograf 2017, and one of the size-limited intros that manages sound as well as visuals.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by mayHem, Alone Coder and Hooy-Program for the ATM Turbo 2 clone, recorded on ZX Evolution with NeoGS sound. It came second in the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2013.
why: A runner-up at ZX AAA Compo 2013 that targets the Russian ATM Turbo 2 clone rather than a stock Spectrum, with music by Yerzmyey on the General Sound card. The scroller notes it was the group's first demo with GS music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC 4K intro by Pulpo Corrosivo, with code and graphics by Toms and music by Tom et Jerry. It placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2023.
why: It made the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist, a sign it stood out among that year's releases despite its modest compo placing.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 demo by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, graphics by Pal, music by Response and text by tFt. It shared second place in the Combined Real-Time compo at Black Valley 2023.
why: A party scroller from two groups working together. It tied for second place in the combined real-time compo at Black Valley 2023.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum demo, placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2006, with code and graphics by evilpaul, more graphics from Eater and Rudsy, and music by 4mat.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2006 from a small team, with three credited graphicians, which shows in the mix of bold blocky shapes and detailed pictures.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Agenda, coded by Svoy, which placed third in the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A podium finish in a crowded size-limited compo at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, from a 256-byte program.

summary: A short C64 demo by Panda Design, with code and music by radiantx and graphics by Frost, that placed third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2010.
why: Sceners praise its stylish design, Frost's graphics and especially radiantx's drum-and-bass soundtrack. The overlay-patterns screen gets singled out, though many wished it ran longer.

quote.text: The first "screen" is amazing. Great gfx through the whole demo and very stylish along with a nice soundtrack.

summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Demo compo at DiHalt 2026 Summer, with code and graphics by Tutty, concept and code by Trefi, and music by C-jeff and Riskej.
why: A first place in the DiHalt 2026 Summer demo competition, and it was well received on Pouët.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, an 8-bit lyric video for Darude's Sandstorm, with code, music and graphics by Gasman and graphics by rc55. It came second in Realtime Wild at Outline 2017.
why: A karaoke-style joke prod that placed second in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2017, done on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: A ZX Spectrum Enhanced demo by Hacker VBI that won the ZX Spectrum Enhanced Demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2014.
why: It took first place in its compo at 3BM OpenAir 2014, which makes it a good look at what Hacker VBI could do on the extended Spectrum platforms.

summary: A Game Boy Color demo by Dual Crew Shining from 2000, with code by Sasq, graphics by Vodka, music by Laxity and a DCS logo by Iridon. The video is filmed on a real Game Boy Color.
why: No compo placing or comments to go on, but it's a Game Boy Color demo from a group whose credits include Laxity on music, and the capture shows it running on original hardware.
highlights: filmed on a real Game Boy Color

summary: A 32-byte-category Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, released in May 2011. The video title gives its actual size as 23 bytes.
why: An example of how much can be squeezed from a couple of dozen bytes on the Atari. It's tagged as a glitch and noise piece, and was well received on Pouët.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K intro from RET and Darklite, code by Neon and music by Ref, that came 9th in the Demo compo at Outline 2023. A big wavy scroller runs across a starfield beneath a static credits screen.
why: Tagged as a demake: the on-screen credits say the original intro was by Dan & Mat, and this brings it to the Spectrum for Outline 2023.

summary: An Oric 40k intro by Dbug of NeXT and Defence Force, made for the C64 Times Revisited compo at STNICCC 2000, where it took first place.
why: It won its compo at STNICCC 2000, an Oric entry coming out on top in a competition themed around revisiting the C64.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Busy and Noro that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Demobit 1995.
why: A compo winner from Demobit 1995, tagged for its use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which gets past the machine's usual attribute-colour limits.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2021.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian-speaking scene parties, and well received on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit (code) and stRing (music) that placed second in the 256b intro compo at Decrunch 2020. It shows a rotating spiral galaxy against a starfield.
why: It was nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, and it fits both visuals and sound into 256 bytes. The source code is available.

summary: Noice's demo for the TI-83 graphing calculator, filmed on the device itself, which placed 2nd in the wild demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2002.
why: A calculator demo that took second place in a wild compo at Mekka & Symposium, and an early example of the TI-8x scene showing up at a major European party.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Osmium Path, with code by Optimus and graphics and music by Ham. It placed 4th in the Combined Demo compo at Demosplash 2024.
why: A recent example of a size-limited CPC intro from Optimus and Ham that held its own in a mixed-platform demo compo at Demosplash 2024.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Dalthon of Joker that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2022.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at DiHalt 2022, a neat example of what fits into 256 bytes on a stock Spectrum.

summary: Booze Design's single-file C64 demo for a 512K REU memory expansion, which won the C64 demo compo at The REU Compo 2015. Code by HCL and Ruk, graphics and music by Dane, charset by Valsary.
why: Sceners saw it as the first demo to push the REU really hard, with record-breaking screens packed into about five minutes. Its sideborder tricks even exposed gaps in REU emulation and in how people thought the hardware behaved.

quote.text: WOW, thats how one utilizes REU :) Great production. And all that in a single PRG.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo that won the Oldschool demo compo at Nordlicht 2014, built around a Chuck Rock-style band scene with a rock soundtrack by Celticdesign, sampled drums and a fast custom loader by Bitbreaker.
why: Sceners singled out the full-frame character animation, the mix of samples and SID, a catchy tune they rated above the original game music, and a loader quick enough to draw comment.

quote.text: Nice little prod. Full frame char animation rocked the most for me! :)

summary: Origo Dreamline's three-part C64 scroller demo that won the C64 demo compo at Horizon Easter Party 1990, with large colourful scrolling fonts, a shiny logo and a Star Wars scroller end part.
why: Sceners remember the reaction at Horizon 1990 and single out the colours above all: a logo that showed the C64 could look that shiny, an early AFLI picture, the big three-colour scrolling font, and music by Mixer and Zardax.

quote.text: First time I saw that logo my jaw hit the floor; I had no idea the hardware was capable of anything that shiny.

summary: Pulpo Corrosivo's Amstrad CPC demo, coded and directed by Toms with music by Targhan, which placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019.
why: A Revision oldskool compo entry from the CPC, with textured graphics from Beb and Barjack and logos and a picture by rexbeng. Tagged for its tunnel and rubber-vector effects.

summary: Megastyle's 1993 Commodore 64 demo, also known as Digital Messiah: a dark, atmospheric piece told in separate chapters, with large drawn pictures, a rune font and an endscroller.
why: Sceners call it an overlooked classic that chose style and concept over technical showing-off. They single out the atmosphere, the chaptered design and the metal SID soundtrack, though several grumble about the slow loader.

quote.text: These guys went for style and a concept, not a tech demo. I love what they did and like a few others they prove you don't always need some tech revolution to impress.

summary: Singular's C64 invitation, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at QBParty 2017. A pixelled city picture by Poison and Leon opens it, then a 3D letter scroller glides over an isometric grid of waving blocks.
why: Sceners liked the scroller and the waving block routine, and one admitted to having no clue how the effect is done. Soci explained that the letters' perspective was switched off in Blender to match the isometric background.

quote.text: I really like the scroller and the waving block routine very much!

summary: Fit's PETSCII demo for the C64, with a Plus/4 version too, that won the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2013. Code by Dr. TerrorZ and Marq, graphics by Dr. TerrorZ, music by Yzi.
why: Sceners praise its character-mode art and animation, the goth girl band and the vertical scroller with a shadow, all carried by Yzi's tune. Some still count it among their favourite PETSCII pieces years later.

quote.text: Awesome PETSCII demo, with brilliant PETSCII art!

summary: A small one-file C64 demo by Gheymaid Inc., placed 8th in the 8-bit demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Code and charsets by Motion, a picture by Helm and music by Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out the moody soundtrack, the lovely charsets and Helm's picture, which one commenter said has a mid-80s Compunet feel. Its appeal is atmosphere rather than technical show.

quote.text: Beautiful little production here...great music and graphics create a wonderful atmosphere

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music) that won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2017. Rows of solid-shaded 3D cubes spin in a grid of colourful panels.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2017 that fits rotating filled cubes and a soundtrack into a single kilobyte.

summary: Censor Design's Matrix-themed C64 demo, third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013, with a borderless Matrix character effect, a plasma, a Trinity picture and a tribute part to Mogwai.
why: Sceners single out the Matrix character effect spilling into the side border, an unusually good-looking 8x8 plasma and Prowler's end picture. The Mogwai part, set to an old Future Freak tune, touched many viewers.

quote.text: It's also amazing that new ways to exploit the hardware can still be found in 2013.

summary: Single-effect C64 demo by Panoramic Designs and Prosonix, code by Bjørn Røstøen and music by Stein Pedersen, released as part 2 of the Pandemoniac series. It placed 3rd in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer.
why: Sceners call it one of the prettiest twister-type effects on the C64, praising how smooth and mesmerising the swirl is and how well Stein Pedersen's tune sets the mood. Several wished it had been part of a bigger demo.

quote.text: One of the prettiest twister-type effects on c-64.

summary: An MSX demo by Lieves!Tuore, with code by Marq, music by Yzi and graphics by Manu. It placed 9th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: A modern MSX production from a Finnish-scene group, entered at Revision 2013. It's worth a look for its blocky, brightly coloured character-grid visuals.

summary: Aids' Atari 8-bit demo from 1999, coded by MacGyver with music by Teque and Ce-Pumpkin, which won the demo competition at Last Party 1999.
why: A compo winner from the late-1990s Polish Atari scene. Its credits screen is candid, with MacGyver writing that only the scroller is the reason for his pride.
highlights: scroller the coder was proud of

summary: A C16/Plus 4 tribute demo by Monarchy, coded by Csio, which won the demo compo at Árok 2011. Its German title translates as "He passed away peacefully".
why: It won its compo at Árok 2011 and is a memorial piece rather than a straight effects show, which makes it a less common kind of Plus 4 demo.

summary: A C64 4K intro by AEG of Smash Designs and Axis of Oxyron, placed third in the C64 4K compo at Breakpoint 2003: a full-screen rotozoomer over a tiled texture of shaded spheres.
why: The authors claimed a full-screen 2x2-pixel rotozoomer at 25 fps had never been done before, and sceners still puzzle over how it fits in 4K, with coders picking apart the technique years later.

quote.text: 2x2 is a wild resolution for a zoom-rotate-stretcher!

summary: A one-person Atari 2600 demo by Tjoppen, who did the code, graphics and music, placed third in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11.
why: A solo VCS production that took third at Silly Venture 2k11, with its source code released for anyone curious how it was done on the 2600.

summary: A short Commodore 64 demo by Slipstream, with code by TMR, graphics by Bully The Kid and TMR, and music by Scarzix. It came 2nd in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2015.
why: Sceners single out Scarzix's music above all, along with the fresh, stylish effects. One called it the best $d016 noise glitch yet on the C64 and praised the line-colour-masking face.

quote.text: Stylish, fresh, solid, powerful. Excellent stuff!

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by The Electronic Knights (TÉK), placed second in the 8-bit demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008.
why: A second place in a mixed 8-bit demo competition is a solid showing for a C16/Plus 4 production against other machines.

summary: Panda Design's C64 demo built around a social-media theme, which won the Combined Demo compo at Gerp 2016. Hires graphics, a twisting mobile phone part and a snake part run to a single soundtrack.
why: Sceners praise its coherent theme and pacing, the stylish hires graphics and the music, and welcome its social commentary. Several say it held their attention to the end.

quote.text: what i miss in contemporary c64 scene productions is exactly THIS - a social commentary, a non-mathematical feeling, a human factor.

summary: A 1K intro for the Vectrex by Realm Of Illusion, a vector-drawn Christmas tree with a "Happy New Year" message, which won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2023.
why: A compo winner squeezed into a single kilobyte on the vector-display Vectrex, and the source is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Camelot's C64 intro from X 2010, where it placed 8th in the demo compo. Code and graphics by Cruzer, music by Linus: a colourful plasma part with palm trees and fruit, plus text pages and greetings.
why: Presented as a part too lame for their coming demo, yet sceners rate its smooth, colourful 2x2-style plasma among the best on the C64. Linus's Hawaiian-flavoured tune gets plenty of praise too, and Cruzer later wrote a white paper explaining the plasma.

quote.text: Everything so smooth and colorful. A short but great gem.

summary: A small C64 plasma demo by Undone, with code and music by Encore, that came 2nd in the demo compo at Gubbdata 2013. A run of plasmas drawn in tiny triangle patterns.
why: Sceners praise the music as much as the visuals and call the plasmas original and fresh. Encore credits late pattern variations on the colour RAM routine, using extended colour mode, for their extra depth.

quote.text: really great, coolest c64 plasma i've seen i reckon. tiny triangles make it rule!

summary: An NES demo by Otomata Labs, with code by AArt1256 and Natt, graphics by Grongy and music by Nik-O. It took third place in the Oldskool Demo competition at Revision 2025.
why: A podium finish in a strong Revision oldskool compo, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist, which marks it as one of the year's notable releases.

summary: Onslaught's Vectrex demo, coded by Razdee and Elder0010 with music by MAT64, which came second in the Retro/alternative intro/demo compo at Flashparty 2020.
why: A rare demo for the vector-display Vectrex from a group better known on the C64, placed second at Flashparty 2020. The video is real hardware footage of the glowing screen.

summary: Xanth F/X's 1986 Atari 8-bit demo, coded and designed by Michael Park: the Atari Fuji logo spins and bounces over a red-and-white checkerboard, captioned "FujiBoink!".
why: One of the early Atari 8-bit demos, from 1986. It is widely known as Atari's answer to the Amiga's famous bouncing Boing Ball demo.

summary: Brainwave's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2001, with code by Vivid, music by Megus, graphics by Pheel and design by Tigrr.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties. It is tagged for stellar mode and Spectrum multicolour, both ways of getting more colour out of the machine than its usual attribute limits allow.

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII demo for the C64, placed 6th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013: an animated pirate story by acidT*rroreast, coded by Mathman with music by Goto80.
why: Sceners single out its direction and tight sync between Goto80's music and the animation, along with its humour and glitchy, deliberately uncomfortable feel. Some found the flicker irritating, though others see it as part of the music.

quote.text: So superb in originality and execution, makes everything else in the compo look a bit like the same.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro coded by JAC!, placed third in the Atari XL/XE 256b compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A podium finish in a 256-byte compo at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, from a prod small enough to fit in a couple of lines of hex.

summary: Atlantis's C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer, with code by Dr. Science and others, graphics by Diamond Design and FatFrost, and music by Ald and DivertigO.
why: Sceners called it Atlantis's best demo to date, praising its flow, transitions, stylish design and effects that aren't trivial to code. Diamond Design's graphics drew particular mention.

quote.text: This is an awesome demo with nice effects, good graphics, coherent theme and cozy beats.

summary: Smash Designs and The Starforce's C64 demo, coded and drawn by AEG with music by SoNiC, which came third in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: Divided opinion at release over polish and recycled effects, but sceners praise the soundtrack, AEG's solid code and the way effects are embedded into the graphics.

quote.text: All together it went wonderfully and the soundtrack is one of the best ones out there.

summary: Chaos is a demo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Absence And Wilds, released in February 2005.
why: A joint production between two groups on the Plus/4, a less-travelled Commodore machine. It's well regarded on Pouët, where nobody has voted it down.

summary: Camelot's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2004: a press-space run of code-first parts by Cruzer, with music from DRAX, Fanta and Jeff.
why: A deliberately oldskool, effects-over-design demo. Sceners single out the diagonal raster bars and the closing 16-colour hires plasma, which some watched for half an hour.
highlights: music by DRAX, Fanta and Jeff

quote.text: despite its simpleness (codewise) the tilted rasters are fucking spectacular, and so well executed it would be hard to top it. Another highlight is the last plasma part.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource and Logicoma, coded by Edhellon and Oswald with music by H0ffman and graphics by Poison. It won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2023.
why: A compo winner at Revision 2023, one of the bigger stages for size-limited oldskool work, and a rare chance to see the Plus 4 in a 4K intro.

summary: Hokuto Force's C64 conversion of the opening cutscene from Another World, coded and drawn by Majikeyric with music by Uctumi. It won the Retro Demo compo at Flashparty 2019.
why: Sceners praise how faithfully the game's famous intro cinematic comes across as full-frame animation on the C64, with the final part where the hero climbs out of the water singled out.
highlights: hero climbing out of the water

quote.text: impressive work guyz!!! what a beautiful full-frame animation.

summary: Fairlight and Genesis Project's C64 demo built around ghostbyte tricks, coded by Trident with graphics by Pal, The Sarge and Redcrab and music by Fegolhuzz. It won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2024.
why: Coders single out hires graphics on the borders that seem to cross every boundary, done with ghostbytes, a field they thought was fully explored. Sceners also praise the soundtrack, the rain scene and the Panoramic tribute.

quote.text: Wow. What a demo. Makes it feel like the c64 never had any borders. Mad coding skills. Fresh ideas.

summary: Unbound is an Atari Lynx demo by New Generation that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Xenium 2025. Code is by Solo and Laoo, graphics by Tiger, kris3d and AquaSixio, and music by ZoltarX and Loop.
why: It won its compo at Xenium 2025 and was nominated for Best production at ZBOWiD 2026. Demos on the Atari Lynx are rare, which makes this a notable recent example for the handheld.
highlights: shaded cubes over a detailed picture

summary: Camelot's 16K C64 intro, coded and drawn by Cruzer with music by Homo Sidiens, which came second in the Intro category at Intro Creation Competition 2018. A cloud-textured Camelot logo sits between scrollers running in the top and bottom borders.
why: Sceners single out the cloud effect in the logo and the border scrollers, which several call impossible. Commenters describe it as demo material in intro size.

quote.text: That is top notch trickery stuff. Demo material in intro size. Both fx are amazing, don't understand the clouds fx yet.

summary: An Amstrad CPC cracktro by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded, drawn and scored by Raft, which placed third in the Intro compo at @Party 2015.
why: A one-person production that placed in a party compo, done in the classic trainer-menu style with options, credits and greetings.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation to Silly Venture 2016 by Mystic Bytes, F#READY and Lamers, which placed 2nd in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2016. A big party logo sits under a cyclist riding across a desert strip while a scroller gives the details.
why: A party invitation that took second place in Outline 2016's Realtime Wild compo, with code by Wieczor and F#READY and graphics from mOOnie, Odyn1ec and Wieczor.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Speccy.pl, coded by Tygrys with AY music by V0yager and graphics by CatMan and Piesiu. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2015.
why: A third place at Riverwash 2015 from the Polish Speccy.pl crew, and it runs on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: EXclusive ON's 16K C64 intro, coded and scored by Jammer with a charset logo by Joe, which won the Intro Creation Competition 2018: a big 3D-looking EXON logo over a bouncing, tilted-letter scroller.
why: Sceners single out the scroller, with each letter tilted as if it had bounced into place, plus the speed-up and slow-down of the scroll, the catchy tune and how tightly it all syncs.

quote.text: the tilting of the charset is especially cool as it gives the impression the letters just bounced there randomly. Also the speedup/slowdown of the scroll is perfect.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Plush, with code by Krill, graphics by Caprice and music by Fanta, that won the C64 4K intro compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000.
why: A compo winner that sceners still rate highly. They single out its clean, clear look and its lined effects, which Krill says were inspired by an earlier release.

quote.text: One of the top productions in the past, looking just as clean and clear today. I always liked those lined effects

summary: Oxyron's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, the joystick-sized C64 clone, which placed joint second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2018. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by dEViLOCk, graphics by Yazoo.
why: A rare chance to see what the DTV can do. Sceners praise how smooth it all runs and single out the rotating triangle tunnel, and some felt it deserved the win.

quote.text: i'm not familiar with DTV specs but all looks so smooth to me, o'som gfx and speed together with sid vibes makes me smile.

summary: Oxyron's New Year 8K intro for the C64, coded by Axis with graphics by Yazoo and music by Linus. It won the 8K Intro Competition 2017 and greets 2018 with a crossed layout of horizontal and vertical scrolling parts.
why: Sceners point to the screen set-up of horizontal and vertical parts and the antialiased vector, and to how much was fitted into 8K. It took first place in its compo.

quote.text: Nice what you put into 8k!! One of my favourites in the compo!

summary: Noice's first demo for the Commodore 64-DTV (the DTV2/Hummer), a short one-filer released in May 2007 and recorded off a TV screen by its author.
why: An early demo made for the C64-DTV hardware. Sceners called it nice for first DTV work and said it showed the machine's potential, though some found it short.

quote.text: shows the potential of the dtv

summary: Desire's Atari XL/XE demo, placing second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k24 WE. The video title calls it a 12k intro, built around flat-shaded 3D scenes.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, with a dedicated 3D engine by Probe and 3D scenes designed by Heaven.

summary: Benediction's 32K intro for the Amstrad CPC, with code and text by Eliot, graphics by Voxfreax and music by Dma-Sc. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #3 in 2023.
why: A compo winner at Benediction's own coding party, and a compact 32K showcase from a long-running CPC group.

summary: Simon Quernhorst's Atari VCS demo, with music by Manuel Polik and design help from Falk Heinzelmann, placed 6th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2008.
why: A rare demo for the Atari 2600, a machine with very little to work with, shown in a mixed console and wild compo at Breakpoint.

summary: A one-file demo by Oxyron for the Commodore 64 DTV: a field of 3068 sine-plotted dots swirls above Yazoo's colourful Oxyron logo while a scroller runs between them.
why: One of the few DTV demos of its time. Sceners praised the fast blitter-driven plotting routine, the logo using more than 16 colours and the music, which manages without the SID filters the DTV lacks.

quote.text: Most beautiful sineplots ever! Stylish logo too!

summary: An invitation intro for Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo and Futurs', with code by Toms, music by Zik on a patched player and graphics by Beb.
why: A joint invitation from two groups, released with little else on record. The fact sheet notes no compo entry or awards, so it stands as a short party invitro for CPC followers.

summary: The Graphic Demo is a 1986 Atari 8-bit demo pack from Compy-Shop, with code, graphics and music by Peter Sabath and additional graphics by Frogdesign.
why: An early Atari 8-bit demo from the mid-eighties, made largely by one person, and a look at what the machine's commercial software scene was showing off at the time.
highlights: Compy Shop logo over colour bars

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, released at Sundown 2014 where it took second place in the Old School Demo competition. The video is a camera recording of the big-screen showing at the party.
why: A podium finish at Sundown 2014 in the Old School Demo compo, and it runs on a stock 48K Spectrum with AY music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders from 2009, coded by Candy with a logo by Beb, font by Barjack and music by Tom&Jerry. A tomato logo sits beside a framed window of greetings text over a moving pattern.
why: No placings or comments to go on, but it's a compact single-screen Overlanders production with a full credit line of code, graphics and music.

summary: wAMMA's Atari 2600 demo, coded by visy, Ilmarque and tatu, which placed 4th in the combined demo compo at Simulaatio 2007.
why: A scene demo on the VCS, one of the most cramped machines there is, with tatu credited separately for raster effects and Ilmarque handling the music as well as code and graphics.

summary: TSJ's tongue-in-cheek C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Fioniadata 2026, with code by Trap, graphics by The Sarge and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners singled out Jammer's soundtrack above all, along with The Sarge's pixels and the cheeky humour. Several call it entertaining and well made despite, or because of, its daft theme.

quote.text: I dig. I hate picking up anyone with such a hard core lineup, but I'm going to do it anyway... that track by Jammer, oh my.

summary: Fairlight's short C64 demo from Big Floppy People 2007, where it came third in the C64 demo compo. Code and graphics by Hollowman and Oxidy, music by Fegolhuzz.
why: Sceners single out Fegolhuzz's tune and the lava-lamp test tube, and like its style despite finding it too short. Some at the party preferred it to the two demos placed above it.

quote.text: Cool style and really neat lavalamp/test tube/alien blood cocktail.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo, coded and drawn by AEG with music by SoNiC, which took third in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001.
why: Sceners single out its Doom-style raycaster part, praised for running in 16 colours, along with SoNiC's soundtrack. Some note it recycles less than other Triage releases, though others find its zoomers and rotators rough.

quote.text: the doom part is still unmatched with its 16 colors.... coders anyone ? :)

summary: Extend's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2026, mixing hand-coded effects with new animation players built over two years.
why: Sceners praise its distinctive, forward-looking style, pacing and a soundtrack that evolves as essentially one track through the demo; several compare its vibe to early Orange PC demos.

quote.text: Far beyond the usual wankery of being able to place one more sprite on the screen compared to the previous record holder and yet it's also technically impressive.

summary: A 2K intro for the Atari VCS, coded by SvOlli with music by SunSpire, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2017.
why: It took first place in Deadline 2017's Oldschool Demo compo, beating full-size entries with a 2K Atari 2600 cartridge.

summary: Reflex's ninth C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1996. Code by Zorc and Adder, music by Jeff and Praiser, and pictures from Earthquake, Felidae, Amoeba and Warp 8.
why: Sceners remember it as a strong showing after several big names had left the C64, with effects new to the machine at the time: landscape, blobs, a fractal colour zoomer, a chessboard flight and rotozoomers. The ski animation drew cheers in the hall.

quote.text: For its time, it had quite some revolutionary effects on C64 such as landscape, blob potentials, fractal colorzoomer, flight through chessboards and many rotzoomers.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo coded by Jack with music by Mad Max, released at the RTS 1998 party, where it won the OldSkool Demos on pre-1990 machines compo.
why: It took first place in the old-school demo compo at RTS 1998, the party it is named after, so it's a good look at the CPC scene's late-1990s work.

summary: Samar Productions and EXclusive ON's C64 tribute to The Prodigy's Keith Flint, second in the C64 demo compo at Forever 2019: a large portrait, a lower-border sprite scroller and Jammer's cover of Voodoo People.
why: Sceners single out Jammer's cover, built without samples on a 50Hz tune, along with the artwork and scrolltext. Most of the code was put together in a single day at the party.

quote.text: The music, the artwork, the scrolltext. A perfect tribute for a heartfelt loss.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2015.
why: It took first place in DiHalt 2015's combined 8-bit demo competition, beating entries from other 8-bit machines.

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII demo for the Commodore 64, placed 7th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Graphics by acidT*rroreast, music by Goto80, code by Mathman, running as an endless loop.
why: Sceners praise the tight sync between Goto80's music and the graphics, the fitting sound effects and the sense of things breaking apart, and say the PETSCII scenes reward repeat viewing.

quote.text: those PETSCII diamonds are watchable so many times, you always find something new you've missed before.

summary: An Easter intro for the Atari 8-bit by Mad Team and Agenda, released on 1 April 2013, with code by Tebe, music by stRing and graphics by Ooz.
why: A small seasonal release from two Polish-scene groups. Its main draw is the large hand-drawn picture by Ooz, paired with stRing's music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders from 2002, with code, graphics and music shared between Madram, Eliot, Epsilon and BDC Iron, and extra graphics by Beb, Fafa and Grim.
why: A group effort from several Overlanders members. Its soundtrack includes AY covers of Harold Faltermeyer's Axel F. and Jeroen Tel's C64 Eliminator tune.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Kpacku, released in January 2017, with code and fonts by Trefi, graphics by Tutty and music by NQE.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it is tagged for the Spectrum's multicolour mode, and the credits show a small team behind code, graphics and music.
highlights: quotes from Picasso and Da Vinci

summary: Cosine's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by TMR with music by Bex, which won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2014. It plays out entirely in shades of grey.
why: It took first place in the Atari demo competition at Forever 2014.

summary: Dual Crew's C64 demo built around an FLI picture of Galactus, with sprite scrollers running over it. It came 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2013.
why: Sceners praised it as one of the best sprites-over-FLI parts they had seen, with the FLI bug so well hidden that it hardly looks like FLI. They also liked ne7's soundtrack.

quote.text: This is real quality shit! One of the best sprites-over-fli parts i have seen.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Taquart, coded by Eru, which came second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2004.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited compo at Forever 2004, showing what Eru could fit into a single kilobyte on the Atari.

summary: A New Year greeting demo by Buyan and Splinter for an enhanced ZX Spectrum, released in January 2015. It won the New Year Gift compo at CC Winter / DiHalt Lite.2015.
why: It took first place in its New Year Gift compo, and is a short seasonal card from the Russian Spectrum scene.

summary: New Generation's Atari Lynx demo that won the Lynx demo compo at Silly Venture 2k20+1 SE in 2021, set to Gydra's drum and bass track "Hearing Damage".
why: A compo winner on a rarely used handheld. Solo and Laoo share the code, and Solo, Tiger and kris3d made the graphics, including 3D work.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music) that won the Atari 1K compo at Forever 2015. Grey silhouettes of objects stand on a beach-like horizon, each casting a long striped shadow.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2015 and was nominated for Best Low-End intro at The Meteoriks 2016, a rare showing for a 1K Atari production.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Transmission64 2023, coded by Trident with music by Fegolhuzz and graphics by Pal, tNG and Soya.
why: Nominated for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023. Sceners praise the char manipulations, the timing to the music and the activity in the borders, and marvel that Trident coded it almost alone.
highlights: scroller that moves with the beat

quote.text: Tasteful! Great code, gfx and music, all timed to perfection! Love the theme. And all the stuff going on in the borders.

summary: Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the 8 bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2004. A political piece in red on grey, with propaganda-style silhouettes and slogans.
why: A placing at Chaos Constructions and an unusual subject: tagged for communism, Lenin and anticapitalism, it's an openly political demo on the Spectrum.

summary: Samar Productions' two-disk-side C64 demo, the final version of the 95% release that won North Party '97, adding a clean directory and part selectors on both disk sides. Code by a large team, music by Daf and Dune.
why: Sceners single out its fast pace and the tight sync between effects and an unusual, break-heavy soundtrack; several call it Samar's best and one of their all-time favourite C64 demos.

quote.text: I'm still impressed by the great connection between the music and the effects.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by g0blinish, with music by Caruso. It came second in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A second place at Silly Venture in a size-limited category, and the source code is available for anyone curious how it fits in 16K.

summary: Crest's C64 demo, largely a one-man effort by Dane on code, graphics, music and text, that won the demo compo at Little Computer People 2002. It's built around X-FLI photographic portraits, with four tunes across the parts.
why: Sceners call it an insane one-man effort and single out the picture conversions and Dane's music, including his cover of Virt's "Flowerguy's Pool Party". The disks also carry extras such as the X-FLI editor and a part selector.

quote.text: Dane is not a trickster, but a full-blown C64 magician.

summary: CopperZoom is a 32-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, released in November 2012.
why: A 32-byte intro is about as small as size-limited code gets. This one is a compact example of what fits into that budget on the Atari.

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo, placing 2nd in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2019, with code by Noby, Mike, Gasman and Busy, and music and graphics by Aki and PG.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2019 from a crew pooling several well-known Spectrum coders, with an AY soundtrack made in Vortex Tracker II.

summary: Extend's C64 demo that came second in the demo compo at X 2006, with code by Barfly, Muhmi and Tape, music by Barracuda and graphics by Duce, all built around a kinky rubber-and-leather theme.
why: Sceners single out the unusual fetish theme carried through the whole demo, Barracuda's fitting soundtrack and the twisters, including a seven-colour one. Some found the graphics uneven.

quote.text: this demo rules. it has a spanking theme throughout the whole demo, which is rare. the awesome soundtrack fits very very well.

summary: Impact's Amstrad CPC demo released on Christmas Day 2023, with code and graphics by AST, further graphics by Kris and Hwikaa, and music by Tomchi.
why: A recent release from a long-running CPC group. The video title marks it as a CRTC-1 demo, written for that specific CPC display chip.

summary: Vanity's 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by e-dredon. A large chunky pixel picture of an eye sits under a scrolling text message.
why: Tagged as an entry in the rotozoomer challenge, it puts a rotozoomer into a 16K CPC intro. It was released in 2025 with no compo placing listed.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo built around subpixel rendering, with lft on music, which took third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2011. A slow, storybook-paced run of hires pictures and smoothly moving text.
why: Sceners praise it for trying something new and pulling it off, and for being a calm, stylish demo that earns its standing without much bang. Many likened it to leafing through a childhood storybook.

quote.text: absolutely loved this - really reminded me of some story books I read as a child.

summary: Phonics' C64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at Zoo 2024 (party version): a fast-cut, glitch-styled ride with rabbit animations and bold typography, split into an A-side and a B-side like a record.
why: Sceners single out its style, pacing and design over raw code, with Flotsam's techno soundtrack, the twerking bunnies and the mixed typography drawing most praise. Many felt it deserved a higher placing.

quote.text: Funky as hell! Great animations. Love the mix of fonts which change on the screen and the fast cut scenes. Really great audio-visual aesthetics!

summary: Noice's MSX2 demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by Rocket and music by Yerzmyey, which came second in the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2015.
why: A second place at Gerp 2015 against other platforms, and a recent example of a Noice production on the MSX2.
highlights: scroller text curving across the screen

summary: Proxima's demo for the original 32K BBC Micro, placing 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2021. Code by Leuat, music by mAZE and Mibri, graphics by Leuat, Optic and Hammerfist.
why: A rare modern demo for the stock BBC Micro that took second place at Deadline 2021. It is built with TRSE, Leuat's Turbo Rascal Syntax Error toolkit.

summary: Babygang's 1992 C64 demo, coded by Chocapoc, Ludwig and Mr. Stark with graphics by Cygnus. Parts include a panther picture and a kickboxer animation taken from the Amiga game Full Contact.
why: Sceners remember it as feeling different and fresh on release and still call it a classic. The panther part and the kickboxer animation are the parts they single out.

quote.text: I loved this for beeing different by the time it was released, and I still like it. One of the classics in my book.

summary: Lethargy's one-file C64 demo, third in the C64 demo compo at X 2024: a parade of recreated computer boot screens, from Commodore BASIC to the Amiga Kickstart ball to a Windows-style login.
why: Sceners call it clever, fun and well sequenced, a visual story about the C64 living on through later machines and emulation, carried by Vincenzo's funky tune.

quote.text: Evolution from C64 and 8bit in general to PC and from there towards emulation.

summary: Assassins' Plus/4 megademo, coded by Skoro with graphics by Kichy, Ati, Csabo and Chronos. It won the demo compo at Árok 2010.
why: A first-place compo winner at Árok 2010 and a full megademo from one of the Plus/4's best-known groups, with four graphicians credited.

summary: Padua's two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001. Code is by Lubber, with graphics from a large team including Hi-Lite and music from several composers.
