why: A runner-up at one of the big German parties of its day. Sceners praise its effects, though some find it long and slow-paced.

quote.text: nice effects

summary: Samar Productions' C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Silesia 8 in 2017, with code by Don Kichote, Skull, Slajerek and Isildur, graphics by Isildur and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners single out Isildur's art and sprites, the stylish design and Skull's fast, smooth filled vectors, which one coder said he had never seen before. Made in about a month before the party.

quote.text:
Beautiful mixture of hires and multicolor gfx with a cool sauce of tech stuff on top.
And damn those vectors are smooth.

summary: Vantage's Atari VCS demo, coded by Moerder with music by Decybel, which won the Alternative Demo compo at Buenzli 2004.
why: A first place at Buenzli 2004 for a demo on the Atari 2600, a machine with very little to work with.

summary: A Vectrex demo by Revival Studios, coded by superogue with music by Ryo-Ohki. Released in 2003, it later placed 4th in the Allround Real Time compo at Outline 2007.
why: A rare demo for the Vectrex's vector display, where everything is drawn as glowing lines rather than pixels. It made the top four of a mixed real-time compo at Outline 2007.

summary: Samar's debut C64 demo, the party version of I Love The Cube, which placed 4th in the demo compo at Silesia 5 2011. Code by Mr Wegi, graphics by Conrad and Isildur, music by Conrad.
why: Sceners praised its large, screen-filling effects, its many cubes and a plot scroller, and Conrad's music, especially the later tunes. Some found the pace slow. A final version followed.

quote.text: Love the last part, slow but big. The way I like it! :)

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Noice, released in 2009, with code by Shadow and music by Paul Slocum, who also supplied the music replay routine.
why: A rare demoscene outing on the Atari 2600, packed into 4K, with a soundtrack from Paul Slocum.

summary: SquoQuo's 32-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit, with sound, that placed 4th in the 256 Byte Intro compo at Function 2012 despite using only an eighth of the allowed size.
why: A tongue-in-cheek 'megademo' squeezed into 32 bytes, tagged as a glitch piece with sound, and its source is available for anyone curious how so little code does this much.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo from Les Sucres En Morceaux, released in 2006, with code and converted graphics by Supersly and music by Targhan. It plays as a run of green-tinted pictures, from a Climax logo to a still life and a cartoon mouse.
why: A small CPC demo that rests on Supersly's picture conversions and Targhan's music. It didn't compete anywhere, but it is well regarded on Pouët.
highlights: Climax logo over a closed eye

summary: Wrath Designs' monochrome C64 demo, coded and scored by Ed with graphics by Joe, which came second in the demo compo at Floppy 2001: greyscale photographic images overlaid with lines of text.
why: Sceners praise its unique style and new tricks, singling out the disk-streamed blur. A note from the group says Joe's darkroom photographs, made in 1998 from a poem by Francis Ponge, became this demo.

quote.text: Has very unique style and some nifty new tricks, that diskstreaming blur is really awesome!

summary: A Commodore PET demo by oobc, running on a CBM 8032, that won the Oldschool 8bit compo at Payback 2014. Code, graphics and music are by Bass Cadet and oo.
why: A compo winner on one of the least-used demo platforms, the monochrome green-screen PET, beating other 8-bit entries at Payback 2014.

summary: Alone Coder's ZX Spectrum border intro, placed third in the ZX Spectrum Border Intro compo at DiHalt 2012. A black cat silhouette sits under falling snow with Russian verse, a scroller and a big "How it works?" sign along the bottom.
why: A third place in a compo built around drawing in the Spectrum's border, an unusual corner of ZX coding, from a single coder who also did the animation.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari XL/XE by Agenda, coded by xeen with Gorgh, Koala and Svoy, with music by Caruso and graphics by Raphis and Piesiu.
why: It won the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k18, packing a run of colourful effects into 16 kilobytes.

summary: A 512-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Joker, with code by Dalthon and graphics by Vasyl, that won the Oldschool 512 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2022.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2022, fitting a procedurally drawn monochrome picture into 512 bytes.
highlights: picture filled in as it plays

summary: Lethargy's C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2022, with code from a large team including Visage, Oswald and Sei, music by Vincenzo and graphics by Grass, Slyspy and zscs.
why: Sceners single out the entertaining, funny tone, the powerful soundtrack and an interlude paying homage to old games, including a recreated Nebulus tower.

quote.text: Fantastic in coding, music & gfx. I love the games tribute interlude!

summary: Booze Design's one-file C64 demo for the ECM Mode Demoeffect Competition 2020, where it won the intro category: diagonal copper-style colour bars sweeping across the screen, built with Extended Colour Mode.
why: Sceners were surprised by how much it does from so little. Several admit the screenshot undersold it, and others are still puzzling over how it is done from just 64 characters. Dane's music gets extra praise.

quote.text: the best magic trick is when you know the trick but are still fooled anyway.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Moonshine Dragons 2024, with code by Bob, Firehawk, Peacemaker and Swallow, music by Linus and Magnar Harestad, and graphics by Carrion, CeD, DeeKay and Talent.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a Censor comeback and single out the colour cycling throughout, the four-colour sprite helix, the scrollers and a very smooth closing plasma. Several compare it to the group's Wonderland series.

quote.text: Censor seems to always say: Here's a cool effect... And oh, btw, here's another cool effect ON TOP of that one.

summary: Tjoppen's Nyan Cat demo for the Atari 2600, placed 6th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2011. The pixel cat and its rainbow trail fly across a starfield while a text scroller runs underneath.
why: A small, cheerful take on the 2011 Nyan Cat meme squeezed onto the VCS, with music by Brandon Carrita played through Paul Slocum's music player.

summary: Agenda's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k13. Code by Probe and xeen, graphics by Ripek and Ooz, music by stRing.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture 2k13, the main Atari 8-bit party, squeezed into 16 kilobytes.

summary: Viti's second C64-controlled laser show, filmed live with Jeroen Tel's Alternative Fuel as the soundtrack. It won the Wild Demo/Animation compo at Function 2014.
why: A rare case of a C64 driving real-world hardware. Sceners at Function say it dominated the wild compo at the party, and it follows Viti's first C64 laser show.

quote.text: It was a jawdropper again - and dominated all the wild compo releases at a multiplatform scene party, the biggest party in its history.

summary: Darklite's 256-byte procedural graphics prod for the ZX Spectrum, which won the oldskool procedural graphics compo at Lovebyte 2025. It draws an isometric city of dithered blocks and roads.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2025, packing a whole generated cityscape into 256 bytes on a stock Spectrum.

summary: bfox's 256-byte ZX Spectrum invitation for Lovebyte 2021, showing the party's logo with a red pixel heart, the dates and the web address. It placed third in the Lovebyte Tinyintro Invitation compo at OMZG 2021.
why: A complete party invitation, with sound, squeezed into 256 bytes on the Spectrum, and placed in a dedicated tiny-intro invitation compo.

summary: An Amstrad CPC 4K intro by Creative People for CPC, a team including Krusty, Eliot, Madram, Optimus and Voxfreax with music by Tom et Jerry, which came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2025.
why: A second place at Revision's Oldskool 4K compo from a large CPC collaboration packing several coders' effects into 4K. The source is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Paulko64's 16KB cartridge conversion of Canabalt for the C64, a one-button endless runner across collapsing rooftops. It placed 2nd in the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2011; the video shows the final cart version.
why: An official port that sceners compared closely with Mr SID's unofficial version, praising its smoothness and how faithfully it keeps the original's scale and look. The final cart added Encore's music and improved building generation.

quote.text: this version is closer to the original, the graphics and especially the scale relation between the figure and surrounding slabs, floor and door hights looks adequate. Fantastic work!

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by JAC!, MotionRide and Lucy that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18: a version of the Bad Apple shadow-art animation in black and white.
why: It won its compo at Silly Venture 2k18. It's an Atari take on the Bad Apple video that gets ported to so many platforms, with code by JAC!, music and graphics by MotionRide and narration by Lucy.

summary: Scoop's 1988 Commodore 64 demo, with code, graphics, charset and music by The Mercenary Cracker plus music by Jeroen Tel, entered in the demo competition at Commodore Dossier Demo Competition 1988.
why: Sceners remember it above all for its music, with the title tune often named among the best SIDs ever. They also credit its graphical style and font design as widely copied and say it still holds up through balance rather than big effects.

quote.text: This must be one of the most influential demos of all time, especially in terms of graphical style.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo from 1998, made single-handedly by HCL on code, graphics and music, which won the C64 demo compo at X 1998.
why: A one-man production that sceners praise for HCL's music as much as his code, with several rating it above Royal Arte and calling it tasteful and stylish.
highlights: HCL did code, graphics and music
sharp scrolling font drawn as it scrolls

quote.text: Nice...so tasteful and stylish.  Inspirational.

summary: Jumalauta's C64 intro by Ruuvari, who did the code, music and graphics alone, placing 3rd in the 64k intro compo at Simulaatio 2005. A raycast dungeon corridor scrolls behind horror-movie-trailer text.
why: A one-man production built around raycasting, an effect rarely seen on the C64, which earned it a podium place at Simulaatio 2005.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by PG and MaPa, with code by MaPa and graphics and music by PG. It won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2011.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2011 that fits its effect, graphics and music into a single kilobyte.

summary: Algotech's 2017 one-file Commodore 64 demo, a backport of Kaos to the 64. It packs sampled sound and animated visuals into a single 44kB file.
why: Sceners single out the quality of the samples and how much high-quality data fits in such a small file. Kruthers had long wanted to see it backported to the 64.

quote.text: This rocks with a violent intensity. C64 Power!

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Marquee Design, coded by superogue, that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Decrunch 2020.
why: Beat full-size entries to first place in a demo compo at just 256 bytes, and was nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021. A making-of writeup is available.

summary: Calodox's ZX81 4K intro, coded by Minas with graphics by Fred, which came second in the 4K compo at State of the Art 2004. It runs silently.
why: A rare ZX81 entry in a mainstream party 4K compo, and it placed second there.

summary: Resource's C64 invitation to the Revision 2011 Easter party, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2011. Text pages promoting the party scroll over a colourful plasma that spills into the borders.
why: Sceners single out the closing border plasma, which makes the grey borders look like part of the design, and Linus's drum'n'bass tune, which one commenter rates above earlier C64 attempts at the style.

quote.text: This track makes all previous C64 D&B tunes look pale. Linus, you rule.

summary: Performers' three-disk-side C64 demo with a pinball and arcade-hall theme, which came second in the demo compo at X 2026. A large team of coders, graphicians and musicians, plus a bonus disk.
why: Sceners single out the parallax train intro, the fluid multilayered transitions, the many zooming and rotating scrollers and the border-breaking vectors. Several said it held its own against the winner.
highlights: bonus disk with Wizard of Four

quote.text: Thank you for another wild ride. I love the attitude, the finesse, the freewheeling style...

summary: Lethargy's three-disk-side C64 demo, third in the demo compo at X 2026, built around an interlaced colour-mixing mode that blends PAL colours into new hues, kept running through a full demo of effects and pictures.
why: Sceners praise how consistently the new colour technique works across every effect, and Vincenzo's soundtrack. Several note it was made for a CRT and looks best on real hardware with saturation turned up.

quote.text: Incredible that you can keep the new color technique working in all the effects.

summary: Lepsi De and Miracles' C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Silesia 3 in 2009, with code by Zielok, music by Psycho8580 and graphics by Carrion and Sebaloz.
why: Sceners single out the polished look, the fresh design and graphics, and Psycho8580's memorable tune. It also marked a returning coder, Zielok, coming back after decades.

quote.text: The music is nice, the graphics are pretty and the 'plasma' is well crafted. The overall look of the demo is polished.

summary: Camelot's 2004 comeback demo for the C64, coded and drawn by Cruzer, with music by DRAX, Fanta, JCH and Jeff. A short run of old-school, spacebar-style parts.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a comeback with fast one-frame routines. They single out the large, smooth plasma, the glenz vector and the code discussion in the last part.

quote.text: The plasma is still an amazing effect. I still don't get how it can be so large, smooth and well.. plasmatic.

summary: Agenda's 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit, coded by Svoy, which came second in the Atari XL/XE 256b compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A runner-up in a competitive 256-byte category at Silly Venture, showing how much one coder can squeeze into a tiny Atari program.

summary: Camelot's ten-part C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1991, with guest music from JCH, Laxity, Jeroen Tel, Steel and others and code from Cruzer, Glasnost, Rex and more.
why: Sceners still call it a classic. They single out Cruzer's splitter, multiplexer and lower-border part, the Kefrens bars part with Steel's music, and the "Mazemania Mix" tune.

quote.text: Cruzer's splitter + multiplexer + logo + stuff in lower border was breathtaking when I first saw it. And it still looks very cool!

summary: Yerzmyey's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, credited on screen to Hooy-Program, written in BASIC with AY music. It placed second in the Multiplatform Small Demo compo at International Vodka Party 2008, and plays out on a theatre stage.
why: A rare compo-placing demo written in Sinclair BASIC, taking second in a multiplatform small demo competition against entries from other machines.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2009: a twister intro by Clarence leading into Leon's large interlaced 'Song of Fall' picture scrolling up through the side borders, with music by 6R6.
why: Sceners single out the twister as one of the better ever done on the C64, and the code behind the side-borderless interlaced picture scroller streaming from disk. Leon's autumn picture and the moody soundtrack win praise too.

quote.text: Impressed by the code, especially on twister, side-borderless interlace, and simultaneous scroll.

summary: Sparta's debut C64 demo for OMG, a one-file run of tunnel and fire effects with text interludes, set to music by Jeroen Tel.
why: Sceners were taken aback that a first release could be this good. They single out the dot tunnel as one of the best on the C64, the radial fire and the music-synced opening minutes.

quote.text: I totally dig that coronal mass ejection part and dot tunnel is one of the absolute best on C64.

summary: Five Finger Punch's 64K intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2026. Code by Morbid, Vilcans and Imodium, graphics by Corel and music by mAZE.
why: It took first place in the Oldschool Demo competition at Edison 2026, beating full demos with a 64K intro.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by The German Chaotics from 1989, with code, text and design by Ingo Tamme and graphics and music by Uwe Loos.
why: A late-1980s German Atari 8-bit demo, tagged for digitised music and a dancer. It's worth a look for its hand-drawn pictures and colourful title screens.

summary: A short C64 demo by Super Larsson Brothers (HCL, Jackasser and Pernod on code, c0zmo on music, Dane and Grip on graphics) that placed 9th in the C64 demo compo at X 2018.
why: Sceners felt it deserved a much higher placing, praising its fast pace, polish and c0zmo's soundtrack. Some found it hard to believe it was thrown together in a week.

quote.text: Short and sweet, but what's in there is excellent.

summary: Quasimodos' Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Glonisz with graphics by Raven and music by Morgoth, which came second in the demo compo at Lato Ludzików 2002.
why: A second place at Lato Ludzików 2002, and one of the less common Atari demos that needs a 320K memory expansion.

summary: Svoy's 256-byte procedural graphics intro for the Atari 8-bit, released by Agenda, which tied for first in the Oldschool Intro 256b compo at Demodulation 2020.
why: A joint compo winner that builds a whole scene from 256 bytes of code. Its source is available for anyone curious how it's done.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 comeback demo, the latest in their Wonderland series, placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2012. Code by Bob, CRT, Lavazza and Swallow, music by Magnar, with a 15.6 kHz digi end part.
why: It marked Censor Design's return after years away, and sceners welcomed it warmly. They single out the big bitmap colour scrollers, the rotating globe, the rasterbars and the all-border circles, all done in the classic Censor style inside a modern trackmo.

quote.text: it has all the key elements Wonderlands used to have (and more), great spirit, big bitmap color scrollers, good music, a digi part.

summary: A short Amstrad CPC demo by cpcitor, with music by Siko after the RodLand theme, that tied for third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Shadow Party 2025.
why: A compo placer at Shadow Party 2025. It reuses Sean Wallis's human and animal figures from the CPC game Fruity Frank alongside cpcitor's own graphics.

summary: Up Rough's PC Engine invitation intro for Datastorm 2018, with graphics by Exocet, music by Octapus and code by MooZ. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nova 2018.
why: An uncommon sight: a scene invitation on NEC's PC Engine, and good enough to place in an oldschool demo compo against other machines.

summary: Lieves!Tuore's MSX demo, coded by Marq with music by Yzi and graphics by Manu, which came second in the demo compo at MSX Info Update 2008.
why: A podium finish at a dedicated MSX party, from a Finnish group known for its work on several 8-bit machines. The dithered two-colour portrait style gives it a strong look of its own.

summary: An Atari 8-bit cracktro-style demo by Computer Platform Unlimited and The Atari OldSkoolerz, coded by TWH and Bobik with graphics by Powrooz and music by 505. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2007.
why: A first place in the Oldskool Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2007, made as a tribute to the look of 1987-era cracktros.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Taquart, coded by Eru with music by X-Ray, which won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2005.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2005, fitting code and music into a single kilobyte.

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo from X 2012, where it placed 4th in the demo compo. A large team of coders plus dEViLOCk's music and graphics by Celtic, Sphinx, Veto and Yazoo, built around a darkly humorous causes-of-death theme.
why: Sceners single out dEViLOCk's soundtrack as what holds it together, along with a fire effect, a big twister and Axis's plotball and surface plotter.

quote.text: Best fire effect I have ever seen. Also twister and plotter is looking very good.

summary: Fairlight's 1987 C64 cracktro for Combat School, cracked by Strider, with music by David Hanlon. A striped Fairlight logo sits over raster bars while a scrolltext runs below.
why: A period Fairlight crack intro whose scrolltext invites people to the Triad & Fairlight Copy Party 1987 in Stockholm, a small snapshot of the late-eighties cracking scene.

summary: Genesis Project's Game Boy demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by illm and music by Z-Nexx. It won the Other Platform Demo compo at Datastorm 2013.
why: A compo winner at Datastorm 2013, and a chance to see a C64 group taking on the original Game Boy.

summary: Artline Designs' two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2019, with code by Scorpion, Adder and Abaddon and music from four composers.
why: Sceners single out the tunnel part with a car driving through it, the screens and the music, with the closing tune picked out as a favourite party tune.

quote.text: Car in the tunnel was my favorite part. Really cool demo over all

summary: Rift's Vectrex demo, coded by Fell with music by Fell and Asherah and graphics by estrellasadie. It won the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2024.
why: A compo winner at Nova 2024 on the Vectrex, a vector-display console rarely seen in demo competitions.

summary: Real Masters' ZX Spectrum demo from 1999, which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 999. Code by Serg and Vlad, music by Den.
why: A Chaos Constructions compo winner that uses stellar mode, the Spectrum trick for chunky multicolour graphics beyond the usual attribute limits. It's tagged NSFW.

summary: Atlantis's PETSCII demo for the C64, starring a band of animated cats, which won the Old School Demo compo at Hogmanay.party 2020. Code by q0w, music by DivertigO, graphics by Lobo.
why: Sceners single out the PETSCII engine: animated, multiplexed, free-size character-mode sprites layered over backgrounds. They also praise its humour, especially the ending, and DivertigO's funky bass lines.

quote.text: Introducing Petscii-sprites, animated, prio, free-size and multiplexing..

summary: A 256-byte Atari XL/XE intro by tr1x that won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k20+1 SE in 2021.
why: A compo winner that fits a racing-game scene, named after the arcade classic, into 256 bytes.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo ANABASIS, which came second in the Oldschool demo compo at Multimatograf 2026.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf, the main Russian-speaking Spectrum party, in the Oldschool demo category.

summary: Lethargy's two-disk-side, Nintendo-themed C64 demo, second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2020. This video shows Vincenzo's 8580 soundtrack playing in SID-Wizard rather than the demo itself.
why: Sceners praise how well it treats the Nintendo theme, with a lightsourced Mario, a multi-layered scroller recalling Mahoney's and a lot of humour. The music gets singled out too, including a Castlevania cover on the Game Over screen.

quote.text: Who doesn't love Mario? What a wonderful, entertaining demo. So many cool details and good humor too.

summary: Masters of Electric City's monochrome hi-res Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Bob-er with graphics by Hospes and music by Makary Brauner. It placed third in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, and a demo that sticks to a stark black-and-white hi-res look throughout.

summary: Dekadence's invitation intro for Assembly 2002 on the Commodore 64, with code and graphics by BriteLite and music by Heatbeat. It opens on a mock game-trainer screen before moving to large dithered portrait pictures with a text line underneath.
why: An official party invite from a well-known Finnish group, and a playful one: the trainer-style menu with 'mullet time: OFF' sets the joking tone. It was also released for several other platforms.

summary: A 16K intro on the Commodore 64 from Booze Design, with code and graphics by Mirage and music by Dane. It came second in the C64 Demo compo at Only Sprites Compo 2020, and it is built around a multicoloured twisting tower.
why: Sceners call it one of the best twisters on the C64. They single out Mirage's colour sense, the way he combines code and art, and Dane's tune.

quote.text: I love twisters and this has to be one of the best twisters ever on the C64.

summary: The Philishave Grew's C64 demo, a parody of lft's Nine, which came second in the Mixed compo at KozMOS 2025. Mick Koalatalo did the code, graphics and music.
why: A comedy demo that sceners keep rewatching for the laughs. They single out the fake side-border routine, the Lambada and Airwolf tunes, and how polished it is for a three-day production.

quote.text: This is an instant mood lifter. I've seen this already for at least twenty times, but it still makes me laugh.

summary: Vanity's 256-byte procedural graphics intro for the Amstrad CPC, placed 2nd in the oldskool procedural gfx compo at Lovebyte 2023. It draws a landscape on screen.
why: Took second place at Lovebyte 2023, squeezing a whole generated scene into 256 bytes on the CPC.

summary: An NES invitation intro by Genesis Project, Oxyron and Nuance for the Nordlicht party (21–23 July 2017, Lichthaus Bremen). Logo, party details and a scrolltext, with code by Widdy and music by Response.
why: A C64-scene invitation made on the NES. It shared 6th place in the combined demo/intro compo at Underground Conference 2017.

summary: Cream's 2006 Atari 2600 demo, coded and drawn by Ultra with music by Tao.
why: A rare demo for the Atari VCS, a machine with very little to work with. It has no compo placings on record, but it is well regarded on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by bfox that placed 4th in the 8bit Intro 256b compo at Multimatograf 2016.
why: A compo-placed 256-byte entry from Multimatograf, worth a look for how much it does in so few bytes.

summary: Byterapers' C64 demo, third in their World of Code series, which won the C64 demo compo at Tribute 1994. Code by Mr. Sex, graphics by Nico, music by Rob Hubbard.
why: A compo winner that was also voted 14th best demo in Design #1 in 1997. Sceners praise the calm pace and real-time effects set to a Rob Hubbard tune, saying what it lacks in polish it makes up for elsewhere.

quote.text: The combination of Rob Hubbard .sid and the pace of the demo complete with real time wizardry gives World of Code 3 a soothing sensation.

summary: Desire and Proxima's PETSCII-heavy C64 demo with a Soviet theme, released on New Year's Eve 2020 and placed 2nd in the Old School Demo compo at Hogmanay.party 2020.
why: Sceners praise its coherent design and mood, the PETSCII screens and the music, and point to it as a showcase of what talented people can do with TRSE.

quote.text: Good coherent design, nice sound plus gfx and really shows possibilities when talented people work with TRSE.

summary: Dekadence's C64 4K intro, coded by BriteLite with music by SounDemoN, which came second in the C64 4K Intro compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001.
why: A podium 4K from a major party. Commenters single out its original take on the scroller and rate it among the best 4Ks.

quote.text: I always keep my eyes out for something new an original done with a scroller.  This is certainly it!!

summary: Dentifrice's Atari 2600 demo, coded by Kezax with graphics by Kezax and Remdy and music by Glafouk. It came third in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main gathering for Atari machines, from a small team squeezing pictures and effects out of the VCS.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2004, coded and drawn by AEG with music by SoNiC and PVCF.
why: A divisive but well-rated AEG coder-demo. Sceners single out the shaded textured X-rotator, the mirror scrollers and a run of new effect ideas, even those who find his low resolutions hard going.

quote.text: Especially the reflection mirror scroll over two mirrors.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC 4K intro, coded by Hicks with design by Beb and music by Tom et Jerry. It placed 4th in the Oldskool 4K Intro competition at Revision 2026.
why: A recent size-limited CPC prod from an experienced team that held its own in a competitive Revision oldskool 4K field.

summary: An intro for the Sharp MZ-800 by Ivory Labs, coded by MuffinHop, who also did the graphics and research. It shows the picture Cat Life framed by a blue and black checkerboard border.
why: Built to break emulators, as its title says, so the video is a capture from real hardware. It needs the MZ-800's expanded video RAM.

summary: Bones' two-disk-side C64 demo from 1989, winner of the C64 demo compo at the Dominators/Upfront/Trilogy Party 1989, packed with technical routines from a 32-sprite DYSP to 3D and a cloud-and-water end part.
why: Sceners remember it as groundbreaking for its time, singling out the 32-sprite multiplexed DYSP, the sideborder DYPP scroller and the controllable spaceship over a real starfield.

quote.text: A true classic, I've watched it manymany times. That 32 sprites multiplexed D.Y.S.P. was my absolute favorite effect back then.

summary: An Atari VCS demo coded by JAC! with music by Paul Slocum, which came second in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k13.
why: A second place at Silly Venture on the 2600, a machine with no frame buffer where every colour line has to be timed by the CPU. The source code has been released.

summary: Triad's C64 concept demo and sequel to Manhood, winner of the demo compo at Little Computer People 2001. Code by Hollowman, graphics by Hollowman and Wiggen, music by Abaddon and Vent.
why: A message demo rather than an effects show: it switches between a spoiled girlfriend's view and her doubting boyfriend's. Sceners call it funny and different, praising its ideas, irony and construction over its effects.

quote.text: Like every good song, Manhood 2 has a non-direct way of delivering a message, backed up by stylish and well thought out construction.

summary: Ate Bit and Desire's ZX Spectrum demo, coded by evilpaul with graphics by BokanoiD and Alien, which placed 3rd in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2015.
why: Nominated for Best Storytelling at The Meteoriks 2016, it's a Spectrum demo built around a story rather than a run of effects.

summary: Zelax's Atari 8-bit demo that won the demo compo at QuaST 2005, with code and graphics by Swiety, extra graphics by Dracon and music by Wacek.
why: It took first place in the QuaST 2005 demo competition, and it's a good look at what Zelax were doing on the Atari 8-bit in the mid-2000s.

summary: Vision's 8K C64 intro by Hein, with music by 4mat, which won the Intro Creation Competition 2014. Grey blocky 3D-style text scrolls in layers while a multicoloured scroller of chunky block letters snakes across it.
why: Sceners loved its 1986 look built with modern coding, calling it hypnotic and different from the usual intros. 4mat's tune "Complete" got plenty of praise, and so did the coloured main scroller against the grey layers.

quote.text: Oldcschool appearance but technically up to date! Well deserved winner!

summary: Padua's C64 demo from Mekka & Symposium 1998, where it placed 4th in the C64 demo compo: a Beatles-tagged sing-along with karaoke lyrics over a hand-drawn yellow submarine scene.
why: Remembered for the moment the whole party hall sang along to "We all live in the 64 scene". Sceners call it cute rather than technical, and the video captures the audience joining in.

quote.text: I will always remember the whole hall singing along "We all live in the 64 scene". Thank you for these memories!

summary: A C64 invitation to the Atari party Silly Venture by Mystic Bytes, Hokuto Force and Genesis Project, placing 3rd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2017. It opens on an Atari logo, then shows a crowd picture under a ring of stars with a scroller.
why: Sceners single out Mermaid's crowd picture for its detail and use of C64 colour, plus MCH's music. Mermaid notes it is Gorgh's first C64 production.

quote.text: Wow that pic is lovely. Such mastery of c64 colour

summary: A 512-byte C64 intro by 4gentE that won the 512 Byte Intro compo at Nordlicht 2022: a hand pressed against a screen of TV static, after the film Poltergeist.
why: Nominated in the Oldschool category at The Nano Awards 2023. Sceners praise its atmosphere in so few bytes and its glitch effects, and note that holding random keys adds extra glitching.

quote.text:
really love your work!
so much atmosphere
and 512 bytes too!

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Marquee Design, coded by superogue with design by Blossom. It won the LowEnd 256b intro compo at CAFe 2022.
why: A compo winner that was also nominated in the Oldschool category of The Nano Awards 2023, and it has sound despite the size. A making-of writeup is available from the group.

summary: Chorus's C64 4K intro by Clarence (code) with music by DRAX, placing third in the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2010. It shows off a new VIC trick billed as nine sprites per line.
why: Sceners took it as a fresh VIC-II trick and argued over how it worked. Coders explained it as eight sprites plus an ECM/bitmap fetch-delay trick drawing on the $3fff area. Some felt it should have won.

quote.text: And one massive beer to Clarence for keeping the tradition of finding new VIC-tricks alive.

summary: Centric's minimal C64 story demo from 2003: a small stick figure beside a line-drawn city skyline, told through short captions, ending in a colourful plasma with German greetings.
why: Sceners call it a little gem: simple, cute and much loved. Some count it among their favourite demos despite the plasma at the end.

quote.text: Simple, yet so fabulous and lovely! One of my favourite demos.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by smfx, coded by spkr with music by Crazy Q and graphics by Exocet and Evil, who rendered the twister. It runs on a 64K machine.
why: A smfx release on a stock 64K CPC, well received on Pouët. The video title notes it targets CRTC types 0 and 1.

summary: Oxyron's 1994 Commodore 64 demo, part of their long-running Coma Light series, with code by Axis, Graham, Slide and TTS and music by PRI.
why: Sceners call it the best of the Coma Light series and Oxyron's first real trackmo, the one where Graham's talent started to show. PRI's soundtrack, especially the opening tune, gets repeated praise. Voted 5th best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: The first real Oxyron trackmo, and an amazing one indeed. I think this demo is the first one starting to show off Graham's brilliance.

summary: Mayday!'s disco-themed C64 demo, winner of the C64 demo competition at BCC Party 2017, with a big team of coders and graphicians and music by Spider Jerusalem.
why: Sceners single out its PETSCII disco characters, funky graphics and catchy soundtrack, calling it entertaining with a nice flow. One commenter said it made him reconsider his opinion of PETSCII art.

quote.text: Very entertaining demo with a nice flow, catchy soundtrack and funky graphics.

summary: A 128-byte Atari 8-bit intro by F#READY that won the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2017: a coiling shape built from scattered coloured dots on black.
why: A compo winner in one of the tightest size classes, and it makes sound as well as pictures in 128 bytes. The source is available for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Desire and Oxyron's Atari 8-bit port of the ST-NICCC 2000 polygon demo, built for the VBXE graphics expansion. It won the Atari Rapidus / VBXE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A compo winner and an entry in the STNICCC challenge, where coders port Oxygene's classic Atari ST polygon stream to other machines. This one shows what VBXE adds to an XL.

summary: The Supply Team's 1988 single-part C64 demo by Kaze: a fullscreen scroller of tall hand-drawn letters over colour bars, with digi samples and a SID soundtrack.
why: Sceners remember it causing a jaw-drop when it came out, showing in 1988 that the C64 still had a future as Amigas arrived. They single out Kaze's coding, the colours and the music.

quote.text: In 1988, it clearly showed the direction of the future for the C64. Amigas started appearing in our rooms but the C64 would prevail - this is one of those demos that made it crystal clear.

summary: Slight's Atari 8-bit demo for 128K machines, coded by Seban with graphics and music by X-Ray. It won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k25 WE.
why: A first place at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, and it made the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist. The source code has been released.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by PU-239, released on 1 April 2009, made of a run of separate effect parts with large raster-coloured text.
why: A rare demo for the VIC-20, with no compo placing or comments on record. It's one for anyone curious about what the machine's small screen and palette can be pushed to.

summary: Desire's 16K Atari 8-bit intro, coded by Heaven with music by stRing, which placed 6th in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2013.
why: A compact 16K production from Desire's 2013 Atari line-up, with graphics from Alien, freakybe and Ramon. The video is the compo version uploaded by the coder himself.

summary: A ZX Spectrum cracktro by Triumph from 2006, made for a crack of Farmer Jack. A colourful vertical logo sits beside scrolling menu and credits text, with a dot-based object moving alongside.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it is a Triumph cracktro, a straightforward example of the Spectrum cracking scene's intro style.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper, which placed second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Under Construction 2015.
why: A 1K intro that held its own against full-size entries, taking second place in an oldskool demo competition.
highlights: streaking horizontal lines in the sky

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo for Alchimie X (2013), coded by Dbug with H2O's original Alchimie X logo converted, which placed 2nd in the demo compo.
why: A runner-up at Alchimie 2013 from one of the Oric's mainstays, and the source code is publicly available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Hackers' PETSCII demo for the Commodore 64, placed 8th in the demo compo at X 2014: a long run of PETSCII scenes and animations made with Marq's PETSCII editor, with music by ROBOT666.
why: Sceners single out the sheer amount of PETSCII content, the jokes and references, and above all ROBOT666's soundtrack, which some still come back to years later.

quote.text: Great story, great jokes, great references, great tunes and all done with PETSCII or something that looks a lot like it.

summary: An intro for the NEC PC Engine by Up Rough, with code by MooZ and music by Octapus. It placed 2nd in the Other Oldskool Platform Demo compo at Datastorm 2014.
why: A rare scene production for the PC Engine, a console with few demos, and it earned a podium place at Datastorm 2014.
highlights: shaded bars bending into a 3D shape

summary: Darklite and Offence's Sega Master System demo, an invitation to the Black Valley party (12–14 July 2024), which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2024.
why: A podium finish in Revision's Oldskool Demo compo is a good showing for a platform rarely seen in demo competitions. Code by Neon, graphics by Pal and music by Response.

summary: Desire's Commodore Plus/4 demo, placed 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2026, with code by Heaven, graphics by Hammerfist and music by mAZE.
why: A runner-up in Revision's Oldskool Demo competition, where the Plus/4 took on other classic machines.

summary: A Halloween-themed four-disk-side C64 megademo from a collaboration of Pretzel Logic, Elysium, Offence, Bonzai, Genesis Project, Lethargy and Atlantis, placed 3rd in the demo compo at Zoo 2026. A fifth side holds a note and the game The Pumpkids.
why: Sceners praise the sheer amount of hand-crafted content across nearly 18 minutes, with jokes, nods to old games and a lot of animation. Several felt it should have won; it ran well over the compo's 10-minute limit.

quote.text: Strong theme, so many disksides, so many parts, so much content, so much goodness!

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by P_Malin that won the Oldskool 256b Intro compo at Outline 2022.
why: A compo winner at Outline 2022, fitting its effects into 256 bytes on a stock Spectrum.

summary: A C64 demo by Samar Productions and Arise that won the C64 demo compo at Stary Piernik 2013. Code by Mr Wegi, music by Randall, graphics by Pardon and Bimber, ending in an Asteroids-style part.
why: Sceners single out the fast, fullscreen hires bitmap zoomer, the unnoticed loading between parts and the Asteroids finale, though several wished it were longer.

quote.text: Now this is just a giant bowl of awesome.

summary: Game Boy Color demo by Octarine, with code by Dalton, graphics by Exocet and music by Mrdeath. It placed 5th in the Console Demo compo at Breakpoint 2003.
why: A Game Boy Color demo from a Breakpoint console compo, with Mr. Death and Exocet appearing as guest artists. The source code is included in the file archive, which makes it useful for anyone curious about GBC coding.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Agenda, coded by Koala, that won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: A compo winner in one of the tightest size categories, fitting two twisting columns and a striped raster backdrop into 256 bytes.

summary: A Vectrex demo by Fit from 2013, with code and graphics by Manu and music by Yzi.
why: A rare example of a demo on the Vectrex. The video's own title calls it a Vectrex scene intro.

summary: A 32-byte intro with sound for the Atari 8-bit by KK, which came second in the intro compo at Decrunch 2017.
why: Fitting both visuals and sound into 32 bytes is the draw here, and it placed second at Decrunch 2017. It's tagged as a glitch piece.

summary: Future Concepts' C64 demo, coded by Kronos with graphics from a long list of artists, that won the demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2011. It's an oldschool-style trackmo of pictures, logos and effects.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a long-delayed comeback for Future Concepts, and praised how its many contributors' graphics are blended into one oldschool journey. They single out the two plasma parts and the soundtrack.

quote.text: This demo is well done and have that oldschool feeling with a fresh touch. Loadsa great graphics and its all blended nicely together.

summary: A 1987 Commodore 64 demo by The Judges, with code by Coko and music by Red. It sets scrolling and on-screen text over a large hand-drawn castle landscape.
why: A well-regarded early Judges demo. Sceners single out Red's music, and one commenter argues he deserves a place among CSDb's top composers.

quote.text: That composer should be in the top 10, at least. Emotional, beautiful, touching, soaring.

summary: Dekadence's fifth Beertime demo for the Commodore 64, coded and scored by BriteLite with graphics by Bracket. It placed 10th in a strong demo compo at X 2012.
why: Sceners praise its fast pace, solid code and Bracket's graphics, and several single out the greetings part, the chessboard with beer and the comic opening screen. The music split opinion.

quote.text: best dekadence demo so far, and the pace is perfect in this one.

summary: R0ger's Atari 8-bit take on Bad Apple, with code, graphics and music all by R0ger: the familiar shadow-play silhouette animation played back with karaoke-style scrolling lyrics underneath.
why: Part of the long tradition of porting the Bad Apple video to old hardware, here done single-handedly on the Atari 800.

summary: Section 31's Commodore Plus/4 trackmo that won the demo compo at Árok 2023, with code by Lavina, BSZ, Murphy, Oswald and Bubis and music by Celticdesign.
why: A first place at Árok 2023 and a spot on the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist mark it as one of the notable Plus/4 demos of its year.

summary: Triad's C64 demo, placed 2nd in the demo compo at S:T Lars Meeting 2007. Code by Killsquad, salvaged from old work disks by Iopop and JFK, with music by Orcan.
why: Code from the mid-to-late nineties finally released a decade on. Sceners single out the blue "tornado" after the opening logo, the closing Triad logo effect and how well Orcan's tempo-shifting tune paces the effects.

quote.text: Looks very good, impressive effects, nice transitions and the music blends well into the effects.

summary: Triad's black-and-white C64 demo that came third in the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2016, with graphics by Twoflower and music by Dalezy, ending on a sampled industrial track.
why: Sceners single out its style and soundtrack, and some call it one of Triad's best demos, praising the group for going its own way. A few wished for more effects.

quote.text: i like when triad not trying to be Oxyron or Censor Design or Booze Design and they going with their (!) own way.

summary: Haujobb and Dekadence's C64 demo, second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2002, with code, graphics and music by BriteLite alongside Droidi, SounDemoN and others.
why: A parody take on My Kingdom, according to the Demozoo notes, that took second place at Assembly 2002. It also ships with a note written in a 1993 OctaNoter by Morris/Extacy.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Commodore 64 by Ilmenit (of Agenda, per the video title), winner of the Oldskool 256b Intro compo at Outline 2021. It has sound, and the source is available.
why: It won its compo at Outline 2021 and was nominated for Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022. Carrion welcomed it as Ilmenit's arrival on the C64 scene.

quote.text: good job ilmenit! great to have you here on c64 demoscene finally

summary: A New Year demo for the ZX Spectrum with TS-Conf hardware by Nik-O, Nodeus and Hacker VBI, placed 2nd in the New Year Gift competition at CC Winter / DiHalt Lite.2015.
why: A festive greeting card made for the enhanced TS-Conf Spectrum, and runner-up in its party's New Year Gift compo.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by LaResistance, with code by Probe and music by Born, that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2005.
why: It took first place in the Atari Demo competition at Forever 2005. It is worth a look for its solid 3D on the Atari 8-bit.

summary: 99.9%'s one-file PETSCII demo for the Commodore 64, themed on subway graffiti: train-station walls, wholecars and tags drawn in character graphics. It came 2nd in the oldskool demo compo at Deadline (Berlin) 2026.
why: Sceners call it the most polished take yet on the train-station graffiti PETSCII idea, praising the teamwork, the wholecar pieces on the trains and theK's tune.

quote.text: That train station graffiti PETSCII idea has re-occurred a couple of times recently, but never before with so much perfection!

summary: Oxyron and Crest's Commodore 128 demo for the VDC 80-column chip, a 2006 update of the 2001 release with Graham's NTSC fix, bug fixes and linking, plus graphics by DeeKay and music by Dane.
why: Sceners call it the best C128 demo, and it surprised viewers with how colourful and refined 80-column mode can look. The update also brought a one-file version and an experimental 60Hz mode.

quote.text: The first time I noticed how different the colors in the 80 column mode are, and the first time I saw a nice font there.

summary: Reflex's C64 4K intro by Quiss, who did the code, music and text, with directory art by Felidae. It won the 4K intro compo at X 2023, and its knock-knock jokes frame large, smooth vector cubes.
why: Won the technical achievement award at Siggraph Asia 2023. Sceners single out the new 'BRR' line-drawing method, the full-screen moving chessboard and the drive doing some of the work, all packed into 4K.

quote.text: the cubes are impressively large and smooth, and cramming all of this into 4k is a small (pun intended) miracle.

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo announcing Arsantica 3, released at Revision 2015 where it placed 11th in the Oldskool Demo compo. Code by Heaven, music by Triace, graphics by BokanoiD, Lowlife and Hammerfist.
why: A teaser from the group behind the Arsantica series, with three graphicians credited, so the pictures carry much of the show.

summary: HARD and Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, released at Nordlicht 2015 where it placed 4th in the Oldschool Demo compo. Code by Heaven, Téli Sándor and Bene Tamas, music by Miker and Triace, graphics by Havoc.
why: A joint Hungarian Atari XL production from a sizeable crew, named after the party it was made for and placed in the top four of a mixed oldschool field.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Ate Bit, with code, graphics and music all by 4-Mat. The soundtrack drives the SID and an external MIDI synth together.
why: Sceners single out the soundtrack, an Outrun-flavoured tune where the SID plays alongside MIDI instruments, and note that the MIDI timing holds up on real hardware. They also praise 4-Mat's music, design and concept.

quote.text: Wow - what a killer demo with a fab Outrunnish soundtrack.

summary: Ukonx's demo for the Amstrad Plus, released in 2007, with code by Power and Deemphasis, music by Deemphasis and graphics by Unison, Grim and Ozane.
why: A demo written for the Amstrad Plus rather than the standard CPC, and the title screen makes a point of saying it runs without acceleration.
highlights: fire effect in a framed window

summary: Onslaught's C64 port of the Bad Apple shadow-art animation, coded by Algorithm with music by Ukimenustah: over 2000 frames streamed from a single disk side at 12fps.
why: A technical proof of concept that sceners called impressive coding-wise, packing each frame to around 70 bytes and streaming the whole animation from one 1541 disk side without swaps.

quote.text: So good considering it's for our beloved humble 64. Sometimes I think Algo sold his soul being able to make this kind of impressive stuff; and on a single side no less.

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum 4K intro, with code, graphics and music all by him, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2005. Japanese-script title cards with romanised captions frame the effects.
why: A one-person 4K that beat full-size demos to first place in the oldskool compo. Its source is available under a Creative Commons licence.

summary: Samar Productions' party version of a C64 demo that came second in the demo compo at Silesia 5 2011, with graphics by Isildur and Skull, music by Jammer and code from five coders.
why: Nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform and Best Graphics at the Scene.org Awards 2011. Sceners single out Isildur's graphics, the mix of hires and multicolour, and the end part with its noisy picture effect.

quote.text: Outstanding use of hires and multicolor in combination!! Must have been alot of work to make those screens look so seemless.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1998, with code and graphics by AEG and DCP and music from SoNiC, Wacek, kb, Q-Man and Shogoon. A sci-fi story told through effects.
why: Often named as Smash Designs' best. Sceners praise its good-resolution effects, music sync and the way music, effects and graphics work together to tell a story.

quote.text: best from smash imho. music/fx/gfx works together nicely to tell a story.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Digital Sounds System and Trilobit, coded by Tjoppen, which came second in the Oldskool intro compo at Revision 2013.
why: A second place at Revision for a 4K on the Atari 2600, a platform that sees few demoscene releases.
highlights: text messages on a framed board

summary: A 16-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum by The Rockonerz, released in 2011. This video shows the colour version: the screen fills with flickering columns of coloured attribute blocks and garbled characters inside a striped border.
why: A 16-byte intro is about as small as a Spectrum prod gets. Its whole display comes from a handful of instructions, and it gets nothing but positive votes on Pouët.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by sibKrew, with code and graphics by rook and music by Nik-O. It took second place in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CAFe 2022.
why: A runner-up at CAFe 2022 that is tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which gives finer colour detail than the machine's usual attribute limits allow.

summary: Amstrad Plus demo by Da Boxon Team, with code by Nicky One, graphics by Bouba and music by Giherem. It placed 2nd in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #5 2025.
why: A recent Amstrad Plus release that took second place in its party's combined demo and intro competition.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Busysoft that won the ZX Spectrum 256b intro compo at Lost Party 2021.
why: A compo winner that went on to be nominated for Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022.

summary: Iris's Oric demo, coded and drawn by Xeron with music by H0ffman, which placed second in the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2023.
why: A recent Oric production that came second in a mixed old-school compo, showing what the machine can still be pushed to do.

summary: An Oric demo by Iris, coded by Xeron with music by H0ffman, that placed second in the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2025.
why: A recent Oric release that took second place at Nova 2025, made by a two-person team of coder Xeron and musician H0ffman.

summary: Resource's single-file C64 demo, coded by Oswald with graphics by Leon and music by guest 6R6, which came second in the demo compo at Árok 2015. Four short effect parts built on dithered, fuzzy light.
why: Sceners praise its use of dithering, the dither fader and the feedback light shafts, and note the feat of fitting every effect into one file. The common complaint is that each part ends too soon.

quote.text: This is how dithering supposed to be used. Neat effects.

summary: Joker's monochrome 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum, coded and drawn by Dalthon, which won the ZX Spectrum 4kb Intro compo at speccy.pl party 2022.
why: A compo winner at speccy.pl party 2022 that fits its effects and a music player into 4K, using Shrinkler and ZX0 compression.

summary: A 512-byte intro for the Atari Lynx by 42Bastian that won the 512 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2025: a voxel landscape of orange and red hills under a blue sky, with a space invader overhead.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2025 that fits a voxel landscape into 512 bytes on the Lynx, a handheld that rarely sees sizecoding. The source is available.

summary: GL.Fusion's demo for the TI-85 graphing calculator, which won the wild demo compo at Blockparty 2007.
why: A compo-winning demo on a pocket calculator, an unusual platform for the scene. It took first place in the wild category at Blockparty 2007.

summary: Dentifrice's Atari Lynx demo, winner of the Atari Lynx Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code by Kezax and Remdy, graphics from four artists and music by Glafouk.
why: It took first place in the Lynx demo compo at Silly Venture 2019, and with Smiley, Exocet, Easy and Esteban all on graphics it is a showcase for pixel art on Atari's handheld.

summary: An Amstrad CPC 4K intro by Benediction, Arkos and Dentifrice that came 4th in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2024. Line drawings of a woman's face and a cat build up inside a red screen border.
why: The title puns on Télécran, the French name for the Etch A Sketch. It is a three-group collaboration with code by Krusty, graphics by Exocet and music by Targhan, and the source is available.

summary: Oxyron's 1993 C64 demo, eleventh in the Coma Light series, which placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1993. Code by Axis, Graham and TTS, music by PRI.
why: Sceners single out PRI's soundtrack, especially 'Cave of Echoes' and 'Sadly Fading', and call it Oxyron's first demo with trackmo elements and a more polished sense of design.

quote.text: Lots of yummy vectors, with a surprise up a glenz cube and Mandelbrot. I loved the zoom at the end.

summary: JAC!'s 4K intro for the Atari VCS, with music by Qotile, placed 5th in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2011. Big blocky text bars frame stacked horizontal colour bars.
why: A rare Atari 2600 entry in a mixed oldskool 4K compo, and its source code has been released for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo released on New Year's Day 2013 by GM BIT, with code by GM BIT and music by MmcM.
why: A small New Year greeting from the Spectrum scene with no compo history. The draw is its waving block-letter text and MmcM's soundtrack.

summary: Lethargy's C64 demo, made entirely in shades of grey, which placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2020. Code by Ego, Strepto and Visage, music by Vincenzo and graphics by Grass.
why: Sceners praise how much it gets out of a deliberately limited palette, with tight sync, inventive parts and a funky Vincenzo soundtrack. Several expected it to win the compo.

quote.text: I love the premise and the idea and there is a lot of gorgeous shading going on in this one.

summary: Genesis Project's Atari VCS demo for the Snowstorm compo at Fjälldata 2023, where it placed 6th: a winter scene with code by Shadow and graphics and music by Mermaid.
why: A small seasonal piece on the Atari 2600, made by a group better known on the C64, and worth a look for anyone curious what a two-person team can draw out of the VCS.
highlights: snowy night scene with pine trees

summary: Megastyle's 1990 C64 demo, with code, graphics and music from a long crew list including Cycleburner, Scroll, Rage and Crockett. A multi-part oldskool demo full of scrollers and raster parts.
why: Voted 4th best demo in Unic News #1 in early 1991. Sceners still rate it highly for its age, singling out the SID tunes, sampled sound in the intro, its sense of humour and a horizontal rasterbar part with a 45-degree scroll.

quote.text: Lots of nice effects, great design and a good sense of humor.

summary: A Commodore 64 crack intro from Genesis Project, coded by L.A. Style and WertStahl with graphics by Wacek and music by Celticdesign. It opens on a starfield, then leads into a multitrainer menu under the group logo.
why: Sceners praised its concept and execution on release, and singled out Wacek's logo and Celticdesign's music.

quote.text: I was blown away when I saw this intro. Great concept, flawless execution!

summary: Cosine's 16K musicdisk for the Commodore 16 and Plus/4, released in April 2006, with a hand-drawn portrait beside a busy panel of shifting colour-striped patterns.
why: A compact musicdisk that fits within the stock 16K of the C16, which makes it a good example of what Cosine squeezed out of the TED machines.

summary: Game Boy demo by Bitnenfer and Foco, coded and drawn by Bitnenfer with music by Foco. It came 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: A runner-up in a mixed-platform oldskool compo at Revision, which is a strong showing for a Game Boy demo. Its source code is available.

summary: Altair's Atari XL/XE demo on a Covid-19 theme, which won the Atari XL/XE Demo Standard compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: It took first place in the stock-machine Atari demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE, with code and graphics shared between KK, mgo, Traq and Dzozef, and music by KK.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Dream Team from 2010, with code by PSV, graphics by Stas and music by Ironman.
why: A Dream Team release with no compo placing or awards on record. The fact sheet is thin, so it's simply a chance to see the group's 2010 Spectrum work.

summary: Blueberry's 128-byte Commodore 64 intro, fourth in the 128b intro compo at Outline Online 2020: a screen-filling grid of dots that swell and shrink in a shifting plasma-like veil, over a heavy, distorted soundtrack.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021. Sceners praise the pattern for its size and how well it sits with the distorted soundscape, and fellow coders admired its VIC setup tricks.

quote.text: Beautiful! Works so well with the heavy sounds in the background.

summary: Samar Productions' Commodore 64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gravity 1997. It is built around chunky real-time 3D: shaded and textured cubes, gouraud-shaded toruses and a Wolfenstein-style maze, followed by a note shown in its own reader.
why: Sceners single out the code. Oswald counts it among the few C64 prods with real-time phong routines, mankeli and Sith praise its ambition, and Oswald says it inspired the texture-mapped cube in Larch.

quote.text: codewise this is quite outstanding. I can count on my one hand realtime phong routines...

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Heaven with graphics by Alien and music by guest artist 505 of Checkpoint. It placed 4th in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2013.
why: A Desire release for the Atari 8-bit that held its own in a mixed-platform wild compo at Outline 2013, with a guest soundtrack from 505.

summary: Abyss-Connection's C64 demo, made almost single-handedly by FieserWolf (code, music, graphics) with text by Mr. Curly. It came 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2017 and shows dancing figures built from glowing dots above a scrolling message.
why: Sceners enjoyed the dance animations and the mood. One singled out the well-synced intro and the music, which FieserWolf wrote alongside the code and graphics.

quote.text: Especially love the well synced intro. Music rocks!

summary: A 1986 one-file C64 demo by We Music, with code and graphics by Ratt and music by Benn. A long piece where a small framed screen tells a story to Ben Daglish's soundtrack. This version opens as a Compunet advert.
why: Sceners call it a classic C64 demo and remember it fondly from childhood. They single out Ben Daglish's music, one of his best-loved tunes, and the story told in the tiny screen.
highlights: story in a small framed screen

quote.text:
Talking about classics? This *IS* a classic C64 demo.
Incredible music by Ben Daglish in combination with the story told in the tiny screen.

summary: A 256-byte Atari XL/XE intro coded by JAC!, placed third in the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: A podium finish in a 256-byte compo at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party. Worth a look to see how much colour JAC! fits into so few bytes.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Vanity, coded mainly by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by Madram. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Intro compo at Revision 2022.
why: A size-limited CPC intro from an experienced team that held its own in Revision's Oldskool Intro compo, packing generated landscapes and a soundtrack into 4K.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Masters of Electric City, coded by bob_er with music by Dhor. It placed third in the Atari XL/XE 16kb Intro compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited Atari compo at Silly Venture, one of the main parties for the platform.

summary: A 512-byte ZX Spectrum intro from Joker, coded by Dalthon with the idea credited to Ilmenit. It won the Demo competition at speccy.pl party 2018.2, and the video lists it at 511 bytes.
why: A procedural-graphics tribute that beat full-size entries to take the demo compo at speccy.pl party 2018.2, all within a 512-byte limit.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Kpacku, released in November 2014 as a birthday present for prof4d, with bilingual English and Russian text lines running under the pictures.
why: A personal tribute prod made for a fellow scener's birthday, and a well-received one on Pouët. Worth a look for its colourful Spectrum pixel graphics.

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2017: a remake of the first Beertime rather than a new entry in the series, with code by BriteLite and music by Flex.
why: Sceners single out Flex's soundtrack and the smooth, beefed-up effects, especially a tunnel that improves on the original. The common complaint is that it's too short.

quote.text: The fx in this remake are nicely beefed up. Especially the tunnel looks way better than the first version.

summary: Dekadence's PC Engine demo, coded by BriteLite with graphics by Bracket and music by Ricky Martin. It won the Wild compo at Zoo 2022.
why: A first-place compo winner on the PC Engine, a console that sees few demos.

summary: A 1K procedural graphics prod for the ZX Spectrum by bfox, which won the 4k procedural gfx compo at DiHALT Summer 2018. It draws a portrait of a woman step by step.
why: It took first place at DiHALT Summer 2018, producing a full colour portrait from just 1K of code.

summary: Breeze's two-disk-side C64 trackmo preview, second in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1998. Code by Bigfoot and BBT, graphics by Rayden and guest Cyclone, music including guest Taki.
why: The full demo was never released, but sceners still call the preview excellent for 1998, and people seeing it decades later have taken it for a new release. Taki's tune gets singled out for the comfortable feel it gives.

quote.text: I ran this on Bunkerparty 2019 and Brainstorm and me thought "must be something fresh". Checked here and WHAT 1998?! really?

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Vanity and Futurs', released in June 2023, with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and music and samples by Zik.
why: Third in the Onescreen Colonies series, combining Hicks's code with Beb's graphics and Zik's sampled soundtrack on a stock CPC.

summary: A ZX Spectrum megademo about cats by AAA Band, released at DiHalt 2010, where it placed second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo.
why: A light-hearted, cat-themed megademo from the Russian Spectrum scene that took second place at DiHalt 2010. It runs on a Spectrum 128 or Pentagon 128.

summary: An Amstrad CPC intro by Benediction and Da Boxon Team, coded by Krusty with graphics and concept by MacDeath. It placed third in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #5 in 2025.
why: A recent CPC party release that took third place at Benediction's own coding party, and its source code has been made available.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Svoy and Piesiu that came third in the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2021.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited compo at DiHalt 2021, and the source code is available for anyone curious how it fits in 256 bytes.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo coded by Den Popov with ideas from g0blinish, music by SCL and graphics by Square. It won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CC Winter / DiHalt Lite 2015.
why: A compo winner at CC Winter / DiHalt Lite 2015, worth a look for its blocky, minimal visual style built from big chunky pixels and bold Spectrum colours.

summary: Blowjobb's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2006, with music by Miker, graphics by dely and lead code by Mikey.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2006. It supports stereo sound and hides a secret part, unlocked by typing "zeuan" at the title screen.

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII story demo for the C64 about a bear, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2012. Graphics and story by acidT*rroreast, code by Mathman, music by Goto80.
why: Sceners single out the narrative and the PETSCII art, calling it disturbing, strange and uncomfortable in a way they can't help loving, with Goto80's music judged spot-on.

quote.text: Wonderfully nice, disturbing and strange. Top notch quality C/G art, folks.

summary: Agenda's Atari VCS demo, coded by Gorgh, which won the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: A compo winner on one of the most constrained machines around, the Atari 2600, from a group with a track record on the platform.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Warriors of the Wasteland that won the Combined Demo compo at Beach Party 2009.
why: It took first place in the combined demo competition at Beach Party 2009. The fact sheet is thin, so the compo win is the main thing on record.

summary: sibKrew's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2024, with code by rook and artёmka, graphics by Robat and rook, and music by Nik-O.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2024, a recent example of the Spectrum scene's current output. Tagged for the Pentagon clone.

summary: An MSX demo by Dromedaar Vision, released in January 2015, that came second in the Oldskool 8bit compo at Payback 2015.
why: A podium finish in a mixed 8-bit oldskool compo at Payback 2015, and a recent example of demo work on the MSX.

summary: A C64 demo by Hokuto Force and Trupa Milosne Spotkania that won the C64 demo compo at Forever 2018, with code and graphics by Gorgh and music by Uctumi.
why: Sceners single out its chunky 4x4 effects, bold colour patterns and sense of humour, along with Uctumi's tune. Brush noted it as Gorgh's first major release on the platform.

quote.text: all in all, a very entertaining and philosophical little demo!

summary: Real Action is a ZX Spectrum demo by Reaction, with code and graphics by Jordan, graphics by Pyza and music by Kriss. It placed joint 10th in the ZX Spectrum demo competition at Enlight 1997.
why: A mid-table entry from a 1997 Enlight compo, worth a look for its period Spectrum effects work. The fact sheet gives little else to go on.

summary: An Amstrad Plus demo by TGS, with code by Shining, graphics by HAL6128 and music by Nik-O and Tao. It placed 5th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2019.
why: A party demo written for the Amstrad Plus rather than the stock CPC, entered at Evoke 2019 and well received on Pouët.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders, coded by Madram with music by Jess, that placed 11th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019.
why: A Revision release from one of the CPC's long-running groups, with Madram on code and Jess on music. The fact sheet is thin, so it's best judged by watching.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit invitation intro for SillyVenture 2013, with code, graphics and music by Wieczor, extra graphics by mOOnie and text by Grey.
why: An official invitation to the Polish Atari party SillyVenture, made by the people behind it, with almost all of it done by Wieczor alone.
highlights: leopard heads flanking the Atari logo

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum by SerzhSoft, with music by Visual, which placed third in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2023.
why: A podium finish at Revision's oldskool 4K compo for a Spectrum intro that fits its visuals and AY music into four kilobytes.

summary: Rift's Vectrex demo, coded by Fell with graphics by estrellasadie and music by Ash. It came second in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2024.
why: A recent Vectrex demo that placed second at Evoke 2024, a chance to see what the vector console's glowing lines can do in a party production.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by sibCrew, coded by rook with music by Nik-O, released in May 2018. It runs through cheeky "no grtz" title screens and a chunky blocky twister.
why: A small, irreverent Spectrum demo that stuck around: in 2025 Spiceboys ported it to the Atari as "No grtz to spkr".

summary: Dentifrice's 8K invitation intro for the Atari VCS, placed 2nd in the Oldschool Intro compo at Simulaatio 2018. Code by Kezax, music by Glafouk, graphics by Easy and Remdy.
why: A second place at Simulaatio 2018 for a small invitation intro on the Atari 2600, one of the most constrained machines in the scene.

summary: Techno Lab's take on the Bad Apple!! shadow animation for an enhanced ZX Spectrum with 512K and TurboSound, placed 2nd in the Demo compo at ZX Enhanced 2016.
why: Bad Apple!! is a popular test of what a machine can stream, and this version took second place at ZX Enhanced. Code is by Kowalski, music by Nik-O and ASCII art by DMan.

summary: Algotech's 2016 Commodore 64 demo that plays back a cheeky, adult-themed video clip in colour on a stock machine, using sprites and flicker to add detail.
why: Sceners single out the smart colour use and flicker mode that squeeze detail into so many multicolour frames. One sees it as a step beyond Algotech's earlier Bad Apple, and the soundtrack gets praise too.

quote.text: So many frames with multiple colors on a stock 64. Amazing.

summary: Lethargy's 4K intro for the Commodore 64, coded by Strepto with music by Vincenzo, which won the 4k Demo compo at Transmission64 2022. A sequence of colourful full-screen effects.
why: Sceners single out the opening effect as perhaps the most colourful plasma-type effect yet seen on the C64, with several comparing it favourably to Amiga plasmas, and they praise Vincenzo's track too.

quote.text: The first effect has to be the most colorful plasma-type effect so far on the C64!

summary: Gogin's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K, with sound, which won the ZX Spectrum 256b intro compo at CAFe 2022.
why: A compo winner at CAFe 2022, fitting moving colour patterns and sound into 256 bytes on a stock 48K Spectrum.
highlights: patterns that build up across the screen

summary: RetroSouls' ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by Denis Grachev with music by Nik-O, which won the CSP-DEMO Battle at Crazy Siberian Party 2016.
why: A compo winner at Crazy Siberian Party 2016, and a chance to see Denis Grachev handling both the code and the graphics himself.

summary: Agenda's Game Boy demo that won the demo compo at Lost Party 2023, with code by Gorgh, music by AceMan and graphics by Raphis and Piesiu.
why: It took first place in the demo competition at Lost Party 2023, and the fact sheet lists no comments yet, so it stands on that win.

summary: Eternity Industry's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2000, with code and music by Sairoos, graphics by Paracels and objects by D-Man.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, and well regarded on Pouët.

summary: Bay 6's ZX Spectrum demo, coded and drawn by Diver with music by Nik-O, which placed third in the 8-bit demo compo at Multimatograf 2015.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf 2015, and a near-solo effort: Diver handled both the code and the graphics.

summary: Altair's Atari 2600 demo, coded by mgo and Traq with music by KK, which won the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture 2k18 on one of the most restrictive machines there is, with a Space Invaders theme running through it.

summary: A one-man Commodore 64 demo by Kribust of Offence, who did code, graphics and music: distorted, glitching digitised-looking images in shifting two- and three-colour palettes, released in April 2011.
why: Sceners praised its raw, trashy style and its topical theme, its distortion effects and music, and noted it as a rare case of uncontrolled $d016 border opening put to good use.

quote.text: For rawness and power, this is a perfect example. Inspiring to bits.

summary: Logon System's Amstrad CPC demo from 2021, tagged as a remake and released as the 2021 revision of their Amazing Demo.
why: A revisit of an older Logon System production for the CPC, worth a look for anyone curious how a group reworks its own earlier demo decades on.

summary: Defence Force's cyberpunk-themed Oric demo, coded and drawn by Dbug with music by H0ffman, which won the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2026.
why: A compo winner on the Oric that tells a story, and the source is available for anyone curious how it was put together.
highlights: Defence Force logo with raster bars

summary: Arise's Commodore 64 demo, also titled Bumpmania, which won the demo compo at North Party 1999. Code by Fenek, Gold Hand, Luke and Stinger, music by Wacek and Rodney, with graphics from several artists.
why: Sceners single out its inventive, well-executed effects, from bump mapping to high-resolution tunnels, along with its flow and music. Some say it deserves a higher rating than it has.
highlights: effect that turns into a cube

quote.text: nifty coderz pron here, awesome effects, a lot of new ideas, wonderfully executed.

summary: Shiru's New Year greeting intro for the NES, released on 1 January 2011, with music by Gibson: sparkling star shapes form pictures and the year over a snowy forest.
why: A small seasonal card from a well-known NES homebrew coder, released the day it greets. It is a short, gentle watch rather than a technical showcase.

summary: Rasternator is a Commodore 64 demo by ript, released at Syntax 2009, where it came 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo.
why: A placing in the Syntax 2009 Oldskool Demo compo. As the title suggests, it's a showcase for raster bars on the C64.

summary: A C64 intro by Bauknecht, coded by Mad with graphics and music by Sire, that came 2nd in the Combined Demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2007. A grey upper screen carries a moving shaded effect above a fixed logo panel.
why: Sceners praised it as a small, solid release made with care, singling out the simple but effective screen layout, the effect, Sire's music and movement that felt very much of 2007.

quote.text: Totally love this one. Love how the screen is so simple yet effectively set up. And awesome effect and music too!

summary: ZX Spectrum demo by introspec (code) and Key-Jee (music) that won the demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2013. It shows an endless run of Suprematist-style abstract compositions, each captioned with a title and a fictional artist and date.
why: A compo winner with an unusual idea: tagged as randomised visuals, it generates its own abstract art rather than playing back fixed parts.

summary: A Commodore PET demo by oobc (Bass Cadet and oo), made for the CBM 8032. It won the Wild compo at Zoo 2017.
why: A compo winner on a rarely used platform. Bass Cadet and oo shared the code and graphics, and Bass Cadet also wrote the music.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by introspec that came second in the Combined 8-Bit 1024b Intro compo at DiHalt 2013.
why: It placed second in a combined 8-bit 1K compo at DiHalt 2013. It is tagged as a minimal prod and runs on 48K and 128K Spectrums as well as Pentagon and Scorpion clones.
highlights: wireframe cube drawn in text characters

summary: New Generation's Atari Lynx demo, which won the Atari Lynx demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE. Code by Solo and Laoo, music by Blasph and graphics by Tiger.
why: A first-place compo winner on the Lynx, a handheld that rarely gets new demos, released at Silly Venture in 2021.
highlights: shaded polygon object over photo backdrop

summary: An Atari 2600 invitation by Mystic Bytes and Noice for the SV2k11 party, with code by Shadow, graphics by Piesiu, music by Jakub Husak and text by Grey.
why: A party invitation on the VCS, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, from Polish groups Mystic Bytes and Noice.
