summary: Hal's 1987 Commodore 64 demo: eight multicolour sprites, drawn as eyes, move in hypnotic patterns to a single tune in a file of around 30 blocks.
why: Sceners call it a minimalist classic that they've watched for hours. They praise the way such simple means, eight sprites and a tune, stay entertaining, and how the movements are synchronised to the music.

quote.text: Lovely minimalistic design that hypnotizes me for hours on end.

summary: Lieves!Tuore's MSX 64K intro, coded by Marq with music and extra code by Yzi and graphics by Manu. It won the 64k combined compo at Alternative Party 2013.
why: A compo winner at Alternative Party 2013, beating PC and other entries in a combined 64k competition with an 8-bit MSX production.

summary: Polish ZX All Stars' ZX Spectrum 48K demo paying tribute to Clive Sinclair, with code by Tygrys, Sachy and Dalthon, graphics by CatMan and Ziutek, and music by Pator. It came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: A Polish group's farewell to the man behind the Spectrum, made the year he died. It placed second at Silly Venture.

summary: PriorArt's Atari Lynx demo, placed third in the Atari Lynx demo compo at Silly Venture 2k19, with code by Enthusi and Jackasser, music by Jammer and graphics by Zooperdan, JonEgg and Dawnbringer.
why: A rare demo for Atari's handheld from a crew of well-credited sceners, and a podium finish in a dedicated Lynx compo.

summary: Booze Design's two-disk-side C64 demo, also known as "1988", a quasi-sequel to their "1991". It placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013, with code by HCL and Jackasser, graphics by Jailbird and Valsary, and music by Dane.
why: Sceners love it as a late-80s-style coder showcase: DYSPs, DYCPs, rasterbars and sideborder action pushed further than the originals. HCL's scrolltexts, Dane's music and Valsary's graphics get repeated praise.

quote.text: I love this demo... this is what demo used to be in the past, just better!

summary: Arkos' Amstrad CPC demo, coded and scored by Targhan with logo and font by Supersly, which placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2026.
why: A recent Arkos release that held its own in Revision's mixed oldskool compo, with Targhan handling both code and music.

summary: Invitation for the Silly Venture 2014 party on the Atari XL/XE, coded by 0xF with music by X-Ray.
why: A party invitation from the Atari 8-bit scene's biggest gathering. It is tagged as using commercial music, arranged by X-Ray.

summary: Proxima's Game Boy demo, coded by Leuat with graphics by Leuat and The Diad and music by Mibri, which came second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Solskogen 2020.
why: A podium finish in a mixed oldschool compo for a Game Boy production. The trse tag marks it as built with Leuat's TRSE toolchain.

summary: Enfys's BBC Micro demo, with code, graphics and music all by Enfys, which placed third in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2024.
why: A one-person BBC Micro production that held its own against other alternative platforms at Evoke 2024, taking third place.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by UriS that came second in the Oldskool 256b Intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2024.
why: A second place in the oldskool 256-byte compo at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Russian-speaking demoparties, is a solid result for a size-limited Spectrum intro.

summary: Amstrad CPC demo by Benediction, Hooy-Program and Revival, coded by Eliot with graphics by Voxfreax and music by Aki. It took second place in the CPC demo compo at Amstrad Expo 2010.
why: A runner-up at Amstrad Expo 2010 and a three-group collaboration. The stills show plasma patterns morphing in a narrow column beneath a logo.

summary: Rabenauge's invitation intro for the Deadline demoparty in Berlin (5th–7th October 2018), listed for the Commodore 64 and Commodore 128. It won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2018.
why: A compo winner at Nordlicht 2018, made to bring people to Deadline. Code, text and charset are by Bodo, with graphics by Titus and music by Dalezy.

summary: A TS-Conf demo for enhanced ZX Spectrum by b-state, with code, music and graphics all by wbc. It won the Demo compo at ZX Enhanced 2016; this is the party version.
why: A compo winner for the TS-Conf clone, and a one-person production, with wbc credited for code, music and graphics.

summary: Wrath Designs' C64 demo from The Party 1994, where it placed third in the C64 demo compo. Code by Ed, graphics by Joe and Blackdroid, music by guest PRI, with a politically themed run of large pictures.
why: Sceners call it mainly a graphics demo and rate the pictures highly, but also praise Ed's fractal flowers, landscape rendering and transitions that blend into the art. Several still return to it years later.

quote.text: Seen so many times by now and i still love it. The music, the graphics, the style, the atmosphere, everything.

summary: A Commodore PET demo by oobc (BassCadet and oo), made for the CBM 8032. It took second place in the Real Wild Demo compo at Assembly 2014.
why: A podium finish at Assembly's Real Wild compo for a machine rarely seen in demos, with code, music and design shared between BassCadet and oo.

summary: Lethargy's Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2019, with code by Visage and Ego, graphics by Grass, music by Vincenzo and Krill's loader.
why: Sceners welcomed it as fresh ideas from an old group, with a 90s feel and some parts they found really impressive. The skulls and the intro's perspective Lethargy letters get singled out.

quote.text: That intro with the Lethargy perspective letters. when I first saw them I fell off my chair ;)

summary: Hoaxers' Commodore 64 demo for a 512K RAM Expansion Unit, coded by Firehawk with graphics from Firehawk, Grasstust and Joe and music by Response. It placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2016.
why: A REU-powered C64 demo, the title's capitals giving away the hardware it needs, and a podium finish at Solskogen 2016.

summary: Padua's C64 intro that won the Intro Remake compo at X 2001, stringing together recreations of classic crack intros with logos, rasters and scrollers.
why: Sceners found it funny and entertaining, with curiosity building as it goes from one intro to the next.

quote.text: real funny and entertaining!!!curiosity builds up while the demo goes on.

summary: Fairlight's C64 invitation for the Axis of Evil 2007 party, coded by Hollowman with graphics by Hollowman and Vodka and music by Fegolhuzz. It placed 4th in the C64 Demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: Sceners singled out its raster effects and the stark black-and-white parts, which give it a distinctive look.

quote.text: Took me by surprise, I sure hadn't expected this kind of quality. Raster fx always make my day.

summary: Sappy is a 2007 Amstrad Plus demo by Semilanceata, with code and graphics by Grim and music by Romeo Knight and Clawz.
why: A demo written for the Amstrad Plus rather than the stock CPC. Grim also converted four-channel music down to three channels for it.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro by MadTeam and Lamers, coded by Tebe with music by Wieczór, that won the intro compo at Glucholazy 2015.
why: It took first place in the Glucholazy 2015 intro compo.

summary: A 512-byte ZX Spectrum intro by drwho that won the Combined 8-Bit 512b Intro compo at DiHalt 2012.
why: It took first place in a combined 8-bit 512-byte compo at DiHalt 2012, beating entries from other 8-bit platforms in the same size class.

summary: Taquart's 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit, coded by Eru with music by X-Ray, which won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2006. It shows a rotating globe in two shades of blue.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2006, fitting a spinning Earth and a soundtrack into a kilobyte.

summary: Rabenauge's 4K intro for the Commodore 64, coded by Bodo with graphics by Titus and music by guest Dalezy of Triad. It placed second in the C64 4K Intro compo at Datastorm 2017.
why: A second place at Datastorm squeezed into 4K, tagged minimal, with a credited guest musician in Dalezy.

summary: An MSX demo by Dvik & Joyrex, released in 2007 and placed third in the Demos compo at BCN Party 2007.
why: A podium finish at BCN Party 2007 from Dvik & Joyrex, a duo of well-known MSX sceners, makes it one for anyone exploring the MSX demo scene.

summary: Oxyron's deliberately 1987-style C64 demo, part of the Coma Light series, which came third in the Combined Demo compo at Maximum Overdose 2007: a logo, scrolltexts and a Fanta tune in old-school style.
why: Sceners enjoyed the retro joke and Fanta's David Whittaker-style tune, but also noticed the lower border scroller is wider than the screen should allow, apparently using the 9th sprite trick plus extra splits.

quote.text: This might look an easy intro, but there's something strange going on about the lower border scroll. It's too wide (seems like 52 chars)!

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Hacker VBI, with music by Brightentayle and lyrics by introspec. It won the Enhanced Demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015.
why: It took first place in its compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015. It also shows lyrics as part of the demo, which few Spectrum prods credit.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Satori and Agenda, coded by Svoy with graphics and design by Zden. It came second in the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k19.
why: A second place in a tough size-limited compo at Silly Venture, fitting sound and glitchy visuals into 256 bytes. It carries an epilepsy warning.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by sibCrew, coded and drawn by rook with music by MmcM and Quiet. It came second in the Low End Demo compo at DiHalt 2017 Lite.
why: A placing in DiHalt's low-end demo compo, and it uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which gives finer colour detail than the stock attribute grid allows.

summary: Code Busters' ZX Spectrum 128K trackmo, coded and designed by RST7 and Max Iwamoto, which placed third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1996.
why: A podium finisher at Enlight 1996 that leans on the Spectrum's multicolour mode, with music by RST7 and Jaan.

summary: Tulou's first Game Boy Color demo, first shown in the Oldskool Demo compo at Dreamhack 2000 (3rd), with a final version placing 6th in the Wild compo at Underscore 2001.
why: An early Game Boy Color demo from Tulou, with code by Altruist and Todi, graphics by Joker and music by Lilja. It placed at two parties, in two versions.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo remade for the VBXE video board, with code by Ajcek, graphics by At0m and music by Wieczor.
why: A showcase for what the VBXE expansion adds to the Atari 8-bit, released by Lamers as a special version of their Oldschool demo.

summary: Kowalski's 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2015, fitting its show into just one kilobyte.

summary: Houbba and Ruk's one-disk C64 demo, a character-mode conversion of the Big Buck Bunny animated film, with an intro by Houbba, an outro by Ruk and Ruk's soundtrack. Released out of competition at Datastorm 2012.
why: Sceners single out how smooth the video playback is and how much was fitted onto one disk, and they liked the intro, the outro and the music.

quote.text: Very smooth and with cool music. Great effort, guys!

summary: A BBC Micro demo by The Master from 2010, made for the BBC Master 128, with music by Jeroen Tel converted by The Master and a music player by RichTW.
why: A fairly rare full demo for the BBC Master 128, and a chance to hear a Jeroen Tel tune on Acorn hardware.

summary: Arise's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at BOOM! Party 2025, with code and design by Wacek, music by Jammer and hires graphics by Bimber and Pozmen Inc.
why: Sceners praise its pace and flow, Bimber's hires pictures and Jammer's single-SID tune, and single out the searchlight and water effects. Some say parts look like REU showcases without an REU.

quote.text: Beautiful graphics, great looking effects, nice pace and flow, and excellently fitting soundtrack.

summary: A ZX Spectrum invitation demo by sibKrew, with code and graphics by rook and music by Andy Fer. It won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2019 Lite and came third in the invitations compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2019 Lite that also placed at CAFe, and an invitation that, as its own text puts it, invites you to all parties at once.
highlights: "invite you to all parties at once"

summary: dA JoRMaS's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2021, a demake of the demo Darkroom, with code and music by Pekka Pou.
why: A compo winner that faithfully replays its source. One commenter notes it even matches the original's runtime. Sceners called it fresh and new on the machine, though some grumbled about it being a copy.

quote.text: Now this was something new on the good old machine.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2022, a large crew effort led by Magnar with graphics by Talent, Soya and Carrion and music by Magnar and Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out Talent's heavily dithered pictures, the bob scroller, the colour-cycling and Psycho8580's end-part tune, and note how much quality went into what Censor called a small in-between demo.

quote.text: So much quality here, really awesome stuff all the way through. The endpart tune is superb

summary: An 8K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Cosine, with code by TMR and music by 4mat. It won the unexpanded C16 (16K) intro compo at 4Ever 2003.
why: A compo winner at 4Ever 2003 that runs on the unexpanded 16K C16, from a small group of TED-machine productions by Cosine.

summary: HARD Software's two-disk-side Atari 8-bit demo from 1995, coded by Téli Sándor and Bene Tamas with music by Felker Farkas. It was entered in the Atari 8bit demo compo at QuaST 1995 but disqualified.
why: A sizeable mid-90s production from the Hungarian group HARD Software, spread over two disk sides. Its tags mark a juggler part, a nod to the classic Amiga animation.

summary: Atlantis's two-disk-side C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2019: a devil-and-angel themed run of effects and bitmaps, with music by DivertigO and Mibri and graphics by srt and Lobo.
why: Sceners praise its consistent evil theme, pacing and humour, and keep naming the snake scroller that twirls into the border, the raster-bar devil and the rotator.

quote.text: Really nicely put together this one, thematically consistent and well paced, with excellent artwork throughout.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K design demo by Not Affiliated with Gemba that won the Wild compo at Forever 2019. It runs from an MB-02 disk interface, with code, graphics and design by mborik and music by Nik-O.
why: It took first place in the Wild compo at Forever 2019, and its source is available. Busy, credited for BS-DOS kernel support, helped it run on the MB-02.

summary: Flush's 32K Atari 2600 demo, coded by flewww, p0ke and g012 with music by Glafouk, which placed second in the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A second place at Silly Venture's dedicated VCS compo, from a team of three coders working on one of the most restrictive machines the scene uses.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 64 by Resource and Royal Belgian Beer Squadron, with code by Edhellon and Oswald, music by 6R6 and graphics by Poison. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2020.
why: Sceners rate it highly for what it fits into 4K, and note that it even has an end part. The tune self-patches at the end to mute its volume.

quote.text: Really superb for the size.

summary: A one-file C64 demo by Gordian (code and visuals) with music by Shogoon, placed 3rd in the C64 Demo compo at Xenium 2024. Tiled, kaleidoscopic patterns animate in sync with the tune.
why: Sceners praise the clever, puzzling kaleidoscope effect, possibly a first on the C64, and how tightly it syncs to Shogoon's SID. The author says it was inspired by the Amiga demo Rule 30.

quote.text: I can't recall ever seeing a caleidoscopic effect like this one on the C64, the formula works very well.

summary: Genesis Project's three-disk-side C64 demo themed as an in-flight entertainment system on a flight from SFO to TPA. It came second in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2026.
why: Sceners praise how the airline story ties a dense run of effects together, along with the graphics, Mermaid's work in particular, and the laid-back music. Several felt it could have won.

quote.text: The fun, engaging and playful presentation really elevated the whole demo. Very nice effects, kickass music and the graphics...!

summary: An interactive glitch demo for the NEC PC Engine by !=, released in 2006 and listed as both a demo and a tool.
why: A rare PC Engine scene release that plays with glitch aesthetics and lets the viewer interact, rather than running as a fixed sequence.

summary: A 1991 ZX Spectrum demo by Ethanol Software Inc for the 48K machine with AY music. The video shows version 3.1 running on a V6Z80P.
why: A thin record, but an early-1990s Spectrum demo from Ethanol Software Inc that runs on a stock 48K machine.

summary: Beyond Force's C64 demo from Assembly 1996, where it placed second: a coder's showcase of big-pixel effects, each shown on a black screen with an explanatory caption, coded by Gremlin with music by Jeff and Boogaloo.
why: Sceners call it a real coders' demo, singling out the fast texture-mapped and shaded 3D objects and how smoothly it runs. Gremlin later explained the texture mapper used an algorithm designed specifically for this demo.

quote.text: Now this is your real "coders" demo. Nothing but black screens, the effect in question and an explanatory text. I like it!

summary: A BBC Master demo by Progen and Desire, with code by Progen, graphics by Luther and music by mAZE. It placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A recent example of the BBC Micro line pushed into a full demo, made for the Master and entered in one of the scene's biggest oldskool compos.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by TmK of deMarche, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2013.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Spectrum parties, and a cheeky title for a 1K entry.

summary: An Amstrad CPC intro by Project Argon and Symbiosis, released in April 2021, with code and music by BSC and graphics by rexbeng.
why: A small collaboration between two groups with no compo entry to its name, so it's one to watch for what BSC and rexbeng put together.

summary: GPRS's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2009: a sequence of hand-drawn monochrome cartoon scenes with typed-out captions telling a story.
why: It took second place in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2009, and its story-led, cartoon-strip approach sets it apart from effect-driven demos.

summary: Tight's Atari 8-bit demo from 1997, coded by Gumi with graphics by Vidol and music by Bac and X-Ray. It placed second in the Atari XL/XE demo competition at QuaST 1997.
why: A runner-up at QuaST 1997 from the Polish Atari scene of the late nineties, with a dedicated design credit for Waldi alongside the usual code, graphics and music.

summary: Shock is a 1992 ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Ethanol Software Inc, coded by Kaz, with a guest part coded by Mat and music and graphics by Ziutek.
why: An early Spectrum megademo that uses multicolour mode on a stock 48K machine with AY music. It is tagged as running on the TK90X clone too.

summary: A VIC-20 demo by Ate Bit, with code, graphics and music all by 4mat, released at Forever 2006 where it placed 4th in the Wild compo.
why: A one-person VIC-20 production from 4mat. It's worth a look for what a lone coder got out of the machine's chunky character-mode graphics.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit and stRing that came second in the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021. It draws curling, branching plant-like lines in monochrome.
why: A second place at Lovebyte 2021 in a size-limited category, from two coders packing a generative drawing into 256 bytes.

summary: Dentifrice's one-file C64 demo, third in the One-Filed Demo compo at BCC Party 2022: a cat rides a tank through a grey townscape while credits and greetings roll past.
why: Sceners love its charm and execution, with one comparing the tank to Metal Slug, and Proton's guest soundtrack gets singled out as something to leave playing for an hour.

quote.text: Absolutely love the music. Had this on my TV playing for over an hour.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by SquoQuo, coded by Hopper, that won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k13.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at Silly Venture 2013. The video is a live recording of the whole 256b compo filmed in the hall, so other entries appear too.

summary: A 1K intro for the Amstrad CPC by m_dr_m, released at Lovebyte 2024 where it placed fourth in the 1k Intro Oldschool compo.
why: A fourth place in a competitive Lovebyte size-coding category, packing its whole show into a kilobyte on the CPC.

summary: JAC!'s Atari 8-bit invitation intro for HomeCon 5, held on 23 January 2010 in Hanau, Germany, with music by 505. The video title describes it as a 16k intro.
why: A compact party invite from JAC! with the source code released. It's a neat example of an Atari 8-bit invitation intro and is well liked on Pouët.

summary: Krill and Dalezy's minimalist C64 demo, placed 12th in the Gravedigger compo at Nordlicht 2013: flat-shaded polygon shapes spinning over single-colour backgrounds, with vertical text spelling out the parts.
why: Sceners liked how it breaks the usual demo format, especially its random mode, and singled out the convex hull effect and the dots bouncing inside a filled shape. Some of it had sat unreleased for close to a decade.

quote.text: I like this as this work breaks the usual demo format, especially in the random mode.

summary: Onslaught's C64 cracktro from 2012, fronting their release of RGCD's The Mollusk Redux: a colour-cycling logo, bubble sprites drifting over the screen and scrolling credits text.
why: Sceners single out the cool music and neat design. One commenter saw it shown on German public television in a 2019 report on retro computing at Gamescom.

quote.text: Ahhh nice intro, very cool music and nice design..

summary: A single-screen Commodore 64 demo by Plush, released at the end of 2018, with code and music by Skate, music by Dgazz and graphics by Eyesee: a picture of hands holding a glass sphere, with coloured balls and a scroller.
why: Sceners praise how good the screen looks and the effect of the reflections, plus the border fades in the intro. Several welcomed it as new work from Skate after a long gap.

quote.text: Who needs a RTX2080 when you can have realtime raytracing on a C64?

summary: Neoplasia's C64 4K intro, coded by Viscid with music by SounDemoN, placed 4th in the C64 4K compo at Breakpoint 2003. It draws a Sierpinski triangle while showing the 6502 code that generates it, alongside live register values.
why: Sceners single out the presentation: a simple fractal turned into a live debugger view of the routine running in real time, which commenters call cool and original.

quote.text: But the whole presentation of this 4k intro is totally cool and original.

summary: A 1993 Atari 8-bit dentro by Code3, with code, graphics and music all by Soused Teat. It runs through shade-bobs, a Star Wars-style scroller, a tunnel and a zoomer, introduced by chunky on-screen text.
why: A one-man production from the Atari 8-bit scene of the early 1990s, packing a set of classic 2D effects into a compact dentro. It's still well regarded on Pouet.

summary: NedoDemo 2 is a demo for enhanced ZX Spectrum hardware (ATM Turbo / ZX Evolution) by mayHem, Alone Coder and Hooy-Program. It won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at DiHalt 2014 Lite.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2014 Lite that shows what the ATM Turbo and ZX Evolution machines can do, with graphics from Alone Coder, Jokov and Joulo and music by Yerzmyey.
highlights: wireframe polyhedron over a painted scene

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Abaddon, coded by TomCat and G.o.D with music by ern0, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 256b Intro compo at CAFe 2019.
why: A second place at CAFe 2019 in one of the tightest size categories, with its source released for anyone curious how it fits in 256 bytes.

summary: A Game Boy Color demo by AntonioND, who did code, graphics and music, with train and city art by jordirafel. It was entered in the demo competition at GBDev 2014.
why: A one-person showcase for the Game Boy Color's colour capabilities, as the title suggests, and its source code has been released for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A one-screen C64 demo by Focus, with code and graphics by Mirage, music by Hein and graphics by Sander: a driving scene salvaged from a larger planned project that previously existed only as a Flash animation.
why: Sceners praise the hires graphics and the four-frame mountain animation, and many liked Hein's quick-cut tune and the calm, cruising mood, though some wished the whole planned demo had been made.

quote.text: Great feel to this.. Smooth music, calm graphics.. Made me want to go for a drive and play some trance it did.

summary: Hoaxers' two-disk-side C64 horror demo, placed 7th in the Demo compo at X 2014. It plays like a film trailer with Alien-style opening titles, an ageing face and a dark end part.
why: Sceners single out Joe's artwork and the movie-like presentation, especially the alien egg with shadowed bobs in the end part. Axis/Oxyron called it underrated, noting that dark horror concepts rarely do well at parties.

quote.text: The whole demo feels like watching a trailer for a new upcoming Alien movie!

summary: Triumwyrat's multi-part C64 demo, winner of the C64 demo compo at Exile 1994, with code by Luke, Poacher, Pubi and Madrom and music from Cane, DOS and Reyn Ouwehand.
why: Sceners praise its polished presentation, humour and small details, and its loading animations. HCL notes it was a long project begun around 1991–92 that only spread years later. The texts in the end part moved at least one viewer.

quote.text: This demo is pure class!! Great code, graphics and music with very polished presentation, humour and fantastic ideas.

summary: A long-awaited C64 demo by 64ever, coded by Cybernator, packed with 2D and 3D effects, pictures and a story, with a hidden part you can continue past.
why: Sceners praised the sheer amount of work and the range of effects, plus a soundtrack by _V_ that several singled out. A few found the graphics uneven, which the graphician put down to them being drawn over years.

quote.text: Lots of graphics, good tricky effects, good story, both 2d & 3d stuff etc. This one has them all.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro by Sword, with code by Mały, music by Miker and graphics by Zajac. It took second place in the Atari XL/XE intro compo at QuaST 1997.
why: A second-place finish at QuaST 1997 makes it a solid example of the late-90s Polish Atari intro scene, with a three-person team behind code, music and graphics.
highlights: shaded vector objects in centre window

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation intro for Datastorm 2012 in Gothenburg, with code by MagerValp, music by Brandon Walsh and text by Sixx and Spot, shown as pages of party information over a blocky purple backdrop.
why: Sceners single out Brandon Walsh's tune above all, and also praise the two-colour font and how the parts work together as a whole.

quote.text: Very cool invite, love the tune and chars. Everything works well together, good job :)

summary: Lepsi Developments and Miracles' two-disk-side C64 demo, sixth in the C64 demo compo at X 2010, with code and graphics by Sebaloz and Zielok, guest art from Carrion and Joodas, and music by Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out Psycho8580's soundtrack above all, along with the large filled vectors, dithered bump-mappers and a custom greetings part designed for each group. Commenters call it raw and a little slow-paced but full of ideas.

quote.text: the biggest highlight of the prod. and, i'm not afraid of saying that, one of the greatest demo soundtracks ever!

summary: Desire's Commodore 64 demo, released at Function 2015 where it placed second in the Oldschool Demo compo. Code by Heaven, Popmilo and Oswald, graphics by BokanoiD and music by No-XS.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a promising debut, singling out No-XS's tune and BokanoiD's graphic style. Early versions crashed on machines with newer CIA chips, so the video is the easy way to see it.

quote.text: Loving the graphic style and the cool choon.

summary: Megahawks Incorporated's C64 demo styled as a lost 1988 production, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2006. It includes a MacGyver picture and a beach scene with a car driving along the road under a scrolltext.
why: Sceners liked how it catches the feel of the C64's golden era, right down to a loader true to the times, and the MacGyver and beach parts got particular mentions.

quote.text: Catches up the atmosphere of the C64's golden era pretty well. Also the loader is quite true to the times. :)

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro from Taquart, coded by Heaven, with music by Miker, Emkay and 505 and graphics by Zero-X. It opens on a text-mode greetings and credits page, then moves to a shaded twister.
why: A small, well-liked intro from Heaven on his return to demo coding, with a group of Atari music regulars sharing the soundtrack.

summary: Code Busters' 1994 ZX Spectrum 128K demo, with code by RST7 and Max Iwamoto and music from RST7, Klav and Andrew Kolesnik.
why: A mid-nineties Spectrum demo that makes use of multicolour mode, one of the tricks tagged on its entry. No compo history, but it has a steady following on Pouët.

summary: A one-screen Amstrad Plus intro by Impact, released in December 2017. Coded by AST over CeD's Sonic background picture, with sprite rings flying around and a scroller along the bottom.
why: A compact showcase of Plus-only hardware: hardware sprites over a detailed hi-colour picture, plus music with SID-style voices by AST and an Atari ST tune transferred by Mad Max.

summary: Null Form is a ZX Spectrum Next demo by Virtual Vision Group, with code by Rcl and graphics by Nodeus. It won the ZX Spectrum Next demo compo at speccy.pl party 2026.
why: A compo winner at speccy.pl party 2026 and a recent example of what the Spectrum Next can do in a demo. It is tagged as using AI-generated code.

summary: Lethargy's steampunk-themed C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2023, built around a story set inside a large, detailed machine.
why: Sceners call it refreshingly original and keep pointing to the small touches: the falling Lethargy letters at the start, steam sprites and the references in the time machine, along with Vincenzo's big tune.

quote.text: Ahhh, finally something original. Loved everything in this demo. The pace, the graphics, the idea, the music, and all the little details going on.

summary: A small one-file C64 intro by DaCapo, placed 8th in the Alternative Platforms compo at Evoke 2011. It shows large, blocky colour pictures mixed from checkerboard-dithered hires pixels.
why: Commenters call it small and enjoyable and praise its colours and Wolf's sound. Karoshier says it began as a 4K and grew to under 6K, and recommends a real TV, where the colour mixing looks best.

quote.text: nice, small and enjoyable. thumbs up and keep on coding

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by tr1x that won the 256b intro compo at Decrunch 2020.
why: A compo winner at Decrunch 2020, fitting several distinct scenes into just 256 bytes.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by MB Maniax and CI5 The Amaters, placed 4th in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2023, with graphics and music by Aki and code by Shrek, Logout and Noby.
why: A recent Spectrum group effort that made the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist after its Forever 2023 showing.

summary: Flush's New Year 2025 greetings demo for the Amstrad CPC, coded by CheshireCat with music by Siko. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at rsync 2025.
why: A seasonal greeting from Flush with graphics from several artists: Nougatine's background image, Exocet's dwarf animation and BDC Iron's cabin. It went on to compete at rsync 2025.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s Atari 2600 demo, coded by SvOlli and Peiselulli with graphics by DeeKay and Veto and music by Skyrunner. It placed 10th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019.
why: A group demo on the VCS, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, made by a team of well-known names across code, graphics and music.

summary: Padua's comeback C64 demo, coded by Dano and Doomed with music by Toggle and graphics by Alias Medron and Twoflower. It placed third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2017.
why: Welcomed as an unexpected return for Padua. Sceners praise its smooth flow, fresh design and the handwriting-style font effect, and single out the textured balls, sprite stretcher and rotator.

quote.text: smooth flow, fresh design, lovely work! luv it!

summary: Outsiders' ZX Spectrum demo that won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2018 Lite, pairing hand-drawn pictures with lines of text in a custom font.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2018 Lite, made by a small team with code by apeape, graphics by Blackbear, music by Nick Roll and text and font by intrigal.

summary: Section 31's C16/Plus 4 demo, winner of the old-school demo compo at QBParty 2018, with graphics by Harry and Shadow, music by Celticdesign and code by Murphy, Lavina and BSZ.
why: It won its compo at QBParty 2018 and is a recent, well-received example of a full demo on the C16/Plus 4. The video is the party version.

summary: Genesis Project's pig-themed C64 demo by Mermaid and Scrap, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2025. Flying piglets, a chessboard part, double 3D scrollers and an end scroller, all on one disk side.
why: Sceners praise Mermaid's cute, consistent style and the piggy animations, with a lot of affection for its feelgood humour. The chessboard and the 3D scrollers with curved corners are the parts they single out.

quote.text: I don't think the animations are praised enough. Best piggy-animation I've seen. That little jumping piglet that suddenly got wings brought a smile to my face.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Joker, coded by Dalthon and bfox with music by bfox and Fatal Snipe. It placed third in the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Forever 2024.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2024 in the 1K category, packing code and music from two musicians into a single kilobyte on a stock Spectrum.

summary: Gasman's 128-byte ZX Spectrum intro, which came second in the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2013. The video is live footage from the party hall.
why: A runner-up in a competitive size-limited compo at Outline 2013, packing its whole show into 128 bytes.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by iNSANE and Desire for the VBXE graphics expansion, placed 4th in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2018. Code by Axis and Heaven, music by Vedder and Triace, graphics by Jamon and Corel.
why: A collaboration between two groups that makes use of the VBXE expansion's extra colour on the Atari 8-bit. It placed fourth in a mixed oldschool compo.

summary: Samar's western-themed C64 demo with music by Jammer, graphics by Isildur and code by Don Kichote. It came 2nd in the Combined Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2017.
why: Sceners single out Jammer's soundtrack, a western-movie mashup with his groove sounds that several call unlike anything they'd heard. The demo itself is described as light and fun, with neat effects and Polish scrolltext.

quote.text: wonderful music, have never listened to anything like it :)

summary: Focus's C64 demo that placed third in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1993. The version shown there was incomplete; the finished demo followed in early 1995.
why: Remembered as classic Focus style, with sceners praising its routines and artwork. Compyx, who coded the final part, rates its bitmap font among his finest.

quote.text: Really great routines and also splendid art work.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 4K intro by Dalthon of Joker that won the ZX Spectrum Intro 4kb compo at speccy.pl party 2018.1: wireframe objects rotating on plain coloured screens.
why: It took first place in its 4K intro compo at speccy.pl party, a tidy example of what fits into 4 kilobytes on the Spectrum.
highlights: coloured title screen with vector shapes

summary: An intro for the Commodore PET by oobc, with code by BassCadet and oo and graphics and music by BassCadet. It placed third in the Old School Intro compo at Simulaatio 2016.
why: A rare modern release for the PET's green-screen, character-only display. The cbm-8032 tag marks it for the 80-column business model rather than the more usual 40-column machines.

summary: CRTC's BBC Micro demo, coded by Puppeh with music by Chip Champion, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2013.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2013 and a recent example of BBC Micro demo work, with graphics by Megmeg (an owl) and Tunk (font and final screen).

summary: Dream's Olympic-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Forever 2014, with code by DJ Gruby and kenji, music by MCH and graphics from six artists.
why: It also took Eternity Award #4 at Forever as the best entry fitting the Olympic party theme. Sceners single out the Winter Games part and MCH's music, and enjoy it as a fun themed demo.

quote.text: I have always loved themed demos and this one is just pure fun!

summary: A 1K intro for the Commodore 64 by Visac, LHS and PCH, coded by LHS and Visac with music from Visac and PCH. It won the Commodore 1K Intro compo at Forever 2009.
why: It took first place in the Commodore 1K intro competition at Forever 2009, so it's a worthwhile look at what this team fitted into a single kilobyte, music included.

summary: Desire's Commodore 64 invitation to Outline 2015, with code by Daison, graphics by BokanoiD and music by No-XS. Text messages and credits appear over a large Desire logo.
why: Sceners praised its clean design and smooth flow, and singled out No-XS's tune as a good fit for an invitation and Daison's return to coding.

quote.text: Cool design, smooth flow and some nice touches! :)

summary: Impact's Amstrad Plus demo, a sequel to 3DManiaks, with code by Demoniak, graphics by Kris and music by Ultrasyd. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2025.
why: A recent Amstrad Plus demo that made the top five in Revision's oldskool demo competition. Note that its graphics are tagged as AI-generated.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by xeen that placed third in the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021.
why: A podium finish at Lovebyte 2021 in a 256-byte category, so everything on screen comes from a very small program.

summary: A Genesis Project crack intro for the C64 from 2011, coded and drawn by Mermaid with music by Mr. Death: a pirate-ship deck scene with a cannon aimed at a galleon on a rolling horizon.
why: Sceners praise the cannon, the fonts and the moving horizon, and Karmic notes the border work that comes from one person handling both code and graphics. Several wished the cannon actually fired.

quote.text: Arrrr! That’s the finest pirate intro I’ve ever laid eyes on.

summary: A Genesis Project cracktro for the C64, released in 2014 with a preview of the game Eggland Mystery. The intro has code by WertStahl, a logo by Alien and music by MCH.
why: The intro was later released on its own. A crack group member said they loved it and singled out Alien's logo, and another commenter praised the tune.

quote.text: Hell Yeah - I *LOVE* this Intro! (Nice Logo by the other AliEN too ;)

summary: Puppeh's Nyan Cat demo for the BBC Micro, placed third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sunrise 2011.
why: A BBC Micro take on the 2011 Nyan Cat meme, made the same year and good enough for third place in the oldskool demo compo at Sunrise 2011.

summary: Proxima's C64 trackmo, coded in TRSE by Leuat with music by Mibri and mAZE, placed third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2022. It mixes fullscreen pictures from several graphicians with coded parts.
why: Sceners praise the fullscreen graphics, the soundtrack and the pacing, with one noting that no single part gets boring. Several call it a polished, stylish trackmo and a welcome return from the group.

quote.text: It's a nice lovely trackmo. Also some good gfx here and i adore the soundtrack.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Bug Powell and AST, with code by Bug Powell, graphics by AST and music by Dark Angel. It placed 11th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2022.
why: A small Revision 2022 entry from the CPC scene, worth a look for AST's big chunky logo graphics and its plea in the scroller to come back and save demomaking.

summary: sibCrew's demo for the TS-Conf enhanced ZX Spectrum, with code by wbcbz7, graphics by rook and music by Nik-O. It won the HiEnd 16mb Demo compo at DiHalt 2018 Lite.
why: A compo winner on TS-Conf hardware, worth a look for what the enhanced Spectrum can do beyond the stock machine.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by evilpaul (code), 4-Mat (music) and Eater (graphics) that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2004.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2004, made by a small three-person team.

summary: Target Team's ZX Spectrum demo, coded by Restorer with music by Fatal Snipe, which won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2020 Lite.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2020 Lite, and its source code has been released, so it's one to study as well as watch.

summary: A Moiré Misszió Bemutatja's C64 demo, coded by Blala with music by Slyspy, which won the C64 demo compo at BCC Party 2025. Expect bold geometric screens: stretched lettering, a warped chessboard and tiled triangle patterns.
why: Sceners call it a fresh take on C64 demos, praising its graphic design, Slyspy's fitting music and effects that look effortless but aren't, all running at a strict 50fps in hires.

quote.text: if you look closely all effects look effortless and trivial but most (if not all) are not trivial at all.

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum Next by Virtual Vision Group, with code, graphics and a music remix by Rcl from Kenotron's original. It won the ZX Spectrum Next Demo compo at speccy.pl party 2025.
why: A compo winner that packs a whole Next production into 4KB, beating full-size entries in the ZX Spectrum Next Demo competition at speccy.pl party 2025.
highlights: bold red, blue and yellow blocks

summary: A 1K procedural graphics prod for the ZX Spectrum by Virtual Vision Group, which won the oldskool procedural graphics compo at Chaos Constructions 2024.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2024 that builds a whole picture from 1K of code.
highlights: dithered spheres in white and cyan

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Phonex, placed second in the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at JHCon 2013.
why: A second place in the 1K intro compo at JHCon 2013, and a well-received entry on Pouët.

summary: NovaStorm's ZX Spectrum intro that came second in the ZX Spectrum Border Intro compo at DiHalt 2012. A dithered sailing ship sits on the sea under a setting sun while a message spells out inside a cloud.
why: A podium finish in DiHalt 2012's border intro category, a compo with tight size limits.

summary: Vision's 1990 Commodore 64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at the Censor and Horizon Halloween Party 1990. An effect-driven run of parts with plasma, a tech-tech scroller, filled vectors and vector bobs.
why: Sceners remember it as a demo of their childhood and a source of inspiration, singling out the plasma, the tech-tech scroller and Lars Hoff's tune Recovery. The carefully pixelled logos get praise too.

quote.text: Nice effect-oriented oldskool demo, which I clearly remember as a source of inspiration back in the days. The plasma and techtech-scroller are top-notch

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Raster, who did both code and music, placing second in the Atari 1K intro compo at Forever 2008.
why: A second place at Forever 2008 in the 1K category, with code and music both squeezed into a single kilobyte by one person.

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo that took second place in the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2013, with code by BriteLite, graphics by Bracket and music by Flex.
why: Sceners single out the design and graphics they see as Dekadence's trademark, sub-pixel balls and Flex's tune, though some wished for more variety. Reviewed in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: Love the design and the gfx, that has become the trademark of Dekadence. Nice little prod!

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by MagerValp, released in 2002 and placed third in the demo competition at Little Computer People 2002.
why: A podium finish at Little Computer People 2002, and a chance to see what the C16/Plus 4 could do in a period when few demos were made for it.

summary: Chorus's C64 demo from Breakpoint 2006, where it came 4th in the C64 demo compo, with code by Clarence, music by DRAX and graphics by Leon. The video shows the later Collectors Edition.
why: Sceners praise how smooth and polished it is, singling out Leon's unicorn pictures, his first in UFLI, along with the filled polygon part and DRAX's tunes. Several called it their favourite of the compo despite the placing.

quote.text: Watching this demo today for the first time - a pleasant surprise. So many nice things in there - fine routines, great music and gfx. Very well-polished.

summary: A small greetings intro for the Atari 8-bit by Desire, made for Nordlicht 2015, with code by Heaven, music by Miker and ATASCII graphics by Mario130XE.
why: A short, thin-on-facts greetro worth a look for its ATASCII logo work and as a party greeting from Desire to the Nordlicht crowd.

summary: No Name's C64 tech demo, placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2014: a sampled rendition of "My Humps" played through the SID, with open side borders, raster splits and scrollers running at the same time.
why: Sceners call it a benchmark in optimisation: clear sample playback alongside open-border sprites, rasterbars and scrollers, building on Algorithm's earlier work. It also marked CyberBrain's return to the scene.

quote.text: This is like a new benchmark in optimization. All this going on at once; splits, samples, like WTF?

summary: Flush's Atari 2600 demo marking the console's 40th anniversary, placed 2nd in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17. Code by g012, p0ke, Tjoppen, flewww and visy, graphics by Exocet and Glafouk, music by Glafouk.
why: A large group effort on one of the most limited demo platforms, made as a birthday tribute to the VCS and placed second at Silly Venture 2k17.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Kael of mayHem, a New Year greeting for 2018 that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2018 Lite.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at DiHalt 2018 Lite, packing a New Year message into 256 bytes.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by JAC!, with music by PG, that placed sixth in the Wild compo at Revision 2013. It is related to the earlier prod Spongy.
why: Its tags point to a Menger sponge and a monochrome look, an unusual subject for a stock Atari 8-bit, and it was strong enough to compete in Revision's Wild compo.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Mad Team, coded by Madman, which placed 4th in the 16kb intro compo at Last Party 1997.
why: A 256-byte entry that held its own against intros with far more room, finishing fourth in a 16kb compo.

summary: Wrath Designs' C64 demo from Assembly 1996, where it placed 4th in the C64 demo compo. Code by TMT and Ed, music by Ed, and graphics by Joe and Oxidy, including a fullscreen facial portrait and a Lenin title picture.
why: Sceners praise its flow and design, saying not a second is wasted, and single out the graphics. It's also remembered as the point where Wrath Designs started getting weird, with a Wolfenstein-style "doom" part coded by TMT.

quote.text: it has an exceptionally good flow. Not a second is wasted.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by tr1x, which placed 5th in the Oldschool Intro 256b compo at Demodulation 2020.
why: A size-coded intro that fits sound into 256 bytes, and its source code is available for anyone curious how it's done.

summary: An invitation for Datastorm 2019 on the NEC PC Engine by Resistance and Up Rough, with code by MooZ, graphics by Fra and music by Octapus. It placed 7th in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2019.
why: A rare scene prod for the PC Engine, made as a party invitation and entered in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2019.

summary: Oxyron's 1995 C64 demo, coded by Graham with graphics by RRR and music by Rob Hubbard, JCH, Jeff and PRI. A short run of effects: a picture wobbler, a fisheye picture scroll and a vector city.
why: Sceners remember Graham's picture wobbler, which combined y-stretching with x-flexing, as one of the most impressive effects they had seen, and praise the vector city whose buildings finally have windows. It was voted 13th best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: Don't think I've ever been that impressed by any effect as Graham's picture wobbler.

summary: Chorus's 2006 C64 demo, the final collectors' edition of Unicorn, with code by Clarence, graphics by Leon, music by DRAX and Krill's loader. It adds bug fixes and a soundtrack selector with bonus tunes.
why: Sceners praise the smooth, full-framerate effects and DRAX's funky music, and many single out the new music selector with its animated unicorn as a welcome extra.

quote.text: To create so many groundbreaking effects with constant full framerate is truly remarkable.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo from 2003, placed third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2003. Code by Hollowman and Puterman, music by Maktone and Abaddon, graphics by Hollowman, Vodka and Hobbit.
why: Sceners single out the last part as showing off Hollowman's skills, and a comeback picture from Hobbit also gets praise.

quote.text: Last part rocks, true Hollowman ninja skillz.

summary: An Amstrad Plus intro by Flower Corp., with code by Roudoudou, graphics by Fra and music by Tom&Jerry. It placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Very Important Party 2016.
why: A podium finish at Very Important Party 2016, and one of the few prods written for the Amstrad Plus rather than the stock CPC, as the ASIC in its title suggests.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 64 by Dekadence, with code, graphics and music all by BriteLite. It came second in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2017.
why: Sceners single out its looks: the rounded screen corners, a simple clean font and effects that aren't all chunky 4x4. One commenter rated it, purely on aesthetics, among the best 4Ks.

quote.text: purely from aesthetics this is up there with the best.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 1998, with graphics and code by AEG and music from several musicians including guest Orcan. It includes AEG's picture Tyrany from the same party.
why: Sceners call it the most polished Smash Designs demo, and one singles out the intro's pixel-by-pixel parallax scroll as an effect done only once. The endscroller also contains what may be the only marriage proposal in a C64 demo.

quote.text: AEG finally did it in the intro of our darkness - one of the best looking effects in C64 history me thinks, and done only once.

summary: A 1996 ZX Spectrum demo by Exodus, coded by Jordan, who also drew the graphics and wrote the script, with music from Agent-X, Roger (digital music) and Kriss.
why: A largely one-man Spectrum demo from the mid-nineties, with Jordan handling code, graphics and script, and three musicians contributing, including a digital music part by Roger.

summary: Dekadence's Christmas 2011 intro for the C64: a large hires DKD logo on a dark red background, scattered snowflakes and a scroller of greetings.
why: Sceners singled out the hires logo and the blocky fade that brings it in, along with a classic tune and a scroller that raised a grin.

quote.text: Love it! That logo is something else...wicked!

summary: Arsenic's C64 demo, released at Nordlicht 2013 where it placed 4th in the oldschool realtime demo compo. Code by Kronos and Yazoo, music by dEViLOCk and Kasmo, graphics by Yazoo, Death and Sphinx.
why: The one CSDb comment singles out its circle scroller. It was also reviewed in Nordic Scene Review #8.

quote.text: Love the circle scroller - just great, always happy to see a nice scroller

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Dalthon of Joker, with music by Pator, that came second in the 1K Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2023.
why: It was nominated in the Size constrained category at Siggraph Asia 2023, a notable nod for a 1K Spectrum production.

summary: R0ger's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2023: an Atari adaptation of Jiří Zmožek and Zdeněk Rytíř's song, with on-screen Czech and Slovak lyrics and two little bell-ringing characters.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2023, and it's tagged for speech synthesis, which gives the Atari a singing part.
highlights: Czech and Slovak lyrics on screen

summary: Fairlight's concept demo for the C64, coded by Abaddon with graphics by Tempest and music by Reed, placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2004. An improved version followed in 2007.
why: Sceners praised its unexpected style, attention to detail and Reed's heavy 8580 soundtrack, with one saying it should have won. The opening part's timing to the music was singled out.
highlights: "We control your red green and blue" text

quote.text: Completely unexpected and very welcome. Love the work put on details. Made my day!

summary: Triad's C64 4K intro that won the C64 4K Intro compo at X 2018, with code by Icon, visuals by Icon and ilesj and music by The Dungeon Master. It runs as an endless loop.
why: Sceners praise its polished design, the twisters and a bass-heavy tune that stands out for something so small. Burglar also singles out the Triad logo fade-in at the start and a motion-blur effect.

quote.text: Very nice, super polished little demo! Great stuff, respect for squeezing all that wobbling goodness out of 4K!

summary: Vengeance is an Atari 8-bit demo by Pentagram and Excellent that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at QuaST 1997. It needs 128K and features code by Bloomer and Kuchara with music by Josh.
why: It took first place at QuaST 1997, and its tags point to a cube, a fire effect and gouraud shading, which were ambitious work for the Atari 8-bit at the time.

summary: Genesis Project's one-file C64 demo built around Facet's futuristic city picture, with code by Shadow and music by Stinsen. It came second in the C64 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k20+1 SE 2021.
why: Commenters single out the futuristic cityscape itself, and Facet notes the train was inspired by Joe's city in Postcard from Earth 2.

quote.text: I love this futuristic picture!

summary: Chorus's C64 4K intro, coded by Clarence with music by Fanta, which came second in the C64 4K Intro compo at Breakpoint 2005.
why: Sceners single out the flipped Kefrens bars and how much, music included, was squeezed into 4K. Cruzer said they would have impressed him even in a full-size demo.

quote.text: the flipped kefrensbars would have impressed me, even if it was a normal size demo.

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 48K demo, placed third in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2015, with code and graphics by Noby, music and graphics by Lamer Pinky and text by Ellvis.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2015 from a small crew, and a farewell of sorts going by the title, told through hand-drawn pictures and a long text scroller.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by sibKrew, with code and graphics by rook and music by djnzx48. It placed second in the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2021.
why: A second place at DiHalt 2021's LowEnd Demo compo. The stills show a demo built around blocky typographic messages about years of scene boredom.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that placed second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2024.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions, one of the main Spectrum parties, makes it a solid pick from the 2024 Spectrum crop.

summary: A monochrome hi-res Atari 8-bit demo by Masters of Electric City, with code by Bob-er and music by Dhor. It came second in the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 SE.
why: A podium finish at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, and a demo that sticks to a strict black-and-white hi-res look throughout.

summary: Zelax's Atari 8-bit demo from December 1994, coded by Święty and Dudek with graphics by Pazur and music from Ramzes, Foster and Maestro.
why: A mid-1990s Polish-era Atari XL/XE demo with a full group credit list; worth a look for anyone exploring the platform's demos of that period.

summary: A 1999 ZX Spectrum demo by Claw, with code and graphics by DC Pak and graphics and music by Cat-Man.
why: A late-1990s Spectrum demo built largely around its artwork, with both credited members contributing graphics. There are no placings or comments to go on.

summary: A PETSCII story demo for the C64 by Hack n' Trade, shown in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011: a knight on horseback meets a big red monster, with music by Goto80.
why: Sceners single out the deliberately glitchy look, the scary monster and how Goto80's music makes the whole thing intense. It crashed on the big screen during the compo, and some thought that was part of the act.

quote.text: The music really made the whole demo intense! Wonderful feeling!

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Agenda, coded by Koala, that won the Atari XL/XE 256b compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at Silly Venture 2016, one of the main Atari 8-bit parties.

summary: Speccy.pl's 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum, which won the ZX Spectrum Intro 4KB compo at speccy.pl party 2019.1.
why: A compo winner on home ground: it took first place in the 4K intro competition at the 2019.1 edition of the Polish Spectrum party.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Dalthon of Joker, who did both code and graphics. It won the Oldschool Intro compo at Xenium 2019.
why: A compo winner at Xenium 2019 that fits a colourful dinosaur, built from triangles, and a greetings line into 1024 bytes.

summary: Vision's 8K C64 intro, coded and drawn by Hein with music by Johannes Bjerregaard, that won the 8K category at Intro Creation Competition 2022: a pack of runners and a dog give chase across a perspective field below a city skyline.
why: Sceners praise the idea as much as the execution: the convincing perspective on both figures and landscape, the animations and colours, and a soundtrack that fits the chase.

quote.text: The perspective and the animations are perfect - just the right level of complexity!

summary: Chorus's C64 demo from X 2008, where it placed 6th in the C64 demo compo: a record attempt at the number of DYCP (different-Y character position) sine scroller characters on screen, with code by Clarence, graphics by Leon and music by 6R6.
why: Sceners hailed it as a record-breaking DYCP demo, singling out Clarence's code alongside a well-liked soundtrack and tidy design, though some found it on the short side.

quote.text: Its not everyday you see a world record. Great work as usual from the Chorus team.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo, placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2026, with code by Eliot and Krusty, music by Warlord and graphics by Voxfreax and Retro-Vynz.
why: A recent CPC demo from an active group that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Revision. The video is a real hardware capture.

summary: Speedfisters' C64 demo that came second in the C64 demo compo at Deadline Harakiri 2006, with code by Demoman, graphics by Graphicsman and music by zabutom.
why: A podium finish at Deadline Harakiri 2006, and a chance to hear zabutom writing for the SID.

summary: Shadows' multi-part Atari 8-bit demo from 1994, placing second in the demo compo at Shadows Copy Party 1994. Code, music and graphics come from a large crew including Bartman, Jordan, Konop and Dave, with guest parts by Seban and Soused Teat.
why: A mid-nineties Polish Atari 8-bit group demo that took second place at its own party, with guest parts from Seban and Soused Teat alongside the core team.
highlights: guest parts by Seban and Soused Teat

summary: Phantasy's Game Boy Color cracktro and trainer menu for Tonka Construction Site, released in February 2003, with code by Lai, a graffiti logo by Desert, a font by Raver and music by 2Flower.
why: A neat example of the cracktro tradition carried over to Nintendo's handheld. It's affectionately known as Titty Twister.

summary: Sphere is an Amstrad CPC demo by Resistance, released in October 2022, with code by Roudoudou, music by Tom&Jerry and graphics by Beb and Hwikaa.
why: A recent CPC production from Resistance with a strong showing on Pouët. The fact sheet holds no compo placings or comments, so it's one to judge for yourself.

summary: Desire's Christmas 2012 intro for the C64: a panda in a Santa hat, pixelled by Alien, framed by two scrollers in Hammerfist's charset, with code by Daison and music by BokanoiD.
why: A warm seasonal greeting that sceners liked for Alien's panda, the sweet Christmas tune and the smooth coloured double scroll, with particular praise for the charset.

quote.text: I like everything about this little demo! If I must highlight something it must be the char and the effect through it!

summary: A new year intro for the Atari 8-bit by Desire, released at the start of 2017, with code by Heaven, music by Miker and graphics by Alien.
why: A small seasonal greeting from Desire. It's worth a look for its colourful raster-style effect running beneath a chrome Desire logo.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Qumi Team and sibCrew, placed second in the 8bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2018. It uses multicolour mode, with code by Denis Grachev and wbcbz7 and music by Nik-O and C-jeff.
why: Took second place at Multimatograf 2018. It is also a showcase for Spectrum multicolour graphics, with three graphicians credited: Denis Grachev, Robat and DMan.

summary: Dbug's Oric demo for the MCP40 printer, which placed 2nd in the Wild compo at Solskogen 2016. Instead of the screen, much of the show plays out on paper as the printer draws it.
why: An unusual take on an 8-bit demo: the output device is an Oric MCP40 printer. It placed second in the Wild compo at Solskogen 2016.

summary: In Memoriam is a C16/Plus 4 demo by Assassins, released in September 2007.
why: A thin fact sheet with no compo placing or comments. It's a Plus 4 demo from Assassins, for anyone exploring the machine's scene.
highlights: graphics credits for Luca and Kichy

summary: bfox's 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2016: rotating wireframe shapes floating above their own reflection.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2016, packing moving vector shapes into just 256 bytes on a stock Spectrum.

summary: Agenda's 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro, coded by Svoy, which won the 256b Atari intro compo at Riverwash 2018.
why: A compo winner at Riverwash 2018 in the 256-byte Atari category, worth a look for how much fills the screen from so little code.

summary: Fairlight's 1989 C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at the Light, Triad, Oneway Bålsta Party, with code by Judge, Wedge and Pernod, music by Wedge, Link and Danko, and a dragon picture by The Sarge.
why: Sceners single out Pernod's sprite-stretching DYSP part, which some argue is the first use of sprite crunching, plus the music and The Sarge's dragon graphics in the last part.

quote.text: The sprite cruncher is still a killer and it was absolutely amazing back then.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE by Ilmenit, placed third in the 128 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2025.
why: A podium finish at Lovebyte in one of the tightest size categories, from a coder whose video credits him to Agenda.
highlights: diagonal dirt track over striped fields

summary: BinCone is a 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Tygrys, released through speccy.pl, that came second in the Oldschool Intro compo at Xenium 2024.
why: A second place at Xenium 2024 against intros without the same size limit, done in just 256 bytes.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro from 1993 coded by JAC! with music by Chip Special Software, released as part two of the Visdom demo.
why: An early production by JAC!, who later became known for WUDSN. It is a short, simple intro with a thin record, of interest mainly for his early work.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Smash Designs, with code and graphics by AEG, code by DCP and music by SoNiC and Decoder. It won the C64 demo competition at Mekka & Symposium 1999.
why: It took first place in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 1999, one of the big German parties of the time. The fact sheet tags it as not safe for work.

summary: Symbiosis's 1994 Amstrad CPC demo, with code and graphics by Prodatron, extra graphics by Made and music by BSC.
why: A well-regarded CPC demo from Symbiosis, the group of Prodatron, who also handled much of the graphics himself. A thin fact sheet, but it has been warmly received on Pouet.

summary: Genesis Project's demo for the Sharp MZ-700, coded by Shadow with graphics by Illmidus and music by MCH. It placed second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly Online 2020.
why: A second place at Assembly against other oldskool machines is a solid result for a demo on the rarely seen Sharp MZ-700.

summary: CyberBrain's party-version C64 intro, placed 3rd in the Combined Oldschool Intro compo at TRSAC 2023: tiled, zoomed and stretched bitmap images flicking past in rapid cuts.
why: Sceners call it hypnotic and note that fast cuts like these are rare on the C64, with plenty of tech hidden inside. Several single out the flashing square zoomer, the beam effect and the multicolour mode switching.

quote.text: Nice!! These kind of fast cuts are rare on the c64

summary: A 32K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo, with code by Toms, graphics by Toxic and music by Mad Max. It opens on a picture of three golfers.
why: A compact CPC intro from a small team. It shows what fits in 32K: a full-screen illustration followed by a colourful scroller part.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, released in 2017 outside any compo, with code by several hands, music by Stone and Scarzix and graphics by Stone and Pal.
why: Sceners called it a nice surprise for a non-compo release, with the shadebobs and the diagonal scroller the parts most often singled out. The intro music also drew requests for a longer version.

quote.text: Nice surprise, very good demo for being released out of any compo. Shadebobs and diagonal stuff sticked out for me.

summary: Censor Design's one-disk-side C64 demo, a follow-up to their first Matrix demo from 2013, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2024.
why: Sceners single out Talent's detailed graphics, Magnar Harestad's soundtrack with well-placed samples and the polished, themed flow. It was nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2025.

quote.text: my winner of the compo. polished themed production with a good flow. and Magnar outdid himself with the perfect soundtrack.

summary: A ZX Spectrum tech demo by Physic, coded by Physic with music by MmcM and graphics by Diver, DMan, Zosya and Grongy. It scrolls full-screen multicolour pictures, as the opening text announces.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at The Meteoriks 2023, and the source code is available.

summary: Alpha Flight's C64 birthday demo for Irata's 50th, coded by The Gothicman and Xenox with music by Celticdesign, carrying birthday messages from a long list of sceners.
why: A warm scene tribute: commenters single out the touching texts and DMD's graphics, and it's a good example of the C64 community marking one of its own.

quote.text: i like it very nice and thanks for the touchy texts.

summary: Impact's Christmas demo for the Amstrad Plus, released December 2023, with code by Demoniak and graphics by Kris.
why: A seasonal greeting from Impact that uses the Plus hardware. It's a short festive watch rather than a compo entry.

summary: The Solution's C64 demo, coded by Silpheed with graphics by Se7en and music by Xiny, placed 3rd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2018. A purple checkerboard backdrop sits behind the group logo and a scrolling message.
why: Silpheed's first C64 production after years on PS1 and Amiga. Sceners praise its style and design, Xiny's tune in particular, and a checkerboard zoom that caught people out.

quote.text: i love this, super stylish, all the music and movement comes together so nice!

summary: An MSX demo by Lieves!Tuore, with code by Marq, music by Yzi and graphics by Manu, which took second place in the demo compo at Alternative Party 1998.
why: A runner-up at Alternative Party 1998 from a Finnish group better known for other platforms, and a rare scene demo on the MSX from that era.

summary: A 512-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K by Siberian Group, with sound, which came second in the ZX Spectrum 512b intro compo at CAFe 2003.
why: A second place at CAFe 2003 in one of the tightest size classes, packing both graphics and sound into 512 bytes.

summary: Dmitry_Milk's ZX Spectrum beeper demo, second in the Demo compo at DiHalt 2026 Summer, built around vocoder-style vocals over a pixel-art scene of a skeleton at a computer.
why: A Spectrum demo where the beeper, not an AY chip, carries vocoder vocals, and it placed second at DiHalt 2026 Summer.

summary: Finnish Gold's two-disk-side C64 demo, third in the Zoo 2022 demo compo, with code by Proton and Serato, music by Proton and Rock, and graphics by Pal.
why: Sceners point to the amount of top-notch code, especially the perspective scroller reflected in a ray-traced mirror ball, along with Pal's hires graphics and the mood of the disk side 2 soundtrack.
highlights: perspective scroller mirrored in a ball

quote.text: What’s not to love about this demo? Everything works perfectly together. Pal’s graphics really made me smile throughout the demo – enjoyed every plotted pixel.

summary: Singular's short C64 demo that won the Commodore Demo compo at Forever 2006, with a plasma, a wireframe object, metaballs, a picture by Leon and an upscroller ending.
why: A compact party winner. Sceners single out the smooth plasma and the nostalgic end upscroller with 1x1 and 1x2 fonts and simple ASCII art, reminiscent of old disk magazines.

quote.text: Quite smooth and good looking effects (plasma rocks!).

summary: A BBC Micro demo by Neurotypical, coded by Puppeh, that came 2nd in the Oldskool demo compo at Sundown 2009.
why: A podium finish in a mixed oldskool compo for a BBC Micro demo, a machine that rarely turned up at demoparties at the time.

summary: A Genesis Project cracktro for the C64 by Mermaid, who did code, music and graphics alone, made in a 1988 style. It won the Oldskool Demo compo at SynchroNY 2016.
why: Sceners loved its nostalgic feel, saying it took them back to watching intros in front of games as kids, and singled out the twinkling logo and its polish.

quote.text: Brings back the time when I was a kid and was looking at these strange stuff infront of my games with wonder ^_^ A lovely release!

summary: Fraction's Commodore 64 demo from 1998, winner of the C64 demo competition at North Party 1998.
why: It took first place in the C64 demo compo at North Party 1998, a solid late-nineties showing from Fraction.

summary: Lethargy's two-disk-side C64 demake of Gargaj's PC demo Median, placing 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2021. This is the party version, built with the Sparkle loader.
why: Sceners praise its fresh, animated design and tight sync, and many didn't realise it was a port until told. Even those who did called it a seriously impressive conversion that shows how much design space is left on the C64.

quote.text: Superb demo! It's fantastic to see how animated demos with great concepts take the whole idea of demo art to another level!

summary: Inka's Game Boy Color demo, second in the Console Demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2002, with code by Lai, music by Psychad and graphics by Gaxar and Zaphod. The video is captured from a real handheld.
why: A podium finish in the console compo at one of the big German parties of its day, and a chance to see the work running on real Game Boy Color hardware rather than an emulator.

summary: Ilmenit's 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari 256b intro compo at Lost Party 2020. It moves through generated patterns, from a Sierpinski triangle to fanned colour stripes and layered hills.
why: A compo winner that fits several distinct generated scenes and sound into 256 bytes. The source is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Realm Of Illusion's Vectrex demo, coded by Frog with music by C-jeff and voice by Random. It placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2015.
why: A rare demo for the Vectrex's vector display. Its Solskogen compo entry makes it a good chance to see what the machine can do in scene hands.

summary: Ancient runes is a ZX Spectrum demo by Q-Bone, released in 2017. It came second in the LowEnd Demo competition at DiHalt 2017.
why: A second place in DiHalt 2017's LowEnd Demo compo makes it a solid example of Spectrum demo work from that year's Russian party scene.
highlights: dithered textures shifting beside the artwork

summary: Orange's first Commodore 64 demo and the third part of their Television series, with code by Galvados, music by Zardax and graphics by Der Piipo and Jate.
why: An Amiga group's long-awaited arrival on the C64. Sceners single out the subpixel rigid-body physics and antialiasing, Zardax's bass-heavy tune and the final Orange logo.

quote.text: Loving subpixel rigid body physics and antialiasing (shown for a bit too short though!). Final logo piece is outstanding too.

summary: ThePetsMode's MSX1 demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019, with code from JamQue, Napalm, Fubu and Mvac7 and music by JosSs.
why: A recent MSX1 group demo that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Revision, with several coders and graphicians pooling their work.

summary: Padua's C64 trackmo that won the Trackmo compo at BCC Party 2020, with code by Dano and Doomed, music by Toggle and graphics by Jailbird, Twoflower, Shine and Cupid.
why: Sceners call it fast-paced, with a good variety of parts. They single out the cube part, the vortex and Toggle's tune, and praise how familiar effects get their own twist and are glued into one stylish demo.

quote.text: Yes, lots of parts we’ve seen in other productions - but you’ve brought something to each one to glue them together into a very cool demo.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Flush, with code by flewww, graphics by Exocet and music by Glafouk. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2018.
why: A size-limited intro on one of the most constrained machines around, and it made the podium at Revision. The source is released under the GPL for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Visac and LHS that placed 4th in the Demo compo at Árok 2011. The video, filmed off the party screen, calls it a 4K intro.
why: A small Plus/4 entry from the Hungarian Árok party, shown here as the audience saw it on the big screen.

summary: Abyss-Connection's C64 anniversary slideshow marking the group's 20 years, with pictures by six graphicians and music by FieserWolf. It placed 5th in Alternative Platforms at Evoke 2011.
why: Sceners praise the pictures, FieserWolf's music and the way the bitmaps fade in and out. One singles out the screen being reinstalled at the end.

quote.text: Very cool demo, I like the way the bitmaps fade, the music and art here is fantastic also!

summary: A Vectrex 64K intro and invitation by the Carnegie Mellon University Computer Club, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at @Party 2019.
why: A first-place compo winner on the Vectrex, a vector-display console rarely seen in demo competitions.

summary: New Generation and Zelax's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 SE, with code by Święty, Yosh, Solo and Laoo and music by Miker, ZoltarX and Tatqoo.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, made by a large crew of coders, musicians and graphicians. It needs a machine expanded to 512K.

summary: Beyond Force's C64 demo from Light and Phenomena Easter Party 1992, where it came second in the demo compo. Coded by Gremlin, Sam and Tnt, it opens with a text flasher over a 3D starfield.
why: Billed by its makers as the first palindromic demo on the C64 (read the title backwards), and a runner-up at a major Swedish party of the time.

summary: EXclusive ON's C64 demo, which came third in the C64 demo compo at North Party 2006. Volcano coded it, with graphics by Jammer, Bedrich and Sunset and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners single out the hires graphics and fast realtime effects, and several felt it deserved a higher placing; it was shown unfinished at the party.

quote.text: the hires gfx are really good

summary: Alone 34 is a ZX Spectrum demo by mayHem and Skrju, released in December 2015 for the enhanced Spectrum models.
why: A joint release between mayHem and Skrju. There are no compo results, notes or comments on record, so the video is the best guide to it.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2008, built on a monochrome, heavily distorted look with bouncing balls, sine screens and transforming letters.
why: Sceners credit its daring, original style and hypnotic, looping atmosphere, and enjoyed seeing effects revived that hadn't been used for a decade. The bouncing balls on the sine screen are the most-praised part.
highlights: balls bouncing on a sine screen

quote.text: Mesmerizing! Hypnotic! And quite original, too! That style, the looping tune (and demo). I found myself watching it two times in a row

summary: Dragon Software Productions' C64 demo from 2000, placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000. Code by Fenek and Wedlock, music by Praiser and Sage.
why: Sceners praise its music and the way the parts' mood fits it. Coders credit Fenek with an early "2nd Pixel FLI" mode that later prods such as The Larch borrowed from.

quote.text: Somehow the music and the feeling of the parts fitted so well together, and the now dated design was really creative.

summary: A joint Amstrad CPC demo by Hardos, Vanity, Benediction, Shinra and Dentifrice, coded by Krusty with music by PulkoMandy, which placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2024.
why: A multi-group CPC collaboration with a deep graphics roster in Voxy, Slyder and Exocet, plus Beb on rasters, that competed at Revision, one of the biggest demoparties.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Arkos from 1999, with code, design and music by Targhan and an end part drawn by Toms.
