why: A largely one-person production: Targhan handled the code, design and music himself. Worth a look for anyone exploring late-1990s CPC demos.

summary: The Megademo is a 1988 Commodore 64 megademo by Higher Intelligence Company: a run of parts with scrolling messages, raster bars and a drummer part with a digitised tune.
why: Sceners remember it as one of the first megademos they saw and still rate it highly. They single out the music throughout, the raster bars and the drummer whose hands are synchronised with the audio.

quote.text: the guy playing drums is so cool: synchronized audio with the guy's hands. And also the drum the guy beats on changes accoring to the played drum.

summary: Gordian's minimalist 16K intro for the C64, with music by Jammer and a font by Tao, that won the C64 intro compo at Xenium 2025: white dots gather, scatter and orbit around a single ball.
why: Sceners praise its minimalism, its originality and how well Jammer's music fits, with several comparing it to watching a short film. Coders singled out the plotting trick of sharing dynamically built characters between dots.

quote.text: A visually minimal impression that becomes something truly enormous in the mind.

summary: Marquee Design's 256-byte procedural graphics prod for the Atari XE/XL, which won the oldskool procedural graphics compo at Lovebyte 2024. It draws a faceted pink seahorse against a banded blue underwater backdrop.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2024, packing a recognisable underwater scene into 256 bytes of code.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Amstrad CPC by Overflow, placed 5th in the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2024.
why: A compact size-coding entry from a dedicated tiny-intro party, showing how much screen activity fits into 256 bytes on the CPC.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by g0blinish, with music by Ahim, that placed third in the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2020.
why: A podium finish at Demosplash 2020's retro compo. It's a small one-coder Spectrum production that asks, in its own words, whether demomaking makes sense.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Gemba Boys, with code from Noby, Busy, UB880D, Logout and Poke and graphics by Noby, Logout and Trixs. It came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2011.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2011 made by a group of well-known Slovak Spectrum coders, with each part credited on screen to its author along a status bar.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource, coded by Oswald, Edhellon and Blala with graphics by Poison and music by Jammer. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2024.
why: A second place at Revision's Oldskool 4K Intro compo, against entries from every classic platform, makes it a good look at what a modern team can fit into 4K on the Plus 4.

summary: Da Boxon Team's Amstrad Plus intro, coded by Nicky One with graphics by Bouba and music by Giherem. It came second in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 in 2024.
why: A comeback release: the scroller says it arrives 26 years after the group's last demo, made for the CPC fans who kept the scene going. It took second place at Benediction Coding Party #4.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by superogue, released under Marquee Design's channel, that placed second in the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2021.
why: A second place at DiHalt 2021 for an intro of just 256 bytes that includes sound, coded and designed by superogue alone.

summary: A 2K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Benediction, coded by Eliot with music by Warlord, which placed third in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #6 in 2026.
why: A compo placer that packs a scene and a soundtrack into 2K, with Voxfreax credited for the palette work.
highlights: sky colours that shift through palettes

summary: Sage's Atari Lynx demo, coded by Sage with graphics by Flash and Lowlife, which placed second in the Intro compo at Error In Line 2003.
why: The notes bill it as showing effects never seen on the Lynx before, including HiColor graphics beyond the handheld's usual 16 colours, set to a digital soundtrack.

summary: A C64 demo by Funkentstört, with code by Kometbomb and graphics and music by Ilkke and Animal Bro, placed 3rd in the Oldschool demo compo at Flashback 2014. A cartoon cat sits over a patterned backdrop while text scrolls beneath.
why: Sceners single out the catchy, stuttering tune and the cute cat art, with one wishing there had been more of it.

quote.text: That stuttering tune is so catchy.

summary: Genesis Project's wintry C64 graphics demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2020: a slideshow of hires pictures by Mermaid, Shadow and Redcrab with scrolltexts and music by Zyron.
why: Sceners praise the warm, nostalgic artwork and the smoothly animated sprite scarf above all, along with the parallax landscape and the scrolltexts. Several thought it deserved a higher placing.

quote.text: This is really a demo, which easily could be shown to almost all kinds of audience outside the nerdy c64 kit and be appreciated.

summary: Overflow's 256-byte intro for the Amstrad CPC, placed 6th in the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2024.
why: A compact size-coding entry from a recent Lovebyte, and a writeup is available for anyone curious how it fits in 256 bytes.

summary: A 1991 Amstrad CPC demo coded by Elmsoft Game Service: a figure walks across a chequerboard floor beneath big colour-gradient scrolltexts, with an on-screen "Demo time left" countdown.
why: A thin fact sheet with no compo history or comments, but a period CPC demo that pairs vector and ball-built 3D figures with raster colour scrolling in a single scene.

summary: A Christmas-themed Amstrad CPC demo by Arkos from 1997, with code by Targhan, Orphée and Rainbird, graphics by Rainbird, and music from Targhan, Tom&Jerry and Rob Hubbard.
why: An Arkos group effort from the French CPC scene of the late 1990s, warmly received on Pouët. It is tagged nsfw, so expect some content not for every audience.

summary: SquoQuo's Atari 8-bit intro, which won the size-limited realtime compo at Demodays 2014. A SquoQuo logo and scrolling text messages sit over a cyan checkerboard.
why: A compo winner at Demodays 2014, with code by Hopper, music by 505 and graphics by Widdy and Raven.

summary: An MSX2 demo by N.I from 2017, built around a single pixel-art picture of an anime-style girl in an MSX-branded sailor top, wired up with cables.
why: A small one-picture demo that leans on the MSX2's palette. The same drawing is recoloured through very different schemes over its run.

summary: Some Old Stuff (S.O.S) is a Game Boy Color demo by R-Lab released in 2000, with code by Quant and Dark, graphics by Juge and Dark, and music by DNK and Dark.
why: A Game Boy Color demo from 2000 that collects R-Lab's earlier material, which makes it a look at the group's work on the handheld at the turn of the century.

summary: Hooy-Program and Raww Arse's ZX Spectrum 48K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2001, with code by Gasman, a large graphics team and a guest part by ZeroTeam.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2001, and it pulls together work from several Spectrum artists and musicians. It's also tagged for using the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Software Failure, with code, graphics and music all by Ham. It placed 4th in the Open Intro compo at Euskal 2024.
why: A one-person production squeezed into 16K that held its own in a mixed-platform intro compo at Euskal 2024.

summary: Atari 8-bit demo by New Generation and Zelax, built around a robot theme, which came second in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2023 from a large joint crew, with kris3d credited for the idea and 3D graphics and music from ZoltarX, Tatqoo, LiSU and Miker.

summary: Genesis Project's one-file C64 demo built around a graffiti theme: a big Genesis Project logo by Alien with a spray-can scroller painting text beneath it, to a hip-hop tune by MCH. Placed 3rd in C64 Demo at Demo of the Year 2014.
why: Sceners single out the spray-paint scroller and how well MCH's music suits the theme, calling the whole thing a stylish little package with plenty of attitude.

quote.text: Everything fits together, with a badass attitude. Really cool.

summary: Desire's 8K intro for the C64, coded by Daison with music by No-XS, a big graffiti-style logo by BokanoiD and a charset by Hammerfist. It came third in the Intro Creation Competition 2013.
why: Sceners single out the logo, praised for being pixelled without heavy dithering, and the way Daison makes simple FLD bouncing look like an Amiga intro.

quote.text: Wow.. the logo is impressive .. another excellent example to pixel without too much dithering. top notch!

summary: Light's C64 demo that took second place in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994, with code by Yabba, Flamingo and Waco and music by Rob Hubbard and Martin Galway.
why: Sceners single out how complex and fast the effects were for 1994, especially the raytracer, the bezier curve morph and the multicolour Doom-style 3D part at the end.

quote.text: Looking at the year (94) it's hard to believe the complexity and speed of the effects.

summary: A cracktro-style Amstrad CPC prod by Vanity, with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and Targhan's remix of the Saboteur 2 music. It came 2nd in the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2018.
why: A second place at ReSeT 2018 from a small team of well-known CPC names. It's a short, single-screen piece worth a look for its split-screen layout.

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Legion Of Doom and Absence And Wilds, with code and music by Csabo and graphics by Chronos. It took second place in the demo compo at Árok 2011.
why: A Plus/4 take on the Nyan Cat meme that placed second at Árok 2011, made by a small team where Csabo handled both code and music.
highlights: pixelled Nyan Cat with rainbow trail

summary: Onslaught's C64 4K intro, coded by Enthusi with graphics by Veto and music by Conrad, placed 6th in the combined compo at BCC Party 2011. It builds a scrolling picture of a swan entirely from raster splits.
why: Sceners praised it as an original use of raster splits, a new graphics trick the group named "PRS" for permanent raster split. Several compared the blocky look to the Atari 2600, and one called it the highlight of the party.

quote.text: Wow! Beautiful to me, this is probably my fave new gfx mode since interlaced PETSCII.

summary: Crest's 1997 Commodore 64 demo, the follow-up to Krestage, coded by Crossbow with an endpart by The Syndrom and music from Mitch, Dane, The Syndrom and guest JCH/Vibrants.
why: A well-rated Crest demo on CSDb. Sceners single out the intro and the stretching logo, and some still prefer the original Krestage.

quote.text: The intro and logo stretch look very nice.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Peiselulli and SvOlli, which placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k compo at Revision 2014.
why: A size-limited intro on the 2600, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, that held its own in an oldskool compo. Its source code is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo from Cosine, coded and drawn by The Magic Roundabout with music by Sack, which came 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006.
why: Sceners call it small, simple and stylish: no killer effects, but tidy oldstyle routines, neat pictures by T.M.R and a short lo-fi tune from Sack.

quote.text: Very wonderful, simple but so stylish. More of this, please.

summary: A 16K C64 intro by EXclusive ON, made single-handedly by Jammer (code, graphics, music), placing 5th in the Intro Creation Competition 2016: a big logo over layered raster stripes with a greetings scroller.
why: Jammer's debut as a coder, and sceners were impressed that he wrote his own sample player alongside a funky original track. They also single out the layered raster effect, which one called a tribute to tape-loading stripes.

quote.text: Feels very oldschool yet very fresh at the same time, impressive!

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Active, coded by Artlace, released at Datastorm 2014 where it placed 14th in the C64 demo compo.
why: A small party demo with a thin record. It's worth a look for its digitised portrait picture and its greetings grid of group names.

summary: Retro Plasma is a Commodore 64 demo by Return, released at 7DX 2011 where it placed 4th in the Demo compo. It runs a blocky colour-cycling plasma behind a checkerboard, with credits for music by Slowhand and logo by Spritus.
why: A small, tidy production that sceners praised for its polish, noting Return seemed to improve with each release.

quote.text: it's just the type of small and polished code I like.

summary: A demo by g0blinish for the ZX Spectrum's TS-Conf enhanced configuration (Pentevo), which won the Low End Enhanced Demo compo at DiHalt 2017 Lite.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017 Lite and a rare example of a demo written for the TS-Conf enhanced Spectrum hardware.

summary: Fatzone's Commodore 64 demo, coded by Pezac and Malmix, which won the Commodore demo compo at Forever 2009. Pezac also wrote the music, Malmix the graphics.
why: It took first place in the Commodore demo competition at Forever 2009. The credits also name a loader by The Dreams and a music player by JCH.

summary: Rainbow is a ZX Spectrum demo by GDC that placed second in the wild demo competition at Riverwash 2016.
why: A podium finish in Riverwash 2016's wild demo compo. The fact sheet has no comments or notes beyond that placing, so the video has to make its own case.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Kpacku, coded by Trefi with graphics by prof4d and Tutty and music by Nik-O. It placed second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015.
why: A runner-up at 3BM OpenAir 2015 that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to push more colour into its artwork than the standard attribute grid allows.

summary: Desire's invitation to Silly Venture 2017 in Gdańsk for the Atari 8-bit, with code by Heaven and Popmilo, graphics by Moonwalker and Veto, and music by Miker. It placed 6th in the 8-bit demo/intro compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2017.
why: An Atari party invitation made by a full Desire line-up of coders, graphicians and a musician, and it was entered in the RetroKomp / Load Error 2017 8-bit compo.

summary: Michael Park's 1985 Atari 8-bit demo for Xanth F/X: a red-and-white chequered ball bouncing across a teal grid, casting its shadow as it goes.
why: An early answer from the Atari 8-bit to the Amiga's famous Boing Ball demo, showing the older machine could put on the same show. One of the oldest prods on the site.

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, placed sixth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2025, with code and graphics by Heaven, graphics by Gaspar, music by mAZE and a 3D engine by Probe.
why: A recent Atari XL/XE entry at Revision with a credited 3D engine from Probe alongside Heaven's code and graphics, placing sixth in a competitive oldskool field.

summary: Iris is a 1997 ZX Spectrum demo by Flash, also credited as Flash Inc in the video title.
why: A late-90s Spectrum demo with no compo record. Worth a look for anyone exploring the Spectrum scene of that era.
highlights: dotted line curves in ornate frame

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, an invitation to Sundown 2013, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2013. Chunky, dithered pictures sit above a text scroller.
why: A runner-up at Assembly's oldskool compo, and an invitation intro on a stock 48K Spectrum with AY music.

summary: Faque's one-file Commodore 64 demo from 1999, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 1999.
why: Sceners point to the code: an animated raytraced shadows effect and an interference part, which one commenter rated good for 1999 and still spectacular years later.

quote.text: good code for 99 but even spectacular today, the raytrace stuff is animated.

summary: A 256-byte tunnel intro for the Atari Lynx by 42Bastian, placed third in the 256-Byte Intro compo at Sommarhack 2020. The video title puts it at 249 bytes.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, and a rare tiny intro on the Lynx. The source code is available.

summary: Offence's one-file C64 demo from December 2018, a tribute to BHF/Abnormal, who died that April. Pal's portrait of Bård sits beside messages from his friends, with code by Perplex and music by GT.
why: Sceners call it a heartfelt tribute where everything feels right, and single out GT's soundtrack of more than ten minutes, especially its SID guitar solo, as one of the finest C64 tunes.

quote.text: This is a really emotional tribute and everything seems just right - coding, phenomenal music, mood and texts.

summary: Impact's Amstrad Plus demo from 2023, coded and drawn by Kris with music by Pator, opening on a grim reaper title screen.
why: A recent one-person code-and-graphics showcase for the Plus hardware, with a soundtrack by Pator. It went down well on Pouët.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Impact, released in 2021.
why: A thin fact sheet, but the title suggests pictures built from triangles, and the stills bear that out with flat-shaded geometric images.

summary: A Commodore 64 intro by Genesis Project, with code, music and graphics all by Mermaid, that came 4th in the Intro Creation Competition 2016. Shaded bubbles drift around big Genesis Project logos above a scroller.
why: Sceners single out the graphics: logos built from multicolour sprites with a hires character overlay, and shaded bubbles mixing multicolour and hires. Several commenters say it has an Amiga feel, and coders expected the technique to be copied.

quote.text: Absolutely brilliant use of hires and multicolor. Thanks for sharing the behind-the-scenes screenshots. Totally blows me on how beautiful this looks.

summary: Finnish Gold's C64 demo, first shown at Zoo 2019 where it placed 5th, then released in its complete 100% version two years later, winning the combined demo compo at Saunasolmu 2021.
why: A long-gestating group effort with code, music and graphics by Proton, plus logos by Pal and Shine. The finished version took first place at Saunasolmu 2021.

summary: Bonzai's two-disk, James Bond-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2022: a run of scroller parts with graphics by Facet, The Sarge, Dize and Fox and music by DRAX, Laxity and Metal.
why: Sceners praise how it pulls off its effects while sticking to one theme, with Facet and The Sarge's graphics and the Bond-flavoured music singled out, along with the comic James Band part.

quote.text: I am deeply impressed by how you pull off all the effects while sticking to one chosen theme, which was James Bond this time.

summary: A three-screen oldschool C64 demo by Noice, released in 2011, styled after early-90s demos: big colourful logos, scrollers and sprite effects, with logos by Rocket.
why: Sceners welcomed it as oldschool done properly, praising the effects, the logo design and the flying logo in the first part. Comments also mention it set a record, with Axis and Cruzer promising to beat it.
highlights: flying logo in the first part

quote.text: finally someone not using oldschool as an excuse for being lame :) very nice.

summary: A ZX Spectrum birthday intro by Togyaf, released in September 2011 as a gift.
why: A small personal prod from the Spectrum scene, made as a birthday present and worth a look as an example of the scene's gift-intro tradition.

summary: A Halloween intro for the Amstrad Plus by Impact, with code by Demoniak and graphics by Kris. It placed 2nd in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 2024.
why: A seasonal piece that took second place at Benediction Coding Party #4, made by a two-person team of coder and graphician.

summary: Atari Programming Champions' Atari 8-bit demo from 1994, coded by Little Beatle Software with music by Marucha and graphics by Dave. It won the demo compo at Shadows Copy Party 1994.
why: A compo winner from the mid-1990s Atari 8-bit scene, tagged as a dentro and built around shade-bob effects.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by Raster of Computer Platform Unlimited, who did both the code and the music. It won the Atari Demo competition at Forever 2004.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2004, and a one-man production with Raster handling both code and soundtrack.

summary: Contrast's 1993 Amstrad CPC demo, coded by Gozeur with graphics by ZZ Top and music by Ric: a full-screen colour plasma above a control panel, with a large scrolling message underneath.
why: A thin fact sheet, but a tidy single-effect CPC demo from 1993 with an original soundtrack by Ric, uploaded by its coder Gozeur.

summary: A New Year 2015 intro for the Atari 8-bit from Desire, with code by Heaven, graphics by Alien and music by Triace. A large logo sits above a fire effect, with a mirrored scroller underneath.
why: A small seasonal greeting from Desire, made by an established Atari XL trio and released on New Year's Day 2015. It's a short, easy watch rather than a compo entry.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by PMWD, with code and design by 0xF and music by Ryxa. It won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2003.
why: A compo winner in one of the tightest size categories, fitting both visuals and Ryxa's music into a kilobyte.

summary: A one-screen C64 demo by Chorus, coded by Clarence with music by DRAX: a band of dense, moving raster-split patterns above a scroller and a colourful Chorus logo. It won the C64 Demo category of Demo of the Year 2014.
why: Sceners were baffled by how the dense colour splits were done, and debated FLI, badlines and bank switching for years. Clarence explained it as sine-moved rasterbars drawn into an FLI area. They also praise the colour and pattern choices.

quote.text: Awesome trick! Colors and patterns are also very well selected.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Madram, released at Revision 2023 where it placed 6th in the Oldskool 4k Intro competition.
why: A size-limited CPC intro from a strong Revision field. Worth a look for how much imagery Madram fits into 4K.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music), which came second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2013.
why: A runner-up in Forever 2013's Atari 1K compo, fitting both code and music into a single kilobyte.

summary: Monopsy 2 is a Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Wilds, released in July 2006. It placed second in the demo competition at Árok 2006.
why: A runner-up at Árok 2006 and a showcase for the Plus 4 scene of the mid-2000s. Worth a look for anyone exploring what the TED machines can do.

summary: Genesis Project's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, placed third in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k19. Code and charset by Shadow, music by MCH, logos by Facet.
why: A small-size compo entry from Genesis Project that placed at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: Padua's Commodore 64 demo, second in the demo compo at Transmission64 2022. Its graphics are built from just five characters, a constraint the Italian title, 'five', hints at.
why: Sceners called it the most original release at the party and praised its minimalist design, its flow and Toggle's music. One commenter found that the idea wore thin without conventional effects.

quote.text: Just takes five to make an awesome demo! Love the approach and minimalistic design!

summary: Fraction's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Rush Hours 1998, with code from six coders and guest graphics from Shell, ALG, Colitt and Talbot, plus music by Kordiaukis.
why: A compo winner at Rush Hours 1998. The disk also carries a note coded by Dux announcing that Shell, Chash and Signor had left for Caution, though Shell's code still made it into the demo.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo that won the demo compo at Castellum Secretum 2007, with code and graphics by Krusty and music by PulkoMandy.
why: It took first place in the Castellum Secretum 2007 demo compo, and it's a short, compact piece of work from a two-person Benediction team.

summary: Atlantis's cow-themed C64 demo that won the Oldschool / Alternative Platforms compo at MountainBytes 2023, with code by Honcho, Dr. Science and Maxlide, graphics by Almighty God and Lobo, and music by theK.
why: Sceners call it fresh and single out the opening, a rotating cow, a cow on a motorbike and a 3D dot cow.

quote.text: Yay, this is fresh! I love the beginning, and the rotating cow is really cool!

summary: Atlantis's C64 demo marking the group's 30th anniversary, winner of the Oldschool Demo compo at Function 2021. A large crew of graphicians, coders and musicians, including Chris Wemyss, Mibri and theK on music.
why: Sceners single out the wild graphics, the mix of animations and graphic modes, and the tempo of parts and transitions, all in the group's recognisable, entertaining style.
highlights: Chris Wemyss, Mibri and theK music

quote.text: Some insane screens. Such a lovely combination of animations, great wild graphics and graphic-modes. Really the best kind of mix I can imagine!

summary: Disaster Area's 4K intro for the unexpanded VIC-20, coded by ript, which won the Oldschool demo compo at Syntax 2007.
why: A compo winner squeezed into 4K on one of the most cramped 8-bit machines, beating full-size oldschool entries at Syntax 2007.

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Virtual Vision Group and Otomata Labs, with code by Rcl and music by Pator, that won the ZX Spectrum Intro compo at Xenium 2025.
why: A compo winner at Xenium 2025 that was also nominated for Best Demo at the GOTY ZX Spectrum Awards 2025, a notable result for a 4K intro. It is tagged for anaglyph 3D.

summary: An Amstrad Plus invitation intro by Impact and Aggression for the Benediction Coding Party, with code and graphics by AST and music by !Cube.
why: A recent invitation for a CPC coding party, made for the Amstrad Plus hardware rather than the stock CPC.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Ate Bit, released in 2009: an interactive music toy where you press keys to jam lead, bass and drum patterns.
why: An unusual take on the 1K format, giving you something to play rather than just watch. It was well received on Pouët.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro by PG and MaPa for issue 55 of the Czech disk magazine Flop, released in April 2012.
why: A short, well-liked intro for a long-running Atari disk magazine. The fact sheet doesn't say much beyond that.

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by FIRE, with code, music and graphics all by Luca. It placed third in the combined 8-bit demo/intro compo at SceneCon 2007.
why: A one-person production on a less-crowded platform, with Luca handling every part of it, and a podium finish in a compo shared with other 8-bit machines.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by introspec, placed 2nd in the Wild compo at Forever 2014. It recreates the look of the Sinclair-era brochure screen, complete with a mock 1982 Sinclair loading screen.
why: A size-limited Spectrum intro that placed in a Wild compo at Forever 2014, made by introspec, who also uploaded the video.

summary: Dream's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at BCC Party 2015, with music by MCH, code by DJ Gruby and kenji, and graphics from five artists.
why: Sceners praise how it holds one dark, pagan mood from start to finish, with the window part and the closing candle screen singled out, along with MCH's tune and a cosy 90s demo feel.

quote.text: Great how this demos manages to keep the theme and mood alive throughout the whole demo!

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Lamers, with code by Ajcek, music by Wieczór and graphics by At0m. It placed 4th in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A small Silly Venture compo entry from a Polish Atari group. Worth a look for anyone exploring the 16K intro category on the XL/XE.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Dalthon of Joker that draws the Deadline party logo, based on Pixtur's original design. It placed third in the 256b intro compo at Deadline 2021.
why: Third place at Deadline 2021 in the 256-byte category, fitting a recognisable line-drawn party logo into a very small size limit.

summary: Genesis Project's demo for the Sharp MZ-700, placed 2nd in the Wild compo at Gubbdata 2022, with code by Shadow, graphics by Illmidus and music by MCH.
why: A rare demo for the Sharp MZ-700 from a group better known on the C64, and it took second place in the Gubbdata 2022 Wild compo.

summary: Code Busters' ZX Spectrum 128K demo, which placed 4th in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997. Credits include RST7, Max Iwamoto, Husein and Iron on code, with music by RST7 and Slash.
why: It is tagged for Spectrum multicolour and stellar modes, which pack more colour into the screen than the standard attribute grid usually allows. That makes it a good look at late-1990s Russian Spectrum graphics tricks.

summary: An April Fools' Day intro for the C64 from Adam West Group, with code and graphics by Mermaid and music by Technic: a big pot-bellied Batman picture over a French scroller boasting about its 'incredible plotters'.
why: A joke at the expense of Amstrad CPC Batman demos that sceners took in good humour. They single out Mermaid's Batman picture and the deadpan plotter, which seems to manage one dot per frame.

quote.text: Brilliant. Simple and effective.

summary: Fairlight's LEGO-themed C64 demo, moh's first for the group, with music by zabutom and graphics by Vodka and Ogami. It came 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2015.
why: Sceners found it fresh and jolly next to the heavily polished demos of the time, and singled out zabutom's new soundtrack and the nostalgia of 1980s LEGO Space sets.
highlights: scrolling text over LEGO spaceship art

quote.text: the demo really catches my nostalgic lego feeling

summary: TSJ's C64 demo, placed 2nd in the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2021: a remake of and tribute to Ratt and Benn's classic Trap demo, with code by Trap, graphics by The Sarge and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners call it a worthy tribute that improves on the original everywhere, praising The Sarge's updated graphics, the animation and Jammer's soundtrack, especially the rendition of a familiar tune at the end.

quote.text: A worthy tribute to the original.  Beautifully updated graphics, great animation (the drummer is so world weary!) and sound design.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Dox of Joker, placed 2nd in the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2022. A Christmas tree drawn in green dots, topped with a red star.
why: A second place at DiHalt in a 256-byte category, fitting a festive scene into a tiny Spectrum program.

summary: Joker's 256-byte procedural graphics entry for the ZX Spectrum, placed second in the oldskool procedural gfx compo at Lovebyte 2024. It draws an image out of rows of black lines that swell and thin like waveforms.
why: A second place at Lovebyte 2024 for a picture generated from just 256 bytes of code, with the title pointing to the Mona Lisa as its subject.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by A Life in Hell that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Syntax 2009.
why: It took first place in the Oldskool Demo competition at Syntax 2009. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best way to judge it.

summary: Taquart's 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit, coded by 0xF with music by X-Ray, which won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2013.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2013 that packs code and music into just 1K.

summary: Ilmenit's 128-byte intro for the Atari XL/XE, winner of the Oldschool 128 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2021 in the 128-byte category, and one of the size-limited intros that also fits in sound.

summary: Inka's Game Boy Color demo, coded with music by Lai and graphics by Gaxar, which won the Other Platform Demo compo at The Project 2001.
why: A compo winner from the early Game Boy Color scene, and an example of a party-made handheld demo from 2001.
highlights: big blocky text over a red picture

summary: Saviour's 256-byte Commodore 64 intro that won the 256B intro compo at Xenium 2025: a chunky, colourful Julia fractal that morphs and splits across the screen.
why: A compo winner in a tight size class. Sceners point out how good-looking and fast the Julia fractal is for 256 bytes, and credit the sound effects for lifting it further.

quote.text: surprisingly good looking and fast julia fractal. the sfx make it very good :)

summary: Baze's 32-byte ZX Spectrum intro that won the 32 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2025: a greyscale procedural pattern with sound, fitted into 32 bytes.
why: A compo winner at Lovebyte 2025 in one of the smallest size categories, and tagged as a tiny intro that manages sound as well as visuals.

summary: Linearix is a 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by Busy and Noro. It won the ZX 1K Intro compo at Forever 2026.
why: It took first place in the 1K intro competition at Forever 2026.

summary: Gorgh's 256-byte intro with sound for the Atari 8-bit, which won the 256 Byte Intro compo at Lost Party 2022.
why: A compo winner at Lost Party 2022 that fits code and sound into 256 bytes on the Atari XL/XE.

summary: Gorgh's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum, with sound, which won the ZX Spectrum 256b intro compo at speccy.pl party 2022.1.
why: A compo winner that fits both visuals and sound into 256 bytes.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Krill and Fanta that won the C64 4K Intro compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001, built around colourful raster bars.
why: Sceners praise its rasters and its music, and the credits screen lists Caprice Design and Seba alongside Krill and Fanta.

quote.text: Very nice rasters and good music too.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by nyuk, with music and graphics by Brightentayle, that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Sochiparty 2014.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Sochiparty 2014. The fact sheet doesn't record anything more about its standing.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by xeen, which won the Atari XL/XE 256b intro compo at Silly Venture 2k21 WE.
why: Won its compo at Silly Venture and was nominated for Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022.

summary: Slipstream's teletext demo for the BBC Micro, coded, drawn and scored by TôBach, which placed 4th in the demo compo at Inércia Demoparty 2023.
why: A one-person production built entirely in the BBC Micro's teletext mode, with TôBach handling code, graphics and music. A solid example of what blocky Mode 7 graphics can do in a modern party demo.

summary: A 1K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Optimus, who also wrote the code. It placed 5th in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #5 in 2025.
why: A size-limited CPC intro with its source code released, so it's worth a look for anyone curious about how much fits into a kilobyte on the Amstrad.

summary: Aids' Atari 8-bit demo, coded and designed by Ars with music by Greg, which won the demo compo at Lato Ludzików 1999. It shows digitised-looking graffiti photos and ends on a text credits screen.
why: A compo winner from the late-1990s Polish Atari scene, and one that needs a 320K-expanded machine to run.

summary: Fairlight and Crest's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Deadline Reloaded 2003, with code by Dane, Hollowman and Puterman and music and graphics by Dane, built around a war theme.
why: A compo winner that sceners remember fondly as short and to the point. Several commenters single out "the note" as a favourite moment, though some felt it ends abruptly.

quote.text: one of my all time fave, short but sweet.

summary: A C64 cracktro by Orb, entered in the Oldskool Cracktro category at the Facebook Oldskool Cracktro Compo 2011, released in February 2011.
why: A modern take on the classic crack intro, made for a compo dedicated to the old-school cracktro style.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, made entirely by Dhor (graphics, code and music), which came third in the Atari demo compo at Forever 2008.
why: A one-person production that placed in the Forever 2008 Atari demo compo, with Dhor handling the code, graphics and music alone.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo from GPA, released in 1995, with code and music by Tom&Jerry and further music by Targhan. On screen, greetings text sits over a starfield of dots that sweeps towards the viewer, with a scroller along the bottom.
why: A mid-nineties CPC demo addressed to the platform's remaining users, from a period when the scene was thinning out. It's a short, simple watch built around its starfield and messages.

summary: Fairlight's C64 intro from December 2017, with code by Trasher, graphics by The Sarge and music by Wiklund. The Sarge finally completes a dragon-and-knight picture left unfinished almost three decades earlier.
why: Sceners welcomed The Sarge's return and the long-awaited finish to the dragon, with its unexpected new head. They also single out Wiklund's soundtrack, the crisp charset and the greetings logos drawn in each group's style.
highlights: greetings in each group's logo style

quote.text: Great to finally see that dragon finished 8) Love the crisp charset and the logos. Soundtrack on repeat!

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by Quasimodos, released in 1995, with code by Kroger, graphics by Raven and music by Morgoth. It placed 4th in the Atari 8bit demo compo at QuaST 1995.
why: A mid-nineties Polish Atari 8-bit demo from the QuaST 1995 compo, where it finished fourth. The fact sheet doesn't say much beyond its credits and placing.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX81 by NollKollTroll, released in 2016: a scroller of large letters built from blocky character-style segments on a white screen.
why: A small, focused example of what fits into a single kilobyte on the ZX81, an unexpected machine for a scroller.

summary: Commodore PET demo by Genesis Project and Distant Future, shown on a Commodore 8296 PET, with code by Elder0010 and graphics and direction by LRNZ. It tied for third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2025.
why: A recent example of a full demo on the rarely used, character-only PET, good enough to share a podium place in a mixed oldschool compo at Nordlicht 2025.

summary: Genesis Project's Amstrad CPC demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by Facet and music by MCH. It placed 4th in the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2023.
why: A C64 group trying its hand on the CPC, with a Gerp compo placing to show for it.

summary: Hack n' Trade's C64 demo made for the Floppy 2003 demo compo, where it placed 7th, and finally put together for release in 2007. Code, graphics and text by Frantic, Gosh, Vinzi and BMX, with music by Goto80.
why: Sceners single out the organic intro part, BMX's graffiti logo and Goto80's tunes, and call it an entertaining, nicely designed group effort with an original style.

quote.text: Love that organic intro part that looks lke LIFE.  The city scape is mighty fine, as is the last scroll part with the subtle colours. Great entertainment! :)

summary: A 32-byte Atari 8-bit intro coded by JAC! of WUDSN, released in 2012. It runs silently, with no sound.
why: Released with no party placing or awards, it shows how much a single coder can put on screen in just 32 bytes.

summary: A ZX Spectrum cracktro by Triumph from 2011, released with a crack of the game Trojan. Greetings scroll in a blue box beside a cyan silhouette and a colourful graffiti-style logo before the game itself starts.
why: A thin fact sheet, but a tidy example of a modern-era Spectrum cracktro, done in the style of the old crack intros.

summary: A ZX Spectrum cracktro by SoftLight and GoodBoy for the game Acolyte, with intro code and graphics by SoftLight, music by Jam, and GoodBoy's crack, trainer and bugfix.
why: A tidy example of 2009 Spectrum cracking-scene work. It bundles a trainer and a bugfix with the crack, and its intro plugs the group's other recent releases.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo from 2002, the final version of Decade, with code by AEG and DCP, graphics by AEG and Fzool and music by SoNiC and Compod. It opens with a laser burning through a fake BASIC screen.
why: Sceners single out the laser effect at the start. Comments note the rest leans on 4x4-pixel effects and that even this '100%' release still feels unfinished.

quote.text: Love the laser effect in the beginning of the demo.

summary: FST's C64 trackmo, coded by Bobi W with music by Wacek, which came 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2010. It runs through chunky, colourful character-resolution effects.
why: Sceners found it smooth and colourful with good music, and rated the code. Others noted that it keeps to 8x8 resolution and reuses its plasma.

quote.text: I really like it - smooth and colorful with good music

summary: A ZX Spectrum game from 4th Dimension, released in 2009 and listed as both a demo and a game. You steer a bat at the bottom of a grid-lined playfield while figures and shapes tumble around the screen.
why: A rare crossover entry that wraps a playable game in demo presentation. The video credits Triebkraft, 4th Dimension and bfox.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by JTN, released at Chaos Constructions 2004, where it came second in the 8 bit 640Kb Demo competition.
why: A podium finish at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties of its time. The fact sheet is otherwise thin, so the video is the best guide to what it offers.

summary: Hooy-Program's demo for the stock 48K ZX Spectrum, coded by Hellboj and Szuwarek with music and graphics by Yerzmyey and graphics by Aki. It placed 2nd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2010.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2010, it was built specifically for the original 48K machine rather than later Spectrum models, with AY music from Yerzmyey.

summary: A small C64 demo by Dekadence, with code and music by BriteLite and graphics by Bracket. It placed 12th in the C64 demo compo at KozMOS 2012.
why: Sceners singled out its colour fades, clean design and graphics, along with the moving 2x2 hires text plotter. One later commenter called it underrated.

quote.text: Spectacular color fades! Fresh design and gfx.

summary: A Plus/4 demo by Legion Of Doom, coded by Csabo, themed on the Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics and released in February 2010.
why: A themed one-off from the Plus/4 scene, timed to the Vancouver Games. Its source code has been made available.

summary: JAC!'s Atari 8-bit demake of an "old cranky style" Amiga intro, with graphics by Rebb and music by Premium. A 12K intro that placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014.
why: A tribute that recreates a classic Amiga intro style on the Atari 8-bit, built as a 12K intro according to the video title.

summary: A C64 music demo by 4mat of Ate Bit, made for the SFX FM Expander cartridge: an FM tune layered over SID, with a scroller explaining the player and test playback of SID songs.
why: Sceners single out the tune and how subtly it uses the FM chip, with the SID carrying the lead voices, so it still sounds good without the expander.

quote.text: Clever how the SID supplies the dominant voices (and still actually sounds OK without the expander too)!

summary: A 1994 Commodore 64 demo by The Obsessed Maniacs, with code by kb and Luke, music by kb and design and charset by Half-Elf. It's tagged as a humorous, interactive parody.
why: An interactive joke demo from a mid-90s C64 group. The one CSDb comment singles out its animation as the best part.

quote.text: the animation is really the best part

summary: A Thomson demo by Puls, with code, graphics and music all by sam. It placed second in the Other 8-bit Demo compo at Forever 2016.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2016 and a rare Thomson entry in that compo. It is tagged as a karaoke prod, and its title doubles as a sing-along line.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by chlumpie, placed 6th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A compact Atari 2600 production with a techno soundtrack. Its source code is available, and the video carries an epilepsy warning for its flashing visuals.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum invitation intro by Neon for Lovebyte 2025, shown in the Size Coding Showcase at Inércia 2024. A blocky red heart sits above the party name, dates and web address.
why: A compact party invitation that fits the Lovebyte "Blind Date" theme and all its party details into 256 bytes on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: Element54's two-disk-side Commodore 64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2026. A four-person team: WVL on code, Hammerfist and Genius on graphics, Youth on music.
why: Sceners single out the double perspective zoom scrollers, the colourful greetings part and a soundtrack likened to a movie score. Several note how much a team of four packed in, and the source code is available.

quote.text: Every single effect is really clever, and the music and graphics really set the mood. I love it!

summary: A VIC-20 demo by K2, coded by Yago with music by AMB and graphics by guest artist James of Wrath Designs. It placed 6th in the 8-Bit Demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008.
why: A rare demo for the unexpanded-looking VIC-20 from a scene that sees few new releases, entered into a mixed 8-bit compo alongside bigger machines.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by xxl (code), Vidol (graphics) and Mister Beep (music), placed 6th in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A small, compact Silly Venture compo entry from a code, graphics and music trio, fitting its show into 16K on a stock Atari XL/XE.

summary: Atlantis and Delysid's zombie-themed C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at ATWOODS Summer Open-Air 2020, with music by DivertigO and graphics by Lobo and Mythus.
why: Sceners praise how consistently it holds its horror theme, with the music matching the mood. The opening logos, the first scroller and the credits part are the bits most often singled out.
highlights: logos moving apart at the start

quote.text: Love this one - especially the small things that make it so great. How everything fits together and the music fits the mood and theme.

summary: Ate Bit's ZX Spectrum intro that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2005, with code by evilpaul, music by 4mat and graphics by Eater.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2005, beating the other entries in the Oldskool Demo competition with a small team of three.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by R0ger and PG, with music by HardCore, that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2019. The video title calls it a demo/invitro, and the scroller invites viewers to Flop 63 from a Czech club site.
why: It took first place in the Atari Demo competition at Forever 2019, and it doubles as an invitation to another party.
highlights: car driving towards a city skyline

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Entire Group, with code and music by Rob F. and graphics by Mellona. It won the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2010.
why: It took first place in the demo competition at ZX AAA Compo 2010, and it makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Neon that placed second in the Oldskool 256b Intro compo at Outline 2023: a cloud of white dots on black, framed by blocky blue and red corner patterns.
why: A podium finish at Outline shows how much a 256-byte Spectrum intro can still do. The title nods to Steven Vickers, who wrote the Spectrum ROM.

summary: Delysid's space and science-fiction themed C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at BCC Party 2017, with code by nomiStake, music by Linus and graphics by Shine.
why: Sceners praise its flow, design and care for detail, and the large amount of hand-made artwork from Shine, who also drew the PETSCII screens. Several felt it should have won the compo.

quote.text: This demo surprised me time and again with its care for detail, lots of nice tiny things to discover, great flow, slick, with decent code!

summary: OMG's C64 demo, coded and drawn by Sparta with music by Jammer, that came third in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2019. Its centrepiece is huge spheres made of vector plots, with a plasma part and a scrolling text.
why: Sceners single out the record-breaking amount of vector plots, with Dane noting one of HCL's records was smashed, plus Jammer's soundtrack. Sparta also wrote his own loader, Sparkle, for it.

quote.text: Classic demo design and super sweet sound by Jammer, but what really stands out is the spheres of course.

summary: Bonzai's Commodore 64 demo, sixth in the Lethal Display series, which came second in the demo competition at Zoo 2024. Code by Trap, Walt and Ricky, graphics by Fox and Facet, music by Metal, Laxity and DRAX.
why: A second place at Zoo 2024 from a large Bonzai line-up, with three musicians and a concept credited to Trap and Facet. The compo slide billed it under a deliberately garbled title.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum invitation demo from 2021, inviting sceners to send work to Out of Compo 2021.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it's an invitation intro from deMarche, tagged nsfw, and well received on Pouët.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo from 1992, which placed 5th in the C64 demo compo at the Light and Phenomena Easter Party that year.
why: One commenter singles out an interactive part where you steer a spaceship and the starfield moves to match.

quote.text: The best part for me is the one where you can fly the space ship and the star field moves accordingly.

summary: 0xc64's debut C64 demo, coded by Jesder with graphics by JSL and music by FeekZoid. It placed joint fourth in the Oldschool Demo compo at Syntax 2014 and takes the shape of a classic logo-and-scroller intro.
why: Sceners welcomed it as a strong first release with real oldschool feel. They single out JSL's logo and FeekZoid's music, and note how well everything fits together.

quote.text: you need no multiplexer when you have good taste!

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo by lft, placed 8th in the X 2026 demo compo: a PETSCII cartoon story about lemmings, with detailed hires lemmings marching across the blocky character graphics.
why: Sceners single out the storytelling and humour, calling it a narrative-driven demo of the old kind, and puzzle over how so many hires lemmings, some in the border, are on screen at once. lft later published a video explaining the trick.

quote.text: i miss narrative-driven demos of yore in general, so this almost brought me to tears (of joy). funny, heartwarming, captivating, of perfect length, 10/10.

summary: An MSX2 demo by Digital Sounds System, coded by visy with graphics by SiikiKala and Lynn and music by Alpha C. It placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2018.
why: A rare MSX2 entry in a major party's oldskool compo, from a small team credited in full on the fact sheet.

summary: Agony Design's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at 4x4 Puke Party 1995, with code by Druid, Inco and Colabor, music by Shogoon and graphics from a large team of artists.
why: Druid describes it as the group's flagship release. Sceners point to the 4x4 3D landscape, Roder's IFLI picture, the fast-paced music and the big font, and it was voted second best demo in Design #1.

quote.text: Some nice effects, graphics and music in there. I love the big font too. Very decent demo for its day.

summary: Tristesse's 1KB intro for the Atari 8-bit, which won the Atari Intro compo at Forever 2012.
why: A compo winner squeezed into a single kilobyte, worth a look as a compact example of what tiny Atari XL/XE intros can manage.

summary: Censor Design's Barbie-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2023, with graphics by Talent, DeeKay, Carrion and Prowler and music by Magnar Harestad and Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out the clouds, the FLI Kefrens bars, the torus with scrolling balls and Peacemaker's $d01d-split sprite stretcher, along with unusual dithered colours and the flamingo scene.

quote.text: the clouds are fantastic, the torus + scrollballs are great, but that sprite stretcher is a fxxking monster - wow!

summary: Debris's 256-byte intro for the ZX Spectrum, coded by Tiboh, which won the 256b intro compo at Raww.orgy 2009.
why: A compo winner in the 256-byte category, packing full-screen moving colour patterns into a tiny Spectrum program. The video title notes AY sound as well.

summary: AAA Band's ZX Spectrum demo, placed third in the ZX Spectrum Demo competition at DiHalt 2011.
why: A podium finish at DiHalt 2011, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, from a thin fact sheet with no comments to go on.

summary: Onslaught's C64 party scroller for Syntax 2009 in Melbourne, which placed 7th in the Oldskool Demo compo: a scrolling greeting message over colour bars and graphics.
why: A small party prod made for an Australian event. The scrolltext calls it an Aussie event long overdue. It's a snapshot of the C64 scene turning up at Syntax's early editions.

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo by Dual Crew, with code by Zaz, graphics by Devistator and music by ne7. It placed 6th in the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012.
why: Sceners praised the colourful logo, ne7's music and especially the DYSP scroller, which runs through the side borders and is cleanly cut at both edges, something HCL said he hadn't seen before.
highlights: DYSP scroller in the side borders

quote.text: That scroller seems to be correctly cut in both sideborders, never seen anything like that on a DYSP-scroller.

summary: Nintendo's own promotional demo for the Game Boy Color, released in January 1999 to show off the new handheld's colour screen.
why: A commercial demo rather than a scene production, made by the hardware's maker itself. It's a curiosity for anyone interested in how Nintendo pitched the Game Boy Color at launch.

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, with code, design and music by Gasman and photography by Natbat. It placed 4th in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007.
why: An unusual Spectrum demo built around photographs, here converted into chunky, dithered colour blocks. It is also released under a Creative Commons licence.

summary: Dirty Minds' Amstrad CPC demo, coded by Optimus with graphics by CeD and Voxfreax and music by Sice. It won the CPC demo compo at Amstrad Expo 2010.
why: A compo winner at Amstrad Expo 2010, put together by a small CPC team.

summary: Antares' ZX Spectrum demo with code by Konex, graphics by Fil and music by EA. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 1999 and placed third at Chaos Constructions 999.999 the same year.
why: A compo winner at CAFe 1999 that also finished on the podium at Chaos Constructions, so it stood up well against the Russian Spectrum scene of its day.

summary: Lethargy's Commodore 64 4K intro, coded by Nicron with music by Vincenzo, which came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2026. Rows of shaded balls move and twist against a grey background.
why: Sceners point out that the SID tune takes up most of the 4K, yet the intro still looks and sounds good. The source is available too.

quote.text: Very good 4K, especially considering that the SID takes 3 of the 4 K.

summary: Defence Force's Oric demo by Dbug, who did code, graphics and music, with a Jochen Hippel tune also used. It placed third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013.
why: A Solskogen podium finish for the Oric, made almost entirely by one person, Dbug, and released for the machine's 30th year, as the title suggests.
highlights: Oric circuit blueprints drawn on screen

summary: Eternity Industry's ZX Spectrum demo from 1999, which won the demo compo at DiHalt 1999 and placed second at Chaos Constructions 999.999 (first in the alternative results).
why: A compo winner at two Russian parties in the same year, with a large crew credited for code, graphics, 3D modelling and rendering, textures and ASCII art.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by The Atari OldSkoolerz and Computer Platform Unlimited, with music by 505, entered in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2007, where it placed 13th.
why: A small Atari 8-bit release from Breakpoint 2007's Console/Real Wild compo. The title translates as "a group of stars", and the stills show a rotating cluster of dots.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 2600 by Ed Fries, which came second in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12.
why: A second place at Silly Venture from a 128-byte VCS program, coded by Ed Fries. It shows how much the 2600 can be made to do in almost no code.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Triad, coded by Iopop with music by Dalezy, that placed third in the C64 4K intro compo at Breakpoint 2006. Minimal, monochrome animated patterns of circles and rings.
why: Sceners single out Iopop's originality and design, and how the shifting patterns and Dalezy's funky, repetitive tune work together until the whole thing turns hypnotic.
highlights: grid of pulsing circles and rings

quote.text: The way the effects and the funky repetitive tune seem to walk hand in hand, together with the strange change of patterns makes it just damn nice.

summary: Up Rough's invitation to Datastorm 2014 on the NEC PC Engine, with code by MooZ, graphics by Spot and music by Octapus. Party details scroll as text over moving rainbow-and-cloud stripes.
why: A rare demoscene production for the PC Engine, and its source code has been released. It is a well-received invitation on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by MKM, who wrote the code. It placed 8th in the combined demo/intro compo at Sommarhack 2019.
why: A small piece of code entered against full-size demos and intros in a shared compo at Sommarhack 2019.
highlights: grey streaks falling down the screen

summary: A short SAM Coupé demo coded by Sir David, with graphics by Ziutek and music by Pyramex. It won the Other plattform Demo compo at Forever 2013.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2013 and a rare demo release for the SAM Coupé, from a small team covering code, graphics and music.

summary: Tristesse's Atari 8-bit invitation to Last Party 2017 in Opalenica, Poland, shown in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2017, where it placed 5th. Code by Mono, music by LiSU, text by Vasco.
why: An invitation for a one-off party marking 20 years since the first copy-party in Opalenica, made by a well-staffed Tristesse crew with graphics from Electron and Replay.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Outsiders, with code by apeape, graphics by Blackbear and music by Nick Roll. It came second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2018, where it was shown with a 16+ warning.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions 2018, one of the main Spectrum parties, makes it worth a look for Blackbear's pictures and Nick Roll's soundtrack.

summary: Black Mail's 1989 Commodore 64 demo Tequila Sunrise: a large hand-drawn planet-over-city picture sits above a chunky logo-font scroller, with a face emblem and the group's signature in the corner.
why: Sceners praise it as a nicely designed intro, and one commenter singles out the tune by cd/mon. Additional graphics are credited to Orc and Skyline in the comments.

quote.text: Now this is a nicely designed intro.

summary: A comeback C64 demo from Digital Excess and X-Ample Architectures, released at Evoke 2017, where it placed 8th in the Alternative Platforms compo. Code by Joachim Multermann, graphics by Björn Odendahl and Thomas Heinrich, music by Gösta Bergfeld.
why: Sceners greeted it as the return of childhood heroes after decades away. They single out its deliberately oldskool scroller style, done with care and a slick finish.

quote.text:
Very oldskool scroller style demo.
You can see however it was coded with love and looks slick.

summary: Genesis Project's Christmas greeting demo for the C64, released in December 2017: a festive picture by Mermaid of Santa, a reindeer and penguins, with a scrolltext of seasonal greetings and music by MCH.
why: A small, warm seasonal release that sceners loved for its cute pixels and catchy Christmas SID, and for seeing Papademos coding again.

quote.text: Very cute. Lovely pixels and sound, nicely put together by papademos

summary: Singular Crew's C64 party invitation with code by Scorpy, Poison and Soci, graphics by Poison and Leon and music by Vincenzo. It placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016.
why: Sceners point out that it's an invite with the effort of a full demo: fast cuts between realtime effects, Poison's design, a hand-written font and a soundtrack that fits the pace.

quote.text: For a party invite, you guys sure put a lot of effort into this! Very fast cuts between effects, giving me way too little time to ponder on how I would do it, if I could.

summary: Wings is a 2005 MSX2 demo by Infinite. The stills show large words such as "currents unseen", "WOLF" and "threadbare" set on plain coloured backgrounds.
why: A thinly documented MSX2 release from Infinite. It's one to try if you're exploring MSX demos beyond the better-known titles.

summary: Extend's C64 demo, finished around four years late and released with help from Crossbow/Crest, that won the demo compo at Zoo 1997. The title on screen is deliberately spelled "Total Epygt".
why: A compo winner whose graphics a 2001 review rated from okay to excellent, singling out a black, white and grey piece. Sceners remember the final twirl effect over a portrait as something new to them.

quote.text: the twirl effect over a picture is real cool

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Pr0be, which placed second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2006.
why: A compo-placing entry squeezed into a single kilobyte, from Forever's Atari 8-bit size-limited competition. Note that the YouTube capture has no sound.

summary: Rebels' Atari VCS demo, coded, drawn and scored by chlumpie alone, which placed second in the Atari VCS 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k22 SE.
why: A one-person 2600 production that took second place at Silly Venture, where the VCS has its own demo competition.

summary: A 256-byte Tetris-style game for the Atari 8-bit by atariBDSM, coded by Sadoslav and Count Ulrich von Chain. It came second in the Atari XL/XE 256b Game compo at Silly Venture 2k24 WE.
why: A playable falling-block game squeezed into 256 bytes, and a podium finish in Silly Venture's 256-byte game compo.

summary: P_Malin's 256-byte BBC Micro intro, written in BASIC, which came second in the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2024.
why: A podium finish at Lovebyte from a 256-byte BBC Micro intro written in BASIC, with a title that nods to 2001: A Space Odyssey.

summary: A C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence, released outside any competition in January 2018, with code by a team including Stone, Perplex and Pantaloon, and music by Kristian Røstøen, Ole Marius Pettersen and Stone.
why: Sceners called it compo-winner grade despite skipping the compos, and singled out the tech-tech DYCP, the wavy checkerboard, the multi-layered parallax scrollers in the greetings part and the tunes. Short but well liked.

quote.text: Compo-winner grade demo released out of competition, great! :)

summary: Bitmunchers' ZX Spectrum demo from 1996, entered in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1996, with code by Megafire and Russian Mouse 2 and music and graphics by Demon.
why: A mid-nineties Spectrum demo from Bitmunchers, shown at Enlight 1996, with graphics shared between Demon, Pink and MiKael.

summary: Genesis Project's 2011 C64 demo So Retro, by Mermaid with music from Mr. Death and a charset by hedning: a deliberately old-school show of swinging logos, rasters, scrollers and hand-drawn pictures.
why: A love letter to 1980s demo style. Sceners praise Mr. Death's music, the flow and the pictures, and it struck a chord as a defence of the scroll text as the soul of a demo.

quote.text: cool music, cool flow, cool pix... welcome back in 1986! :-)

summary: A one-file C64 demo by Cascade, released on CSDb for its Christmas Fun Competition 2013. It shows a colourful flare effect, billed as a small expansion of a well-known demo effect, framed by Cascade logo sprites.
why: Sceners praised the look of the flare, the music and the logo sprites, and welcomed Cascade's return. Its speedcode-driven effect sparked a coding discussion among Bitbreaker, Oswald and the author.

quote.text: the flare looking amazing and music as well as the cascade logo rox!

summary: Censor Design's 1991 Commodore 64 demo, the eighth and, per the video title, final chapter of the Wonderland series, with code from Psycho, Bob, Guran, Swallow and Geggin, graphics by four artists and music by Danko.
why: Remembered fondly by sceners who saw it at the time. Geggin's part gets singled out for its design and surprising effects, with one viewer saying its scroller still impresses.

quote.text: The scroller really blew me away when first seeing this in 1991. Still does actually :)

summary: Genesis Project's C64 invitation for Gubbdata 2020, a one-woman show by Mermaid with Razorback on design. It won the one-filed demo compo at BCC Party 2020 and shows a grumpy old man in hires with scrolling text.
why: Sceners single out the hires picture of the grumpy old man, and the way he grumbles along to SID sound effects. Several joke that he sounds just like them.
highlights: hires picture of grumpy old man

quote.text: Magnificent pic. With the big luminosity gap between black and blue, it's not trivial at all to make something like this truly work.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 64 by Radwar Enterprises, built around speech synthesis through the SID. It came 5th in the C64 Demo compo at Breakpoint 2007 after the 4K compo was cancelled for lack of entries.
why: Sceners were impressed that it does speech synthesis from standard SID sounds without pre-sampled phonemes, something few had tried since SAM, and welcomed it as a comeback release from Radwar.

quote.text: Very nice speechsynth! Pretty impressive, especially since nobody has done anything like this since back when SAM came out!

summary: A ZX Spectrum cracktro-style trainer for Ant Attack by Ate Bit, with code by evilpaul, music by 4mat and graphics by Ray Manta. The video is evilpaul's (Paul Grenfell's) ARTtech seminar at Assembly on hacking retro games.
why: A rare chance to hear the coder explain how a modern trainer for a classic Spectrum game was made, in a talk titled "When Is A Trainer Like A Space Rocket?"

summary: A 4K VIC-20 intro by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, with code, graphics and music all by Viznut. It placed third in the intro competition at Stream 2003.
why: A one-person 4K production for the unexpanded-friendly VIC-20 from Viznut, which earned a podium place at Stream 2003.

summary: Phat is an Amstrad Plus demo by Condense, coded by NoRecess and released in 2008.
why: A non-competing 2008 demo written for the Amstrad Plus rather than the stock CPC, with code by NoRecess.

summary: Noice's 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit, placed third in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2013: a colour-cycling plasma behind the group's chunky logo.
why: A neat example of fitting a full-screen plasma and logo into a kilobyte on the Atari XL/XE, good enough for a podium place at Forever.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by introspec, placed 2nd in the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: A second place at Chaos Constructions in one of the scene's tightest size categories, with a monochrome look built to fit in a single kilobyte.

summary: An Atari 8-bit intro by LaResistance, with code by Probe and music by Miker, that won the 8bit Intro compo at Glucholazy 2010.
why: It took first place in its category at Glucholazy 2010, so it's worth a look as a small, compo-winning Atari intro.

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Return, with code by joker_, music by Slowhand and graphics by Spritus. It won the demo compo at 7DX 2013.
why: A compo winner that sceners singled out for its visuals, praising the intro logo and the setting picture, and seen as a step forward for the group.

quote.text: Really lovely. The logo in the intro and the setting picture are very nice.

summary: oobc's Commodore PET intro for the CBM 8032, by oo and BassCadet, placing 2nd in the Oldskool Intro compo at Simulaatio 2015. Green-screen PETSCII patterns frame big block-letter text and a drawing of a party bus.
why: A rare intro for the Commodore PET that placed second in its compo at Simulaatio 2015. oo and BassCadet shared the code, graphics and design, and BassCadet also wrote the music.

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by evilpaul, released under the Ate Bit name, which won the ZX Spectrum 1K Intro compo at Forever 2007.
why: It took first place in its 1K compo at Forever 2007, so it's a good example of what fits into a kilobyte on the Spectrum.

summary: Genesis Project's PETSCII intro for the C64, squeezed into 4K, which won the C64 4K intro compo at Datastorm 2019.
why: A compo winner that sceners praise for how much it fits into 4K. iAN CooG singles out its PETSCII plasma.

quote.text: amazing work, especially for just 4k..!

summary: Genesis Project's Commodore 64 demo that won the Mixed compo at Syntax Society Summer Party 2012, with code by Shadow and H Macaroni, music by Mr. Death and graphics by Uka, Redcrab and Illmidus.
why: Put together in a day as a nod to smaller parties, it won sceners over with its plasma part, the logos above it and Mr. Death's soundtrack. Several also praise the last part.

quote.text: nice music and the logos above the plasma are just perfect!

summary: Outsiders' ZX Spectrum demo that won the Intro compo at Undefined 2022, with code by apeape, music by Nik-O and graphics by Shuran33.
why: A first-place compo winner at Undefined 2022, and its source code has been released for anyone curious about how it works.

summary: A 1K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Legion Of Doom, with code and music by Csabo. It won the 1K competition at LimiTED 2007.
why: A compo winner in the 1K category at LimiTED 2007, packing code and music into a single kilobyte on the Plus 4.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Only Sprites Compo 2023, made without sprites, bitmaps or characters: everything is drawn with the border and background colour registers and ghostbytes.
why: A cheeky, technically extreme answer to a sprites-only compo. Sceners single out the timing work, the use of the VIC grey-dot bug for effects and Fegolhuzz's tune.
highlights: smooth moving bar near the end

quote.text: This demonstrates the scene-spirit: unintended hardware bug/feature is used for effects that should not be visible in the first place :)

summary: SerzhSoft's 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum 48K with AY music, which won the Grave Digger compo at Chaos Constructions 2021.
why: A compo winner at Chaos Constructions 2021, packed into 4K by a single author who handled the whole production.

summary: Seban's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, with music by Greg and X-Ray, which won the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k24 SE.
why: A compo winner at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, in the 16K intro category.
highlights: big chunky text over a striped planet

summary: A 1K intro for the ZX Spectrum by artёmka that won the Oldschool Intro compo at Xenium 2026.
why: It took first place in its compo at Xenium 2026, fitting its whole show into a kilobyte of code.

summary: Slipstream's demo for the Dragon 32 / TRS-80 family, which won the combined demo compo at Field-FX 2022. The video shows it running from a cassette release on real hardware.
why: A compo winner at Field-FX 2022, and a recent example of new demo work on a machine that rarely gets it.

summary: An invitation ROM for the NES by Battle of the Bits, released in February 2009 to advertise the WinterChip IV chiptune contest.
why: A small piece of chiptune-community history: the flier for a Battle of the Bits contest, made as a ROM that runs on the console itself.

summary: A 512-byte C64 intro by lft that placed 4th in the Oldskool 4K compo at Revision 2015: mirrored, cellular-automaton patterns grow across the screen to a dark ambient soundtrack, running for about eight minutes.
why: A whole slow-building piece from 512 bytes. Sceners pick out the menacing images that seem to emerge from the patterns, and ptoing calls it one of his favourite things anyone has made on the C64.

quote.text: This one one of my favourite things anyone has ever made on the C64. So great.

summary: Samanasuke's ZX Spectrum demo that won the demo compo at Hackers Top Autumn 2010.
why: A compo winner at Hackers Top Autumn 2010, and a good example of a Spectrum demo built around a single drawn portrait.
highlights: woman's portrait built up in stages

summary: sibKrew's ZX Spectrum demo that won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2018, with code by wbcbz7 and rook, graphics by rook and music by Nik-O.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2018. Its title promises a demo with no twister effect, and its tags point to a space invader theme.

summary: Flush's 4K intro for the Atari VCS, coded and drawn by g012 and p0ke, with music by p0ke. It won the 4K intro compo at Very Important Party 2014.
why: A compo winner at Very Important Party 2014, squeezing a full intro into 4K on the Atari 2600, one of the most restrictive machines to code for.
highlights: chunky Flush and Presk title logo

summary: A 16K Amstrad CPC intro by cpcitor, with music by The Other Days and a font by Slime. It placed 6th in the Oldschool Intro compo at Shadow Party 2021.
why: A small, focused CPC intro from a 2021 party compo. Its 60Hz video carries a note that it is meant to be seen at a smooth 50Hz on a real CPC.

summary: Twin is a 32K Atari VCS prod by All You Can Execute from 2024. Its video credits the track to petriform featuring Natt Akuma, played on the TIA sound chip using TIunA.
why: A recent example of what a 32K cartridge can do on the Atari VCS. Its video is titled after the music, with a petriform and Natt Akuma track on the console's TIA chip.

summary: Smash Designs' two-disk-side C64 invitation for the tUM 2008 party, an animated remix of farbrausch's fr-08 invitation. It won the Wild (Alternative Platform) compo at Evoke 2004.
why: A C64 take on a well-known PC invitation that split opinion. Its fans single out Sophira's tunes and the way it goes well beyond the usual logo-and-scroller invitation.

quote.text: Its the best invitation demo I have seen so far.

summary: Icebird's 1998 Game Boy demo, with code by Exoticorn and Mr. Hill, graphics by giZMo and music by Exoticorn. It runs from a 1Mbit cartridge and loops endlessly.
why: An early Game Boy demo from the late 1990s scene. It shows what a small team could get out of the handheld's four shades of grey.

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Commodore VIC-20 by Orb, released in November 2013.
why: A very small VIC-20 intro. There are no compo results or comments to go on, so the size limit is the main reason to look.

summary: Offence's 1992 Commodore 64 demo, shared third in the C64 demo compo at Hurricane and Brutal Summer Party 1992, with guest music from Geir Tjelta, Trond K. Lindanger and others.
why: A favourite of many sceners, who praise it as well coded, pixelled and tuned throughout, singling out Pal's graphics, the soundtrack, smooth effects and the lightning intro.

quote.text: One of my all time favourites. All parts are brilliantly coded, pixeled and tuned.

summary: A 1K intro for the SAM Coupé by Optimus, placed second in the Other 8-bit 1k Intro compo at Forever 2024.
why: A compo-placing size-limited intro on the rarely seen SAM Coupé, from a coder who works across many 8-bit machines.

summary: A small Oric demo from 2006, released under the name of the Centre Marseillais de Paleo Informatique and presented by 6502 Man: a CMPI logo, scrolling French text and a moving checkerboard floor.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it's a modest example of an Oric demo from a French retro-computing club.

summary: An MSX demo by Lieves!Tuore from 1997, coded by Marq with graphics by Marq, Manu and Duke Nemo and music by Yzi.
why: A late-90s MSX demo from the Finnish group Lieves!Tuore, with its source code released. It's well liked on Pouët.

summary: A Christmas intro for the Sharp MZ-700 by Flush and Up Rough, released on Christmas Eve 2018, with code and graphics by MooZ and music by Glafouk.
why: A rare seasonal greeting on the Sharp MZ-700, a machine with little demo activity, and its source code has been released.

summary: A Vectrex demo by Defame and Disaster Area, coded by Krion with music by cTrix, which placed 4th in the oldschool demo compo at Flashback 2015.
why: Demos for the Vectrex's vector display are rare, and this one competed at Flashback 2015. The video is filmed off a real Vectrex rather than captured from an emulator.

summary: Dual Crew Shining's Game Boy Color cracktro for Trouballs, based on the Quartex version of the game, with code by Gilligan, graphics by Adam and music by Heatbeat.
why: A tidy example of a Game Boy Color crack intro from 2001, with a hand-drawn underwater scene and a soundtrack played through the Carillon player.

summary: Assassins' 16K game for the Commodore 16/Plus 4, released in 2010, titled Uwol: Quest for Money.
why: A rare example of a full game squeezed into 16K on the C16, listed as both a 16K intro and a game.
